Arrows in the road point toward the next drop, while a crazy drift around traffic builds the fare and the chain. Passengers shout destinations, and missing the stop burns the tip that was about to land.

The home port keeps the cabinet's urge to ignore lanes. Later sequels changed cities, but this disc is the original fare rush with Axel behind the wheel.
sonic-adventure-2:
Shadow's debut splits Sonic Adventure 2 into a hero story and a dark story, a pairing Sonic Team first released on the Dreamcast. The 2001 scripts put Sonic, Tails, and Knuckles on one side and Shadow, Doctor Eggman, and Rouge on the other.

The hero path climbs toward the Space Colony ARK while the dark path explains why Shadow was woken at all. Rail grinding, treasure hunting, and mech shooting sit in the same campaign instead of one shared moveset.

A later cube edition called Battle added more multiplayer on top of those two stories. This record is the adventure that introduced Shadow, with the extra battle modes arriving as a follow-up.
sonic-adventure-dx:
Mission cards turn Sonic Adventure DX: Director's Cut into an enhanced port of the Dreamcast adventure, not a new numbered sequel. The 2003 cube edition adds Game Gear games and a stack of missions on top of Station Square, the Mystic Ruins, and the Egg Carrier.

Metal Sonic can be met again through those mission goals, and the Chao garden still raises the little creatures hatched from the original gardens. The point of the disc is the first adventure plus those extra tasks, not a numbered sequel.

Players who already finished the Dreamcast story come back for the mission list and the handheld games tucked in the menu. The plot of Chaos and Perfect Chaos stays the one they already know.
kao-the-kangaroo-round-2:
A boxing kangaroo returns in KAO the Kangaroo: Round 2, the sequel Poland's Tate Interactive sent to the cube. Kao still fights with gloves in a cartoon platformer, and this round continues the European series rather than rebooting it.

Levels mix punching foes with the usual run to the exit, and the gloves are the joke and the weapon at once. The first game had already introduced the character; Round 2 is the follow-up that reached Nintendo's disc console.

European players who knew the earlier Kao adventure meet a brighter, broader set of stages here. The cube release is that sequel, gloves and all, not a sports sim about real boxing.
beyond-good-evil:
Jade's camera is the tool that matters in Beyond Good & Evil, Michel Ancel's adventure about a photographer on the planet Hillys. Ubisoft released that story in 2003, and the cube disc is one of the original versions, not a later remaster.

Pey'j, the pig-like uncle, shares the hovercraft and the fights against the DomZ, while Jade files photo reports for a resistance group that does not trust the official news. Stealth sections ask for a snapshot of a conspiracy rather than a louder gun.

Hillys looks like a Mediterranean city under occupation, and the photography assignments are how the plot advances. Players still talk about Jade because the cube original let them walk that city with a camera instead of a helmet.
splinter-cell-chaos-theory:
Sam Fisher's quietest toolkit is Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Chaos Theory, the third Splinter Cell and the 2005 entry many players treat as the peak of the early stealth games. Ubisoft let him jam lights, whistle guards apart, and read a co-op partner's position on the cube build.

The handheld release is a different top-down game, so the cube campaign is the one with the third-person shadows and the interrogation grabs. Banks, lighthouses, and a cargo ship each ask for a different route through the dark.

Chaos Theory is where the series' early rules feel most complete: a knife, a pistol, and a choice to leave everyone asleep. The top-down handheld story should not be confused with Fisher's cube missions.
xiii:
Panel borders slice the gunfights in XIII, Ubisoft's cel-shaded adaptation of the Belgian comic by Van Hamme and Vance. The 2003 shooter cuts to a drawn panel when a shot lands, matching the page layout of Jason Fly's amnesia story.

A conspiracy, a tattooed number, and a hero who does not remember his own name drive the missions from a seaside start into government offices. The flat colors are not a filter on a realistic war game; they are the comic itself moving.

The cube disc is that panel-to-panel campaign. Readers of the albums meet the same plot device, a man called thirteen, now aiming a gun between illustrated frames.
tcs-sc-double-agent:
Undercover work defines Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell Double Agent, the 2006 Splinter Cell that shipped as two different campaigns. The cube and motion-console discs carry the last-generation version, a separate story path from the Xbox 360 game released under the same name.

Sam Fisher is planted inside a terrorist cell, and trust with the criminals can rise while trust with his agency falls. The last-generation campaign builds that double life with its own missions rather than a cut-down copy of the high-definition one.

Players who own both generations are effectively holding two games. The Nintendo discs are the last-generation campaign, with Fisher's cover identity at the center.
red-faction-ii:
Volition left the destructible Mars tunnels behind for Red Faction II, a more linear 2002 campaign built around squad chatter. Alias fights through a city under a dictator, and the Geo-Mod caves of the first game are no longer the main trick.

Squadmates call targets while the route pushes forward, so the pace is closer to a scripted shooter than to a miner carving his own door. The Nano weapons and the urban siege replace Parker's Martian rebellion.

The cube disc is that linear sequel. Players who came for collapsing tunnels find a tighter war story and a squad that will not stop talking.
street-racing-syndicate:
Nightlife reputations sit beside the races in Street Racing Syndicate, the 2004 street racer from Eutechnyx. The cube release shipped alongside the PlayStation 2 and Xbox versions, with the same mix of city driving and after-dark status.

Winning a sprint is only half of the loop; the other half is being seen in the right car once the sun goes down. Licensed cars and a respect system tie the daylight races to that nightlife scene.

The cube build is not a later portable cut. It is the same syndicate career those other consoles offered in that year, neon included.
need-for-speed-underground-3:
Pink slips open the career in Need for Speed: Underground, the moment EA Black Box turned the series toward illegal street racing. The 2003 cube disc is that customization campaign, where a lost race can cost the car itself.

Neon, vinyls, and performance parts matter as much as the racing line, and the city circuit is a loop of circuit races, drifts, and drag sprints. The visual style is the magazine look of tuner culture, not a police pursuit.

Later most-wanted stories added cops and a blacklist. This disc is the earlier pink-slip career, the one that made the garage the real menu.
sonic-the-hedgehog-2:
Miles Prower joins the dash in Sonic the Hedgehog 2, Sega's 1992 Genesis sequel that also introduces the spin dash. Tails follows Sonic through Chemical Plant, Casino Night, and the Death Egg, and the spin dash starts a run without a downhill slope.

Chaos emeralds still turn a fast hedgehog into Super Sonic, and the split-screen race on one television was a reason to own a second pad. Later motion-console and glasses-free handheld releases reissue that same 16-bit game.

The reissues are the Genesis stages, not a 3D remake. Tails and the spin dash are the two ideas this sequel added to Green Hill's formula.
resident-evil-2002:
Spencer Mansion is rebuilt from the ground up in Resident Evil (2002), the remake Shinji Mikami directed for Capcom. The new construction replaces the 1996 house with defense items, crimson-head corpses that rise again, and a tighter map of locked doors.

Jill Valentine and Chris Redfield still search the halls for their missing team, and Lisa Trevor's story sits in the bones of the estate. A later motion-console edition reissued that same remake rather than returning to the older camera angles.

The cube original is the full rebuild. Players who knew only the 1996 doors meet a harsher mansion, with ink ribbons still limiting how often a typewriter can save them.
twilight-princess:
The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess lets Link become a wolf whenever the twilight covers a province. Midna argues with Link instead of offering the polite hints of an older companion.

Eiji Aonuma directed it as the darker follow-up to Wind Waker, and it shipped both as a Wii launch game with motion swings and as a GameCube game with a mirrored world and a traditional controller. Midna, not a fairy in the old style, is the companion who actually argues.

The tears of light, the hero's bow, and the double clawshot structure a Hyrule that is larger and more rural than Ocarina's. Wolf Link's senses find ghosts and scents the human form walks past. The last duel with Ganondorf is staged as a swordfight in a field, deliberately old-fashioned after the wolf chapters.

Twilight Princess HD on Wii U is a separate remaster. This page covers the Wii and GameCube releases of Twilight Princess as one work.
broken-sword-3-the-sleeping-dragon:
George Stobbart returns with Nico Collard in Broken Sword 3 - The Sleeping Dragon, the 2003 sequel that was the first Broken Sword in 3D. Revolution Software moved the pair off the point-and-click cursor and onto direct control, and the cube was among the platforms.

The conversation-and-puzzle habit of the earlier games stays, but George now climbs and shoves crates in spaces the flat scenes could not show. Nico is a partner in the plot again, not a voice on a telephone.

The cube disc is that 3D chapter. Fans of the Paris cafe opening meet a sequel that finally lets George walk around a puzzle instead of naming a verb for it.
legend-of-zelda-the-wind-waker:
The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker replaces Hyrule Field with an ocean and makes the King of Red Lions the overworld. Sailing is the journey, and conducting the wind is how the boat gets anywhere.

Eiji Aonuma directed the GameCube game in a cel-shaded style that was controversial before release and then became the thing players defended. Link conducts the Wind Waker baton to change the wind, sails between islands, and finds Tetra, a pirate who is not introduced as a princess.

The Forsaken Fortress, the Earth and Wind temples, and a late stretch of triforce charts are the parts people still time. Ganondorf's last scene, and the flooded kingdom under the waves, reframe the older legends instead of repeating them.

The Wind Waker HD on Wii U is a separate remaster page. This page is the GameCube voyage.
bloodrayne:
A dhampir agent is the lead of BloodRayne, the 2002 action game Terminal Reality made and Majesco published. Rayne feeds on enemies, fights with arm blades, and works a 1930s mission against vampires and Nazi occultists.

The cube disc is one of the console versions of that same campaign. Vision modes and a bloodlust meter change how a fight plays once she has fed, which is the loop the studio built around her.

A film later used the name. The game itself is the earlier blade-and-bite campaign, with Rayne as an agent rather than a movie still.
gun:
Colton White rides for revenge in GUN, the 2005 western Neversoft made and Activision published. The cube version is that open-country shooter, with horseback travel between duels, posses, and a town that remembers every slight.

Quickdraw standoffs punctuate the riding, and the story is a personal feud spread across a wide frontier rather than a corridor of missions. Colton's family history is the fuse; the country is the level select.

The cube disc does not swap the west for a smaller map. It is the same horseback revenge story the other consoles told that year.
the-sims:
Household meters are the drama in The Sims, the 2000 PC phenomenon Will Wright and Maxis built around ordinary needs. Hunger, comfort, hygiene, and friendship tick down in a house the player furnishes, and a neglected Sim will refuse to perform.

The cube release is a separate console game inspired by that PC sandbox, not the same open-ended neighborhood on a disc. Console life has its own goals and a tighter house, while the computer original is the freeform toy people meant when they said the title.

The cube household still runs on needs and objects. It simply is not the PC phenomenon copied bit for bit onto a disc.
harry-potter-and-the-chamber-of-secrets:
Hogwarts corridors can be wandered between classes in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, EA's 2002 tie-in to the second book and film. That free roam is a step past the first game, so Harry learns spells in the castle and then uses them when the plot returns to the Chamber.

The basilisk, the diary, and the forbidden forest sit inside a school the player can cross on foot. Fred and George's shop energy is in the castle's side rooms, while classes gate the next spell.

The cube disc is that roaming Hogwarts. Players who only fought through levels in the earlier tie-in get a castle with a timetable.
ikaruga:
Polarity swaps are the entire weapon in Ikaruga, Hiroshi Iuchi's 2001 shooter for Treasure. The ship flips between black and white, absorbing shots of the matching color and dying to the other, and the cube disc is a home port of that arcade design.

A chain builds when destroyed enemies share a polarity, so survival and score ask for opposite habits. Bullet curtains are dense enough that the color flip is the dodge.

The cube port brings the arcade pattern home without turning it into a story campaign. Players still learn the stages as color routes, not as cover shooters.
super-mario-sunshine:
Isle Delfino is the vacation Super Mario Sunshine ruins with goop, and Nintendo arms Mario with a water pack for the cleanup. The 2002 adventure is a set of tropical missions rather than a line of short flags, and Shadow Mario paints the mess Mario has to erase.

FLUDD sprays, hovers, and rockets, so a nozzle change is a jump change. Yoshi can be ridden where the fruit allows it, and Shine Sprites mark a finished mission the way stars once marked a finished painting.

Pianta Village, Sirena Beach, and Noki Bay each hide a different use for the same water tank. A limited compilation, Super Mario 3D All-Stars, included this adventure for a time and is not kept here as a standing listing.

The cube disc is the Delfino campaign itself. Later all-stars bundles were a temporary shelf, while the hover nozzle and the shadow frame-up remain the reason to replay the island.
conflict-desert-storm:
Gulf War squads are the subject of Conflict Desert Storm, the tactical shooter Pivotal Games made and SCi published. Special forces move through desert objectives together, and the cube received a port of that campaign.

Laser markers, bounding movement, and a four-soldier team replace a lone commando. The missions follow the war's ground fighting rather than a fictional near-future arsenal.

The cube port keeps the squad orders and the desert objectives. It is the Gulf campaign on a Nintendo disc, not a later numbered sequel in the Conflict line.
super-smash-bros-melee:
Super Smash Bros. Melee sped the Nintendo 64 fighter up until a wavedash became a real technique instead of a glitch to ignore. Trophies turn the menus into a museum of props from older Nintendo games.

Masahiro Sakurai and HAL Laboratory built it as a GameCube launch-window game with a roster far larger than the first Smash, plus trophies that act as a museum of Nintendo props. Adventure mode, event matches, and a brutal single-player climb sit beside a versus mode that tournaments adopted.

Wavedashing, L-canceling, and character-specific movement turned Melee into a competitive game with a scene Nintendo did not design and, for years, did not sponsor. That split, between a party fighter and a lived-in ruleset, is the reason the disc is still on tournament setups.

Brawl, Wii U, and Ultimate changed the physics on purpose. They are other pages. This one is Super Smash Bros. Melee.
killer7:
Garcian Smith answers the calls in killer7, the 2005 on-rails assassin game Suda51 and Grasshopper Manufacture made for Capcom. Cel shading flattens the Smith syndicate into a comic, and the game debuted on the cube and PlayStation 2.

Harman Smith and the other personalities switch in when a different gun is required, while Heaven Smiles charge down corridors that do not allow a free camera. Kun Lan's opposition is philosophical and bloody at once, which is the tone Grasshopper chose.

The cube debut is that on-rails, cel-shaded campaign. Players expecting a free-aim stealth game meet a line of targets and a cast that shares one body.
call-of-duty-black-ops:
Alex Mason hears the numbers in Call of Duty: Black Ops, the 2010 Cold War shooter with which Treyarch opened the Black Ops line. Interrogation flashes send him through Cuba, Vietnam, and a Soviet program that will not stay buried.

Viktor Reznov's presence ties the missions together, and the campaign is a memory being pulled apart rather than a single front. A motion-console build shipped beside the main releases, while the dual-screen edition is a separate portable campaign with its own missions.

The line that followed took its name from this Cold War story. Mason's numbers, not a World War II beach, are the start of that line.
call-of-duty-modern-warfare-3:
Makarov's war closes in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, the 2011 finale Infinity Ward and Sledgehammer used to end the original Modern Warfare story. Captain Price and Soap MacTavish are still in the fight, and the campaign hops cities as the conspiracy stops being a single country's problem.

The motion-console version adapts that campaign for motion controls, so aiming and gestures follow the remote rather than only a stick. The plot beats remain the trilogy's ending, including the hunt that began in the previous game.

Players on that remote are not getting a side story. They are playing the same closing campaign, retuned for the way that console asks you to point.
lego-lord-of-the-rings:
Middle-earth studs litter LEGO The Lord of the Rings, Traveller's Tales' 2012 retelling of the three Peter Jackson films. Between story beats the map opens, so a hobbit can wander from the Shire toward Mordor without waiting for the next cutscene.

Characters carry film abilities into brick form: a ring that turns the bearer invisible, a wizard's blast, an elf's agility. Puzzles are built from the props of the movies, and the open country sits between those scripted chapters.

The three films are all in this one brick journey. It is not a single-battle spinoff; the walk across the open map is the feature Traveller's Tales added on top of the scenes.
tomb-raider-underworld:
Lara Croft's search for her mother continues in Tomb Raider: Underworld, the 2008 continuation of the Legend-era story from Crystal Dynamics. Norse ruins and underwater halls replace the mansion tutorial of the older games, and Thor's hammer is part of the myth she is chasing.

The motion-console version is a reduced adaptation of that campaign, with a smaller scope than the main release. The dual-screen game is a separate side story, not a tiny copy of the same tombs.

Legend-era Lara, the one who already reopened her father's work, is who you play on the big-screen cut. The handheld tale should be read as its own excursion.
call-of-duty-world-at-war:
Peleliu's ridges and Stalingrad's streets share Call of Duty: World at War, Treyarch's 2008 World War II shooter covering the Pacific and the Eastern Front. Sergeant Reznov narrates the Soviet half, while the Pacific half follows a marine campaign through caves and airfields.

A motion-console build exists, and the dual-screen edition is its own portable game rather than the same two fronts squeezed onto a small map. Grenades, banzai charges, and the Red Army's push are the texture of the big-screen campaign.

This is the World War II game that sat beside the modern reboot, not a return to the medal-of-honor beaches of the early 2000s. The portable edition tells its war separately.
world-of-goo:
Goo balls become load-bearing joints in World of Goo, the 2008 physics puzzle 2D Boy built about living construction. Kyle Gabler and Ron Carmel had players weld creatures into bridges, towers, and pipes while the World of Goo Corporation loomed in the background.

A structure that looks stable will sag once one ball too many is added, and the exit pipe only drinks the goo you can spare. The computer release and the WiiWare release were the hit; a hybrid-console port arrived much later with the same squishy engineering.

The joy is structural failure you can see coming. Later ports did not replace the WiiWare towers that taught people how far a triangle of goo could lean.
modern-warfare:
Captain Price's regiment restarts the series in the present in Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, Infinity Ward's 2007 break from the World War II campaigns. Soap MacTavish's training mission hands you to Price, and an early sniper chapter in Pripyat, All Ghillied Up, became the mission people quoted.

A motion-console port came later, and the dual-screen version is a separate campaign. The main story still runs through the Middle East and a civil war, with the AC-130 sequence as the moment the scale jumps.

The reboot is this present-day war, not the later games that reused the Modern Warfare name. The handheld campaign is its own set of missions under that famous title.
bully-scholarship-edition:
Bullworth Academy is the campus in Bully: Scholarship Edition, Rockstar's 2008 expansion of the 2006 school satire. Jimmy Hopkins still attends class, dodges cliques, and gets into trouble between bells, and the motion-console version includes the extra classes from that expanded edition.

The town outside the gates is as important as the dorms: shops, bikes, and a slingshot turn errands into mischief. Cliques, prefects, and the principal give the day its schedule, which is the satire.

The 2006 original is the first release; this edition is the expanded one, extra classes included. The motion-console disc is that scholarship package, not the earlier unexpanded school year.
tomb-raider-anniversary:
Natla's expedition is rebuilt in Tomb Raider: Anniversary, the 2007 reconstruction Crystal Dynamics made of the 1996 mansion-and-tomb raid, using the Legend engine. Peru's lost valley, the Greek halls, and Egypt return with Lara's newer moves, including the grapple that the 1996 raids did not have.

A motion-console version followed the PlayStation 2 and PC releases. The villain is still Jacqueline Natla, and the artifact hunt still starts in the Andes rather than in the Norse ruins of the later sequel.

Anniversary is a rebuild of the first raid, not a chapter of Legend's own plot. The motion-console disc is that rebuilt expedition arriving after the other platforms.
need-for-speed-hot-pursuit-2:
Autolog taunts turn pursuits into a social race in Need For Speed: Hot Pursuit, the 2010 reboot Criterion made of the police-chase idea. Racers and cops share weapons, spike strips, and a county full of long coastal roads, and the online log posts who just busted whom.

Seacrest County is the map, and a pursuit can flip from fleeing a helicopter to driving the interceptor. The motion-console version was built around that console's controllers, so the same chase fantasy uses the remote's input rather than a standard pad layout copied blindly.

This reboot is not the earlier Hot Pursuit 2, which had its own teams and its own year. Autolog and the weapons-on-both-sides design belong to this Criterion game.
far-cry:
Jack Carver's boat job collapses into Far Cry, the 2004 computer shooter Crytek set on a tropical archipelago. Mercenaries, an experimental serum, and Dr. Krieger's operation fill the island, and the first CryEngine showed off long views through jungle canopy.

Stealth approaches and loud assaults both work because the vegetation is real cover, not a painted backdrop. The series that followed took the title far from this one boatman's bad day, but the original is the island and the engine demo that happened to be a campaign.

The computer original is the record here. Carver, Krieger, and the canopy are the start of the line, before later numbered sequels changed protagonists.
star-wars-the-force-unleashed-2:
A cloned apprentice wakes in STAR WARS: The Force Unleashed II, the 2010 sequel LucasArts built around Starkiller's copy. Darth Vader wants a loyal weapon, and the clone's trip runs through Kamino's facilities and a fight over whether the copy is anyone at all.

Motion-console and dual-screen versions are scaled adaptations, apart from the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 game. Force grips and saber throws remain the fantasy, trimmed to the hardware rather than retold as a different clone.

The story only makes sense after the first unleashed campaign. This chapter is the clone's, and the Nintendo builds are the scaled ones.
rayman-origins:
Globox returns to a side-scrolling brawl in Rayman Origins, the 2011 platformer Ubisoft Montpellier made playable with up to four characters. Michel Ancel's team painted the Glade again after years of 3D entries, and a second, third, and fourth hero can pile onto the same screen.

Teensies need rescuing, mosquitoes swarm, and the slapstick is the combat. Motion-console and glasses-free handheld releases both received that painted adventure, so the four-player idea is not locked to one living-room machine.

Origins is the side-scrolling return, not Rayman 3's lock-on shooter. The painted levels and the pile-on of friends are the whole offer.
lego-star-wars-tcs:
Episode studs from two earlier brick games combine in LEGO Star Wars - The Complete Saga. Traveller's Tales' 2007 compilation joins the prequel game to the original-trilogy game. Motion-console and dual-screen versions include that combined episode list, from The Phantom Menace through Return of the Jedi.

Dexter's diner and the bonus rooms still sit between episodes, and characters unlocked in one trilogy can wander another episode's levels. The compilation is a joining, not a new film adaptation with its own script.

Players who owned only one of the earlier brick Star Wars games get the missing trilogy here. The episode list is the product.
lego-batman:
Gotham bricks split into hero chapters and villain chapters in LEGO Batman, Traveller's Tales' 2008 debut and the first brick Batman. Batman and a sidekick clean up one set of cases, then the Joker, the Penguin, and the rest of the roster play through their own crime spree.

Studs, suits, and gadget puzzles are the language, and the villain half is not a bonus gallery. It is a second campaign with its own bosses and its own reasons to smash the furniture.

Motion-console and dual-screen releases carry that two-sided Gotham. Later brick Batman games added voices and a bigger city; this is the first, with the chapter split as its structure.
lego-batman-2:
Spoken jokes fill an open Gotham in LEGO Batman 2 DC Super Heroes, the 2012 sequel in which Traveller's Tales gave the bricks real dialogue. Lex Luthor's plot pulls Superman and the wider league into Batman's city, and the streets between story missions can be flown.

Motion-console, Wii U, dual-screen, and glasses-free handheld releases all received that open Gotham. The voice work is the break from the mumbled first game, and the map is large enough that a cape is transportation.

This sequel is the one with the spoken lines and the league guests. The first brick Batman kept its jokes in silence; here the punchlines are performed.
cave-story:
Quote's cave is redrawn in Cave Story+, the enhanced edition Nicalis published of Daisuke Amaya's freeware. Extra modes and new art sit on top of the robot's descent, and motion-console, dual-screen, and glasses-free handheld releases carried that version.

Curly Brace, Balrog, and the island's doctor remain in the story Amaya, as Pixel, had given away. The freeware original came first; this plus edition is the commercial redraw, not a sequel with a new island.

Players who never met the doctor still get the same ending questions. They simply see them in the redrawn sprites and the added modes.
mini-ninjas:
Hiro's animal spells carry Mini Ninjas, the 2009 family adventure IO Interactive made after years as the Hitman studio. The young ninja frees creatures and turns into them, and both the motion console and the dual-screen handheld received versions of that journey.

An evil samurai's ash-covered land is the map, and the tone stays light even when the studio's other series was about contracts. The other young ninjas train beside him, and Hiro is the one the story follows into the mountains.

The surprise, at the time, was the studio name on a gentle adventure. The motion-console and handheld releases are that same young ninja, not a tactical contract.
lego-harry-potter:
Hogwarts bricks retell the first four stories in LEGO Harry Potter: Years 1-4, Traveller's Tales' 2010 walk from the philosopher's stone through the Triwizard year. Motion-console and dual-screen versions cover those Hogwarts years, with spells becoming brick abilities.

Polyjuice, a hippogriff, and a maze each show up as a level gimmick rather than a cutscene-only nod. Students unlocked along the way can be dropped into earlier years' corridors to find studs the plot characters walked past.

Years five through seven are a later game. This one stops at the fourth story, with the cup and the graveyard as the far end of the syllabus.
metal-slug-3:
Branching missions make METAL SLUG 3 the 2000 run-and-gun SNK fans still call a high point of the arcade line. Marco and the squad ride new vehicles, drown in zombies, and end in a place the earlier slug games never reached, and a motion-console release later brought that Neo Geo game over.

Paths fork so a second credit is a different route, not only a harder copy of the first. The slug tank is still the joke and the shelter, but the branches are why this chapter is the one arcades pointed at.

The motion-console release is that Neo Geo game, forks included. It is not a new numbered slug built for the remote.
bittrip-runner:
CommanderVideo runs without a stop button in BIT.TRIP RUNNER, the 2010 WiiWare rhythm game from Gaijin Games. Every jump, slide, and kick has to land on the beat, and failing the rhythm long enough strips the color out of the stage.

It is the fourth BIT.TRIP release, so the bouncing hero already had a history before this auto-runner. Gold bars and pitfalls are arranged like a chart, and the score is a music performance as much as a distance.

The WiiWare original is this forced sprint. Later sequels added their own heroes; here CommanderVideo is alone with the beat.
back-to-the-future-the-game:
Doc Brown has Christopher Lloyd's voice again in Back to the Future: The Game, Telltale's 2010 episodic sequel to the film trilogy. A motion-console version collected those episodes, and Marty McFly is dragged through a Hill Valley that the movies never filmed, including an alternate town under Citizen Brown.

The episodes ship a story that starts after the locomotive ending, with the DeLorean still the problem and the solution. Conversation puzzles replace the films' action set pieces, which is Telltale's method.

Lloyd's Doc is the bridge to the movies. The motion-console collection is those episodes in one place, not a rail shooter of the clock tower.
broken-sword-1-dc-espanol:
Nico Collard gets a playable chapter in Broken Sword 1 - Shadow of the Templars (The Director's Cut), Revolution's 2009 remake of the 1996 adventure. A Paris cafe bombing still starts George Stobbart's case, and the new chapter lets Nico investigate before the American tourist arrives.

Motion-console and dual-screen releases use that expanded script, with painted scenes updated from the original's pixels. Templars, a manuscript, and the Syrian sites remain the spine of George's trip.

The 1996 game is the first telling. This director's cut is the remake that adds Nico's chapter and asks both consoles to carry the longer script.
pirates-3:
A Caribbean captain's career is Sid Meier's Pirates! Firaxis remade Sid Meier's 1987 seafaring game during 2004, mixing sailing, sword fights, and formal dances. The Wii version is a later port of that remake, with the same mix of plunder and politics.

Fencing duels are timed swings, ballroom dances are rhythm, and the ship is steered into the wind between ports. A governorship, a hidden relative, and the Spanish Main all sit on one map the 1987 game had already imagined.

The bang in the title matches the tone of a duel that can end a promising career. The Wii port is that Firaxis life, not the original 1987 screens.
uno:
Wild cards and a forced draw keep UNO faithful to Mattel's shedding deck, matching colors and numbers the way the tabletop pack does. Motion-console and dual-screen editions let a room play without the physical cards, including the reverse and the skip.

A player who forgets the color call still eats the penalty the kitchen-table rules demand. The computer opponents follow that same shed, so a solo game is the deck without needing three friends on the couch.

The editions are the tabletop rules on a console, not a new sport built around the logo. Four colors, a wild, and the growing hand are the whole design.
fifa-14:
Ignite matches are a different game from FIFA 14, the soccer annual EA Sports built for the 2013 season. Wii and Nintendo 3DS editions keep their own presentation, apart from the Ignite-engine game on newer consoles.

Club seasons and licensed sides are still the annual's job. What changes on those Nintendo discs is the engine under the kits, not the idea of a year-long football calendar.

Players who bought the newer-console Ignite game are not holding this edition. The Wii and 3DS releases are separate builds under the same annual name.
swords-and-soldiers-hd:
Viking barracks face Aztec temples and Chinese gates in Swords and Soldiers HD, the sharpened edition of Ronimo Games' side-scrolling strategy. The 2010 HD edition cleans up the WiiWare original, and the three armies still spend gold on a line that only marches one way.

Each culture brings its own units and a super weapon, so a Viking push does not play like an Aztec ritual or a Chinese artillery line. The camera stays on the flank, which is why a base on the left and a base on the right are the whole map.

Ronimo's upgrade is this HD picture of that flank war. The WiiWare original is the earlier, rougher telling of the same three armies.
lego-harry-potter-years-5-7:
Phoenix order business opens LEGO Harry Potter: Years 5-7, Traveller's Tales' 2011 brick telling of the last three stories. Dementors, Horcrux hunts, and the Battle of Hogwarts carry the syllabus from the fifth year through the seventh.

Wii, Nintendo DS, and Nintendo 3DS releases share those late Hogwarts years, including the Ministry and the camping chapters of the Deathly Hallows. Spells learned in the earlier brick game are assumed; this one starts with a school already at war.

The graveyard of the fourth story is behind you. Here the castle itself becomes the last battlefield, and the brick students are conscripts.
nfs-undercover:
An undercover cop's garage is the cover story in Need For Speed Undercover, EA's 2008 street racer set in the open city of Tri-City. Highway races and canyon duels sit inside a police assignment, so the pink slip is also evidence.

Wii and Nintendo DS versions are scaled-down games under that name, with smaller maps than the main console career. The fantasy is the same: drive badly for the law, and do not get made.

Tri-City's free roads are the point of the big versions. The Nintendo builds keep the cop premise and shrink the city around it.
sniper-elite:
Bullet cameras follow the shot in Sniper Elite, Rebellion's 2005 World War II sniper game. Karl Fairburne works Berlin at the end of the war, and a successful hit can leave the rifle view to show the round traveling.

The Wii release is a later port of that first game, scope and all, rather than the sequel set on the V2 program. Wind, distance, and a held breath are the tools, and the camera is the reward for a clean hit.

Fairburne's first Berlin job is this campaign. Later numbered sniper games reused the camera; the Wii port is the original assignment.
lego-star-wars-iii:
Separatist tanks roll through LEGO Star Wars III - The Clone Wars, Traveller's Tales' 2011 brick game based on the animated Clone Wars. Large ground battles join the usual stud-collecting, with Anakin, Ahsoka Tano, and clone squads holding a line instead of only platforming through a corridor.

Wii, Nintendo DS, and Nintendo 3DS received versions of those battles. Republic and Separatist vehicles can be commandeered, which is the addition beyond the earlier complete-saga compilation.

The animated series, not the live-action prequel films alone, supplies the missions. Ground battles are why this chapter feels wider than a hallway of droids.
and-yet-it-moves:
Paper collage rotates under your feet in And Yet It Moves, the 2009 puzzle from Broken Rules. Turning the whole scene gives the runner a new floor, so a wall becomes a ledge and a fall becomes a walk.

The WiiWare version brought that collage to a console, with the remote handling the rotation the computer version did with a key. Scissors-cut animals and torn-paper caves are the art, and the rotate is the only verb that matters.

Vienna's studio built a platformer you solve by turning the page. The WiiWare release is that page on a television.
toribash:
Joint angles are the inputs in Toribash, Nabi Studios' turn-based fighter. You set each joint, commit the turn, and watch the physics decide whether a kick connected or a fighter simply fell over.

The WiiWare release is a console edition of that computer original, dojo and all. There is no combo string to memorize; the next pose is a guess about gravity, and the replay is the verdict.

Dislocated limbs are a normal result, not a glitch. The WiiWare dojo lets a living room argue about whose hip rotation was wiser.
rec-room:
Avatar hangouts fill Rec Room, Against Gravity's 2016 social virtual-reality place full of user-made rooms. Mini-games sit next to those rooms, and players meet as avatars on computer headsets rather than on a living-room disc.

Charades, a paintball court, and a quest someone else built can share one evening. The point is the room you join, not a campaign with a final boss and a credit roll.

Against Gravity's hangout is a place that keeps changing because the rooms are made by the people in them. The headset is the doorway the original release expected.
toki-tori:
A chick's egg hunt is Toki Tori, the puzzle Two Tribes reissued on WiiWare in 2008 after the Game Boy Color original. Later Wii U and Nintendo 3DS releases keep that same hunt, with the little bird still too small to jump every gap unaided.

Tools laid out in a limited pack, a bridge here and a warp there, are how an egg on a high ledge becomes reachable. The order you spend those tools is the puzzle, and a wasted bridge strands the chick.

The Game Boy Color hunt came first. These later releases are that egg map again, not a sequel with a grown bird.
lego-indiana-jones:
The Ark, the stones, and the grail share LEGO Indiana Jones: The Original Adventures. Traveller's Tales retells Raiders, Temple of Doom, and The Last Crusade in brick form. Indy's whip is a grab and a swing, and Wii and Nintendo DS versions cover those three movies.

Sankara stones, a mine cart, and a tank chase each become a brick set piece. Characters from one film can be used in another once they are unlocked, which is how a grail knight ends up in the jungle.

The fourth film is not in this set. The original three adventures are the whole syllabus, whip cracks included.
rayman-3-hoodlum-havoc:
Hoodlum cans screw onto Rayman's hands in Rayman 3: Hoodlum Havoc, Ubisoft's 2003 trip through the Glade of Dreams. He can lock onto several targets at once, and Globox's belly is both a joke and a plot problem Andre the hoodlum caused.

Each can changes the fist: a rocket, a shock, a metal claw. The Glade's forests and discos are the stages, and the lock-on is how a crowd of hoodlums is cleared without a free-aim gun.

The GameCube disc is that lock-on adventure. Later side-scrolling Rayman games dropped the cans; here the cans are the combat.
resident-evil-3-nemesis:
Jill Valentine flees a pursuer who will not stay dead in Resident Evil 3: Nemesis, Capcom's 1999 sequel set in a dying Raccoon City. Nemesis crashes through walls the earlier mansion never allowed, and live choices at key moments fork the escape.

Carlos Oliveira meets Jill between those interruptions, and the clock tower and the city streets replace the Spencer estate. The GameCube version is a later port of that PlayStation game, with the same rocket-launcher ending waiting for anyone who lasts.

Nemesis is the campaign's structure: a boss who is also a random encounter. The cube port is that city escape, not the mansion rebuild Mikami directed afterward.
sonic-the-hedgehog-3:
Angel Island falls at the start of Sonic the Hedgehog 3 (1994), Sega's Genesis sequel that adds save files and a story built to lock onto Sonic & Knuckles. Carnival Night, Ice Cap, and Launch Base continue the hunt for emeralds while Knuckles works against Sonic for reasons the cartridge only half explains.

Wii Virtual Console later reissued that 16-bit cartridge. The lock-on port on the follow-up cart is how this story was meant to finish, with the Death Egg still in the sky.

Save data was new for this hedgehog. The Virtual Console reissue is that same cartridge, island and all, not a 3D remake of the carnival.
tom-clancys-ghost-recon:
Ghost squads take orders in Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon, Red Storm's 2001 shooter about commanding specialists in a near-future war. The GameCube version is a console port of that tactical game, with fireteams still the unit you actually play.

A planned route through a treeline matters more than a sprint, and losing a named Ghost hurts the next mission. The war is a near-future clash, not a historical beach, and the cube port keeps the squad view rather than turning it into a lone-hero campaign.

Red Storm's first Ghost game is this command puzzle. Later Ghost sequels added fancier kits; the cube port is the early doctrine.
the-simpsons-hit-run:
Springfield traffic is the open world of The Simpsons: Hit & Run, Radical Entertainment's 2003 driving tour published by Vivendi. The GameCube disc is one of the original releases, with Homer, Bart, Lisa, Marge, and Apu each taking a chapter of the town.

Black sedans, wasp cameras, and a collector-card scavenger hunt tie the missions together while you wreck the family car. Evergreen Terrace, the school, and the downtown are connected roads, not separate loading menus.

The tone is the show's, and the structure is a driving game with gags in the mission text. The cube original is that Springfield, stoplights included.
metroid-prime:
Tallon IV is a ruined planet you scan rather than sprint through in Metroid Prime, Retro Studios' first-person debut for Samus. Nintendo published that 2002 exploration, and the scan visor turns creatures, lore, and locks into entries the suit can read.

The Varia and Gravity suits reopen rooms the starting gear could only look at, which is how Chozo ruins and Phazon mines become one map. Meta Ridley waits in the crater story, and the Frigate Orpheon is the cold open that teaches the visor.

A Wii edition later reissued the same investigation. Metroid Prime Remastered on Nintendo Switch is a separate record, not a replacement for this one.

Retro's debut is the scan, the suits, and Tallon IV. Later prime sequels changed planets; the ruined one with the visor is this campaign.
star-wars-bounty-hunter:
Jango Fett's jetpack pays the bills in Star Wars Bounty Hunter, the 2002 LucasArts game about contracts taken before Attack of the Clones. Zam Wesell is tied into the hunt, and a posted bounty from Count Dooku's circle sends Jango through crime dens with dual pistols and a whipcord.

The cube release is that prequel-era job list. Toxic darts and a missile on the pack are the tools, and the story exists to show how the clone template ended up in a certain Kaminoan's file.

Attack of the Clones shows the end of this man's career. The game is the contracts that come before that arena.
harry-potter-and-the-prisoner-of-azkaban:
Expecto Patronum joins the timetable in Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, EA's 2004 tie-in to the third book and film. The GameCube version adds that year's spells to another Hogwarts roam, with Dementors on the grounds and Buckbeak's fate in the plot.

Harry, Ron, and Hermione each get stretches of the castle and the forest. The time-turner business of the story shows up as a reason the year cannot be played as a straight line of classes.

The cube roam is the third year's school, patronus and hippogriff included. It is a different spell list from the chamber game that came before it.
sonic-knuckles:
Master Emerald duty is playable in Sonic & Knuckles, Sega's 1994 Genesis cartridge famous for a lock-on port that clips Sonic 2 or Sonic 3 on top. Knuckles glides and climbs in his own route, and the lock-on is how Hidden Palace and the rest of the combined quest were meant to be seen.

Later compilations keep that team-up, including releases on the GameCube and Wii. Without a second cartridge clicked into the port, you still get Knuckles' standalone journey and the Death Egg waiting at the end of it.

The hardware trick is the legacy. Compilations preserve the team-up the plastic port invented, with Knuckles as a lead rather than a trap.
need-for-speed-hot-pursuit-2-2:
Hot pursuits return with helicopters in Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit 2, EA's 2002 revival of cops versus racers. Spike strips and roadblocks are back, and the PlayStation 2 version was built by a different team than the GameCube, Xbox, and PC releases.

That split means the cube disc is not a straight copy of the PlayStation 2 career. Routes, traffic, and the feel of the chase differ because the teams differed, even though the box name matches.

Players comparing notes across consoles were not always describing the same handling. The cube, Xbox, and computer releases share one build; the PlayStation 2 game is the other.
mario-kart-double-dash:
Two riders share one kart in Mario Kart: Double Dash, Nintendo's 2003 GameCube entry that lets the partner throw items. A special item belongs to the pair: a chain chomp for the babies, a shell for the turtles, a bob-omb family for someone else entirely.

Baby Park is a tiny oval that becomes chaos because the laps are short and the items are constant. Waluigi Stadium and Rainbow Road sit at the other end of the cup list, and the back rider is why a banana can fly while the driver steers.

It is a home-console Mario Kart with a passenger. Later karts went back to one hero per vehicle; this cup list is the one that required a friend in the same seat.
luigis-mansion:
King Boo frames a vacuum job in Luigi's Mansion, the GameCube launch game in which Luigi tours a locked house room by room. Professor E. Gadd's Poltergust 3000 sucks portrait ghosts in once the flashlight has stunned them, and the 2001 mansion started the series.

Keys, elements, and a ghost's joke tell you which room is next. Boolossus and the gallery of painted spirits are the bosses, and Mario is the reason Luigi walked through the door, not the hero holding the nozzle.

Later numbered games are sequels set in other places, not this same foyer. The launch disc is the original house, the vacuum, and King Boo's portrait trick.

E. Gadd's lab in the basement is where the captured ghosts go. Anyone who starts the series elsewhere is visiting a follow-up; the flashlight tour begins here.
judge-dredd-dredd-vs-death:
Mega-City One's lawman books perps between firefights in Judge Dredd: Dredd vs. Death, Rebellion's 2003 clash with the Dark Judges. Judge Death and his undead colleagues are the threat, and the 2000 AD comic's tone shows up whenever a citizen can be sentenced instead of only shot.

The Lawgiver's fire modes cover the shooting, while the arrest system covers the satire. A perp who survives can be booked, and that bookkeeping is a score, not a cutscene you can skip without losing something.

The cube release is that city shift. Dredd versus Death is the plot; the booking computer is the mechanic that makes it feel like the comic.
paper-mario-the-thousand-year-door:
Rogueport's curse hangs over Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door, the GameCube role-playing game Intelligent Systems made with Nintendo. Stage-play battles open with a curtain, an audience throws items, and partners such as Goombella, Koops, and Vivian each bring a move the hammer cannot cover.

Crystal Stars and the X-Nauts pull Mario through trains, a wrestling league, and a moon. Peach and Bowser have their own interludes, and the Thousand-Year Door itself is the lock the stars open. The 2004 adventure is this town's story.

A 2024 Nintendo Switch remake has its own record. The cube original is Rogueport, the stage battles, and the partners under the cursed plaza.

Ms. Mowz and Admiral Bobbery are optional flavor and required muscle, depending on the chapter. The remake can wait; the audience in the cube battles is already throwing turnips.
freedom-fighters:
Occupied Manhattan is the map in Freedom Fighters, IO Interactive's 2003 shooter about a Soviet-held New York. Christopher Stone moves from a plumber's day job into a resistance, and charisma spent on squad orders recruits more fighters as the flags change.

The GameCube received a port of that squad campaign. A fountain you capture is a spawn and a symbol, and the alternate history is the whole premise: the Cold War did not end the way the real one did.

Stone's voice on a pirated broadcast is how the city tips. The cube port is that uprising, borough by borough, not a historical documentary of the real Manhattan.
tmnt:
Four brothers tag into combo strings in TMNT, Ubisoft's adaptation of the 2007 computer-animated movie. Leonardo, Raphael, Donatello, and Michelangelo swap mid-fight, and both the GameCube and the Wii received that brawler.

The film's split among the brothers is the story frame, with Raphael's double life in the city and the others trying to pull the team back together. Platform sections between the combo fights use each turtle's weapon as a tool.

The computer-animated movie, not the older cartoon, is the plot. Tagging a brother is how a fight stays the point of a licensed brawler.
tom-clancys-rainbow-six-lockdown-2:
Rainbow squads drop the planning map in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Lockdown, Red Storm's 2005 entry that plays as a more linear shooter than the earlier games. Pre-mission diagrams matter less, and the cube is one of the console ports of that tighter campaign.

Rooms are cleared in sequence, with fewer pauses to assign a whole team on a blueprint. The Rainbow name remains, but the fantasy has shifted toward the doorway in front of you.

Players who learned the series on a planning screen meet a different pace here. The cube port is that linear Rainbow, not the Raven Shield mission editor.
medal-of-honor-frontline:
Omaha Beach opens Medal of Honor: Frontline, EA's 2002 World War II shooter that starts in the water and then moves inland. Lieutenant Jimmy Patterson is the soldier, and the GameCube version followed the PlayStation 2 original through occupied Europe after the landing.

Hedges, a manor, and a submarine pen continue the campaign once the sand is behind you. The beach is the set piece people remember because the landing craft ramp is the tutorial.

The cube disc arrived after the PlayStation 2 original had already stormed that beach. Patterson's war is the same operation, now on Nintendo's disc.
harry-potter-and-the-goblet-of-fire:
Triwizard tasks are built for three pads in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, EA's 2005 tie-in to the fourth book and film. The GameCube version supports three players in the dragon, the lake, and the maze, with Harry, Ron, and Hermione sharing the challenges.

The cup's year is not a school roam like the earlier tie-ins. It is a run of set pieces, and the three-player support is what the cube build adds to those tasks.

A dragon over the castle and a dive in the lake are co-op problems. The graveyard still belongs to the story, but the pads are why this tie-in feels like a party.
sonic-heroes:
Team Chaotix joins the formation gimmick in Sonic Heroes, Sonic Team's 2003 platformer that groups characters into speed, flight, and power. The GameCube was a lead Nintendo version of that multiplatform adventure, with Team Sonic, Team Dark, and Team Rose each running the same stages for different reasons.

Swapping the leader mid-run changes whether you grind, fly, or smash a barrier. The Chaotix are the detective team, and their story is the comic one beside Shadow's heavier plot.

Formation swapping is the whole move set. The cube release sits among the lead versions, not a much later portable cut.
neighbours-from-hell-season-1:
Mr. Rottweiler's house is a trap gallery in Neighbours from Hell: Revenge Is a Sweet Game, the console telling of the German prank series about tormenting a noisy neighbor. Woody sets up the gags, and a GameCube version brings those trap-setting levels off the computer.

A vacuum, a cake, and a badly placed rake are weapons only because the neighbor will walk into them on camera. The laugh track and the television-show frame are part of the presentation, since the series pretends to be a broadcast of the pranks.

The cube levels are the computer traps on a disc. Woody's revenge is the plot, and the neighbor's routine is the puzzle timer.
legacy-of-kain-blood-omen-2:
Meridian's vampires follow Kain again in Legacy of Kain: Blood Omen 2, Crystal Dynamics' 2002 hack-and-slash sequel set years after the first Blood Omen. Dark Gifts return as powers, and the Hylden plot pulls Nosgoth's later history into a city you can climb.

Kain is already a tyrant in the wider timeline, and this chapter shows a stretch of that life as melee rather than the older overhead quest. Glyphs and feeding keep the combat from being only a sword.

The cube release is that melee chapter. Players who only knew the first Blood Omen's map meet a Kain who fights in the street.
spider-man-the-movie:
Green Goblin's glider is the boss language of Spider-Man: The Movie, the 2002 tie-in Treyarch developed for Activision from Sam Raimi's first film. The GameCube version is that 3D action game, with web swinging across a city and the parade sequence among the set pieces.

Oscorp, Harry Osborn, and the bones of the film's plot give the missions their order. Combat is aerial as often as it is on a roof, which is how a licensed brawler of that year tried to feel like the movie's camera.

The cube disc is the film's action in a free-roam city of the time. It is not the later open-world Spider-Man games that reused the movies' titles.
enter-the-matrix:
Niobe's hovercraft shares billing with Ghost in Enter the Matrix, the 2003 game Shiny Entertainment set beside The Matrix Reloaded. Footage shot for the films plays between levels, and the GameCube version stars those two operators rather than Neo.

Focus mode slows a room so a kick can be lined up, and a hacking minigame sits on the terminals. The Logos is their ship, and the plot fills gaps the theatrical cut left around the freeway and the burly brawl.

Shiny's tie-in is a side story with film-grade inserts. Niobe and Ghost are the playable half of Reloaded's off-screen work.
resident-evil-zero:
Rebecca Chambers shares an item box with Billy Coen in Resident Evil Zero, Capcom's 2002 prequel made first for the GameCube. A train, a leech, and James Marcus's history sit before the Spencer Mansion outbreak, and the partner system lets one character pick up what the other had to drop.

A Wii edition later reissued that story. Herbs mix in the same pockets, and leaving Billy behind a door is sometimes the puzzle, because the two cannot always stand in the same room.

The cube original is the train and the partnership. The Wii edition is the same prequel brought back, Rebecca's lighter still the starting tool.
fifa-street:
Gamebreaker tricks replace the season sim in FIFA Street, EA Sports BIG's 2005 street-soccer spinoff. Small courts, walls, and a trick meter are the sport, and the GameCube was part of that original multiplatform release.

The annual FIFA game is a different product. Here a goal is often the end of a juggle, and the roster is there to style on a playground rather than to hold a formation.

BIG's street spinoff is this disc. The cube release sits in the first wave, not a later numbered street sequel.
terraria:
The Guide warns you once, then the night belongs to Terraria, Re-Logic's 2011 sandbox of digging, crafting, and bosses on a flat plane. An Eye of Cthulhu can spawn if the surface is too busy, and the Wall of Flesh waits under the map when the underworld is ready.

Ports reached Wii U, Nintendo 3DS, and Nintendo Switch. Wood becomes a workbench, a workbench becomes a furnace, and the Corruption or the Crimson chooses which side of the world hates you.

The computer original is the crafting loop. Those Nintendo ports are the same flat world, guide and all, not a 3D mining game with a different engine.
assassins-creed-iv-black-flag:
Edward Kenway steals the Jackdaw in Assassin’s Creed IV: Black Flag, Ubisoft's 2013 pirate story set in the Caribbean. Havana, Nassau, and boarding actions are the daily work, and the Wii U version is a full release of that naval game.

The Assassin plot shares the ship with a crew you actually sail, which is the break from the earlier cities-only chapters. A man-of-war on the horizon is a fight you can choose, and the Wii U pad can carry the map while the television shows the wheel.

Kenway is a pirate who stumbles into the order. The Wii U release is the full Caribbean, not a text recap of the boarding.
super-meat-boy:
Dr. Fetus fills the saw halls of Super Meat Boy, the 2010 platformer Team Meat built as a precise successor to the Flash game Meat Boy. Edmund McMillen and Tommy Refenes made the runs short and the deaths instant, and Bandage Girl is the reason the meat cube keeps moving.

Wii U and Nintendo Switch ports followed the computer release. Salt factories, hospitals, and hell are chapters, and a replay ghost of the last failure often dies on screen beside the next attempt.

The Flash predecessor is the sketch. This is the full game, and the later ports carry those same saws.
minecraft:
Creeper blasts teach caution in Minecraft, the block sandbox Markus Persson started at Mojang. The 2009 public build already had nights when the surface stops being a quarry, and a crafting table turns logs into the tools that dig the next cave.

Wii U, Nintendo 3DS, and Nintendo Switch editions are later ports of that world. Redstone, beds, and the Nether came in as the computer version grew, and the Nintendo editions inherit a world already past its earliest public form.

Persson's public build is the origin. The Nintendo ports are that world on a console, creepers included, not a different brick toy.
watch-dogs:
Aiden Pearce hacks Chicago through ctOS in Watch Dogs, Ubisoft's 2014 open-world game about a city run by one network. Traffic lights, phones, and security gates are switches, and the Wii U port puts a map on the gamepad.

The profiler reads a stranger's secrets in the street, which is the fantasy the title is named for. Pearce's family grievance is the plot; the network is the weapon.

The Wii U gamepad map means the television can stay on the street while the tablet shows the hack. Pearce's Chicago is that port's campaign, ctOS and all.
deus-ex-human-revolution-directors-cut:
Adam Jensen's augmentations get a second pass in Deus Ex: Human Revolution - Director's Cut, Eidos Montreal's expanded cyberpunk role-playing game. The 2013 Wii U launch restored boss fights to the toolkit the rest of the game uses, and a commentary track rides along.

Detroit and Hengsha remain the two hubs, with Sarif Industries at the center of the conspiracy. Other platforms received that cut afterward, so the Wii U pad was the first place the revised bosses shipped.

Jensen's gold eyes are the same. The cut is the one that stops the boss rooms from ignoring every stealth aug you bought.
assassins-creed-iii-2:
Connor Kenway's frontier war is Assassin’s Creed III, Ubisoft's 2012 chapter set in the American Revolution. Boston, the homestead, and Haytham Kenway's earlier scenes share the campaign, and the Wii U port uses the gamepad for the map.

Naval scraps in the Revolution are smaller than a later pirate game's ocean, and the tree-running is this chapter's travel. Connor's village and the redcoats are the conflict, not a Caribbean crew.

The Wii U map on the pad lets the television hold the frontier. This is the Revolution, with Connor, and the pad is the cartography.
darksiders-warmastered-edition:
War's Chaoseater gets a cleaner picture in Darksiders Warmastered Edition, the 2016 remaster of Vigil Games' horseman adventure. The 2010 original's ruined Earth, the Charred Council, and the four horsemen's politics remain, updated rather than rewritten.

Wii U and Nintendo Switch both received that edition. Ruin, the horse, and the crossblade still cross the same wasteland, with the seventh seal's story intact.

Warmastered is a refresh of the first horseman game. It is not the sequel in which Death carries the scythe.
dont-starve:
Wilson's campfire is a timer in Don't Starve, Klei's 2013 wilderness game where hunger and darkness are the usual killers. A science machine turns scavenged junk into tools, and Maxwell's portrait on the examine text keeps the tone mean.

The Wii U port is a console edition of that computer roguelike. Winter, hounds, and a failed fire can end a week that was going well, and the next life remembers almost nothing.

Klei's wilderness is hostile by default. The Wii U edition is that same night, not the multiplayer togetherness spinoff that came later.
rayman-legends:
Murfy's touch stages were shaped on the Wii U gamepad for Rayman Legends, Ubisoft's 2013 follow-up to Origins. Musical levels ask the whole group to run in time, and a Nintendo Switch port later carried the same painted levels.

Daily and weekly challenges rotated invasions from earlier paintings, while the story worlds stayed on the disc. Murfy tickles enemies and lifts platforms only in the stages built for that extra finger.

The gamepad sections are the Wii U original's signature. The Switch port keeps the paintings, including those Murfy rooms, without requiring that particular pad.
guacamelee-super-turbo-championship-edit:
Juan Aguacate's wrestler toolkit expands in Guacamelee! Super Turbo Championship Edition. Drinkbox took its 2013 luchador adventure and added stages for Wii U and Nintendo Switch. The uppercut, the rooster, and the swap between the land of the living and the dead remain Juan's answers to Calaca's skeletons.

Extra arenas and a harder route sit on top of the original metroid-like map of towns and temples. The chicken form is still a key for small gaps, and the slam still needs a stunned foe.

The 2013 journey is the base. The 2014 championship set adds those extra stages, still starring the dead man in the mask.
sniper-elite-v2:
Berlin ruins hide the V2 program in Sniper Elite V2, Rebellion's 2012 sequel known for an X-ray bullet camera. Karl Fairburne is back, and a Wii U port brought those Berlin missions over, bone and organ on the slow-motion hit.

Windage and distance still decide the shot, and the X-ray view is more anatomical than the first game's traveling bullet. Snipers in the rubble hunt you while you hunt a rocket program.

The first Sniper Elite is a different Berlin job. V2 is the sequel, and the Wii U port is those missions with the X-ray camera.
breath-of-the-wild:
The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild lets you leave the Great Plateau and walk toward the castle without finishing a single divine beast. Weapons break, meals restore you, and the castle is visible from the first cliff.

Hideto Fujibayashi directed and Eiji Aonuma produced it as a break from dungeon order: climbing, cooking, weather, and weapon breakage replace the old key-and-lock temples. The Sheikah Slate's bombs, magnesis, and stasis are tools the player combines with the landscape rather than with a marked door.

It launched the same year on Wii U and Nintendo Switch. Calamity Ganon, the four divine beasts, and a century-old failure are the story, told mostly through memories Link recovers in any order. Shrines are the puzzles, scattered so the map stays a place instead of a checklist you must clear.

Tears of the Kingdom is the sequel and has its own page. This entry is Breath of the Wild.
bayonetta:
Witch Time slows the angels in Bayonetta, the 2009 character action game Hideki Kamiya and PlatinumGames made and Sega first published. Guns on heels, hair that becomes a giant fist, and a moonlit city are the style, and Nintendo later funded Wii U and Nintendo Switch ports, then a sequel.

Jeanne is the rival witch, and Rodin sells the weapons from a bar that should not exist. Dodge at the last moment and the world slows, which is the mechanic the combos are built to reward.

Sega's original release is the first home of that dodge. The Nintendo ports came afterward, and the sequel they funded is a different record from this one.
cod-black-ops-ii:
Raul Menendez links two wars in Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Treyarch's 2012 campaign split between the 1980s and a near-future fight. David Mason inherits pieces of his father's story, and the Wii U version was a launch title, with loadouts on the gamepad.

Strike missions can change the future map, which is the branching the campaign advertises. The gamepad holds the class while the television holds the gunfight, a split the launch lineup used as a selling point.

The Cold War Black Ops that came before this one is Mason senior's nightmare. This chapter adds Menendez and the future, and the Wii U pad holds the gear.
the-binding-of-isaac-rebirth:
Mom's basement resets in The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, the 2014 rebuild Nicalis and Edmund McMillen made of the 2011 roguelike. Tears are the bullets, items rewrite the run, and Wii U, Nintendo 3DS, and Nintendo Switch ports followed the computer release.

A floor plan that was kind once will be cruel on the next descent, and Mom remains the chase at the end of the early path. Rebirth is a new engine for that descent, not a patch on the older Flash version.

The 2011 original is the first telling. This rebuild is the one the Nintendo ports carried, tear rate and all.
lego-the-hobbit:
Bilbo Baggins signs a contract in LEGO The Hobbit, Traveller's Tales' 2014 brick telling of Peter Jackson's Hobbit films. Dwarves, a burglar, and the road east fill the levels, and Wii U and Nintendo 3DS were part of that release.

Barrels, a riddle game, and the dragon's hoard show up as set pieces rather than only as clips. The One Ring is a brick power, and the company's song is the excuse to keep adding dwarves to the roster.

Jackson's Hobbit films supply the plot. This is the brick walk east, not the earlier brick war for the other ring.
darksiders-ii:
Death's scythe replaces War's sword in Darksiders II, the 2012 sequel in which Vigil Games switched horsemen and added loot. Possessed weapons, a skill tree, and the Kingdom of the Dead make the journey a longer action role-playing game than the first.

Despair carries Death between realms, and the Crowfather's scheme sits under the loot chase. Wii U and, later, Nintendo Switch ports carry that campaign, dungeons included.

The previous game follows War across the ruined Earth. Death carries the inventory here, and a new scythe changes the next fight.
child-of-light:
Aurora's poem is the script of Child of Light, Ubisoft Montreal's 2014 fable told in rhyme with a watercolor look. Igniculus, a small firefly, lights puzzles and interrupts enemy turns, and Lemuria is the dream kingdom she has to cross.

Wii U was an original platform, and Nintendo Switch came later. Battle timing lets a second player, or the firefly, bump a casting bar, which is how the rhyme stays a game and not only a picture book.

Aurora's father the duke is the human world she leaves behind. The watercolor and the couplets are the presentation; the interrupt is the fight.
mass-effect-3:
Commander Shepard's last argument with the Reapers is Mass Effect 3, BioWare's 2012 finale of the trilogy. Earth is under invasion, the Normandy still has a crew to disappoint, and the Wii U version is a port that followed the Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, and computer releases.

Garrus, the Crucible, and the war assets you bothered to gather all press on the ending. The Wii U pad can hold powers and the map, but the campaign is the same finale the other platforms already had.

The trilogy's argument ends here. The Wii U disc is that ending's port, not a side story about a different commander.
the-swapper:
Clone puzzles on a derelict station are The Swapper, Facepalm Games' 2013 game about making copies and moving your mind into them. Orbs place a body and swap consciousness into it, and the Wii U version ports that atmospheric computer game.

A clone left behind can stand on a switch the original body cannot reach. The station's rocks and the ethics of the copies are the story, told mostly by terminals and by what the swap lets you abandon.

Facepalm's station is a mood piece with a strict mechanic. The Wii U port is that mechanic on a television, orb and all.
resident-evil-revelations-biohazard-reve:
Queen Zenobia's decks host Resident Evil Revelations, Capcom's cruise-ship story built first for the Nintendo 3DS. The 2012 voyage puts Jill Valentine and Parker Luciani between Resident Evil 4 and 5, and Raid mode is the extra arcade of missions.

Wii U and later Nintendo Switch ports expanded the release, Raid mode included. A scanner picks out hidden objects on the ship, and the terror sections are about being hunted in a corridor rather than about managing a mansion's typewriter.

The 3DS original is the ship's first home. The later ports keep Jill on the Zenobia and keep Raid mode beside the campaign.
never-alone:
Nuna's fox shares the blizzard in Never Alone, also called Kisima Ingitchuna, Upper One Games' 2014 puzzle platformer drawn from Inupiat folklore. A bola, a spirit helper, and the wind are the tools, and Wii U and Nintendo Switch versions include the cultural videos.

The fox can reach ledges the girl cannot, so the pair is the puzzle. Interviews and story clips sit beside the levels, which is how the game treats the folklore as something to hear as well as to jump.

Upper One's collaboration with Inupiat storytellers is the reason the videos exist. The Nintendo releases keep those clips with Nuna's walk.
lego-marvel:
Galactus arrives over a brick New York in LEGO Marvel Super Heroes, Traveller's Tales' 2013 packing of a large Marvel roster into an open city. Stark Tower is a landmark you can actually enter, and Wii U, Nintendo DS, and Nintendo 3DS were part of that release.

Silver Surfer, Doctor Doom, and a long list of street-level heroes share the stud hunt. The open boroughs sit between story missions about the cosmic threat, which is the scale the title is bragging about.

The roster is the toy. Galactus is the reason the toy has a skyline.
steamworld-dig:
Rusty digs under Tumbleton in SteamWorld Dig, Image & Form's mining adventure. The 2013 Nintendo 3DS eShop launch sells ore for upgrades that change how fast the robot falls, and Wii U and Nintendo Switch ports followed that prospector.

Light is a resource in the deeper caves, and a trip back to the surface to sell is part of the loop. Steambots and the old miner's mystery give the digging a western plot.

The eShop original is Rusty's first claim. Later ports keep that downward map, while the numbered sequel is a separate adventure.
thomas-was-alone:
Danny Wallace narrates the rectangles of Thomas Was Alone, Mike Bithell's 2012 puzzle about colored shapes with personalities. Thomas jumps, Chris complains, Claire floats, and Laura's bounce pad personality is a square you have to ferry, with Wii U and Nintendo Switch ports coming after the computer original.

Each shape's physics is the character sheet. A tall thin rectangle cannot do Claire's job, and Wallace's lines are why you remember which one is selfish.

Bithell's shapes are a platformer told as a novel. The Nintendo ports keep Wallace's voice with the same colored cast.
scribblenauts-unlimited:
Maxwell types a ladder into existence in Scribblenauts Unlimited, 5th Cell's 2012 puzzle where words become objects. Lily's curse is the reason he travels, and Wii U and Nintendo 3DS share that spawning trick.

An adjective glued to a noun changes the solution, so a tiny ladder and a giant ladder are different tools. The globe of places is wider than the earlier handheld word puzzles, and the notebook is still the inventory.

Maxwell's spelling is the controller. Both Nintendo releases are that notebook, Lily's curse included.
race-the-sun:
Solar wings fail at dusk in Race The Sun, Flippfly's 2013 endless racer about a craft that dies when the sun sets. Speed picks up on its own, obstacles arrive in silhouette, and the Wii U version ports that minimalist computer game.

Collecting light keeps the systems alive for another few seconds of daylight. There is no lap marker, only a horizon and a clock made of the sky.

Flippfly's sunset is the fail state. The Wii U port is that same race against the light.
oddworld-new-n-tasty:
RuptureFarms returns in Oddworld: New 'n' Tasty, Just Add Water's 2014 rebuild of Abe's Oddysee, a new pass at the 1997 factory escape. Mudokons still need chanting and stealth, Sligs still patrol, and Wii U was among the console releases.

Possessing a guard, hiding in a shadow, and leading a line of coworkers to a bird portal are the old verbs in a new view. Abe's stomach and the meat processing plot remain the reason to sneak.

The 1997 game is the first escape. New 'n' Tasty is the rebuild, and the Wii U disc is one of the consoles that received it.
call-of-duty-ghosts:
Riley's leash is a mechanic in Call of Duty: Ghosts, Infinity Ward's 2013 shooter with a new cast after Modern Warfare. Logan and Hesh carry the campaign, the dog is a controllable partner in places, and the Wii U version includes that campaign and uses the gamepad for extras.

The Federation war and a ruined American map replace the old Task Force 141 roster. Space weapons and a submarine set piece sit beside suburban infiltration, which is the range this cast was given.

The Wii U gamepad extras do not swap the story for a side mode. Riley, Logan, and Hesh are the campaign that pad is attached to.
sonic-all-stars-racing-transformed:
Mid-lap boats replace cars in Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed, Sumo Digital's 2012 Sega crossover whose karts switch among car, boat, and plane. A water section grows pontoons, a drop deploys wings, and Wii U and Nintendo 3DS received that transforming race.

Sega characters beyond Sonic fill the grid, and the course itself forces the vehicle change. All-Stars racing had existed before; the transformation mid-lap is this sequel's addition.

The Wii U and 3DS releases are that transforming grid. A lap that stays a car the whole way is a different game.
how-to-survive:
Island scrap becomes spears in How to Survive, Eko Software's 2013 zombie game about crafting weapons on an island. The view is overhead, camps need light, and the Wii U port is a console edition of that camp.

Zombies on the beach are the pressure, and a recipe for a better axe is the reward for exploring instead of hiding. The tone jokes while the hunger and the horde do not.

Eko's island is a crafting camp with the undead as weather. The Wii U port is that overhead camp, recipes included.
stealth-inc-2-game-of-clones:
Test chambers grow meaner in Stealth Inc 2: A Game of Clones, Curve Studios' stealth-puzzle sequel. The 2014 Wii U release uses clones and light puzzles to extend the traps of the first game, and the pad can show a camera the television hides.

A guard's vision cone and a timed gate are the old problems. The clone is the new body you can leave on a switch while the one you inhabit sneaks.

Curve's sequel expects the Wii U's two screens. The first game's test subject is the ancestor; the clones are this chapter's joke and tool.
little-inferno:
Catalog toys exist to burn in Little Inferno, the 2012 fireplace Tomorrow Corporation made after World of Goo. You order from a catalog, combine objects in the flames for letters and stamps, and the Wii U version was an early home for that fireplace.

Combos have names, and a delivery boy brings the next box while the snow sits outside. The game is a stove with a plot, not a physics sandbox of the earlier goo.

Tomorrow Corporation's fireplace is the whole interface. The Wii U release was an early living-room place to strike the match.
lego-batman-3-beyond-gotham:
Lantern Corps rings pull Batman into space in LEGO Batman 3: Beyond Gotham, Traveller's Tales' 2014 sequel built around those corps. Brainiac's threat leaves Gotham, and Wii U and Nintendo 3DS were part of the release.

Green, yellow, and the other lantern colors become suits with different brick powers. The Watchtower and the corps' planets replace the alley for long stretches, which is the scale the subtitle promises.

The second brick Batman opened the city and gave everyone a voice. This one leaves orbit, rings first.
tom-clancys-splinter-cell-blacklist:
Fourth Echelon's faster pace defines Tom Clancy’s Splinter Cell Blacklist, Ubisoft's 2013 Splinter Cell with a new voice for Sam Fisher. Ghost, Panther, and Assault are the approaches a mission will score, and the Wii U version ports that campaign.

The Paladin aircraft is the hub between countries, and the new voice replaces the one longtime players expected from Fisher. Mark-and-execute kills are part of the speed, which is the break from the slower early entries.

The Wii U port is that scored campaign. Chaos Theory's patience is a different game; Blacklist wants the room cleared in a style you chose on the plane.
need-for-speed-most-wanted-a-criterion-g:
Fairhaven City is a reboot, not a sequel, in Need for Speed: Most Wanted - A Criterion Game, Criterion's 2012 open-world racer. It is a different game from the 2005 Most Wanted, and the Wii U version was part of that multiplatform release.

Billboards smash into cops, and a most-wanted list of cars waits in the world to be found and driven. Easy entry into almost any parked vehicle replaces the older garage-and-blacklist career.

The 2005 Rockport story had Razor and a heat ladder. Fairhaven has a list of cars and a city you enter without that feud.
giana-sisters-twisted-dreams:
Punk Giana swaps places with her cute form in Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams, Black Forest Games' reboot of the 1987 platformer. The 2012 swap changes gems, hazards, and music between dream worlds, and a Wii U version brought that revival to Nintendo's console.
