A scream becomes a fireball in one world and a different answer in the other. The 1987 game is the ancestor; the twist is the mid-jump swap between sisters who share a body.

Black Forest's reboot is the two worlds. The Wii U version is that mid-jump swap on a Nintendo disc, gems included.
the-bridge:
Escher stairs rotate with gravity in The Bridge, a 2013 puzzle about impossible architecture inspired by M.C. Escher. The man in the engraving walks a black-and-white drawing, and the Wii U release ports that computer game.

Turning the world makes a floor into a wall so a key can fall toward a door that was upside down. Menace from a pursuing shape keeps the stroll from being only a gallery of prints.

The inspiration is the lithograph. The Wii U port is that rotating drawing, not a platformer with a painted background.
fifa-2002:
Power bars time the shot in FIFA 2002, the soccer annual EA Sports built around a new kicking meter. The 2001 release joined the GameCube multiplatform set, with the bar under the kicker as the argument about penalties and long shots.

Licensed clubs and a season structure are the annual's usual furniture. The bar is the piece players argued about, because a full meter was not always the smart kick.

The cube edition is that annual, power bar included. It is the season that shipped with the bar, on Nintendo's new disc console of the time.
sonic-adventure-2-battle:
Chao gardens sit beside extra multiplayer in Sonic Adventure 2 Battle, the GameCube edition of the hero and dark stories. It was a launch-window title for the console, adding battle modes on top of Shadow's introduction and the Space Colony ARK.

Hero and dark campaigns still split Sonic's friends from Eggman's, and the garden still raises Chao between those stories. The Dreamcast original told the plot first; this edition is the one that padded the versus menu for the new machine.

Launch-window buyers met Shadow here if they had missed the Dreamcast. The extra multiplayer is why the title grew the word Battle.
fifa-street-2:
Trick goals return in FIFA Street 2, EA Sports BIG's 2006 continuation of street soccer. New venues and a deeper trick list sit on the small courts, and the GameCube version arrived near the end of that console's sports lineup.

Gamebreakers still decide a playground match, and the annual simulation is still a different product. Headers, volleys, and wall passes are the language, with the cube disc showing up while the machine's sports shelf was thinning.

BIG's second street game is this trick sequel. The cube release is that late sports guest, not the first playground disc.
mario-party-7:
Microphone parties join eight players in Mario Party 7, the 2005 board game Hudson and Nintendo shipped as the last Mario Party on the GameCube. Bowser still owns a hostile board, and the microphone accessory is required for some of the minigames.

Eight controllers around one television was the sell, a count earlier cube parties did not ask for. The boards are cruises and castles, and the mic turns a shout into an input.

Hudson's last cube party is this eight-player set. Later parties moved to other machines; the microphone and the eighth pad belong to this one.
super-monkey-ball:
AiAi rolls inside a transparent ball in Super Monkey Ball, Amusement Vision's launch game taken from the arcade Monkey Ball. The 2001 cube debut tilts the stage, not the monkey, and MeeMee, Baby, and GonGon share the same fragile sphere.

Party games sit beside the courses: bowling, billiards, and a target flight off a ramp. A fall off the edge is instant, which is why the tilt has to stay small.

The arcade Monkey Ball is the parent. This launch disc is the home version, with the party menu the cabinet did not need.
mario-party-6:
Daylight boards flip to night in Mario Party 6, Hudson's 2004 GameCube party game. Spaces change when the sun and moon trade places, and the microphone peripheral is used again for minigames that listen.

A star on a day space may not be the star you want after dusk. The cycle is the board's gimmick, and the mic is the accessory carried forward from the idea that a shout can be a button.

Hudson's day-night party is this one. The following cube party added an eighth player; this one is the board that owns a clock.
nba-live-06:
Season rosters for that winter live in NBA LIVE 06, the basketball annual EA Sports built around one club year. The 2005 GameCube edition is that season of the long NBA Live series, with franchise play and the clubs of the time.

Dunks, picks, and a season schedule are the annual's ordinary furniture. What pins it to a year is the roster, not a street-court spinoff or a management sim.

EA's cube edition is that season's Live. It is one entry in a yearly line, the one that reached Nintendo's disc alongside the other consoles of the time.
burnout:
Near-miss boosts fund the crashes in Burnout, the 2001 racer with which Criterion started the series. Traffic is both the obstacle and the fuel, and a GameCube port followed the PlayStation 2 original.

A scrape that does not quite hit fills the meter, and a real hit ends the run. The later games added a crash mode you play on purpose; this first one still wants you to survive the traffic you are using.

Criterion's opening argument is the near miss. The cube port is that argument after the PlayStation 2 release, wrecks included.
capcom-vs-snk-2:
Groove selections change the meter in Capcom vs. SNK 2, Capcom's 2001 crossover of both companies' fighters. Ryu and Terry Bogard can share a team, and the GameCube edition is the EO revision of that arcade game.

Grooves decide whether a bar is a cancel, a parry, or a custom stock, which is the system the title is built on. The ratio of strong and weak fighters from the earlier crossover is part of the team building.

EO is the revision on the cube. The arcade grooves are the fight, and this edition is that revision rather than the first cabinet people had to leave downtown.
final-fantasy-crystal-chronicles:
Myrrh trees are the quest in Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles, Square Enix's 2003 action role-playing game built for four players linked to Game Boy Advances. Caravans of Clavats, Lilties, Yukes, and Selkies carry a chalice through miasma, and the handheld shows each player's personal menu.

It opened a spinoff line rather than continuing the numbered games. A dropped link cable means the shared screen loses the private inventory the design expected.

The cube and the handhelds are one machine in this caravan. Numbered Final Fantasy games do not ask a friend to bring a second console.
harvest-moon-a-wonderful-life:
Forget-Me-Not Valley ages with you in Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life, Marvelous's GameCube story of one farmer across chapters of a life. Natsume published the Western release of the Japanese original, with marriage, a child, and a farm that does not reset every spring in the old way.

Cows, a dig site, and the neighbors' gossip mark the chapters as years pass. The child grows, which is the feature the title is promising, and the valley's cliffs are the whole map.

Marvelous's life-chapter farm is this valley. Natsume's Western box is the 2003 Japanese story, translated onto the cube.
james-bond-007-everything-or-nothing:
Brosnan's Bond speaks in James Bond 007: Everything or Nothing, EA's third-person game with Pierce Brosnan's voice on the agent. The 2004 GameCube disc is one of the original releases, and cover shooting and driving share a campaign that is not adapted from a single film.

Gadgets and a third-person camera put this Bond closer to an action adventure than to the on-rails shooters of the 1990s. Brosnan's voice is the bridge to the films even though the mission set is original.

EA's cube original is that voiced campaign. It is not the later Connery likeness game, and it is not a retelling of one movie's plot.
the-lord-of-the-rings-the-third-age:
Gondor's war gets an original party in The Lord of the Rings: The Third Age, EA's 2004 role-playing game with turn-based battles running beside the film trilogy. The fellowship's journey is the news in the background, while your company fights its own battles from the Shire's shadow toward Mordor.

Turns, spells, and a party that is not Aragorn's are the structure. Film locations still appear, so Minas Tirith and the bigger war are visible without being the party you control.

EA's side party is the campaign. The films supply the timeline; the turn order supplies the fighting.
burnout-2-point-of-impact:
Crash junctions score the pileup in Burnout 2: Point of Impact, Criterion's 2002 sequel that adds a mode where the points come from causing the biggest traffic disaster. The usual races and near-miss boosts remain beside that new way to play.

A junction, a full boost, and a deliberate wreck are the crash mode's inputs. The first Burnout wanted you to avoid the hit; this mode wants the hit to be enormous.

Point of Impact is the subtitle because of that mode. Races are still here, but the pileup is the chapter the first game did not have.
from-russia-with-love:
Connery's likeness returns for James Bond 007: From Russia with Love, EA's 2005 adaptation of the 1963 film, jetpack sequence included. Sean Connery's face is on Bond, and the GameCube version includes that added jetpack alongside the story's trains, Istanbul, and Red Grant.

Rosa Klebb's shoe and the film's intrigue are the plot. The jetpack is the piece the movie did not hand you as a level, which is how the game stretches the 1963 script.

EA's cube adaptation is Connery's Bond with that extra flight. It is the film's story plus the pack, not an original mission set with a different actor's voice.
james-bond-007-agent-under-fire:
Original missions, not a film plot, structure James Bond 007: Agent Under Fire, EA's 2001 Bond game. The GameCube version adds split-screen multiplayer the PlayStation 2 release lacked, so a second pad on the cube is a mode the earlier disc did not have.

Q's gadgets and a driving section still frame the solo missions. The multiplayer maps are the cube-specific reason to care which Bond disc is in the tray.

EA's original mission set is the campaign on every platform. The split-screen is the cube's addition, and the PlayStation 2 game simply does not have it.
i-ninja:
Grade belts mark progress in I-Ninja, Argonaut's 2003 cartoon platformer about a small ninja scoring his own combat. The GameCube shipped with the PlayStation 2 and Xbox versions, with a master who grades the fights.

Rage and a sword bigger than the hero are the joke, and the levels are bright obstacle courses between those graded brawls. The ninja is small on purpose, so the enemies look like toys he is determined to outrank.

Argonaut's graded ninja is this cartoon. The cube release is one of the three consoles that got it, not a later handheld demake.
dragon-ball-z-budokai-2:
Fusion dances and a board-game story arrive in Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 2, Dimps' 2003 fighting sequel. Goku and Vegeta can combine, the story moves as a board of spaces, and Atari published the Western release that includes the GameCube version.

Capsules and a roster of transformations sit beside the board, so a fight is a square you landed on. The first Budokai was a more straightforward ladder; this sequel adds the fusions and the map.

Dimps' board is the campaign structure. The cube disc is part of that multiplatform release, fusions included.
tom-clancys-rainbow-six-3-raven-shield:
Planning maps shrink on the cube in Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six 3: Raven Shield, Red Storm's 2003 tactical shooter. The GameCube release is the action-led console edition, not the full computer mission planner with its long setup phase.

Terrorist hunts and room entries remain, but the console asks you to play the breach more than to draw it. The computer game is where the planning fantasy is complete.

Red Storm's third Rainbow is the name on both. The cube edition is the action-led one, and the planner stays on the computer.
star-fox-assault:
Aparoid queens are the threat in Star Fox Assault (2005), the campaign Nintendo and Namco sent Fox back to after Star Fox Adventures left the series on dinosaur-back. Arwing flights and on-foot shooting share the missions, and this is the GameCube entry, not Star Fox 64.

Krystal, Falco, Slippy, and Peppy are in the squadron again, and the on-foot sections are the piece Adventures did not fly. Sauria's dinosaur chapter is the previous game; the Aparoids are this one's invasion.

Tricky the dinosaur belongs to the previous adventure. Namco's boots-on-the-ground guns share the Aparoid war with the Arwing, which is the campaign people mean when they are not asking for the 64 remix.
spyro-a-heros-tail:
Red's scheme replaces the older sorcerers in Spyro: A Hero's Tail, the 2004 sequel Eurocom made after Insomniac's trilogy. Vivendi published that home-console adventure, with Spyro, Sparx, and a Dragon Kingdom that is not the same backyard as the first three games.

Breath, charge, and a wider set of companions carry the new studio's take. Insomniac's trilogy had ended; Eurocom's job was a home-console continuation with a different villain in Red.

The cube release is that Eurocom sequel. It is not a port of the first three playgrounds.
fifa-2003:
Club Championship cups sit inside FIFA 2003, the annual EA Sports built around a licensed bracket. The 2002 release puts those teams in a cup on top of the usual season, and the GameCube joined that set.

The power bar of the previous annual is yesterday's argument. This year's addition is the club cup, a bracket of licensed sides rather than a new physics trick.

EA's cube edition is that cup-bearing annual. The bracket is the feature the box was selling beside the season.
rock-band-2:
Tour setlists grow longer in Rock Band 2, Harmonix's 2008 instrument sequel. A career tour mode structures the nights, and the Wii version supports the guitar, drums, and microphone.

Setlist size is the practical sequel feature: more songs, and a tour that treats the band as a calendar. The plastic kit from the first game still speaks to this one.

Harmonix's second band is the longer tour. The Wii release is that tour with the three instruments, not a guitar-only track list.
check-vs-mate:
Animated captures turn chess into a skirmish in Battle vs Chess, a 2011 game where fantasy scenes play out the moves. A knight's jump can become a short fight, and Wii and Nintendo DS versions were released around that idea.

The board still obeys chess rules. The spectacle is what happens in the square when a piece is taken, which is the whole reason to wrap a battle around a legal move.

The Wii and DS releases are that battle-chess idea. They are not a new ruleset; they are a costume on the old grid.
metal-slug-2:
Mummy transformations join the squad in METAL SLUG 2, SNK's 1998 run-and-gun sequel. Fiolina Germi arrives, new vehicles roll in, and a Wii release later reissued that Neo Geo game.

Getting hit by the wrong projectile turns a soldier into a mummy or a slower, heavier form, which is the joke the first slug did not tell. The tank is still the shelter, and the transformations are the risk of standing in the wrong sparkle.

SNK's second slug is the one with those curses. The Wii reissue is that Neo Geo board, not a new mission set drawn for the remote.
final-fantasy-iv:
Ceodore Harvey carries FINAL FANTASY IV: THE AFTER YEARS, Square Enix's sequel to Final Fantasy IV, following a new generation after the original cast. It began on mobile phones and later reached Wii, Nintendo DS, and Nintendo 3DS, with the moon and Baron still haunting the family.

Cecil and Rosa's son is the new lead, and the older heroes are the previous generation rather than the default party. The subtitle is the point: years have passed, and the crystal problem is not finished with the children.

The mobile original is the first telling of Ceodore's trip. The Nintendo releases are that sequel arriving later, not a remake of Cecil's own game.
sonic-unleashed:
Werehog nights interrupt the boost in Sonic Unleashed, Sonic Team's 2008 switch between daytime speed stages and a nighttime beast. Chip travels with Sonic, the planet is in pieces, and the Wii version was built separately from the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 game.

Day stages are the sprint. Night stages are slower brawls as the werehog, and the Wii build does not share its level geometry with the high-definition version.

Sonic Team's split personality is the design. The Wii release is its own construction of that split, not a shaved copy of the other consoles' continents.
spider-man-3:
Black-suit venom sticks to the swinging in Spider-Man 3, Treyarch's 2007 tie-in to Sam Raimi's third film. Sandman, the New Goblin, and the symbiote share the plot, and the Wii version uses motion controls for that movie's action.

The black suit changes combat, which is the film's temptation turned into a moveset. Motion swings on the Wii are how a web line gets thrown on that console.

Treyarch's tie-in is the third film's mess of villains. The Wii build is that mess with the remote in your hand.
a-boy-and-his-blob:
Jellybean shapes revive a partnership in A Boy and His Blob, WayForward's 2009 remake of David Crane's 1989 puzzle. Feed the blob and it becomes a tool, a ladder or a trampoline depending on the flavor, and Wii, Nintendo DS, and Nintendo 3DS all received that remake.

rock-band:
Band kits sold guitar, drums, and a microphone together in Rock Band, Harmonix's 2007 argument that one living room could be a group. A Wii version followed the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 launch, using that same three-instrument idea.

The note highway is shared, but each plastic instrument has its own part. Dropping the singer does not stop the drum chart, which is the point of a kit instead of a single guitar peripheral.

Harmonix's first kit is this bundle. The Wii version is that bundle arriving after the other two consoles had already plugged in.
toy-story-3:
Andy's toys get an open box in Disney•Pixar Toy Story 3: The Video Game, the 2010 tie-in Avalanche Software developed for Disney from the Pixar film. Woody and Buzz move through a toy-box mode as well as the story, and Wii and Nintendo DS versions both shipped.

Sunnyside and the film's daycare plot give the missions their stakes. The toy box is the mode that lets you set up play without following Lotso's scene order.

Avalanche's tie-in is both a story and a box of toys. The Wii and DS releases are that pair of modes, not a single rail of film clips.
the-amazing-spider-man:
Oscorp's outbreak spills into an open city in The Amazing Spider-Man, Beenox's 2012 game based on the Marc Webb film. Cross-species creatures roam, and Wii, Wii U, and the DS family received versions that differ from the main console release.

Peter Parker's web-rush through Manhattan is the big-machine fantasy. The Nintendo builds are smaller cousins, so a dual-screen copy is not the same open city the high-definition release sold.

Beenox's film game is the outbreak. The Nintendo versions exist, and they are not the main console campaign copied line for line.
puzzle-quest:
Match-three spells fight a war in Puzzle Quest: Challenge of the Warlords, Infinite Interactive's 2007 mix of gem puzzles and a fantasy campaign drawn from the Warlords line. Mana from the board casts the spell, and Wii and Nintendo DS carried that board to consoles.

Capturing territory between puzzles gives the gems a map. A skull on the board is not decoration; it is the combat system wearing a match-three costume.

The Warlords lineage is the campaign's family. The Wii and DS boards are that hybrid, not a plain gem swap with no siege.
mario-kart-wii:
Plastic wheels shipped in the box with Mario Kart Wii, Nintendo's 2008 kart that added bikes and online play. A wheel-shaped shell spins down the road, and bikes can wheelie on a straight while the Wii Wheel turns the remote into a rim.

Mario Kart 8 is a different, later kart with its own anti-gravity tracks. This one is the motion-console race, Rainbow Road and half-pipes included, and the online rooms were part of the sell beside the plastic in the box.

Bullet Bills and the blue shell still punish a clean race. The plastic wheel is the object this entry added to the living room, and the later eight is not this roster or this rim.
brothers-in-arms-road-to-hill-30:
Matt Baker's squad needs orders in Brothers in Arms: Road to Hill 30, the 2005 Normandy campaign with which Gearbox opened its World War II line. Hill 30 is the objective in the title, hedgerows break the fields into rooms, and giving an order matters as much as the shooting.

The 101st Airborne framing puts Baker with a squad that will stall if nobody is told to suppress. Ammunition and a flanking fireteam are the puzzle, not a lone commando's health pack.

Gearbox's first Hill 30 campaign is this Normandy walk. Later brothers-in-arms games continued the squad; this is the opening road.
super-smash-bros-brawl:
Subspace Emissary gives a story mode to Super Smash Bros. Brawl, the 2008 fighting game from Sora Ltd. and Nintendo, directed by Masahiro Sakurai. A large roster includes Sonic and Solid Snake, and stage hazards turn the platforms into part of the fight.

It sits between Melee and the later pair on Nintendo 3DS and Wii U hardware. Stickers, a more elaborate adventure mode, and Final Destination's flat dare are all in this Wii entry.

Sakurai's subspace story is the single-player epic. The 3DS and Wii U games that followed are a different pair, and Melee is the earlier cube battle this one had to follow.
fifa-11:
Motion swings replace the pad on the Wii edition of FIFA 11, EA Sports' club-season football sim. The 2010 season on other consoles stayed on a traditional controller, so the Wii game asks the remote to be the foot.

The season and the clubs are the annual's spine. The swing is the Wii-specific skin on that spine, and a mistimed flick sends the shot the same way a mistimed button would on the other versions.

EA's annual is the season underneath the swing. The Wii edition is the one that kept the motion kicks while the rest of the lineup stayed on the pad.
strong-bad-episode-4-dangeresque-3:
Dangeresque poses through Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 4 - Dangeresque 3: The Criminal Projective. Telltale's 2008 Homestar Runner episode also reached WiiWare. Telltale's fourth episode is this film set. WiiWare buyers got Dangeresque's production, not a compilation of the whole season in one file.
strong-bad-episode-2-strong-badia-the-fr:
Strong Badia is founded in the living room during Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 2 - Strong Badia the Free. Telltale's 2008 Homestar Runner episode on WiiWare turns that declaration into a click-adventure. Strong Bad tries to declare a country inside his own house, and the borders are furniture.

Homestar, The Cheat, and the rest of the cast become a diplomatic problem. The joke is sovereignty over a room you already live in, which is the episode's whole plot engine.

Telltale's second episode is this secession. The WiiWare release is that room-sized nation, not the later band competition or the film set.
strong-bad-episode-5-8-bit-is-enough:
Retro cabinets take over Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 5 - 8-Bit Is Enough, the season finale that closed Telltale's 2008 Homestar Runner run. A WiiWare release sat alongside the computer version, and old video-game forms invade the house until the cast has to play their way out.

The finale is still a point-and-click, even when the screen pretends to be a cabinet. Season-long jokes pay off here, which is why it is the last episode rather than a mid-run sketch.

Telltale's fifth episode is this invasion of old games. WiiWare and the computer shared that ending, and it is not a port of an actual 1980s cartridge.
spider-man-shattered-dimensions:
Madame Web splits the hero four ways in Spider-Man: Shattered Dimensions, Beenox's 2010 game across comic versions of Spider-Man. Amazing, Noir, 2099's Miguel O'Hara, and Ultimate each get a shard of a broken tablet, while the Wii and Nintendo DS releases are smaller cousins of that high-definition campaign.

Beenox's four-comic campaign is the high-definition game. The Wii and DS releases are reduced relatives, not that full tablet hunt copied onto a smaller disc.
strong-bad-episode-3-baddest-of-the-band:
Band battles take the house over in Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People: Episode 3 - Baddest of the Bands. Telltale's 2008 Homestar Runner chapter also reached WiiWare. Strong Bad enters a contest of groups, and the instruments are household objects with ambitions.

The episode is a click-adventure about egos and a gig, not a plastic-instrument music game. Homestar's world already had bands; this chapter makes the contest the plot.

quantum-of-solace:
Casino Royale's Venice chase shares a disc with Quantum of Solace, the 2008 shooter that also covers the later Bond film. A Wii build used pointer aiming, so the remote's crosshair replaces a stick for the firefights.

Daniel Craig's Bond is the face of both plots, and the first film's events are not skipped just because the title names the second movie. Pointer aiming is the Wii-specific way those gunfights are played.

the-beatles-rock-band:
Apple Corps licensed the catalog for The Beatles: Rock Band, the 2009 instrument game Harmonix built entirely from Beatles songs. Dreamscapes of studios and rooftops replace a fictional band's career, and plastic guitars, drums, and a microphone play the real recordings.

Abbey Road and the earlier years are chapters rather than a shuffle of unrelated hits. The note charts are the game; the footage and the rooms are the history lesson Apple allowed.

the-godfather-the-game:
Corleone rackets become a business sim in The Godfather: The Game, the 2006 open-city crime game EA Redwood Shores adapted from the film trilogy. Aldo Trapani, an original enforcer, rises through extortion and favor, and a Wii port followed the original consoles.

The baptism, the don, and the family's wars are the films' skeleton. The play is the shop you lean on and the block you take, which the movies only imply.

EA's city is that rise. The Wii port is the same racket map arriving later, not a rail of film scenes with no territory to hold.
lostwinds:
Drawn gusts carry Toku in LostWinds, the 2008 game with which Frontier launched WiiWare. You sketch the wind on the screen so it can lift the hero across floating islands, and a wind spirit is the power doing the lifting.

new-super-mario-bros-wii:
Propeller mushrooms lift four players at once in New Super Mario Bros. Wii, Nintendo's 2009 side-scroller with a midair spin carried over from the handheld idea of 2D Mario. Penguin suits, Yoshi on some maps, and a Super Guide that can finish a stage you keep failing all sit on the world map.

rock-band-3:
Pro keys arrive with a keytar in Rock Band 3, Harmonix's 2010 sequel that added pro-difficulty parts for real instruments. The Wii release used that same band setup, with charts that expect more than the five buttons of the earlier kits.

A pro guitar part and a keyboard part sit beside the old drums and vocals. The training angle is the sequel's pitch: the plastic can inch toward the instrument it imitates.

pes-2010:
Motion kicks lead the Wii edition of Pro Evolution Soccer 2010, Konami's football sim that favored a remote swing. The 2009 versions on other consoles kept simulation controls on a pad, while the Wii game makes the strike a gesture.

Master-league habits of the wider series are not what the motion edition is selling. The kick itself is the input argument, and the clubs still take the field around that swing.

Konami's roster is still on the pitch. The Wii edition is the one that chose motion over the simulation pad used elsewhere.
streets-of-rage:
Axel Stone, Adam Hunter, and Blaze Fielding walk the street in Streets of Rage, Sega's 1991 side-scrolling brawler that began on the Genesis. Mr. X runs the syndicate, and Virtual Console later reissued the game on Wii and Nintendo 3DS.

disney-universe:
Costume platforms let four players wear Disney characters in Disney Universe, the 2011 adventure that included a Wii release. A Mickey or Donald outfit is the avatar, and themed worlds are the levels those costumes run through.

The four-player idea is the co-op, with each costume still able to jump the same hazards. Film worlds supply the scenery, and the costume is the character select.

guitar-hero-5:
Party drops let a friend join mid-song in Guitar Hero 5, Activision's 2009 entry, also on Wii, developed by Neversoft. A track already in progress can take another instrument, which is the party feature the box was selling.

donkey-kong-country-returns:
Tiki Tak Tribe hypnotists steal the hoard in Donkey Kong Country Returns, the 2010 return Retro Studios built for Nintendo on the Wii. Mine carts, rocket barrels, and levels that expect both Kongs share the island, and blowing on the remote can clear a dandelion or a gust puzzle.

Diddy on Donkey's back is the two-Kong idea the levels are drawn for. Retro's mine carts and rocket barrels are this return; the HD switch release is another listing.
dead-space-extraction:
Ishimura's earlier outbreak is the rail in Dead Space: Extraction, Eurocom's 2009 on-rails prequel that debuted on Wii with pointer aiming. A rescue team meets necromorphs before the later events of the main game, and a PlayStation 3 port followed.

Eurocom's Wii debut is this pointer rail. The PlayStation 3 port came after, and the campaign is still the earlier outbreak.
nba-2k12:
Jordan Challenge games sit inside NBA 2K12, the release Visual Concepts built with Michael Jordan on the cover. The 2011 highlights from his career become playable scenarios, and the game also reached Wii.

The cover is not only a photograph. The challenge mode is a season of specific nights, and the association career around it is the ordinary basketball sim of that year.

Visual Concepts' Jordan mode is the feature the cover promises. The Wii release is that package, challenge list included.
silent-hill-shattered-memories:
Harry Mason's phone profiles the player in Silent Hill: Shattered Memories, Climax's 2009 reimagining of the first Silent Hill. There is no combat, the Wii remote is a flashlight and a handset, and the psychological profile changes the town, with later ports to PSP and PlayStation 2.

safecracker-the-ultimate-puzzle-adventur:
Combination locks fill the mansion of Safecracker: The Ultimate Puzzle Adventure, Kheops Studio's puzzle adventure about opening safes. Dials, clues in the rooms, and a fortune behind the doors are the campaign, later brought to Wii from the computer.

A painting, a ledger, and a half-remembered combination are the way forward, not a jump or a gun. The heir's job is the cracking, and each safe is a level.

Kheops' mansion is a stack of locks. The Wii release is that stack brought over from the computer, dials included.
rogue-trooper:
Rebellion lifted the last Genetic Infantryman out of 2000 AD, and Rogue Trooper follows that blue soldier across the poison wastes of Nu Earth. Nu Earth's chem-clouds would kill an ordinary soldier, which is why only the blue infantryman can cross them.

Gunnar, Bagman, and Helm survive as biochips in his rifle, pack, and helmet, so the dead squad still argues while he fights. Quartz Zone's betrayal is the wound that keeps him moving toward the traitors who sold the regiment.

manhunt-2:
British classifiers blocked Rockstar's stealth sequel until the worst footage was removed, and Manhunt 2 spent that fight waiting on a rating. Pickman and the Project's doctors sit behind the killings Daniel Lamb cannot remember choosing.

Daniel Lamb wakes between a clinic and a trail of executions, hiding long enough to trigger each kill. The camera treats those takedowns like found footage, which is the material the UK board refused to pass uncut.

just-dance-2019:
Disc presses were still running for living-room dancers when Just Dance 2019 arrived for the original motion console and its successor together. A sweat playlist and on-screen coaches are what a household actually starts after the disc spins up.

2010-fifa-world-cup:
South Africa's national tournament got a licensed pitch in 2010 FIFA World Cup, EA Sports' one-off built around that competition. Host-nation grounds and the knockout bracket matter more here than a club's league table.

Kits, stadiums, and the national squads follow the real draw rather than a club calendar. Remote swings stand in for casual kicking, apart from the stick simulation sold on other hardware.

The trophy bracket is the structure, so knockout night in that country is the mode that matters. A season-long club career from the annual series is not what this tie-in is for.
luxor-3:
Colored spheres have to hit rolling chains before the line reaches the pyramid gate, and Luxor 3 is MumboJumbo's chain-shot built on that race. The shooter slides under the chain and looses the next colored sphere toward a matching gap.

The shooter slides along the bottom while Egyptian ruins push the path faster. Matching a pair opens a gap, and a longer run collapses neighboring balls into the scarab's collected stones.

xenoblade-chronicles:
Monolith Soft set a colony on a fallen titan, and Xenoblade Chronicles follows Shulk from that Bionis outpost toward the Mechonis on the horizon. Colony 9's stand against a faced Mechon is the fight that wakes Shulk's vision of the future.

Attacks keep swinging on their own while arts have to be timed against a vision of the next blow. The Monado shows those flashes, and standing behind a faced Mechon changes which art actually lands.

dragon-ball-z-budokai-tenkaichi-3:
Spike packed an arena fighter with nearly every fighter the anime had drawn, and Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi 3 lets them fly across open battlefields. A beam struggle can still be won by mashing while both fighters hang in the air.

Beam struggles, vanishing steps, and rush chains replace the tighter flat duels of earlier Budokai discs. Transforming spends the same energy used for specials, so a Super Saiyan change is a tactical spend.

That roster shipped in 2007 on the motion console and on PlayStation 2 beside the same fusions. Capsule allies share the select screen with the tournament regulars.
g-force:
Disney's spy rodents left the film for a mission pack, and G-Force: The Video Game puts Darwin's team into separate console builds. Darwin, Juarez, and Blaster keep their film personalities even when the level geometry changes by machine.

pirates-of-the-caribbean-at-worlds-end:
Jack Sparrow's third film became a cutlass tie-in, and Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End sends the crew through ship fights and island duels. Barbossa and Elizabeth join Jack when a deck needs more than one cutlass.

Remote swings drive sword strikes while Davy Jones, Calypso, and the East India Company supply the targets. A separate handheld telling uses its own maps for the same movie beats.

resident-evil-the-umbrella-chronicles-2:
Capcom put the mansion, the city, and the train on rails, and Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles retells those outbreaks with a light gun. Herb sprays and a dodge shake are the only relief once a crowd of hunters fills the corridor.

Rebecca, Chris, Jill, and Leon walk chapters that restage the early disasters while files fill gaps the old cameras skipped. One remote is the gun, and a second remote lets a partner cover the same zombie lanes.

The 2007 release later returned on the successor's shop as the same rail shooter. A closing chapter follows Albert Wesker as Umbrella itself comes apart.
mega-man-10:
Capcom and Inti Creates followed their previous 8-bit revival with Mega Man 10(2010), bringing back limited lives and steep stage design. Wily's castle still waits after the Robot Master select screen, with the same spare lives you saved.

Robot Masters still fall to weakness chains, and a shop between stages sells tanks only if the score can pay. Proto Man and Bass become playable bodies once their unlocks are met.

That arcade sting is the point, with no modern checkpoint cushion after a pit. WiiWare buyers got Dr. Light's charge shot and the same continue pressure on a remote.
wwe-13:
Yuke's framed the career around the Attitude Era, and WWE '13 replays that television period as story matches instead of a blank exhibition card. A steel chair at ringside can decide an Attitude Era objective the referee was never meant to see.

Stone Cold, The Rock, and the Ministry angles return as bouts with objectives pulled from the broadcasts. A creation suite sits beside those scripts for anyone who wants a custom wrestler in the same arenas.

nba-2k13:
Jay-Z took an executive producer credit and curated the songs, and NBA 2K13 is the basketball season people still name for that soundtrack. Blacktop games and association nights sit under the same Jay-Z tracklist.

Association play, blacktop runs, and broadcast presentation sit in the usual season structure. The motion edition was part of the same window, with gesture shooting in place of the stick work on high-definition consoles.

just-dance-2018:
Late shelves in the motion era still had room for Just Dance 2018, Ubisoft's pop-routine carton aimed at the original living-room remote. Gold stars depend on the remote's path, not on how loud the living room sings.

Coaches perform at the side of the screen while the sensor scores how closely the room follows. Pictograms telegraph the next move, and a run of songs becomes the night's whole activity.

metroid-prime-2-echoes:
Retro Studios split Aether between light and dark, and Metroid Prime 2: Echoes makes Samus Aran walk both copies of the same map. A light crystal is a safe pocket, and leaving it on Dark Aether starts the suit's drain again.

madden-nfl-13:
EA kept the new Infinity Engine on high-definition hardware, and Madden NFL 13 on the motion console stayed with the older feature set. Franchise weekends still schedule the real clubs even without the newer physics engine.

Playcalling, franchise weeks, and Sunday exhibitions remain the loop. The remote handles snaps and throws without the physics rewrite that engine was built to show elsewhere.

bittrip-core:

bittrip-fate:

samurai-shodown-ii:

Haohmaru, Nakoruru, and Genjuro settle scores with clashes, recoils, and a rage gauge that bursts into a furious stance. Spacing decides the first cut, because a blade's reach is the whole neutral game.

secret-neighbor-beta:
Hologryph turned the Hello Neighbor house into an online hide-and-seek test, and Secret Neighbor Beta is that computer trial rather than a motion-console release. Keys hidden in those crooked rooms are the children's win condition before the Neighbor grabs them.

rooms-the-main-building:
Corridors do nothing until the chambers slide into place, and Rooms: The Main Building is a puzzle about shoving those rooms until doors finally meet. A door that faces a wall stays shut no matter how many times it is clicked.

The building behaves like a stack of blocks on WiiWare. A hallway that looks adjacent on the map stays sealed until the correct faces touch.

tales-of-graces-f:
Namco's PlayStation 3 edition adds the future arc, and Tales of Graces f is that expanded telling rather than the first home version of Asbel's story. Windor's politics still sit under the artes, but the future chapter is the piece the first disc never stored.

brothers-in-arms-earned-in-blood:

Gearbox shipped both sergeants' stories in 2005, and a later motion-console port kept Hartsock's campaign. Squad commands still matter more than a lone sprint through the fields.
the-simpsons-game:
Springfield's family knows the levels are a product, and The Simpsons Game lets Homer, Marge, Bart, and Lisa talk back to checkpoints while they clear them. Marge's megaphone and Maggie's pacifier moments are powers the movie tie-in would never have given them.

secret-files-tunguska:
Nina Kalenkov hunts for her missing father, and Secret Files: Tunguska is Animation Arts' point-and-click wrapped around the Siberian blast. A photograph of the impact site becomes an inventory item rather than a cutscene to skip.

just-dance-2017:

dream-pinball-3d:
Themed cabinets stand in for a physical table, and Dream Pinball 3D fills its nights with video-pinball boards instead of a single wood machine. A nudge that is too hungry still tilts the table and kills the ball in play.

harry-potter-and-the-half-blood-prince:
Motion-controlled spells carry the living-room build of EA's film tie-in Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince, with a separate handheld game for the sixth movie. Quidditch and potion class break up the corridor sneaking Dumbledore assigns.

Hogwarts corridors, Quidditch, and potion class supply the activities between story scenes. The remote stands in for a wand, so a flick is the cast rather than a button assigned to a spell name.

camerons-avatar:

doc-clock-the-toasted-sandwich-of-time:
Stickmen Studios rotates each room so a clockwork hero can cross the gaps, and Doc Clock: The Toasted Sandwich of Time is that WiiWare puzzle. Turn the room too early and the clockwork hero drops into the gap his own floor just became.

spider-man-web-of-shadows:
The black suit drives an open Manhattan, and Spider-Man: Web of Shadows on the motion console is its own build rather than the PlayStation 3 game. Tendrils from the black suit reach ledges the red-and-blue web line treats as a swing.

Activision's symbiote story lets Peter switch between red-and-blue web swings and the darker tendril attacks. City blocks stay climbable while invading creatures spread across the avenues.

trackmania-2010:
Nadeo brought restart-friendly time trials into a living room, and TrackMania on that motion console is the 2010 release of the racing toy. A restart is instant, so a blown boost pad costs a second instead of a repair bill.

disney-epic-mickey-2-the-power-of-two:
Junction Point, led by Warren Spector, put Oswald beside Mickey, and Disney Epic Mickey 2: The Power of Two is that co-op cartoon on two Nintendo home machines. Thinner melts a toon wall that paint would have restored, and Oswald can stand on what remains.

tcs-hawx:
Arcade dogfights inside the Clancy universe define Tom Clancy's H.A.W.X. when the remote is allowed to tilt the jet. Missiles still need a lock even when the wrist is doing most of the banking.

Ubisoft's squad of private military pilots flies fast strikes rather than a cockpit study of every switch. Assistance on the motion build helps the turn while missiles and guns still have to be lined up by the player.

kung-fu-panda:
Po's film became a brawler, and Kung Fu Panda is the tie-in that shipped separate living-room and handheld versions alongside the movie. Tai Lung's threat is staged as short brawls rather than as one long open valley.

The Dragon Warrior rolls, slams, and eats his way through Tai Lung's threat in short fights. DreamWorks' animal masters appear as allies and obstacles rather than as a wrestling roster with weight classes.

transformers-the-game:
Traveller's Tales tied a robot-and-vehicle switch to the first Michael Bay film, and Transformers: The Game includes living-room and handheld versions of that idea. A city street is a road while the hero is a vehicle and a weapon range once the body unfolds.

wii-sports:
A sensor bar and a wrist were the whole gym in Wii Sports, the pack-in that taught tennis, bowling, baseball, golf, and boxing. A late tennis swing sails long, and a crooked bowling wrist finds the gutter the same way.

Miis stand in for the athletes, and a swing of the remote is the shot, the roll, or the punch. Bowling gutters and late tennis swings became the living room's shared language for the new controller.

Nintendo packed the collection with the console launch in 2006, as the original five-event lesson. Resort and the later Switch sports pack are different products.
guitar-hero-3-legends-of-rock:
Cartoon guitar bosses define the career, and Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock is the first package in that series built for the motion console. Star power saved for the devil duel is worth more than spending it on an easy verse.

Neversoft's note highways still scroll colored gems toward the strummer. The devil-guitar duel and the guest shredders turn set pieces into boss fights instead of another encore of the same chart.

x-men-origins-wolverine:
Logan claws through a milder living-room build, and X-Men Origins: Wolverine on that hardware is not the bloodier Uncaged Edition from high-definition consoles. Regeneration covers the lunges, but the milder build does not stage the Uncaged gore.

The film's Weapon X story still supplies the missions, with regenerating health and feral lunges as the combat. High-definition copies pushed gore past the movie, while this separate version dials that spectacle down.

no-more-heroes:
Travis Touchdown ranks up by earning cash at odd jobs between duels, and No More Heroes is Grasshopper Manufacture's motion-sword assassin game. Sylvia calls with the next ranked target only after the entry fee leaves Travis's motel wallet.

Santa Destroy's ranked killers wait at the end of each beam-katana fight, while lawn mowing and grocery runs fund the entry fee. The remote is the blade, so a shake finishes a downed rival.

The 2007 release was a third-party original that grew into further Nintendo entries. Travis's motel, his anime obsession, and Sylvia's phone calls are the tone between those ranked deaths.
virtua-tennis-4:
Sega aimed the racket at a wrist, and Virtua Tennis 4 on the motion console swings the remote as the racquet. A baseline rally still punishes a swing that starts before the bounce.

Licensed players and a motion-friendly club structure carry the matches. Timing the swing replaces the button-tap precision of earlier Virtua cabinets, which changes how a baseline rally feels.

The 2011 edition still cares about footwork position before the shot. A party in the living room can pick up a remote and rally without learning a six-button grip first.
golden-axe:
Death Adder's fantasy brawl came from the arcades, and Golden Axe is the Sega cabinet the motion console's Virtual Console later reissued. Kicking a gnome drops the potion that fills the magic meter for Tyris's screen-wide spell.

Ax Battler, Tyris Flare, and Gilius Thunderhead hack through thugs and mounted beasts on the road to that villain. Magic pots cracked from kicked gnomes still call the screen-filling spells.

The 1989 original was not born on Nintendo hardware. The reissue sells the same three heroes and the same potion magic rather than a new quest.
sam-max-season-1:
Six episodic cases share one carton, and Sam & Max Season One: Save the World is Telltale's first season of the Freelance Police packaged for a motion console. The Freelance Police insult every witness before the inventory puzzle actually opens.

Sam the dog and Max the rabbit talk through point-and-click scenes about hypnosis, talk shows, and a toy mafia. Each episode ends, then the next absurd threat picks up their banter.

The 2007 collection puts that season on a disc instead of leaving it as separate computer installments. Inventory jokes and conversation trees remain the way the pair saves the day.
flight-control-hd:
Drawn routes keep aircraft from meeting, and Flight Control HD is Firemint's console upgrade of the phone puzzle about that job. A jet assigned to the short runway will circle forever if the ink trail never reaches it.

Planes, helicopters, and faster jets enter from the screen's edge and need a path to the matching runway. A crossing line is a crash, so the drawing has to be revised while new blips appear.

The 2010 upgrade raises the resolution and the traffic compared with the pocket original. The handheld edition in the same family still asks for ink trails that never cross.
guitar-hero-world-tour:
Drums and vocals joined the guitar, and Guitar Hero World Tour turns the series into a full band on the motion console. The drum chart and the vocal line can fail separately while the guitarist is still in the song.

Four instruments can fill a song: lead, bass, kit, and a microphone. The note highway splits by part, and a living room can assign each one to a different person.

The 2008 set supports that same four-piece idea as the other home versions. A solo career still exists, but the new fantasy is the whole group clearing one chart together.
okami:
Amaterasu's celestial brush began on PlayStation 2, and Okami is Clover Studio's paint adventure later mapped to a pointer. A lily pad drawn on water only appears if the brush stroke matches the technique Issun just nagged about.

Ink strokes become slashes, gusts, and lily pads when the wolf goddess draws on the paused world. Issun nags from the edge of the screen while cursed Nippon waits to be restored one brush technique at a time.

The 2006 port lets the remote act as that brush, which suits the ink better than a stick ever did. Blooming trees and the rising sun meter still mark how much of a region has been cleaned.
mdk2:
Kurt Hectic, Doctor Hawkins, and Max the dog share the missions, and MDK 2 is BioWare's sequel to Shiny's original rather than a motion-console debut. Max the dog's close brawl hands back to Kurt's sniper chute when the level demands a distant shot.

The janitor still snipes from a ribbon chute, the scientist swaps absurd guns, and the six-legged mutt brawls in close. Levels hand the camera among those three instead of locking one hero for the whole campaign.

The release in 2000 landed on computers, Dreamcast, and PlayStation 2 before any Nintendo shelf. A later appearance did not rewrite Kurt, Hawkins, and Max or pretend the rotation started there.
driver-parallel-lines:
Reflections split a New York crime story between 1978 and a later decade, and Driver: Parallel Lines is that two-era driving tale. The skyline and the car radio are the clues that TK's revenge has jumped decades.

TK's undercover revenge changes the skyline, the cars, and the soundtrack when the story jumps forward. Missions still mix getaways with on-foot shooting, but the city itself is the clue that time has moved.

The original release is 2006, and a motion-console port followed. The Hudson-side missions and the era swap remain the reason to play, not a new borough invented for the remote.
bejeweled-2:
PopCap followed its breakthrough match-three with Bejeweled 2, adding puzzle boards and an endless mode on top of swapping gems. Puzzle mode asks for a specific pattern, while the endless board runs until no swap remains.

A pair of jewels trades places, and a line of three or more clears. Puzzle mode sets a target pattern, while the untimed cascade lets a board run until no move remains.

The 2004 sequel spread far beyond the first browser habit. Later living-room versions still turn on that same swap, not on a story campaign laid over the grid.
sengoku:
Three demon-fighting arcade brawlers share a box, and SENGOKU Anthology is SNK's collection of those Sengoku beat-em-ups. Transforming aids and demon warlords belong to those cabinet brawlers, not to a new living-room campaign.

Armor-clad heroes hack through ghosts and warlords across the trilogy's stages. The games began in cabinets, then reached computers and PlayStation 2, which is where this anthology lived.

The 2011 package is not a motion-console debut. Sword swings, transforming aids, and the occult feudal setting stay tied to those earlier releases.
disney-infinity:
Plastic figures unlock play sets, and Disney Infinity is Avalanche Software's toys-to-life sandbox built around that swap. The Toy Box ignores the play set's mission and lets a figure from another film knock the props around.

A character from one film can enter another's world once the base reads the figure. The Toy Box lets players scatter those licensed pieces into a homemade scene instead of following only the packaged mission.

The 2013 lineup included a motion-console build, a successor-console build, and a separate handheld game. That pocket version is not the home sandbox squeezed smaller; it is its own figure-driven product.
428-shibuya-scramble:
Live actors fill a branching sound novel, and 428: Shibuya Scramble is Chunsoft's scramble through that Tokyo crossing. A bad flag on one protagonist's hour can freeze a second character who has not even reached the crossing.

Several protagonists occupy the same hour, and a bad flag in one timeline jams another character's path. Photographs and phone calls replace a drawn sprite, so the crowd at the scramble intersection looks like a filmed street.

de-blob-2:
Paint returns to a gray city, and de Blob 2 is Blue Tongue's sequel about rolling color back across those streets. Mixing two absorbed hues on Blob's body paints a building a color neither paint alone would make.

Blob absorbs a hue, then slams it onto buildings, enemies, and the trail behind him. Comrade Black's forces drain the palette again, so each district is a race to repaint before the gray returns.

syberia:
Kate Walker leaves a law office for a clockwork journey east, and Syberia is Benoit Sokal's point-and-click about that train. Hans Voralberg's automatons will not move until Kate solves the mechanism in the station.

Automatons, a wounded heir named Hans Voralberg, and empty European stations fill the investigation. Puzzles sit in machinery rather than in combat, and the mammoth legend pulls the route toward Siberia.

The 2002 adventure later reached a handheld and, much later, the hybrid console. Both ports keep Kate's resignation from the firm as the emotional track under the puzzles.
grid:
Codemasters rebuilt its circuit line as GRID (2008), and the handheld release is a separate pocket racer rather than that console simulation. Sponsor goals and a wreck rewind belong to the big-circuit simulation, not to the pocket cart.

The big-machine version is remembered for professional teams, sponsor goals, and a flashback that rewinds a wreck. None of that cabinet-scale presentation is what the small dual-screen cart promises.

Damage, reputation, and a season of closed courses define the main line. Treating the handheld cartridge as the same garage would flatten a different product into the name.
plants-vs-zombies-goty-edition:
Extra modes sit on top of the lawn, and Plants vs. Zombies GOTY Edition is PopCap's expanded reissue of the defense comedy. Crazy Dave's shop still sells the cherry bomb between the extra modes and the music video.

Sunflowers still fund peashooters while waves shuffle toward the house. The reissue adds a music video and further ways to play beyond the original daytime rows.

The 2010 package keeps Crazy Dave's shop as the voice between levels. A handheld listing does not invent a new war; it points at this fuller carton of the same garden.
the-sims-3:
Whole neighborhoods opened at once, and The Sims 3 is EA's life sim that stopped locking a household inside a single lot. A wish can point a Sim toward a park two lots away without a loading break.

Create-a-Sim still sets traits, and then a person can walk to a neighbor's park without a loading curtain between addresses. Jobs, wishes, and chance meetings in town replace the older one-house view.

The 2009 computer game is the one with that open map. Handheld and glasses-free editions are smaller separate toys, not the neighborhood squeezed onto a dual screen.
plants-vs-zombies:
George Fan's lawn-defense comedy made PopCap a household name, and Plants vs. Zombies lines pea-shooters up against a shuffling horde. A walnut in front of a peashooter is the basic fort, and a pool lane later adds a lily pad under both.

Sun is the currency, dropped by flowers and collected before a cherry bomb or a walnut can be planted. Each row is a lane, and a breach in the last tile costs a life as the undead reach the door.

A handheld version later recreated those lanes in 2009's wake. Crazy Dave's advice and the escalating roof and pool stages remain the joke as much as the grid.
bejeweled-3:
Quest boards and new gem powers surround the classic grid, and Bejeweled 3 is PopCap's match-three follow-up best known on computers. A hypercube from a long chain can clear a color the ice layer was protecting.

Ice, gold, and timed challenges sit beside the familiar swap. A special jewel can clear a cross or a color once the chain that creates it is long enough.

sonic-sega-all-stars-racing:
Sumo Digital seated Sega characters in karts, and Sonic & SEGA All-Stars Racing gives each one a signature move on the motion console and the handheld. AiAi's all-star burst is a personal item, not a random crate dropped on the track.

Sonic, AiAi, and the rest bring courses that quote their own worlds. The all-star burst is a temporary power tied to the driver, closer to a kart item with a personality than to a plain speed pad.

The 2010 pair uses separate versions rather than one build scaled twice. Drifting into a boost still decides whether a quoted Green Hill curve is won or wall-hugged.
mx-vs-atv-reflex:
Leaning the rider shifts the bike's weight, and MX vs. ATV Reflex is Rainbow Studios' off-road racer built around that body English. Preloading the landing keeps a quad straight only if the rider leans before the wheels touch.

Bikes and quads share tracks where a preloaded landing matters as much as the throttle. The reflex in the name is the rider moving opposite the machine to keep a jump straight.

dirt-2:
Festival weekends replace a lone rally season, and Colin McRae: DiRT 2 is Codemasters' off-road event with reduced living-room and handheld editions. Loose gravel still slides the car even in the smaller editions that lack the full damage model.

The high-definition game piles trucks, rallycross, and guest drivers into a touring series. Those Nintendo versions are not that full simulation; they are smaller takes on the same dusty brand.

The 2009 split matters when someone expects the big damage model on a remote. What remains is still a course of loose surfaces rather than a closed asphalt grand prix.
star-wars-the-force-unleashed:
A secret apprentice hunts between the film trilogies, and Star Wars: The Force Unleashed follows that assassin under Darth Vader's orders. A Force grip can yank a trooper off a walkway the lightsaber has not reached yet.

LucasArts built the high-definition story around Force grips that yank scenery and foes into the air. The motion-console and handheld versions were made apart from those discs, with their own stages for the same hidden student.

The 2008 premise still turns on Starkiller's place between Jedi and Sith. Proxy's training duels and the imperial targets differ by edition, but Vader remains the master who can end the lesson.
agatha-christie-the-abc-murders:
Poirot follows an alphabetical killer, and Agatha Christie - The ABC Murders is Artefacts Studio's point-and-click of that novel. The railway timetable and the ABC guide keep reappearing as the initials advance through the towns.

Clues, interviews, and the little grey cells structure the case as the letters predict each town. This telling is a different game from the earlier handheld title that used the same book.

The 2016 adventure keeps the railway timetable and the ABC guide as recurring objects. Catching the pattern in the initials matters more than a chase scene between the interrogations.
nfs-prostreet:
Sanctioned race days replaced open-road police, and Need for Speed: ProStreet is EA Black Box's turn toward organized events. A drift meet scores angle and speed, while a grip race only cares about the clean lap.

Grip, drift, speed, and drag each score a meet in their own way. The wanted-level chase that defined earlier entries is gone, so a clean lap is the prize instead of a smashed roadblock.

Living-room and handheld versions arrived with the 2007 shift. Both still stage closed courses and festival branding rather than a citywide pursuit.
transformers-wfc:
Cybertron is the battlefield, and Transformers: War for Cybertron is High Moon Studios' shooter set on the robots' home world before they ever reached Earth. Megatron's chapter of the civil war is playable, not only a briefing before Optimus takes the gun.

Autobots and Decepticons each play chapters of the civil war, with Optimus and Megatron both taking a campaign. Guns and transformation share a corridor fight that reviewers treated as more than a disposable license.

The 2010 praise attached to that home-world campaign. Motion-console and handheld releases are separate games, not the same corridor shrunk onto a remote.
lego-indiana-jones-2:
Crystal Skull joins rebuilt scenes from the earlier films, and LEGO Indiana Jones 2: The Adventure Continues is TT Games' brick sequel covering that spread. The campus and the jungle from the fourth film sit beside a restaged ark chase built from studs.

Studs, smashable props, and character-specific tools still open the tombs. The fourth movie's jungle and campus sit beside restaged moments from the ark, the temple, and the grail.

Living-room and handheld versions shipped in 2009 with those plastic set pieces. A level built from bricks can joke about a death trap that the live-action frame played straight.
pokemon-heartgold:
A chosen partner walks behind the trainer, and Pokemon HeartGold is Game Freak's remake of Gold in which Johto leads on into Kanto. The Pokewalker counts real steps so the follower can gain experience away from the dual screen.

might-and-magic-clash-of-heroes:
Colored troops match in rows before they charge, and Might and Magic Clash of Heroes is Capybara Games' puzzle debut on the handheld. A wall unit stops the enemy column, which is as important as matching three swordsmen of the same hue.

Units of the same hue stack until the column is ready to attack, and walls or spells interrupt the other side's build. The fantasy map between battles gives the matching a campaign instead of an endless score.

steamworld-heist:
Ricochet shots are the main trick, and SteamWorld Heist is Image and Form's turn-based crew shooter built around bouncing bullets. Piper's crew spends the haul on a gun that banks more sharply off scrap metal.

Piper Faraday aims a laser so a slug can bank off scrap and hit a bot behind cover. Between heists the steam-powered crew upgrades guns and recruits on a ship that hops to the next derelict.

ducktales-remastered:
Scrooge's pogo cane returns with new paint, and DuckTales: Remastered is WayForward's rebuild of Capcom's old hop across the moon, the Amazon, and the Himalayas. A clean pogo onto a narrow ledge is still how Scrooge opens the chest in the Himalayas.

The cane-jump still bounces on spikes and foes, then opens a treasure chest when the landing is clean. Huey, Dewey, and Louie wait at the margins while Flintheart Glomgold schemes over the same five destinations.

octodad-dadliest-catch:
Ordinary chores become a physics farce, and Octodad: Dadliest Catch is Young Horses' game about puppeteering an octopus through them. Pouring coffee means steering one tentacle while the others keep the suit looking married.

Each limb is steered separately, so pouring coffee or climbing a staircase is a wrestling match with tentacles. The family must not notice, which turns a grocery aisle into stealth comedy.

A successor-console port followed the computer release in 2014, wedding suit included. The supermarket scramble remains the showpiece of that disguise.
qube-directors-cut:
Colored cubes extrude, vanish, or become springs, and Q.U.B.E: Director's Cut is Toxic Games' longer first-person puzzle set. Yellow cubes spring, blue cubes vanish, and red cubes slide, which is the whole vocabulary.

The original room-to-room toy grows a narrative layer in this cut, with a voice guiding the gloves that paint each block's behavior. Red, blue, and yellow commands stay the vocabulary for crossing a white test chamber.

The expanded edition reached the successor console in 2014, with the same colored verbs. Solving still means assigning the right command to the right cube before the gap can be crossed.
shantae-and-the-pirates-curse:
Pirate gear replaces genie magic, and Shantae and the Pirate's Curse is WayForward's half-genie adventure about that swap. Risky Boots' pistol covers a gap the hair whip cannot, which is why the genie is borrowing pirate tools.

Risky Boots' items, a pistol and a hat among them, give the jumps and the attacks while Shantae's hair whip still handles close range. Islands hide dungeon routes back toward the curse that binds the two rivals.

teslagrad:
Magnetism is the only vocabulary inside a silent tower, and Teslagrad is Rain Games' wordless climb that uses blue and red poles. Blue gloves attract the iron block and red gloves throw it, with no caption naming either color.

The young wizard charges his gloves, then attracts or repels metal to cross gaps and stun iron foes. No dialogue explains a puzzle; the next room's magnets are the instruction.

back-to-bed:
A sleepwalker will march off an impossible path, and Back to Bed is Bedtime Digital's puzzle about placing objects in his way. An apple placed on the tile is the only reason the sleepwalker turns before the Escher stair ends.

Escher stairs bend the route, so a bridge that looks connected may drop him into a fish-filled void. An apple or a blocking piece has to sit where his fixed stride would otherwise leave the tile.

The 2014 release treats that nudge as the whole verb. There is no jump button for the dreamer; someone else has to furnish the detour.
ziggurat:
Floors reshuffle and wands replace guns, and Ziggurat is Milkstone Studios' first-person crawl through a wizard's randomized dungeon. Mana spent on the wrong wand leaves the wizard empty when the portal room's brute arrives.

Rooms deal a layout of cultists and beasts, then a portal drops to the next stratum. Mana feeds the spells, and finding a stronger wand matters as much as aiming the one already equipped.

bittrip-presents-runner2-future-legend-o:
Gaijin Games timed every fork to the soundtrack in BIT.TRIP Presents... Runner2: Future Legend of Rhythm Alien sends Commander Video down those branches. A missed kick ends the run before the alternate path can even appear.

Jumps, slides, and kicks have to land on the beat or the run ends. A signpost offers a split in the course, so the same song can hide a harder line of obstacles.

shovel-knight:
A shovel replaces the usual sword, and Shovel Knight is Yacht Club Games' Kickstarter homage that treats that tool as a primary weapon. The shovel drop bounces off a slime and up to a relic ledge a normal jump would miss.

The drop bounce stomps foes and springs the knight toward relics hidden in side rooms. Shield Knight and the Enchantress frame a campaign that looks like an old cartridge and plays like a modern treasure map.

The 2014 launch included the successor console, the glasses-free handheld, and computers. Order of no-quarter rivals each guard a stage with a relic worth backtracking for.
the-cave:
Seven wanderers share one cavern, and The Cave is Ron Gilbert's Double Fine adventure about choosing which trio goes inside. A knight and a time traveler can hold two switches the adventurer's solo route would leave unpressed.

A knight, a time traveler, an adventurer, and the others each carry a sin the caves will stage. Puzzles often need two of the three bodies, so a ladder and a switch are rarely solved by one pair of hands.

The 2013 release included the successor console. The narrator is the cavern itself, commenting as the chosen three uncover what they came to steal or confess.
unepic:
A pizza-delivery worker is trapped in a castle, and Unepic is the computer parody that later reached the successor console's shop. The guidebook mocks the pizza guy while a torch-lit boss door still demands a real stat check.

Stats, loot, and a mocking guidebook dress a side-view search in role-playing furniture. The joke depends on knowing torch-lit corridors and boss doors, then stuffing them with an ordinary guy who only wanted to finish a route.

The 2011 original spread by port after players found that contrast. Weapon durability and snarky item text keep the castle from playing as a straight dungeon crawl.
lego-movie-videogame:
Emmet's construction fantasy is retold in bricks, and The LEGO Movie - Videogame is TT Games' tie-in released with the film. Emmet's instructions fall apart so Wildstyle can rebuild the double-decker couch as a weapon.

Instructions versus free building is the movie's argument, and the stages let that conflict smash apart. Wildstyle, Batman, and the other master builders join the hard-hat hero across sets that quote the picture.

Successor-console and glasses-free versions arrived in 2014 with the film's sets. Studs and character tools still open the next gag, including the western town.
lego-star-wars-tfa:
Scenes that the film only implies get their own brick levels, and LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens is TT Games' version of the seventh movie. A scene the film skips, such as a gap between Jakku and the Resistance base, becomes its own stud-filled level.

Rey, Finn, and Poe still hit the familiar beats, then extra chapters fill the gaps between them. Studs, disguises, and multi-character switches keep the usual plastic toolkit on Starkiller and Jakku.

Successor-console and glasses-free editions shipped in 2016 alongside the film's brick gaps. A joke built from a missing scene can last longer than the shot it expands.
road-redemption:
Motorcycle weapons in the spirit of Road Rash define Road Redemption, which first appeared through computer early access rather than on a successor console. A pipe swung from the motorcycle is the weapon, and the next bike is stolen after the crash.

Riders swing pipes and chains while the pack fights for position on a highway. A crash throws the body forward, and the next bike has to be taken before the race leaves.

The 2014 early sessions built that melee on a desktop, with procedural roads and a campaign of gangs. A living-room listing does not change where those first brutal laps were played.
lone-survivor-the-directors-cut:
Jasper Byrne expanded a sparse apartment horror, and Lone Survivor: The Director's Cut is the larger edition of his two-dimensional survival story. The radio in the apartment is as important as the pistol, because a neighbor's voice changes the ending's tone.

Pills, canned food, and a radio are the scarce tools while something stalks the hall. Choosing whether to talk to a neighbor or barricade the door changes the tone as much as any weapon.

The game's larger cut is tied to 2012, and a successor-console port followed. The thin pixel figure and the heavy footsteps in the corridor remain the scare.
lego-marvels-avengers:
The first two Avengers films get the brick treatment, and LEGO Marvel's Avengers is TT Games' retelling of those battles. Sokovia's city in the sky is a brick set piece, and Hulk is the character who smashes the gold locks under it.

New York's invasion and the later Sokovia crisis supply the big set pieces, with extra scenes between them. Hulk, Iron Man, and the rest swap in when a gold object needs a particular power.

Successor-console and glasses-free versions shipped in 2016 with both invasion set pieces. Cameo hunts and the talking bricks keep the tone lighter than the live-action rubble.
edge:
A cube rolls from tile to tile, and Edge grew out of an earlier mobile challenge before later living-room and handheld versions carried it. Clinging to a side face lets the cube pass a gap that rolling on the top would fall through.

Balancing on an edge, clinging to a side, and dropping onto a switch are the moves. A fast clear is part of the scoring, so the same small course invites a quicker line.

The 2011 form of that rolling test spread beyond the phone. Prism-colored blocks and a minimal soundtrack keep the focus on the next ledge rather than on a story cutscene.
lego-jurassic-world:
Four films of dinosaurs become studs and jokes, and LEGO Jurassic World is TT Games' retelling from the first park through the later island. A raptor can open a vent a scientist cannot, which is why the visitor-center escape changes bodies.

Raptors, a breakout tyrannosaur, and character abilities open gates that a human figure cannot. The visitor center, the aviary, and the later theme park each get smashable versions of their movie disasters.

Successor-console and glasses-free editions arrived in 2015 covering the four parks. Playing as a dinosaur, not only as a scientist, is the twist this license gets.
forced:
Spirit orbs rewrite a fighter's kit mid-trial, and FORCED is BetaDwarf's co-op arena game about surviving those tests. Ignoring a spirit orb leaves the squad with the basic strike the trial was designed to outgrow.

Gladiators stand together while the orbs offer a temporary rule change, such as a new strike or a shield. The arena itself is the dungeon: waves, hazards, and a goal that fails the whole squad if one person ignores the orb.

The 2013 battles reward planning the next pickup instead of only mashing a basic combo. Leaving a spirit unused is often worse than taking the wrong one, because the trial was built around that rewrite.
human-resource-machine:
Inbox tiles become outbox tiles by a program the player writes, and Human Resource Machine is Tomorrow Corporation's visual coding set in a dreary office. A jump command that skips the zero in the inbox is the optimization the manager grades after the first working program.

Commands such as copy, jump, and add are the only staff the employee may follow. Each floor's manager demands a new transformation of the numbers, and a sloppy solution can be optimized once it works.

The 2015 launch put that office on the successor console beside the computer version. The joke is the fluorescent misery, while the pleasure is a shorter routine that still satisfies the boss.
axiom-verge:
Glitches are weapons, and Axiom Verge is the Metroidvania Tom Happ built alone around a scientist who can corrupt the world. Trace's glitch gun can turn a turret into a platform, which is a key as much as a weapon.

Trace fires ordinary guns, then a glitch gun that rewrites an enemy or a block into something else. Sudra's ruined labs hide upgrades behind those corruptions, so a wall may be a door only after it is deliberately broken.

A successor-console version followed the computer and PlayStation 4 releases in 2015, glitch gun included. Backtracking still depends on a new tool, except here that tool might be a useful bug.
pinball-arcade:
Real Williams and Bally machines were licensed into a cabinet, and Pinball Arcade is FarSight Studios' collection of those tables. The callouts and the ramp rules follow the Williams machine, not a fictional table drawn for the console.

Rules, ramps, and callouts follow the physical games rather than a fictional board drawn for a console. A season pass of additional tables grew around classics the publisher could clear.

The 2012 lineup included a successor-console version. Nudging and flipper timing remain the skill, because the dot-matrix goals still match the machines collectors already knew.
blackgate-deluxe-ed:
A handheld search of the prison moved to the television, and Batman: Arkham Origins Blackgate - Deluxe Edition is Armature's home version with extra maps. Black Mask holds one wing of the jail, so Catwoman's keys do not open every tier on the first visit.

Catwoman, Bronze Tiger, and Black Mask divide the blocks of Blackgate after the Origins story. Metroidvania keys open wings of the jail that a straight brawler would have treated as a corridor.

The 2014 deluxe cut adds maps the first handheld release lacked. Detective vision and gadget gates still structure how Bruce returns to a locked tier.
minecraft-story-mode-complete:
Choices replace digging as the main verb, and Minecraft: Story Mode is Telltale's episodic take on that world. Jesse's dialogue pick can spare a friend the Wither Storm sequence would otherwise write off.

Jesse and the friends vote, argue, and live with a dialogue pick while the Wither Storm threatens the Order of the Stone's legend. Quick-time swings still happen, but a conversation can matter more than the sword.

A successor-console release carried that season in 2015, choices included. Blocks and creepers are set dressing for a story steered one line at a time.
the-fall:
A combat suit's artificial intelligence wakes with one order, and The Fall is Over the Moon Games' adventure about that program hunting medical help for its pilot. ARID looks for a medical bay while the facility's rule against harming humans blocks the obvious door.

ARID may not harm humans, yet the facility's rules keep forcing a loophole. Side-view rooms mix shooting with conversations that the suit is barely allowed to have.

The 2014 story was ported to the successor console. The tension sits in the restrictions written into ARID, not in a large arsenal.
olliolli:
Landings are the trick, and OlliOlli is Roll7's skateboard game about flicking the stick at the exact moment the wheels meet the ground. A grind that looks clean still scores nothing if the landing flick is a frame late.

Manuals, grinds, and spins chain only if that landing input is clean. A sloppy touch wastes the score even when the aerial looked right.

Born on PlayStation Vita, the 2014 game later reached the successor console and the glasses-free handheld. Each short lane is a chart of bumps that has to be memorized like a rhythm line.
tumblestone:
Matching runs are pulled out of columns, and Tumblestone is the versus puzzle that clears a stack by yanking one color in a connected line. Gravity after a pull can line up a color the player did not mean to free.

Gravity drops the remainder, which can complete or ruin the next pull. Opponents race the same idea on adjacent boards, so a slow read of the column loses the round.

The 2016 launch included a successor-console version. Spells that rotate or freeze a stack sit on top of that simple yank, without turning the match into a story campaign.
mighty-no-9:
Beck absorbs a boss's power after the fight, and Mighty No. 9 is Keiji Inafune's Kickstarter project with Inti Creates, widely received as a troubled successor to Mega Man. Dashing through a stunned robot absorbs its weapon, which is Beck's answer to a weakness chain.

Dashing through a weakened robot finishes it and grants a new weapon. The stages promise that old weakness-chain structure, and the troubled production became part of the game's reputation.

The 2016 release did reach the successor console and the glasses-free handheld. Players judging the dash-absorb loop were also judging the long, public road that led to those stages.
toki-tori-2:
Two Tribes refused text tutorials, and Toki Tori 2+ makes each creature's effect something the player has to learn by trying it. A stomp that scares one creature may be the only way to lure a second creature onto a switch.

A whistle and a stomp are the bird's whole kit, and the forest answers differently depending on which animal hears them. A fruit may lure one species and scare another, with no pop-up naming the rule.

The successor console was a lead platform in 2013 for the tutorial-free forest. Later puzzles stack unspoken habits until one stomp rearranges half the clearing.
lovely-planet:
