Tiny stages and a single shot define the pace, and Lovely Planet is quicktequila's brightly colored first-person run. The single shot has to land before the pastel platform throws the player off the room.

Pastel geometry hides targets that must be hit in a tight rhythm before the platform throws the player off. There is little ammo management because the weapon fires one deliberate hit at a time.

The 2014 release favors memorizing a thirty-second room over exploring a large map. A successor-console version keeps that candy-colored speed.
rush:
Conveyors and warps route a cube toward colored exits, and RUSH is Two Tribes' puzzle about painting the right path. A warp tile dumps the cube to the wrong exit if the belt was painted the other color.

Switches change belts, and a wrong warp dumps the block back to the start of the room. The goal square has to match the cube's color, so two exits side by side can still be a trap.

A later successor-console version plays on the GamePad screen in 2010's design. Spinning the route in the hands makes the next belt easier to read than a distant television view.
shovel-knight-treasure-trove:
Later knight campaigns share a carton with the original shovel quest, and Shovel Knight: Treasure Trove is Yacht Club's bundle of those stories. Plague Knight's potions replace the shovel drop, so the same Order of No Quarter is fought with vials.

Plague Knight's potions, Specter Knight's scythe climbs, and King Knight's shoulder bash each replace the shovel drop. The 2014 game sits underneath those added campaigns on the successor console and the glasses-free handheld.

Treasure maps and the same Order rivals return, seen from the villain's side of the fight. Buying one knight no longer means missing the others' towns and final bosses.
slender-the-arrival:
A free prototype and an internet myth sit behind the commercial hunt, and Slender: The Arrival is Blue Isle's horror game about that tall figure. Static thickens on the flashlight beam as the tall figure takes another step closer to the page.

Pages or generators have to be collected while the static thickens and the pursuer steps closer. Flashlight batteries are the scarce resource, and looking at the figure too long ends the walk.

The 2013 release followed the short demo that had already spread the myth. A successor-console version keeps the same rule: finish the objective before the next appearance.
lego-city-undercover:
Chase McCain returns to a brick city undercover, and Lego City Undercover is TT Fusion's police comedy that began as a successor-console exclusive. A miner disguise opens a shaft Chase McCain cannot enter while he is still wearing the police uniform.

The GamePad acts as a scanner and a map while the television shows the open streets. Disguises, from miner to farmer, open districts that a uniformed cop cannot enter, and Rex Fury is the criminal the costumes are meant to reach.

The 2013 original used that second screen before ports years later. Vehicle chases and the radio gags make the city feel closer to a comedy cop show than to a stud-collecting movie tie-in.
sky-force-anniversary:
A rebuilt vertical shooter chases scores, and Sky Force Anniversary is Infinite Dreams' anniversary pass at its own shmup. A medal on a cleared stage demands a route that also rescued the stranded pilots.

Ships upgrade between runs, and medals on each stage demand a cleaner route through the bullets. The view looks down on formations that still punish a greedy grab for every pickup.

The 2015 edition also reached the successor console. Memorizing a pattern matters, yet the medal goals keep a cleared stage from feeling finished.
stick-it-to-the-man:
Ray slaps stickers onto other people's thoughts with a spaghetti arm in Stick it to The Man! Zoink's comedy uses that limb as both a climb and a way to rewrite a mind bubble.

The pink arm stretches to a thought, then a sticker changes what the person believes. Side-view rooms in a conspiracy open when the right idea has been pasted over the wrong one.

The 2013 release plays as a joke with adventure-game logic under the jumps. A successor-console version keeps the arm as the tool for both reaching a ledge and vandalizing a belief.
volgarr-the-viking:
Ghosts 'n Goblins is the model, and Volgarr the Viking is a harsh arcade climb where armor strips off in a single hit. Losing the armor leaves one hit before the screen restarts, which is the cabinet bargain the pits enforce.

Spears, jumps, and a careful approach to a pit matter more than a long health bar. Losing the armor leaves the viking one mistake from the start of the screen, which is the bargain the old cabinets offered.

The 2013 computer game later showed up on the successor console's shop. Checkpoints are scarce enough that a memorized pattern is the real reward.
140-itch:
Geometry pulses with the music, and 140 is Jeppe Carlsen's one-button test of jumping in time with that throb. A color shift marks the beat where the single button will clear the spike instead of landing in it.

A single input hops or flips the shape through spikes that appear on the beat. Color shifts signal a safe moment, so listening is as useful as watching the next platform.

The 2013 release stays abstract: no character name, no dialogue, just the square and the kick. A successor-console version preserves that tight sync between a hit and a hazard.
nihilumbra:
Paint changes how the ground behaves, and Nihilumbra is BeautiFun Games' puzzle-platformer about coloring a path out of the Void. Born's paint supply runs out, so an ice path cannot cover every tile the Void is chasing across.

One pigment makes ice, another makes a trampoline, and a third can stop a pursuer. Born flees that darkness by painting only a short stretch at a time, because the supply is limited.

The mobile original later reached the successor console in 2012, pigments included. Mixing the wrong color under a jump is enough to end Born's escape.
xeodrifter:
A drifter hops tiny planets to rebuild a damaged ship, and Xeodrifter is Renegade Kid's pocket search across those small maps. The phase shift walks through a wall the first landing's gun could only dent.

A gun upgrade and a phase shift open caves that the first landing could not reach. Each world is only a few screens wide, so the Metroid-style loop is compressed into a short session.

The 2014 release covered the glasses-free handheld and the successor console. Backtracking to a colored door with the new module is still the way off a rock.
earthlock:
A Norwegian studio's first project is a turn-based journey, and EARTHLOCK: Festival of Magic is Snowcastle Games' debut. A bonded stance changes which skill the next turn can spend, which is the party system the debut is built on.

Party members bond into stances that change which skills they bring to the next fight. The bright overworld and the festival of the title sit over a traditional battle screen rather than an action dodge.

The 2016 release introduces that cast without assuming an earlier chapter. A successor-console version carries the same stance system and the same first-game scope.
whispering-willows:
Elena can step out of her body, and Whispering Willows is the ghost-story search built around that separation. Elena's spirit passes a grate her body still has to walk around once she returns.

The spirit walks through barriers the living girl cannot, then returns before a danger in either state becomes fatal. A mansion's staff and family linger as ghosts with unfinished business tied to her father's disappearance.

The adventure reached the successor console in 2014, out-of-body search included. Reading a note as the spirit, then pulling a lever as the body, is how a room opens.
freedom-planet:
Speed and a dragon heroine invite classic comparisons, and Freedom Planet is GalaxyTrail's fast side-scroller led by Sash Lilac. Carol's motorcycle and Milla's float are different engines on the same slope Lilac just dashed.

Slopes, loops, and a fuel meter for special moves push the pace past a careful walk. Carol and Milla join as playable allies with their own movement, so a rerun can feel like a different engine.

A successor-console port followed the computer release in 2014, Lilac's war included. The fight over a power source gives the dashes a plot without slowing the next hill.
bayonetta-2:
Hair becomes a demon-summoning weapon, and Bayonetta 2 is PlatinumGames' spectacle fighter published by Nintendo. Witch Time opens only after a last-instant dodge, and the hair-woven attack spends that window.

The Umbra witch dodges at the last instant to trigger Witch Time, then a combo finishes in a torture attack woven from that hair. Angels and demons both crowd the fights, and Jeanne remains the rival who can match her.

The 2014 original on the successor console and the later hybrid-console version are the same game. Bayonetta 3 is a sequel, not a second name for this Inferno-bound rescue.
costume-quest-2:
Halloween costumes turn into battle forms again, and Costume Quest 2 is Double Fine's sequel about Wren, Reynold, and a dentist's time scheme. A cardboard robot becomes a giant only after the battle starts, not while Wren is still knocking on doors.

A cardboard robot or a wizard sheet still becomes a giant version of itself when a fight starts. Trick-or-treat logic remains, but the sequel adds a timeline meddled with by Dr. White's plan.

The 2014 release shipped on the successor console among other machines. Grubbins and the neighborhood crawl survive, now with a past and a future neighborhood to save.
shantae-riskys-revenge-directors-cut:
A DSiWare sequel was upgraded for the television, and Shantae: Risky's Revenge - Director's Cut is WayForward's home version of that half-genie chase. The elephant form breaks a floor the monkey form only climbs, so both dances have to be bought.

Magic transformations into a monkey, a harpy, and an elephant return as the dungeon keys. Risky Boots has stolen a magic seal, and Scuttle Town is again the hub that points toward the next form.

The 2014 director's cut includes a successor-console release with sharper art than the small shop original. Learning which animal fits which gap is still the map's real legend.
electronic-super-joy:
Electronic tracks score a brutal series of jumps, and Electronic Super Joy is the computer original later brought to the successor console. A sarcastic message between rooms does not add a checkpoint to the laser that follows.

Lasers, spikes, and a deliberately awkward slide punish a late button. The humor in the messages between stages does not soften the next screen, which often kills in a single touch.

The 2013 challenge treats memorization as the progression system. A living-room version keeps that same demand: dance to the drop, or restart the room.
super-mario-galaxy-2:
Super Mario Galaxy 2 returns to small planets and then hands Mario a dinosaur the first Galaxy did not have. A world map replaces the first journey's observatory, and Yoshi joins the gravity tricks.

Yoshiaki Koizumi directed it at Nintendo EAD Tokyo as a sequel with a world map, Bowser Jr. as a recurring chaser, and Yoshi, whose tongue and flutter jump change how round platforms work. The hub is a face-shaped starship rather than the first game's observatory and Rosalina story.

Green stars, found after the main path, send the player back through stages for one more comet. The drill, the rock, and the cloud flower are tools that exist for a handful of galaxies and then leave, which keeps the toy box rotating.

It is not a level pack inside the first Super Mario Galaxy. A later Wii U reminder of the Wii library is not assumed here. Lubba's starship and the green-star mop-up are the sequel's own frame, not a menu inside the first Galaxy.
nova-111:
Turns and real-time blasts share one grid, and Nova-111 is the hybrid where a step is a turn until a bomb is live. An armed blast resolves in real time even though the step that triggered it was a turn.

Moving, bumping an alien, and waiting all spend the timeline, but an explosion resolves in real time across the tiles. The scientist's crash site has to be escaped by using that mix rather than by aiming a free cursor.

Bombs that resolve in real time also reached the successor console in 2015 alongside the hybrid grid. A hasty step can walk into a blast that the previous turn armed.
ultratron:
Twin-stick waves homage a robot massacre, and Ultratron is Puppy Games' take on that arena, later brought to the successor console by Curve Digital. Helper drones picked up between waves cover the flank the lone robot cannot watch.

Helper drones, collected between stages, add fire the lone robot cannot produce alone. The field fills with hostile machines, and survival is a circle-strafe while the helpers cover a flank.

The computer original dates to 2005, long before the living-room port. The fantasy is still the last unit in a room of enemies, not an exploration map.
the-swindle:
Each burglary is laid out differently, and The Swindle is Size Five Games' steampunk heist about banking enough before a final score. A failed lockpick still burns one of the days before the final security system locks the city.

A limited run of days means a failed break-in still burns time the gang needed. Security gadgets, steam-powered upgrades, and procedural buildings keep the next roof from matching the last.

Procedural rooftops from the 2015 heist were also sold on the successor console. Spending loot on a better jump can matter more than finishing every safe in the current house.
pumped-bmx:
Timed flips on a side-view course define the run, and Pumped BMX + is that trick racer on the successor console's shop. The rotation has to meet the ramp lip, or the line resets before the next scoring gap.

A button held over a jump sets the rotation, and the landing has to meet the lip of the next ramp. Crashing resets the line, so a clean combo is a memorized sequence of tucks.

The 2015 lanes favor speed between tricks rather than an open park to wander. Scoring windows on specific gaps keep a fast finish from ignoring the stunts.
castlestorm:
Physics rocks meet castle defense, and CastleStorm is Zen Studios' mix of a ballista shot and a side-view siege. A ballista shot needs lead time because the boulder has weight, not a hitscan laser.

Walls are built from blocks, then a projectile with real arc smashes the enemy keep. Sending troops across the field joins the artillery, so a repaired gate and a well-aimed boulder share the same battle.

A successor-console version followed the 2013 release. The humor of the kingdoms does not remove the need to lead a shot as the target moves.
shutshimi:
Power-ups are absurd and expire quickly, and Shutshimi is a short horizontal shooter about a fish grabbing whatever the banner offers. The fish grabs a banner that expires in seconds, so a silly weapon is also a short one.

A few seconds of a ridiculous weapon replace a permanent loadout. The stage is brief on purpose, because the joke and the bullet pattern both reset before they wear out.

The 2015 shop release on the successor console leans on that temporary chaos. Choosing a bad banner is part of the comedy, then surviving it is the score.
chariot:
A royal coffin has to be hauled through treasure caves, and Chariot is the co-op climb built around that awkward cargo. Loot stuck to the royal coffin makes the haul richer and the rope swing harder to control.

Ropes, swings, and a second player keep the casket from tumbling into a spike pit. Loot stuck to the coffin changes how heavy and how valuable the trip becomes.

Ropes from the 2014 coffin climb also reached the successor console. Leaving the dead monarch behind to grab a gem, then coming back for the ropes, is the usual greed.
sonic-lost-world:
Parkour on floating continents replaces a pure sprint, and Sonic Lost World is Sonic Team's successor-console game about the Lost Hex. Running on the underside of a Lost Hex tube is the camera trick the Deadly Six stages keep repeating.

The Deadly Six have hijacked the animals, and Wisps still offer temporary powers. Curved tube stages let the hedgehog run on the underside of a world, which is the camera trick the ground levels keep using.

The 2013 handheld version uses its own stages rather than a shrunk copy of those tubes. Both tell the same kidnapping of the creature energy, with different geometry under the shoes.
year-walk:
Swedish year-walking folklore supplies the dread, and Year Walk is Simogo's horror about attempting that ritual. The huldra and the brook horse punish a walker who breaks the ritual's silence.

The phone original hid extra clues in a companion app, so a vision in the woods sometimes required a fact stored outside the story. Huldra, brook horses, and the church grim appear as the walker breaks the rules of the tradition.

A successor-console port in 2013 folded more of that guidance into the game itself. The ritual's direction and silence remain the point, not a combat system against the creatures.
frederic-resurrection-of-music:
A revived Chopin fights with piano battles, and Frederic: Resurrection of Music is Forever Entertainment's Polish rhythm game about that composer. Club arrangements replace a recital, but the hands on the keys are still Chopin's.

Notes scroll as modern tracks that the undead pianist has to answer. The joke is the formal portrait dropped into club music, with the hands still doing the work of a keyboard.

Chopin's club battles later sold on the successor console in 2012 with the portrait still on the keys. Clearing a song means hitting the arrangement, not exploring a Warsaw map between concerts.
citizens-of-earth:
Ordinary townspeople join the party, and Citizens of Earth is the turn-based joke about recruiting a barista, a farmer, and a conspiracy crank. A barista in the party is a combatant, which is the census joke under the turn order.

The player character is less a chosen warrior than a politician who sends constituents into battle. Each new neighbor brings a role, so the roster is a census instead of a band of knights.

That census of odd fighters reached both the successor console and the glasses-free handheld in 2015 with the barista still in the roster. Winning a fight still uses classic turns, but the victory screen looks like a neighborhood directory.
skyward-sword:
Motion swings cut through a sky of islands, and The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword opens on Skyloft above a surface unlocked one region at a time. Fi's dowsing pings when the surface region below Skyloft is the one the blade wants next.

Link's loftwing crosses the cloud barrier, and Fi guides the sword once the hero drops to the sealed ground. A remote slash has to match the angle of the blow, which makes a vertical cut and a horizontal cut different inputs.

Nintendo released that voyage in 2011 with the motion slash intact. The high-definition remake on the hybrid console is a separate product from this Skyloft departure.
starwhal:
Narwhals poke each other in space, and STARWHAL is the local multiplayer couch game about stabbing a heart with a tusk. The floppy neck makes the tusk miss the heart even when the narwhal is aimed at it.

Low gravity and a floppy neck make the horn hard to aim, which is the joke and the skill. Up to four players share one screen of stars with no story campaign required.

Couch matches of tusks and hearts also shipped on the successor console in 2014 with the floppy necks intact. A match ends when the right jab lands, not when a lap counter finishes.
fifa-13:
Launch-window football on the new living-room box was not the high-definition feature set, and FIFA 13 is EA Sports' edition that drew that line. The GamePad build keeps real kits while leaving the fuller broadcast presentation on the other consoles.

The big consoles carried the season's fuller presentation, while this build kept a slimmer match. Kits and clubs still come from the real league, so the roster is the part that matches the other versions.

The 2012 release sat in that console's early months. Expecting the complete broadcast package from the GamePad version means expecting a different product.
guitar-hero-live:
Live-action crowds replace cartoon venues, and Guitar Hero Live is FreeStyleGames' restart that throws out the old five-color notes. A missed chord draws boos from the filmed crowd instead of only breaking a combo meter.

A new guitar uses a two-row fret layout, and the highway shows the player's own hands on a real stage. The television mode that streamed extra songs sat beside the story set's fixed set list.

The 2015 package included a successor-console version. Missing a chord draws boos from the filmed audience, which is a different failure than a broken combo meter.
ittle-dew:
A short dungeon teases classic top-down quests, and Ittle Dew is Ludosity's Swedish homage led by Ittle and the fox Tippsie. Tippsie comments while Ittle's stick and fire wand open one compact castle, not a continent.

A stick, a fire wand, and a few tools gate the rooms of one compact castle. The jokes assume the player has seen old green-tunic adventures, then finishes the idea in an afternoon.

Ludosity's compact castle also opened on the successor console in 2013 with Tippsie still commenting. Backtracking for a switch is still there, just on a map small enough to finish between longer games.
knytt-underground:
Combat barely matters underground, and Knytt Underground is Nifflas' long wander through caverns joined by climbable slopes. Mi's ball form rolls through a pipe the climbing body can only hang beside.

Mi can shift into a ball to roll through tight gaps, then return to a climbing body for the walls. The quest to place orbs is an excuse to keep moving through hand-drawn dark.

The 2012 exploration reached the successor console's shop. Getting lost, then recognizing a landmark mushroom or a pipe, is the progression.
spy-chameleon:
Color is the hiding place, and Spy Chameleon - RGB Agent is the shop puzzle about matching a chameleon to the surface under him. A red floor is safe only while the agent is red, and a laser sees every other hue.

Lasers and guards see only the wrong hue, so a red tile is safe solely while the agent is red. Collecting the objectives means crossing a room that changes paint from tile to tile.

The 2014 successor-console release makes that swap the entire verb. There is no gun to clear a patrol; the patrol is avoided by becoming the floor.
shantae-half-genie-hero:
A Kickstarter brought the half-genie back in high definition, and Shantae: Half-Genie Hero is WayForward's return to transformation dances. The dance that buys a new form is performed in town before the dungeon gap will allow it.

Hair whips clear the foreground, then a dance turns Shantae into a form that can cross the next gap. Risky Boots and the baron's machines supply the bosses across stages that look like animated cartoons.

The successor console was one of the 2016 launch platforms. Buying the dances in town, then applying them in a dungeon, still structures the map.
ballpoint-universe-infinite:
Ink on paper is the entire look, and Ballpoint Universe - Infinite is the shooter drawn as if a pen had doodled the enemies. Crosshatched enemies still fire patterns that have to be dodged like any other shooter wave.

Scribbled ships and margin notes replace metallic sprites. The side-scrolling firefight still asks for dodges and weapon pickups, only the shading is ballpoint crosshatch.

The 2013 release received a successor-console version. A boss that looks like a notebook monster is still a pattern of shots to memorize.
puddle:
A bead of liquid has to be tilted through machinery, and Puddle is the physics puzzle about keeping that blob intact. A steep tilt splits the bead, and the lost half may be too small to finish the hot plate.

Water, then nastier fluids, smear across pipes, fans, and hot plates. Too steep an angle splits the drop, and a lost portion may be too small to finish the course.

The computer puzzle later reached the successor console's shop in 2012, hot plates included. Success is a controlled pour, not a character who can hop back to a missed ledge.
scribblenauts-unmasked-a-dc-comics-adven:
Typed words summon objects inside a superhero universe, and Scribblenauts Unmasked: A DC Comics Adventure is 5th Cell's crossover starring Maxwell. Maxwell can write Batman into a room and still solve the ledge with the word ladder.

Batman, the Justice League, and a villain of the week can be written into existence alongside a mundane ladder or a helicopter. Puzzles in Gotham and beyond still accept a surprising noun if the game's dictionary holds it.

Maxwell's notebook of DC names reached both the successor console and the glasses-free handheld in 2013 with Gotham still accepting a typed ladder. The notebook remains the real gadget, even when the guest star is Superman.
plantera:
Gentle plant-raising fills a small garden, and Plantera is the sim about tending sprouts on the glasses-free handheld and the successor console. A rare seed is the prize for getting light and water right, not a boss at the end of a path.

Water, light, and a little decoration decide whether a pot thrives. There is no invasion to repel; the session ends when the plants look after themselves.

The 2016 release keeps that calm scope. A rare seed is the prize, not a boss at the end of a dungeon.
space-hulk:
Terminators clear a derelict corridor, and Space Hulk is the video adaptation of Games Workshop's squad board game. Overwatch on a door spends action points a Terminator might have used to step into the genestealer's vent.

Genestealers pour from vents while action points limit how far a marine can move and fire. Overwatch at a door is often wiser than rushing the next tile of the ship.

A successor-console edition arrived in 2013 with the same tight corridors. Claustrophobia comes from the board's line of sight, translated into a passage with the same action-point budget.
gravity-badgers:
Flipping gravity launches a badger through caves, and Gravity Badgers is Wales Interactive's physics puzzle about that burrow. A second gravity flip too early slams the badger into the roof the cannon just left.

A shot from a cannon, then a mid-air reversal, threads spikes and switches. The goal pad only counts if enough of the team-colored animals arrive.

The 2013 shop release on the successor console treats each cave as a trick shot. A second flip too early slams the badger into the roof it just left.
wind-waker-hd:
The Swift Sail shortens the voyage, and The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD is Nintendo's sharper reissue of the same cartoon sea. The King of Red Lions holds a wind heading longer once the Swift Sail is fitted.

Toon Link still conducts the Wind Waker baton, and the King of Red Lions still carries him between islands. A pictograph, a treasure chart, and the Triforce hunt remain, only the boat can be told to hold a wind direction without as much tacking.

This reissue is the 2013 version. The 2002 disc original has its own place in the catalog, with the slower sail and the same Great Sea.
mutant-mudds-deluxe:
Extra levels join the mud-blasting hop, and Mutant Mudds Deluxe is Renegade Kid's expanded set of the handheld original. A background plane hides the real ledge while the foreground is only mud and spikes.

The water gun washes creatures and muddy barriers while the hero jumps between a foreground, a middle, and a background plane. A ledge that looks decorative on one layer is the real road on another.

The 2013 deluxe addition is what the successor-console release adds to the first cart. Pixel-perfect landings over spikes stay as stern as they were on the small screen.
mario-kart-8:
Mario Kart 8 bends tracks through anti-gravity so a course can drive on a wall and still be a race. Courses drive on walls and ceilings, and the hover chassis is what makes those surfaces legal.

Nintendo EAD made it for the Wii U, with hover-karts, a revised drift, and a roster that included the Koopalings as separate racers. Mercedes-Benz guest cars in a later update annoyed some players and delighted others; they are part of this version's history, not a rumor.

The track design is the reason it lasted: Mount Wario's downhill, Electrodrome's neon, and Rainbow Road's figure-eight. Twelve-player online races were the living-room version of a battle the local split screen could not hold.

Mario Kart 8 Deluxe on Switch reworks battle mode and adds a booster course pass. That edition has its own page. Anti-gravity, the Koopalings, and the Mercedes guest carts mark the Wii U release Deluxe later revised.
kung-fu-panda-showdown-of-legendary-lege:
DreamWorks animals brawl on floating stages, and Kung Fu Panda: Showdown of Legendary Legends is the platform fighter built around Po and the Furious Five. Tigress can ring out Po even when the panda is winning the damage on that floating stage.

Ring-outs replace a health-only duel, so a slam off the platform ends a stock. Tigress, Shifu, and the film villains join the panda on those small arenas.

Successor-console and glasses-free versions arrived in 2015 with the floating stages. A special move can ring out a heavier fighter who was winning the damage race.
donkey-kong-country-tropical-freeze:
Snowmads freeze the islands, and Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze is Retro Studios' sequel after Returns, with Dixie Kong as a partner. Dixie's hover ponytail crosses a sawmill gap Diddy would need a barrel to clear.

Her hover ponytail and pop-gun ride change the jumps Diddy and Cranky also approach in their own ways. Cold stages, from a sawmill to a juice mill, replace the volcano mood of the previous cart.

The 2014 original and the later hybrid-console port are the same adventure. Funky's flyers still sell extra hearts, and the fruit goals still hide off the main vine.
dungeons-dragons-chronicles-of-mystara:
Two arcade beat-em-ups share a collection, and Dungeons & Dragons: Chronicles of Mystara is Capcom's bundle of Tower of Doom and Shadow over Mystara. The thief joins in Shadow over Mystara, a class Tower of Doom never put on the cabinet.

Fighters, clerics, elves, and dwarves hack through the same tabletop setting with cooperative joins. The second cabinet adds branching paths and a thief that the first tower did not field.

The 2013 package reached the successor console with both quests intact. Online or couch partners can still pile onto a red dragon the way the cabinets allowed.
quest-of-dungeons:
Small generated floors and a compact party define the crawl, and Quest of Dungeons is the roguelike that ships those short delves. A potion in the pack matters because the next generated stairs will not revive a dead knight.

A knight, a wizard, or another class starts with almost nothing, and the next stairs reshuffle the rooms. Permadeath makes a potion in the pack more important than a long scripted conversation.

Generated stairs and a short party reached both the successor console and the glasses-free handheld in 2014 with permadeath still on the stairs. A run can end in one sitting, which is the scale the generator was built for.
shiftlings:
Two aliens share one body, and Shiftlings is the co-op game about stretching that body across a puzzle. The torso between the two alien heads snaps off a switch if either player lets go.

Each player owns a head, and the space between them is a torso that has to stay intact. Buttons, crates, and hazards sit far enough apart that the pair must agree how far to pull.

The 2015 shop release on the successor console is built for that argument on the couch. Letting go at the wrong time snaps the shared body off the switch it was holding.
girls-like-robots:
Seating charts are the puzzle, and Girls Like Robots is the logic toy Adult Swim Games published about who may sit together. A human who cannot sit beside a robot has to be moved, not deleted, before the chart scores.

Humans, robots, and the relationships between them score the grid. A forbidden neighbor has to be moved, not destroyed, so the solution is a rearrangement.

The 2012 computer puzzle later reached the successor console. Later tables add rules about pairs that want to be adjacent, which fights the rules about pairs that must not touch.
tekken-tag-tournament-2:
Tag teams and a huge roster define the cabinet, and Tekken Tag Tournament 2 is Namco's fighter that lets one partner save another. A tag in the middle of a juggle lets the resting fighter continue the combo and recover a sliver of life.

A tag in the middle of a combo continues the juggle, and the resting fighter recovers a sliver of life. Bound and tag crashes give the pair tools a solo duel in earlier Tekken games did not center.

The 2012 successor-console version added modes the arcade release lacked. The fight system and the character list remain the reason to pick a duo.
mario-kart-ds:
Mission tasks and a wireless lobby share a handheld, and Mario Kart DS is Nintendo's kart racer that uses both screens for the race and the map. The bottom screen holds the map while a mission on Tick-Tock Clock asks for a specific character's errand.

Boss cars, coin collects, and character-specific errands fill the mission booklet between grand prix cups. Online play arrived on this pocket machine, sitting in the series after Super Circuit and before Mario Kart 7.

The 2005 cartridge also later appeared on the successor console's virtual shelf. Snaking a mini-turbo through a drift still decides a tight course such as Tick-Tock Clock.
new-super-mario-bros:
A wall jump and a Mega Mushroom mark the return of side-scrolling Mario, and New Super Mario Bros. puts those moves on two screens. The Mega Mushroom smashes a brick house the fire flower would only scorch.

The top screen is the course and the bottom screen tracks stored items and the progress map. Blue shells, tiny doors, and the giant mushroom that smashes brick houses sit beside the classic fire flower.

Nintendo's 2006 handheld restart led to later home versions and a Deluxe follow-up. Those sequels are separate games; this cartridge is the one that brought the side view back.
jones-on-fire:
A firefighter outruns the blaze he is standing in, and Jones On Fire is the short runner about staying ahead of that heat. Stopping for a trapped civilian can let the blaze catch the lane Jones had already cleared.

Jumps across rooftops have to keep moving because the fire fills the space just left. A stumble is a restart of the short lane rather than a health bar to manage.

The 2015 shop release on the successor console keeps the run brief. Collecting a trapped civilian is the detour that can cost the lead on the flames.
the-book-of-unwritten-tales-2:
A comedy point-and-click returns with a larger cast, and The Book of Unwritten Tales 2 is KING Art's sequel to that fantasy adventure. Nate's inventory gag still has to satisfy a wizard who talks as if the novel belongs to him.

Wilbur, Ivo, and Nate still solve inventory gags while the mage's novel threatens to rewrite them. The tone stays theatrical, with a critter companion who comments on the puzzles.

A successor-console port followed the computer release in 2015, comedy puzzles included. Combining a ridiculous object with a self-important wizard is still how a scene unsticks.
draculas-legacy:
Hidden objects fill a vampire story, and Dracula's Legacy is Jetdogs Studios' search built on that theme. A candle that changes the clutter reveals an object the first glance at the gothic room hid.

Scenes hide keys, letters, and ritual pieces inside cluttered gothic rooms. Finding the list of items advances the count's plot more than a combat system would.

The computer original gained a successor-console shop port in 2015, gothic rooms included. A scene that changes when a candle is lit is the variation those hidden-object hunts use.
phantom-hourglass:
Touch-screen sailing and a temple on a timer follow the cartoon sea, and The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass is Nintendo's sequel after The Wind Waker. Linebeck's steamboat follows the stylus route, and the hourglass keeps running inside the Ocean King's temple.

Link draws routes on the dual screen for the steamboat of Linebeck, who grumbles across the voyage to rescue Tetra. The Temple of the Ocean King must be replayed as the hourglass sand runs, and a new sea chart shortens the next descent.

The 2007 handheld adventure is this journey, not the earlier disc. Bosses drawn with the stylus, including a path the player sketches, use the same touch idea as the sail.
angry-video-game-nerd-adventures:
The web-series host becomes the avatar of a deliberately harsh throwback, and Angry Video Game Nerd Adventures puts that nerd through cheap deaths. A fake block over a pit is the kind of death the nerd would pause the review to yell about.

Pit spikes, fake blocks, and a limited continue supply mock the cartridges he reviews. A beer-powered shot and a sidekick pickup are the tools, and they do not stop the next gag death.

Cheap deaths and the nerd's continue count reached both the successor console and the glasses-free handheld in 2013 with the beer shot still equipped. Surviving a stage means recognizing a cruel pattern the show would have yelled about.
super-mario-3d-world:
A cat suit and clear courses set a pace closer to side-scrolling Mario than to a sandbox, and Super Mario 3D World is Nintendo's four-player run of those boards. The Super Bell's climb lets a cat Mario scratch up a wall a normal jump in the Sprixie kingdom cannot reach.

Mario, Luigi, Peach, and Toad each move differently, and the Super Bell turns a hero into a climber who scratches up walls. Captain Toad's no-jump dioramas hide between the longer stages.

The 2013 original and the later hybrid-console edition share this adventure. That later edition adds Bowser's Fury as an extra story rather than replacing the Sprixie kingdoms.
woah-dave:
One screen holds the whole scuffle in Woah Dave! Choice Provisions built that small multiplayer throwback around a pit that fills with aliens.

Objects the creatures leave can be thrown before the floor is lost. Rounds are short enough for a couch rematch, which is the design rather than a long campaign map.

The one-screen pit of aliens reached both the successor console and the glasses-free handheld in 2014 with the egg still deadly if dropped. A single missed catch turns a useful egg into the thing that ends the life.
master-reboot:
Memories are stored in a machine, and Master Reboot is Wales Interactive's first-person horror about walking through that archive. A childhood room inside the Soul Cloud repeats with corruption, which is how a damaged memory looks.

The Soul Cloud holds the dead's recorded lives, and something in the system is wrong enough to hunt the visitor. Rooms shift from a childhood scene into a corrupted repeat, which is how the facility shows a damaged file.

Walking the Soul Cloud also shipped on the successor console in 2013 with the corrupted childhood room intact. Progress means opening the next memory, not winning a gunfight against the corruption.
forma8:
A small probe crosses an alien surface with no dialogue, and forma.8 is that quiet exploration. The probe's drill opens a cave the boost alone cannot enter before the charge runs out.

The craft boosts, drills, and scans ruins while the planet stays unexplained by text. Energy for the tools is the limit, so a deep cave has to be left before the charge fails.

The 2017 release was brought to the successor console. Landmarks of crystal and wreckage replace a quest log.
ninja-pizza-girl:
Schoolyard cruelty shares the route with a delivery timer, and Ninja Pizza Girl is the Australian momentum game about a courier who is also a target. Bullies on the pavement break the wall-run that was keeping the delivery inside the timer.

Speed along walls and rails keeps the pizza intact, while bullies on the pavement try to break that flow. The story treats the harassment as part of the level, not as a separate lecture menu.

The 2015 successor-console release keeps the sprint as the answer. Slowing down to fight every taunt can ruin the delivery the stage is scored on.
bridge-constructor-playground:
Homemade spans get stress-tested by vehicles, and Bridge Constructor Playground is the sandbox from the bridge-building series. A truck sent across a pretty truss is the test, and a buckle means the anchors failed.

Girders, cables, and anchors have to hold a rolling load the player sends across. A pretty truss that buckles under the truck is a failed experiment, which is the feedback.

The 2012 workshop includes a successor-console version. There is no campaign medal required before a wilder span can be attempted.
armikrog:
Clay animation returns with the Neverhood team, and Armikrog is their Kickstarted point-and-click about Tommynaut and Beak-Beak. Beak-Beak sniffs a clay lump Tommynaut's hands treat as decoration.

Stop-motion rooms hide levers inside sculpted walls. The blind dog companion sniffs out clues the astronaut's hands cannot reach, and the tone stays as strange as that earlier clay world.

Tommynaut's clay rooms later sold on the successor console in 2015 with Beak-Beak still sniffing. Solving means noticing a lump in the clay that a painted scene would have drawn as a clean button.
spirit-tracks:
A train replaces the boat, and The Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks makes Zelda a spirit partner rather than a distant goal. Zelda's phantom armor swings beside Link, so the spirit princess is in the dungeon rather than waiting at the end.

She possesses a phantom suit of armor inside dungeons while Link fights beside her, and the rails between realms have to be restored before the locomotive can pass. This is the second handheld adventure in the cartoon sea's art, and a different voyage from Phantom Hourglass.

Nintendo released the cartridge in 2009 with the spirit princess in the party. Drawing a route on the touch screen drives the train, and a flute duet opens several gates.
letter-quest-remastered-2:
Spelling is the attack, and Letter Quest: Remastered is Bacon Bandit Games' word battle against a queue of monsters. A rare letter on the grid can finish a monster a three-tile word would only scratch.

Tiles on a grid form a word, and the letters' value becomes the damage. A longer word or a rare letter can finish a creature that a three-letter poke would only scratch.

The remaster reached the successor console in 2016, spelling attacks included. Buying a vowel between fights is as tactical as choosing a weapon in a more ordinary dungeon.
captain-toad-treasure-tracker:
Rotating a small diorama leads Toad to a star he cannot jump for, and Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker is Nintendo's puzzle spun out of those no-jump boards. Turning the diorama shows a coin the front camera hides behind a brick.

The courses began as asides inside Super Mario 3D World, then became their own set of gardens, mine carts, and ghost houses. A turn of the camera reveals a coin the front view hides.

The original successor-console release, the glasses-free version, and the later hybrid-console port share that walk. Picking up the star ends the diorama, because there is no flagpole sprint.
1001-spikes:
Spikes, darts, and falling blocks fill a cruel temple, and 1001 Spikes is the arcade challenge Nicalis published on two Nintendo machines. An idol off the main drop is optional only until the player learns the fatal tiles beside it.

Lives drain in seconds until a pattern is memorized. The explorer's descent after a lost expedition is the frame, but the play is the next trap two tiles ahead.

Memorized spike rooms reached both the successor console and the glasses-free handheld in 2014 with the idol still off the fatal path. A hidden idol off the fatal path is the reward for a route that looked optional.
the-deer-god:
Reincarnation as a deer is the sentence, and The Deer God is the pixel side-scroller about living that animal life. Eating the wrong animal changes the deer's karma and the body the next stretch will wear.

Karma from what the deer eats and whom it helps changes the body and the ending. Predators, hunters, and a spirit trial replace a gun-toting avatar.

The pixel deer and its karma also reached the successor console in 2015 with the karma body still changing. A wrong kill can cost the progress the antlers were starting to show.
injustice-gods-among-us:
A regime of superheroes is the story, and Injustice: Gods Among Us is NetherRealm's one-on-one fighter about that split in the DC universe. A clash triggers when both fighters spend a super, and Superman's regime is the story that set the teams.

Superman's authoritarian side faces Batman's resistance, and interactive stages let a fighter be smashed through a wall into a second arena. Meter spends become clashes when both players trigger a super at once.

The 2013 successor-console version carries those same duels. A character's trait, such as a gadget or a power, still decides the matchup more than the living-room controller does.
severed:
Touch swipes sever limbs, and Severed is Drinkbox Studios' first-person slash about a girl reclaiming her family. Sasha's rhythm of swipes removes an arm that becomes the resource for the next painted room.

Sasha fights monsters that fill the screen's edge, and a successful rhythm of cuts removes an arm that becomes a resource. The painted world and the missing relatives keep the tone closer to a dark fable than to a gun range.

The 2016 release covers the successor console and the glasses-free handheld, both suited to a finger. Guarding at the right moment is what allows the next sever to land.
tengami:
Pop-up paper is the world, and Tengami is Nyamyam's puzzle adventure styled as a book that folds into rooms. A paper tab pulled upright reveals a path that was a flat illustration a moment earlier.

Tabs pull a scene upright, revealing a path that was flat a moment earlier. Japanese folklore imagery fills the paper, and the pace stays quiet enough to watch the fold finish.

The 2014 shop release on the successor console uses that mechanism as the main verb. Turning a page is closer to solving than to reading.
tetrobot-and-co:
Blocks shove other blocks into sockets, and Tetrobot and Co. is Swing Swing Submarine's puzzle about robots built from those shapes. One tetromino body cannot fill the socket, so a second robot has to be slid in beside it.

A tetromino-like body has to be slid until its silhouette matches the hole. Extra bots on the team can be moved as separate pieces when one shape cannot cover the gap.

The 2013 puzzle was ported to the successor console after its other digital releases. A wrong push can pin a robot against a wall it cannot climb.
world-of-keflings-a:
A giant hand helps tiny villagers, and A World of Keflings is NinjaBee's toy-like god game about building their town. A beam lifted by the giant hand is how a Kefling house gets its roof.

The player picks up a Kefling, a tree, or a beam and sets it where the blueprint asks. There is no army to command; the scale difference is the joke and the tool.

The Xbox original gained a successor-console version after its 2010 debut. A misplaced house can be lifted and turned until the little workers accept it.
giana-sisters-twisted-dreams-directors-c:
Cute and punk forms twist the same stage, and Giana Sisters: Twisted Dreams - Director's Cut is Black Forest Games' revival of the older series. A gem line that exists only in the punk form forces a swap in mid-jump.

Swapping sisters changes the world from a dreamy pastel to a harsher punk layout, and the platforms move with that swap. A gem line may exist only in one form, so the switch is the solution rather than a cosmetic costume.

The expanded cut reached the successor console in 2014, both sister forms included. Precision jumps remain as stern as the cabinet-era name suggests.
extreme-exorcism:
A previous life replays as a hostile ghost, and Extreme Exorcism is the local party game about fighting that recording. The ghost copies the last life's shots, so the safe tile is wherever that recording is not aiming.

Every movement of a failed attempt returns as an enemy pattern in the next life. Weapons picked up in the haunted rooms change the recording the ghost will imitate.

The 2015 successor-console release is built for a couch, not for a long solo plot. Clearing the room means standing where the earlier self is not about to shoot.
electronic-super-joy-groove-city:
A new city of music-driven stages continues the brutal jumps, and Electronic Super Joy: Groove City is that follow-up. A new skyline of lasers still kills in one touch if the slide misses the beat.

Grooves, lasers, and sarcastic billboards fill a fresh skyline while the one-hit deaths stay. The soundtrack still tells the player when to slide, and ignoring it restarts the block.

Groove City's one-hit lasers also reached the successor console in 2014 with the sarcastic billboards intact. Players who finished the earlier game meet new geometry with the same demand to move on the beat.
super-smash-bros:
Floating arenas and a blast line define the rules, and Super Smash Bros. is HAL Laboratory's four-player fight starring Nintendo characters. A Poké Ball dropped on the platform can interrupt a smash that would have crossed the blast line.

Mario, Pikachu, Link, Samus, and the rest of the original roster knock each other off platforms instead of draining a traditional health bar. Damage raises the distance a hit will throw, which is why a late smash finishes what an early jab cannot.

The 1999 Nintendo 64 original is the first of the series that later grew on every home console. Items such as the Poké Ball and the home-run bat already turn a duel into a scramble.
pirate-pop-plus:
Bubble popping wears the shell of a tiny handheld, and Pirate Pop Plus is 13AM Games' arcade toy presented like a toy machine. The bezel around the bubbles pretends the playfield is a tiny machine sitting on a table.

Match a color to pop a cluster while the frame around the playfield looks like a pocket gadget, screen bezel and all. The pirate theme is the costume on a familiar falling-bubble fight.

The 2016 release covers the glasses-free handheld and the successor console. A ceiling crush still ends the run if the cluster is left unmatched.
zombie-defense:
Units drop into lanes against incoming waves, and Zombie Defense is the defense game about holding that line. A sandbag chokepoint upgraded early holds a wave that a scattered row of troops would leak.

Towers and troops spend a limited purse, and a breach in the sandbag row costs the round. The undead keep to the path they are given, so the layout of those purchases is the strategy.

The 2010 design later sold on the successor console's shop. Upgrading a chokepoint matters more than steering a single hero through a story mission.
cubemen-2:
Cube squads attack each other's bases, and Cubemen 2 is 3 Sprockets' blocky strategy game about that siege. Nnooo's cross-platform match lets a cube base fall to a squad that is not in the same room.

Little cubes with different weapons spawn from a base the player reinforces. Nnooo brought cross-platform matches to the successor console, so a living-room squad can face opponents beyond the couch.

The 2013 battles reward spending the next cube on a counter instead of mirroring the enemy's first build. A collapsed base ends the match even if a few soldiers are still walking.
super-toy-cars:
Miniature coupes thread between chair legs in Super Toy Cars. Books, mugs, and rug fringes become barriers that dwarf each plastic body.

A living-room lap asks for a boost timed around a pet-scale jump rather than a pit stop. Rivals are other toy shells, so a missed corner bounces off a baseboard instead of a gravel trap.

That household circuit reached the Wii U eShop in 2014 as a small indie racer rather than a boxed motorsport license. Finish lines are measured in carpet, and the whole heat stays indoors.
twilight-princess-hd:
Wolf Link crosses a sharper Hyrule in The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess HD. Nintendo rebuilt the 2006 adventure for a higher resolution and added amiibo caves the earlier release did not contain.

Midna still rides the wolf form through twilight fields, while the Cave of Shadows is the amiibo extra waiting off the main road. Sword practice, beast combat, and the tear-collecting hunt all return with cleaner edges on the castle town.

The Wii and GameCube original stands as its own separate game. This HD reissue is the wolf-Link journey with those amiibo caves and the sharper map, dated 2016 on Wii U.
warriors-orochi-3-ultimate:
Koei Tecmo folded Dynasty Warriors officers into Samurai Warriors blades for WARRIORS OROCHI 3 Ultimate. The 2013 crossover piles both armies into one battlefield under the serpent Orochi.

Musou strings clear hundreds of rival soldiers while playable heroes from each roster switch mid-stage. Coalition battles, camp conversations, and the huge guest list are what the Ultimate set added on top of the base clash.

The Wii U edition was part of that Ultimate set, sharing the combined officer roster rather than a slimmed spinoff. Dynasty and Samurai fighters share the same demon-war map.
mahjong-deluxe-3:
Stacked tiles wait for a solitaire match in Mahjong Deluxe 3, where pairs clear off a layered layout. The Wii U eShop got this late casual release in 2016.

A dragon tile or a season tile only leaves the board when its twin is free on both sides. The session is single-player tile clearing, not a four-player table with discards and a wall.

Pick exposed pairs until the pyramid empties, which is the whole session. It sits among the last casual tile games that shop offered.
lone-survivor:
Jasper Byrne drew a scavenging apartment crawl in Lone Survivor. The 2012 original is the PC release, a 2D survival horror that a director's cut later expanded.

The masked survivor rations pills, food, and flashlight batteries while infected neighbors patrol the halls. Talking to a stranger through a door can matter as much as slipping past a figure in the dark.

Mood comes from the grainy side view and a thin synthesizer pulse, not from a squad of heroes. The director's cut is a later expansion of this PC original, not a replacement of the first release.
new-super-mario-bros-u:
Boost blocks drawn on the GamePad set New Super Mario Bros. U apart from earlier side-scrollers. Nintendo's 2012 platformer lets a second player tap those blocks when the person holding the pad wants to help.

Mario, Luigi, and the Toads still run Acorn Plains toward Peach's stolen castle, with the boost squares appearing only where the pad player places them. A mis-timed block can lift a jumper onto a ledge or shove him into a Spiny.

Those GamePad blocks are the Wii U idea. The Switch package that adds New Super Luigi U is a different release, not this game.
level-22:
Patrolling managers turn an office into a top-down stealth puzzle in Level 22: Gary’s Misadventure - 2016 Edition. Gary has to sneak past them without a combat move to fall back on.

Cubicles, coffee corners, and sight cones decide whether the worker reaches the next desk. A bad route gets him spotted, and the puzzle resets around the same floor plan.

Gary has no weapon, so the plan is a path between the managers' routes. The office floor, not a dungeon map, is the whole puzzle.
lego-dimensions:
Warner licenses share one Toy Pad in LEGO DIMENSIONS. TT Games' 2015 toys-to-life kit drops those properties into a single brick world, and Wii U had a starter set.

Physical minifigures placed on the pad call Batman, Wildstyle, or Gandalf into the same hub, depending on which pack sits on the studs. Vehicle builds and keystone puzzles gate the portal into each licensed world.

The starter set is the Wii U way in: a base, a portal, and the first trio of figures. Further level packs swap the story without leaving the brick hub.
twd-survival-instinct:
Activision's first-person spinoff, widely panned and separate from Telltale, is The Walking Dead: Survival Instinct. The 2013 Wii U release sits in that same criticized set.

Merle and Daryl move through rural Georgia before the TV group's prison story, scavenging fuel and ammunition from walker-filled stops. Shooting is the main verb, unlike Telltale's conversation trees with Lee Everett and Clementine.

Critics treated the gunplay and the thin missions harshly, and the Wii U release drew the same complaints. It is not an episode of Telltale's season and does not share that studio's choice menu.
just-dance-2016:
Ubisoft paired an on-disc tracklist with Just Dance Unlimited inside Just Dance 2016, while the Wii U disc still holds its own songs. The streaming library sits beside that disc, and the season is 2015.

A dancer on screen calls the moves, and the GamePad or a remote reads the player's arm path for a score. Unlimited was the new piece: a streaming catalog of extra routines rather than only the songs pressed on the disc.

The on-disc list remains playable without treating the service as the whole product. Choreography, pictogram cues, and the star rating are still the round.
super-mario-maker:
Course parts from several Mario eras snap together in Super Mario Maker. Nintendo's 2015 tool was the first course editor that let players upload 2D Mario stages in classic styles.

Ground, pipes, and enemies from the NES, SNES, and later side-scrollers share one grid, and a clear-check forces the maker to finish the level before sharing it. Costumes and the GamePad's draw tools are part of building, not a separate game mode pasted on top.

Super Mario Maker 2 on Switch is a sequel, not this tool. The Wii U editor, and the 3DS sharing of those courses, is the first upload workshop.
shiny-the-firefly:
Padaone Games carried a mobile garden over to Wii U in Shiny The Firefly. A firefly's glow both leads the way and draws danger, and the port is the 2013 release.

Dark leaves hide the path until the insect brightens them, yet the same light pulls predators toward the glow. Collecting stars through the garden means choosing when to shine and when to slip past.

The phone game came first, and the Wii U version keeps that risk-and-light loop on a television. No second combat system replaces the glow.
sonic-generations:
Anniversary stages pair a classic Sonic with a modern Sonic in Sonic Generations. The 2011 game marks the series anniversary, and the 3DS version uses its own stages rather than the console levels.

One hedgehog plays with a physics hop and a spindash, while the other boosts through a faster layout of the same theme. On 3DS those maps are handheld layouts, not cropped copies of the home-console acts.

Rival fights and the time-eater chase still frame the reunion. The dual kits are the point, and the 3DS stage list is its own set.
vvvvvv:
Captain Viridian flips gravity instead of jumping in VVVVVV. Terry Cavanagh's 2010 PC platformer was later ported to 3DS and Switch.

Spikes line the ceiling and the floor, so the only safe move is often a reversal onto the opposite surface. Crewmates stranded in the dimension each sit behind a different cluster of those screens.

The name is a row of identical letters because the flip, not a jump button, is the verb. Checkpoints are frequent because a single mistimed flip ends the attempt.
steamworld-dig-2:
Dorothy descends into a larger mine in SteamWorld Dig 2, a dig-and-upgrade sequel from Image and Form. The 2017 adventure reached both 3DS and Switch.

Ore veins pay for lamps, engines, and stronger picks, and the tunnels the player digs become the map. Rusty's absence is the reason Dorothy keeps drilling past Vectron blocks and pressure puzzles.

The first digger's run is the predecessor, and this sequel widens the caves and the tool shop. Both 3DS and Switch carry that same larger mine.
punch-club:
Lazy Bear Games runs a pixel gym where training hours decide the bout in Punch Club. The 2016 boxing manager is about training and fight nights, and it reached 3DS.

Strength, agility, and stamina compete for the same clock, so a roadwork morning can leave no time for the heavy bag. Fight night then tests whether that split was right, with a manager's cut waiting after the bell.

The tone jokes through movie posters on the gym wall while the calendar stays strict. The 3DS release is that same training loop in a handheld session.
fifa-15:
EA Sports left the Ignite engine off the simplified handheld FIFA 15, a 3DS season that is not the console game. The football sim belongs to 2014.

Kickoff, through balls, and a smaller roster presentation replace the broadcast camera and the physics model of the living-room version. Career tools are thinner because the handheld cart was built as its own season, not a shrunken Ignite match.

Licensed clubs still fill the menus, but the touch controls and the reduced presentation mark the 3DS cart. It is that year's football release in handheld form.
mega-man-legacy-collection-2:
Capcom boxed the first six robot-master campaigns, plus extra challenges, as Mega Man Legacy Collection / ロックマン クラシックス コレクション. A 3DS version followed the console release of that 2015 collection.

Mega Man still steals a boss weapon after each fortress room, from Bomb Man's bombs through the later stages of the sixth game. Challenge remixes restage those fights with extra hazards the original carts did not stack together.

The Japanese title on the same box points at the Rockman numbering of those six games. The 3DS edition arrived after the console collection, carrying the same six campaigns and the extra challenges.
nightsky:
Nifflas rolls a silhouetted orb through quiet machinery in NightSky. The 2011 puzzle was later brought to 3DS.

Momentum, not a run button, carries the sphere up slopes, across seesaws, and through gates that open only when the weight sits on a plate. Night insects and a lantern glow keep the stages nearly wordless.

Failing means the orb settles in the wrong bowl, and the restart is immediate. The 3DS release is that same rolling puzzle after the earlier computer versions.
retro-city-rampage-dx:
Brian Provinciano packed an 8-bit open city with crime-spoof missions in Retro City Rampage DX. The DX edition expanded his PC original on 3DS, and the game is from 2012.

Theftopolis traffic, baseball bats, and a story mode full of 1980s game jokes sit under a top-down camera. DX adds missions and presentation on top of the freeware city that came first.

The joke is the open-city crime spree told with NES-era sprites, not a realistic driving model. The 3DS DX cart is the expanded edition of that PC original.
metal-gear-solid-3-snake-eater:
Naked Snake crawls a jungle survival mission in Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater. Hideo Kojima's 2004 stealth game began on PlayStation 2, and a 3DS version later carried that same mission.

Camouflage percentages, a cure menu for leeches and broken bones, and food caught in the grass all sit beside the guard cones. The Boss waits at the end of the Operation Snake Eater story, with the Cobra Unit hunting between those codec calls.

The 3DS release keeps the jungle mission rather than inventing a side chapter. Circle-pad camera control and the survival viewer are how that PlayStation 2 operation fits the handheld.
dragon-quest-xi:
Square Enix opened the Luminary's journey in Japan on DRAGON QUEST XI: Echoes of an Elusive Age. The 2017 mainline RPG launched there on 3DS beside PlayStation 4.

Erdrea's party still recruits companions, equips skills on a panel grid, and rides across a continent-sized map. The Japanese 3DS edition shares that launch window with the PlayStation 4 version rather than waiting for a later western handheld.

Pep powers, the forge, and the Luminary's mark are the new-quest pieces. This is the Japanese twin launch, 3DS beside PlayStation 4, not a western-only port.
ace-attorney-phoenix-wright-trilogy-hd:
Maya Fey channels spirits across three courtroom games collected as Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney Trilogy. Capcom's package holds the cases that began on the Game Boy Advance, and the collection is dated 2013.

Phoenix Wright shouts objections over evidence, Miles Edgeworth prosecutes, and the first trilogy's witnesses each hide a contradiction in the court record. The Game Boy Advance originals grew the series before this 3DS package gathered them.

Turnabout stories from the borrowed sister through the bridge case stay in one cartridge. It is those first three games, not Apollo Justice and not the Investigations side path.
ghostbusters-the-video-game:
Proton streams and a film-style script define Ghostbusters: The Video Game. Dan Aykroyd and Harold Ramis helped write the 2009 game, often treated as a third film, while the Wii version is a separate on-rails take.

The bigger edition puts the proton pack, the trap, and the original firehouse crew into a third-person job alongside Stay Puft-scale set pieces. On Wii the same license becomes an on-rails shooter, a different camera and a different way through the ghosts.

A DS release sat in that same season and is not the third-person story the two writers shaped. The Wii on-rails take is the split the license is known for on Nintendo hardware.
lego-pirates-of-the-caribbean:
Jack Sparrow's four films get retold in minifigs in LEGO Pirates of the Caribbean: The Video Game. TT Games shipped that 2011 brick adventure on Wii, DS, and 3DS.

Cursed gold, the Black Pearl, and the later voyages break into studs when a character smashes scenery for bits. Character swapping and red-brick extras carry over the usual LEGO treasure hunt across those four movies.

Handheld editions and the Wii edition all follow that film order rather than an original pirate plot. Davy Jones and Barbossa return as brick bosses inside the movie chapters.
gauntlet:
Thyra, Merlin, Thor, and Questor lend their arcade names to Gauntlet. Midway made the four-hero dungeon crawl famous in arcades, and this 2009 release is a DS-era game rather than the 1985 cabinet.

Food, keys, and generators belong to the cabinet fantasy, but the handheld release is not that upright machine in a new shell. The title borrows the four heroes and the dungeon crawl instead of reproducing the 1985 joystick maze.

Death's taunt and the original generator rooms stay with the arcade machine. What carries the name here is a DS-era release using that four-hero fame.
marvel-ultimate-alliance-2:
The Superhuman Registration Act splits the roster of Marvel: Ultimate Alliance 2, a team brawler drawn from the comics' registration conflict. Separate Wii and DS versions of that Marvel game arrived in 2009.

Iron Man's pro-registration side and Captain America's resistance each field fusion moves when two heroes stand together. Choosing a side changes which street fight and which boss lineup the squad walks into.

The Wii version and the DS version are separate builds, not one disc squeezed onto a smaller screen. Both follow the registration war rather than the first Alliance's broader tour.
ys-i-ii-chronicles-2:
Adol Christin climbs Darm Tower and a floating island in Ys I & II Chronicles. Falcom's remake package bundles the first two Ys action RPGs, and that Chronicles edition is associated with PSP rather than a DS launch.

Bump combat, where walking into a foe deals the hit, still defines those early adventures of the red-haired swordsman. Esteria's tower and the second quest's airborne land sit together in the Chronicles package.

Darm Tower belongs to the first quest's era, while Chronicles itself is the later remake bundle. It is tied to PSP, not to a DS launch day.
zumas-revenge:
Marble chains roll toward a skull mouth again in Zuma's Revenge! PopCap's sequel continues the frog-and-marble matching of Zuma, and the follow-up is from 2009.

Colored balls fired from the frog's mouth insert into the chain, and three matching spheres vanish before the line reaches the end. New powerups and longer temple routes distinguish the revenge trip from the first frog's ponds.

A DS edition carries that same insert-and-match loop. The skull, the chain, and the frog are the whole round.
pokemon-pearl:
Palkia guards a different wild roster in Pokemon Pearl, the Sinnoh pair Game Freak and Nintendo shipped beside Diamond. It is the other 2006 DS edition, not the Switch remake.

Water routes, the absence of a distortion detour, and Pearl-exclusive species separate the cartridge from Diamond's Dialga story. Trading between the pair fills the dex that one cart leaves blank.

Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl on Switch are later remakes, not this cartridge. Pearl remains the DS partner with its own legendary and its own grass encounters.
pokemon-black:
Team Plasma questions whether trainers should catch creatures at all in Pokemon Black. Game Freak and Nintendo's Unova game from 2010 is one half of that pair, and seasons turn on the calendar.

Reshiram waits on Black's side of the story while N argues against Poké Balls, and the overworld shifts from spring routes to winter snow. Black 2 is a sequel set later, not a third version of this first trip.

White is the other half of that pair, with its own legendary and its own version exclusives. Seasons, the Plasma speeches, and the catching debate are what this half plays.
tron-evolution:
Identity discs and a system conflict tie TRON: Evolution - The Video Game to TRON: Legacy. Propaganda Games made the 2010 game, and the DS release is a separate handheld from the console action game.

The console edition follows a program through the Grid with disc combat and lightcycle stretches tied to the film. The DS release does not reuse those console stages; it is its own handheld beside the same movie.

Legacy's glow and the war inside the system are the shared premise. Only the console build is the third-person Grid campaign Propaganda shaped for HD machines.
cut-the-rope:
Om Nom waits under a hanging candy in Cut the Rope. ZeptoLab's 2010 phone game swings that sweet by slicing ropes, and DS and 3DS ports followed.

Bubbles, ropes, and spikes change which cut drops the candy into the green mouth for three stars. A wrong slice sends the treat into a spike or out of the level.

The phone original came first, with the monster, the candy, and the scissors as the puzzle. DS and 3DS editions carry that same feed-the-monster loop onto handhelds.
pokemon-platinum:
Giratina's Distortion World fills out the Sinnoh story in Pokemon Platinum. Game Freak and Nintendo's third Sinnoh version, from 2008, is the refined DS edition of the fourth generation.

The Distortion World, a longer Team Galactic plot, and the Battle Frontier expand what Diamond and Pearl left shorter. Wild tables and the post-game change with that refined script.

It is not a new region and not a Switch remake. Platinum is the fuller fourth-generation DS cartridge, distortion world included.
tcs-endwar:
Headset orders made the console battles of Tom Clancy's EndWar famous. Ubisoft's 2008 near-future strategy game is known for voice commands, while the DS version is a separate handheld campaign.

Europe, the United States, and Russia field units across a World War III map when the console player speaks a unit order. The DS campaign does not rely on that microphone grammar; it is its own handheld war.

The voice-controlled battlefield is the console identity. The DS cart keeps the near-future factions without being a microphone port of those orders.
pokemon-white-2:
Unova, two years later, continues in Pokemon White 2, the paired sequel to White. Game Freak and Nintendo share that timeline with Black 2, and this is the other DS sequel from 2012.

New leads, a changed map of the same region, and a story that assumes the first Unova crisis already happened separate it from White. It is not a third version of the 2010 pair and not a swapped legendary of the first games.

Black 2 tells the matching two-years-later quest with its own exclusives. White 2 is the other half of that sequel pair.
myst:
Linking books on a pre-rendered island define Myst. Cyan's 1993 point-and-click landmark began on Macintosh, and a DS port arrived years after that computer original.

Atrus's sons, Sirrus and Achenar, wait inside ages reached by those books, and the puzzles are machines rather than conversation trees. The DS port puts the same island on a handheld long after the Macintosh release, and a 3DS listing also carries the island puzzle.

The library, the tower rocket, and the ages are the computer game's famous rooms. Handheld editions follow that Macintosh original rather than replacing it.
puzzle-kingdoms:
Sieges resolve through match puzzles on the kingdom map of Puzzle Kingdoms. Infinite Interactive's 2009 strategy-puzzle hybrid is a DS cousin of Puzzle Quest.

Armies meet, then a gem board decides the battle, and the map remembers which castle changed hands. It borrows the match-to-fight idea from Puzzle Quest without being that wizard's quest.

Capturing territory and clearing gems are the two halves of a turn. The DS release is that cousin, kingdom map included.
kingdom-hearts-3582-days:
Roxas clocks in for Organization missions in Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days. Square Enix told that mission-based chapter on DS in 2009, and it was later folded into HD collections.

Ice cream on the clock tower, panel-built abilities, and daily sorties with Axel fill the handheld loop. The story sits between longer console chapters and explains Roxas's time inside the Organization.

HD collections later replay the chapter with cutscenes and a different structure. The DS game is the mission diary itself, not only the compilation movie.
gta-chinatown-wars:
Huang Lee arrives in Liberty City with a stolen sword in Grand Theft Auto: Chinatown Wars. Rockstar Leeds' 2009 top-down DS original was praised far above a typical handheld spinoff.

Drug deals, scratch-card minigames, and a top-down camera tell a crime story built for the stylus rather than a console import. The tone and the mission writing are why it stood apart from throwaway handheld tie-ins.

Liberty City here is a DS map with its own Triad plot, not a cropped edition of an earlier 3D entry. The praise followed that original handheld design.
carcassonne-2:
Meeples score cities, roads, and fields in Carcassonne. The tile-laying board game came to DS in 2010, scoring those features the way the tabletop original does.

Each drawn tile must touch a matching edge, and a meeple claims a city, a road, or a field until that feature closes. Farmers, thieves, and knights are the same wooden roles the table uses, just tapped on a screen.

Cloisters and incomplete roads still punish a greedy placement. The DS edition follows the tabletop scoring rather than inventing a video-only board.
999-nine-hours-nine-persons-nine-doors:
Junpei wears a numbered bracelet aboard a sinking ship in Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors. Chunsoft's escape-room puzzles branch into endings that take more than one play, and the DS original of the Zero Escape series is from 2009.

Digital roots on the bracelets decide which numbered door a pair may open, and the bottom screen holds the puzzle while the top holds the room. Zero's Nonary Game forces the nine captives through those doors before the hull fails.

One ending does not show the whole diagram, so a second route rewrites what the first route seemed to prove. This is the DS original of Zero Escape, before Virtue's Last Reward and Zero Time Dilemma.
lotr-conquest:
Pandemic staged the film trilogy's wars as The Lord of the Rings: Conquest. The 2009 battle game has a DS edition that is a smaller companion to the console release.

Console matches throw soldiers of Rohan, Mordor, and the other film armies into objective fights rather than a single hero's adventure. The DS companion shrinks that war into a handheld campaign beside the larger release.

It is a battle game set in the movie wars, not a retelling of the books' quieter chapters. The DS edition stays the smaller companion.
n-2:
Gold crumbs and mines fill the punishing levels of N+, Metanet's expanded edition of the earlier jumper. A DS release in 2008 carries a large stack of user levels.

The stick figure hops across tiny platforms, and a mine or a homing missile ends the run in a burst. User levels pile on top of the built-in set, which is why the plus edition is thicker than N.

Precision, not combat combos, is the skill. The DS cart is that expanded jumper with the user-level stack.
dragons-lair-hd:
Dirk the Daring lunges through animated scenes in Dragon's Lair HD. Don Bluth's laserdisc arcade cartoon returned in 2009 as quick-time fantasy played as scenes rather than free movement.

A late press toward the right opening, or a sword swing a beat too early, cuts to Dirk's comic death instead of the next room. Princess Daphne and Singe the dragon still wait at the end of those clips.

There is no walking simulator between the pictures. The HD release is the cartoon's timed choices, the same laserdisc idea on a handheld.
super-mario-64-ds:
Yoshi, Luigi, and Wario join Mario in the castle of Super Mario 64 DS. Nintendo's 2004 reworking adds touch controls and extra stars the Nintendo 64 game did not have.

A rabbit theft opens the grounds, and each character's move set finds stars the others cannot, with the touch screen blowing out ghosts or grabbing distant ledges. The 1996 Nintendo 64 castle remains its own separate game.

Extra stars, the character gates, and the stylus are the DS additions. It is the reworking, not the 1996 original under a new label.
professor-layton-and-the-curious-village:
Hershel Layton and Luke Triton take a puzzle hunt to St. Mystere in Professor Layton and the Curious Village. Level-5 and Nintendo's 2007 game is the first Layton adventure in the DS line, and Nintendo published it in the West.

Villagers hand over riddles about a golden apple, a tower, and a robot secret under the streets. Hint coins buy a nudge when a sliding puzzle or a logic grid stalls the gentleman and his apprentice.

Later Layton cases assume this village already happened. The western DS line starts here, with Nintendo as the publisher outside Japan.
7-wonders-ii:
Wonder tiles continue MumboJumbo's casual line in 7 Wonders II. The 2007 sequel keeps the ancient-wonder tile matching of that series.

Boards themed on monuments ask for runs of tiles to be cleared before a timer or a blocked layout ends the round. It follows an earlier wonder matcher rather than starting a new puzzle family.

The sequel number is the relationship: more monument boards in the same tile-matching line. MumboJumbo's casual series is the home of both games.
puzzler-world:
Crossword clues, word searches, and logic grids from the Puzzler brand fill Puzzler World. The DS compilation arrived in 2009.

A crossword square, a hidden word in a letter grid, and a logic puzzle with houses and colors each take a turn in the menu. The brand's magazine puzzles are the source, gathered onto one cartridge.

No single story links the grids. The compilation is the variety: words, searches, and logic from Puzzler.
ghost-trick:
Sissel possesses a lamp, a bicycle, or a dog to rewind four minutes before a death in Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective. Capcom's 2010 adventure is Shu Takumi's DS puzzle story, from the Ace Attorney director, and it is its own plot.

The ghost can hop between objects in a room, trigger a chain, and jump back to the moment four minutes earlier when someone is about to die. Missile the dog and a lineup of strangers in one night are not courtroom witnesses under new names.
