Takumi directed Ace Attorney, but Phoenix Wright does not take this case. Ghost Trick stands as its own DS story about the four-minute rewind.
wwe-smackdown-vs-raw-2010:
Yuke's and THQ packed a DS cart into WWE SmackDown vs. RAW 2010, a wrestling season of grapples and signature moves. That annual shipped in 2009.

Exhibition matches, a story mode, and the roster of that year's television brands fill the console game, and the DS edition is part of the same annual. Grapples, pins, and signature moves are the match, scaled to the handheld card.

It is that SmackDown versus Raw season, not a later annual with a different roster. The DS cart belongs to the same shipment, cover branding and all.
fifa-08:
Season kits and league schedules mark EA Sports' FIFA 08, with a DS edition beside the console game. The football season arrived in 2007.

Club badges, formations, and a match engine of that year sit on the console disc, while the DS cart carries a handheld kickoff of the same season. It is not a later FIFA numbered after this one.

The pairing is the point of the release window: console and DS together for that season. Touch controls on the handheld replace the pad layout of the television match.
iron-man:
Arc-reactor flight over the first Marvel film's battles is Sega's Iron Man. A DS cartridge joined the console builds in that 2008 movie window.

Repulsor blasts and a missile barrage follow the movie's armor scenes on the console builds. The DS version joins that same licensed set rather than standing as an unrelated metal-suit story.

Obadiah's rivalry and the suit-up fantasy come from the first film, not from a later sequel's Monaco fight. Sega's tie-in is that package, DS edition included.
kingdom-hearts-recoded:
Data-Sora debugs bugs inside Jiminy's journal in KINGDOM HEARTS Re:coded. Square Enix remade its mobile Kingdom Hearts story for DS in 2010, a journal-data chapter later compiled in HD.

System sectors turn familiar worlds into glitching floors, and the bugs are combat encounters inside the journal rather than a new cast's vacation. The mobile original came first, and the DS game is the remake of that data story.

HD compilations later folded the chapter in beside other side stories. Re:coded on DS is the journal bug-hunt itself.
mario-and-luigi-bowsers-inside-story:
Fawful shrinks the brothers so they can travel inside a giant Bowser in Mario and Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story. AlphaDream's 2009 DS role-playing game splits play between those brothers and Bowser's own giant battles.

Inside the body, Mario and Luigi jump organs and nerve paths as timed Bros. attacks, while the overworld Bowser breathes fire at enemies too big for the brothers. The top screen and the touch screen divide those two scales.

Fawful and the Blorb epidemic are the crisis, not a simple castle rescue. The inside-Bowser map is the DS game's signature split.
lego-rock-band:
Plastic drums and a family setlist define Lego Rock Band. Harmonix and Traveller's Tales aimed the 2009 game at younger players, and the DS edition is a simpler rhythm game than the console instruments.

Console sessions expect guitars, drums, and a microphone on licensed songs with brick characters on stage. The DS edition drops that instrument rig for a simpler handheld rhythm game with the same brick-band theme.

Studios, venues, and the kid-friendly roster are the console toy. The DS cart keeps the name without the living-room drum kit.
zoo-tycoon:
Lion exhibits, guest paths, and animal happiness are the PC management of Zoo Tycoon. Blue Fang and Microsoft's 2001 sim is distinct from the later DS spinoff that reused the name.

Fences, zookeepers, and donation boxes build a park on a computer, with dinosaurs and marine packs arriving as later computer expansions. The handheld game that borrowed the title is a different product, not this management sim in a pocket.

That computer game is the PC park, remembered for exhibits and guest needs. A DS spinoff reused the name later and does not replace that original management sim.
dark-void-zero:
A pixel jetpack carries the DSiWare prequel Dark Void Zero. Capcom released the 8-bit side-scroller in 2010 as a retro prequel tied to the bigger Dark Void shooter.

Side-view rooms, short enemy waves, and a tiny flight model nod at the jetpack of the larger game without using its third-person camera. DSiWare is where that pixel episode lived.

The bigger shooter is a separate release with a vertical flight suit. Zero is the small prequel, not a level select for that shooter.
7-wonders-of-the-ancient-world:
Pyramid boards and other monuments theme MumboJumbo's 7 Wonders of the Ancient World. The 2007 tile-matcher received a DS version beside the casual PC original.

Tiles clear in monument layouts, and the ancient-world dressing is the theme of this entry in the line. The PC casual game came first, with the DS version joining it.

It is the monument matcher itself, and the numbered sequel is a later board set. Both belong to MumboJumbo's tile line.
animal-crossing-wild-world:
Tom Nook's shop serves a pocket town you can visit online in Animal Crossing: Wild World. Nintendo's 2005 DS game is smaller than the GameCube village and sits between that original and City Folk.

Weeds, fossils, and a late-night visit from K.K. Slider still fill the days, while Wi-Fi lets another player's train stop in your acre. The town fits a handheld, with fewer acres than the GameCube map and no city plaza yet.

City Folk on Wii comes after this pocket town, and the GameCube original comes before it. Wild World is the DS Animal Crossing in that line.
smackdown-vs-raw-2009:
Steel-chair finishes and a television roster fill THQ's WWE Smackdown vs. RAW 2009, and a DS edition shipped beside the console game. The wrestling season arrived in 2008.

The console game carries that year's creation suite and match types, and the DS edition is the handheld card of the same season. It is not the following year's cart with a new cover star.

Pins, submissions, and the brand split belong to the annual THQ was shipping then. The DS edition is part of that arrival, not a later season with a new cover star.
spider-man-friend-or-foe:
Green Goblin and other foes team up with Spider-Man in Activision's lighter brawler Spider-Man: Friend or Foe. The 2007 game is aimed at kids, and a DS version shipped with it.

Punching waves of identical minions, with a villain as a co-op partner, replaces a grim crime story. The tone stays cartoon-bright, which is why it sits apart from darker Spider-Man campaigns of the same era.

The DS version shipped in that kid-aimed set. Team brawls with familiar foes are the round, not an open Manhattan simulator.
apollo-justice-ace-attorney-2:
A perceive bracelet catches witness tells in Apollo Justice: Ace Attorney. Capcom introduced the new defense attorney on DS in 2007, the fourth main courtroom game after the Phoenix Wright trilogy.

Apollo Justice watches a nervous twitch, zooms in, and breaks a testimony that looking alone would miss. Phoenix Wright's situation has changed, and the new attorney leads the cases rather than sitting as a sidekick.

The 3DS listing came later, while the DS game is where Apollo's first cases shipped. It follows the original trilogy and is not a reprint of those three games.
the-incredible-hulk:
Abomination's fight anchors the film tie-in The Incredible Hulk (2008), and a DS version shipped with the other editions. The Marvel film named in the title is the source of the action.

Console rampages smash streets and military hardware in the green giant's strength fantasy. The DS version belongs to that same tie-in wave rather than to an earlier Ang Lee story under a similar name.

Soldiers, tanks, and the film's antagonist are the set dressing. The DS cartridge belongs to that movie's licensed brawler alongside the other editions.
madden-nfl-09:
Brett Favre's Packers cover, later swapped for a Jets cover after he changed teams, is Madden NFL 09, and EA put that first cover out for the 2008 season. The Nintendo DS cart is that year's handheld edition, not a later Madden.

Playbooks, hit sticks, and the roster of the season live on the console disc. The handheld cart is the pocket edition of the same season, cover controversy and all.

The Jets reissue followed the real trade, so two covers exist for one season. Neither cover makes this a Madden from a different year.
bolt:
Penny's TV dog, who thinks the studio powers are real, headlines Disney Bolt. The animated film got that platform tie-in in 2008, and a DS version shipped in the movie season.

Super-bark set pieces and chase levels follow the dog from the soundstage into the world outside the show. Rhino the hamster and the film's cross-country idea color the licensed levels.

The DS version is part of that movie-season set. It is a platform tie-in to the film about the deluded super-dog, not a pet simulator.
the-world-ends-with-you:
Neku Sakuraba fights on two screens in Shibuya during The World Ends with You. Square Enix and Jupiter's 2007 handheld game gives him fashion pins for powers and a week-long deadline.

The top screen and the touch screen each control a partner in the Noise battles around Scramble Crossing, and the pin deck changes which psych fires. The Reapers' Game lasts a week, with trends in the shops affecting how strong a brand is that day.

Later ports and a sequel exist, while this remains the DS original. Shibuya, the pins, and the deadline belong to the handheld game, not the follow-up.
secret-files-2-puritas-cordis:
Nina Kalenkov follows Tunguska with another point-and-click case in Secret Files 2: Puritas Cordis. Animation Arts shipped the 2009 sequel, including a DS port of that mystery.

Inventory combines, dialogue trees, and a conspiracy about Puritas Cordis push Nina through locations the first Tunguska case left unfinished. The DS port carries that same mystery onto a handheld.

It is a sequel, so the earlier Secret Files story is assumed. The DS edition is a port of the point-and-click, not a new side episode.
puzzle-quest-2:
Spells fire when colored gems match in Puzzle Quest 2, and Infinite Interactive's match-puzzle RPG continues the Puzzle Quest idea. A DS version was part of the 2010 release.

Mana from the board pays for attacks, and a dungeon crawl sits under the gem grid. The sequel changes the setting and the items while keeping the match-to-cast loop of the first game.

The DS version belongs to that release rather than to a much later spinoff. Gems, mana, and equipment are still the turn.
thrillville-otr:
Coaster blueprints and midway minigames share Frontier's Thrillville: Off the Rails. The 2007 theme-park sequel includes a DS version.

Track pieces build a ride, then a minigame or a coaster run tests whether the park guests stay happy. It follows an earlier Thrillville park rather than starting the series.

The DS version carries building and minigames in that sequel's season. Roller coasters remain the headline attraction.
layton-diabolical-box-in-hd:
The Molentary Express carries another suitcase of riddles in Professor Layton and the Diabolical Box. Level-5's 2009 DS puzzle adventure followed the curious village, and Europe knows it as Pandora's Box.

A mysterious box, a train car full of suspects, and village stops each hide a puzzle behind the conversation. Hint coins return, and Luke Triton still writes the facts in his notebook.

The European title Pandora's Box is the same train mystery, not a different case. It is the second DS Layton adventure after St. Mystere.
4-elements:
Fire, water, earth, and air tokens clear boards in 4 Elements. The casual puzzle from 2010 was sold in editions on DS and 3DS.

Matching a run of the same element removes it, and the board's obstacles change which element is useful. Fire and water sit as neighboring tokens, and a blocked line forces a different element.

DS and 3DS editions both sell that board-clearing. The elements are the tiles, not a combat spell list from another game.
castlevania-dawn-of-sorrow:
Soma Cruz draws magic seals on the touch screen to finish a boss in Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow. Konami's 2005 DS game is the sequel to Aria of Sorrow.

Souls taken from enemies change the skill set, and a seal traced badly lets the boss survive the last hit. The castle, the dark chapel, and the cult around Soma continue the Aria story rather than resetting to Simon Belmont.

Touch-screen seals are the DS addition on top of the soul system. It is the sequel to Aria of Sorrow, with Soma returning.
harry-potter-and-the-deathly-hallows-par:
Camping chases and a cover shooter replace class periods in Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 1, a sharp break from the earlier Potter adventures. EA turned the seventh film into that 2010 game, and a DS version shipped with it.

Spells snap to targets from behind crates during the Ministry and the road scenes, instead of a Hogwarts hub full of classes. The break is the camera and the gun-like aim, not another year of Quidditch.

The DS version sits in that same break from the school games. Part 1 stops with the film's first-half events rather than the battle at the castle.
ace-attorney-investigations-miles-edgewo:
Dick Gumshoe radios Miles Edgeworth while the prosecutor walks the scene in Ace Attorney Investigations - Miles Edgeworth. Capcom's 2009 DS game moves the series onto investigation scenes starring the prosecutor instead of the defense.

Logic connects two facts into a deduction, and a third-person search replaces the courtroom bench until a confrontation. Kay Faraday and the crime-scene tools belong to Edgeworth's side of the franchise.

Phoenix Wright is not the lead counsel here. The DS game is the prosecutor's investigation chapter.
sudoku:
Pencil candidates fill a number grid that long predates Nintendo in Sudoku. The 2008 DS release is one of many handheld editions of that logic puzzle.

Each row, column, and box must hold every digit once, and the stylus writes a guess or a firm answer. The grid itself is the product, the same logic newspapers used long before a cartridge.

Newspapers and paper booklets used the same rules for years before any cartridge. This is one handheld copy of that older puzzle, not an invention of the DS era.
madden-nfl-08:
GameCube snaps and a DS cart both carry EA's Madden NFL 08, and the 2007 season still shipped on Nintendo's disc console. It sits among the last Madden seasons on that disc machine.

Playbooks of the year and the roster sit on the GameCube disc, while the DS edition is the handheld card beside it. Later Madden seasons left the disc console behind.

The dual Nintendo release is the historical point of this season. It is not a modern handheld rebuild of a much older roster.
mario-luigi-partners-in-time:
Shroob invaders force the adult brothers to team with their baby selves in Mario & Luigi: Partners in Time. AlphaDream and Nintendo's 2005 DS follow-up to Superstar Saga splits the pairs across two screens.

Babies ride on the adults or explore a lower screen path, and timed hits still trigger Bros. moves against the mushroom aliens. Time holes open the past Princess Peach's castle to the invasion.

Superstar Saga is the previous game, and this is the DS follow-up. The babies and the Shroobs are the new cast on top of the brotherly timing.
sonic-colors:
Cyan Wisp lasers and other alien powers change the moves in Sonic Colors. Sonic Team's 2010 game defines itself by those Wisps, and the DS version is its own stage set rather than a shrunk Wii port.

A Wisp picked up mid-stage becomes a drill, a rocket, or a laser for a few seconds, then the stage design expects that burst. DS acts use that idea on layouts built for the handheld, not on cropped Wii tracks.

Egg Planet Park and the captured Wisps frame both editions. The DS stage list is original to the handheld.
professor-layton-and-the-unwound-future:
Future London closes Level-5's original puzzle trilogy in Professor Layton and the Unwound Future. The 2010 DS case is known in Europe as Professor Layton and the Lost Future.

A time-displaced city, a huge puzzle count, and the consequences of the earlier village and train cases bring Hershel Layton and Luke Triton to the end of that trilogy. The European title Lost Future names the same future-London mystery.

It is the third case, not the prequel that arrived afterward. The DS trilogy's last future story is this one.
pokemon-mystery-dungeon-explorers-of-sky:
Special episodes sit on top of Time and Darkness in Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Sky. Chunsoft's 2009 expanded third version of the Explorers story adds those episodes for DS.

A human-turned Pokémon still joins Wigglytuff's Guild, and the extra episodes follow side characters the paired games left offstage. The main mystery of the paralyzed future remains, with more scenes around it.

Time and Darkness are the pair, and Sky is the fuller third cartridge. The added episodes are why it is not just a rerelease with a palette swap.
wall-e:
EVE's directive and a lonely trash-compacting robot drive THQ's WALL-E: The Video Game. The 2008 tie-in to the Pixar film includes a DS edition in that licensed set.

Cube stacks, the Axiom's corridors, and the plant in a boot follow the film's images through licensed levels. The DS edition is part of that set rather than a separate short about a different robot.

Buy n Large branding and the cockpit romance are the film's furniture. The game is the licensed tie-in, DS cart included.
puzzle-quest-galactrix:
Hex fleets replace the square gem board in Puzzle Quest: Galactrix. Infinite Interactive moved the Puzzle Quest formula onto that hex grid for the 2009 sci-fi spinoff, including a DS release.

Ships, starbases, and a match on six-sided cells carry the combat instead of a medieval dungeon. It is a spinoff, so the wizard of the first game is not the captain here.

The DS release belongs to that hex-grid spinoff. Science-fiction fittings are the change, while matching to power an action stays the turn.
pokemon-ranger:
Capture Styler loops, rather than battles, define Pokémon Ranger. The 2006 DS spinoff is the first game in that handheld line.

A circle drawn around a wild Pokémon fills the styler gauge until the creature agrees to help, then the help clears an obstacle instead of entering a Poké Ball forever. The Ranger Union in the region sends the player on those capture jobs.

Later Almia and Oblivia adventures follow this first styler. Battles with turns and type charts are not the verb here.
cars-2-the-video-game:
Finn McMissile and a spy World Grand Prix fuel Disney•Pixar Cars 2: The Video Game. The 2011 racing tie-in to the spy sequel shipped with DS and 3DS versions alongside the consoles.

Lightning McQueen and Mater still race, but gadgets and weapons from the film sit on the karts. Handheld versions join the console releases of that movie season rather than waiting for a later anniversary port.

World Grand Prix stops supply the courses, with spy gadgets strapped to the cars. DS and 3DS both sit in that licensed movie-season set.
sonic-sega-racing:
Kart cameos of Sega characters fill Sonic & SEGA Racing. The 2010 DS game is a handheld cousin of Sumo Digital's All-Stars Racing.

Boost pads, weapons, and tracks dressed as famous Sega places carry the race, with Sonic among a roster that nods at other series. It is a cousin, not the home-console All-Stars track list copied onto a small screen.

Sumo Digital's console racer is the relative, and this DS kart game keeps the crossover idea. Drifting and items are the lap.
shrek-the-third:
Fairy-tale stages follow the third DreamWorks film in Shrek the Third. Arthur's coronation year on the poster is 2007, and the DS cart traveled with the other movie editions.

Arthur, the kingdom, and the film's villains frame the licensed levels rather than an original swamp episode. The DS version shipped with the other editions of the movie game.

It is a film tie-in, so the plot beats belong to that third movie. The handheld cart is part of the same licensed wave.
harry-potter-and-the-deathly-hallows-par:
The Battle of Hogwarts becomes a cover shooter in Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 2, EA's tie-in to the eighth film. The 2011 release includes a DS version beside the consoles.

Courtyard pushes, shield charms, and the castle siege replace the school-year hubs of the early games. The DS version sits beside those console shooters for the same film.

Part 1 stopped on the road, and this follow-up takes the aim-down sights into the castle. It remains a sharp break from the class-and-Quidditch adventures.
spider-man-edge-of-time:
Miguel O'Hara shares a breaking timeline with the modern hero in Spider-Man: Edge of Time. The 2011 game puts Spider-Man 2099 in that crisis, and the DS and 3DS releases are separate from the HD console game.

Walker Sloan's tampering links the present suit to the 2099 suit, and each hero's chapter uses a different gadget set. Handheld releases do not reuse the HD console stages; they are their own builds.

The future city and the present city are the two clocks. DS and 3DS stay separate from the high-definition version.
alice-in-wonderland:
The Mad Hatter and Underland follow Tim Burton's film in Disney Alice in Wonderland. The 2010 tie-in launched in that movie's season, and a DS version shipped with it.

Bandersnatch chases, shrinking potions, and the film's pale color palette dress the licensed levels. The DS version is part of the season rather than a Lewis Carroll text adventure.

Burton's Hatter, not the older cartoon Hatter, is the reference. The handheld release belongs to that movie window.
fifa-street-3:
Panna tricks and street courts replace the rulebook in FIFA Street 3, where EA dropped simulation rules for trick-heavy street football. A DS version carried that spinoff in 2008.

Offside and long career sliders give way to skill moves and small pitches. The DS version keeps the street idea rather than the full FIFA season sim of the same year.

It is the third street spinoff, so the earlier Street games are the line behind it. Trick strings are the match.
world-of-zoo:
Plush-like animal care, closer to toy creatures than to Zoo Tycoon, is World of Zoo. THQ's 2009 sim plays that way, with a DS release.

Feeding, washing, and mini-challenges with a single animal replace budget spreadsheets and guest paths. The older Zoo Tycoon model of fences and donations is the contrast the design avoids.

The DS release carries that creature-care approach. Exhibits are intimate and toy-like, not a full park economy.
castlevania-order-of-ecclesia:
Shanoa absorbs glyphs for weapons and spells in Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia. Koji Igarashi's 2008 DS action RPG was the last of the handheld search-action Castlevanias before the series changed direction.

Villagers of Wygol can be rescued, and a glyph combination changes whether Shanoa swings a blade or calls a spell. The map is a set of locations rather than one uninterrupted castle corridor.

After this game the series moved toward the Lords of Shadow continuity. Ecclesia is the last of those handheld search-action entries.
superman-returns:
Metropolis flight in an open city is EA's Superman Returns: The Videogame. The 2006 film tie-in shipped with a separate DS game under that license.

Console play emphasizes lifting objects, racing to crimes, and flying between daily events in the city. The DS game is a separate cartridge, not the open-city build squeezed onto a dual screen.

The film's return of the hero is the license. Only the console side is the open Metropolis; the DS release is its own companion.
band-hero:
Pop vocals and a brighter setlist spin Guitar Hero toward younger players in Band Hero. Activision's 2009 spinoff has a DS edition that is a simpler rhythm game than the console band set.

Console sessions still want a guitar, drums, and a microphone on pop songs. The DS edition strips that living-room rig down to a simpler handheld rhythm game with the same pop lean.

It is not the main Guitar Hero numbered release of the year. The DS cart keeps the spinoff's tone without the full band instruments.
labyrinth:
Sliding corridor tiles open a path to treasure in Labyrinth. Ravensburger's shifting-maze board game came to DS in 2008.

A row or a column shifts, the walls reconnect, and a token moves only along the open line. The handheld version follows that slide-and-seek rather than a free-roaming dungeon.

Treasure cards and the moving maze are the tabletop rules. The DS edition is that board game on a screen.
the-witcher-3-wild-hunt:
Geralt of Rivia takes monster contracts across a wide map in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. CD Projekt Red's 2015 open-world RPG collected a pile of year-end awards, and a demanding Switch port followed in a later year.

Signs, oils, and a silver sword prepare a hunt, while Novigrad, the Skellige isles, and the war with the Wild Hunt fill the roads. Dialogue choices change who survives a contract, not only the sword damage.

The awards followed that scale, without this account naming a single trophy. The Switch port came afterward and is known as a demanding fit of the same hunt.
portal:
GLaDOS watches Chell link two holes in space with a portal gun in Portal. Valve's 2007 puzzle game later reached Switch in the Companion Collection.

One portal is orange and one is blue, and momentum through the pair crosses pits that a jump cannot. The Weighted Companion Cube, turrets, and the cake lie are the Aperture Science furniture around those shots.

The Companion Collection is the Switch home of this test and its sequel. The gun that joins two surfaces is the whole mechanic.
the-elder-scrolls-v-skyrim:
Dragon shouts and a civil war fill Bethesda's often re-released The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. The 2011 fantasy became one of the most re-released RPGs of its decade, including a 2017 Switch port.

The Dragonborn learns Fus Ro Dah, joins or resists the Stormcloaks, and clears barrows full of draugr around Whiterun. That same open map is what kept arriving on new hardware.

The 2017 Switch port is one of those re-releases, not a different Elder Scrolls numbered sequel. Shouts, dragons, and the province of Skyrim are the content that traveled.
bioshock-infinite:
Elizabeth tears open a sky-line above the floating city of Columbia in BioShock Infinite. Irrational Games set the 2013 shooter there, and it was later included in the Switch collection.

Booker DeWitt rides the rails between monuments, and Elizabeth's tears pull in cover, hooks, or a freight car from another possibility. Songbird hunts the pair through Comstock's holiday of flags and racism.

Columbia is not Rapture, even though the series name connects them. The Switch collection later held this sky-line campaign with the other games.
limbo:
A silhouette boy crosses sawblades and a giant spider in Limbo. Playdead's 2010 puzzle-platformer was a breakout indie, and a Switch port followed the original releases.

Bear traps, rising water, and brain-slugs that reverse direction punish a mistimed jump in a black-and-white forest. The only color is a rare glow, usually on the eyes of something hostile.

The breakout reputation came from that wordless hazard course. The Switch port followed the earlier computer and console releases.
doom:
Glory kills keep the pace aggressive in DOOM (2016), and Panic Button later brought that campaign to Switch. id Software rebooted the series as a fast demon shooter rather than a slow corridor crawl.

The Doom Slayer rips a demon for health, and Argent energy feeds weapons across the UAC Mars base. Standing still is the losing plan, which is the reboot's argument with older marine shooters.

Panic Button's Switch campaign is that same aggressive run, not a top-down spinoff. Mars, the Slayer, and the glory-kill heal are what that port had to keep intact.
cyberpunk-2077:
Johnny Silverhand haunts a broken Night City launch in Cyberpunk 2077, the RPG CD Projekt Red shipped in a famously broken state. The 2020 release was rebuilt over years of patches.

V's chrome, fixer gigs, and the Relic's glitching rocker sit inside a dense city of cars and corporate towers. The early weeks were infamous for broken systems, and the later patches rebuilt quests, police, and performance.

Night City is the setting that survived that repair. The launch reputation and the long patch cycle are part of the game's history, not a footnote outside it.
warframe:
Tenno in living suits drop into squad missions in Warframe. Digital Extremes' free-to-play shooter has run as a live game since 2013, and a Switch version joined it.

Warframes, weapons, and foundry crafting change between alerts, while a squad of four revives one another in the Origin system. The live service keeps adding factions rather than ending on a single campaign disc.

The Switch version joined that ongoing game. It is a squad shooter with a persistent foundry, not a one-weekend campaign.
rocket-league:
Octane bodies boost into a soccer ball in Rocket League. Psyonix's 2015 surprise hit is a sequel to Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars, and it later arrived on Switch.

Boost pads, aerial flips, and a demolition send the ball toward a goal the size of a garage. The earlier Battle-Cars game supplied the car-soccer joke, and this sequel made the match a full sport.

The Switch release came after the surprise success. Five-minute matches and overtime goals are the loop.
batman-arkham-knight:
Scarecrow's fear toxin and the Batmobile close Rocksteady's Arkham series in Batman: Arkham Knight. The 2015 game was built around that car on PC and that generation's HD consoles.

Tank sections, the city of Gotham under militia drones, and detective scans share the night with predator rooms full of armed thugs. The Knight's identity and Scarecrow's toxin are the campaign's two pressures.

The Batmobile is not a side gadget here; races and combat use it as a main verb. Rocksteady framed the game for PC and the HD consoles of that generation.
apex-legends:
A dropship throws squads into a shrinking ring in Apex Legends. Respawn's 2019 free shooter spun a battle royale out of the Titanfall universe.

Legends with different tactical kits ping loot, revive teammates, and race the ring on a map born from that universe's frontier. There is no single titan the player pilots as the whole match; the squad and the guns are the round.

The Titanfall connection is the fiction and the movement, not a numbered titan campaign. The free squad format is how the battle royale plays.
hollow-knight:
Hornet and the ruins of Hallownest frame Team Cherry's Hollow Knight. The 2017 hand-drawn bug kingdom became a landmark indie, and the Switch version was part of its wide release.

The Knight swings a nail, banks geo at a bench, and equips charms that change soul healing or attack reach. Benches are the save, and a death drops geo that must be recovered from a shade.

The wide release included the Switch version rather than treating the handheld as an afterthought years later. Hallownest's districts and the charm notches are the exploration.
the-walking-dead:
Clementine follows Lee Everett through Telltale's choice-driven The Walking Dead: Season 1, the comic adaptation that revived the studio's reputation. The 2012 season later reached Switch.

A timed dialogue pick, a withheld axe, or a promise to a child changes who trusts Lee in the next episode. The comic's tone and the episode structure replaced Telltale's earlier reputation for adventure experiments that had gone quiet.

The Switch release came after that reputation shift. Season 1 is Lee and Clementine's story, not the Dixon spinoff shooter.
little-nightmares:
The Janitor's long arms hunt a tiny girl aboard the Maw in Little Nightmares. Tarsier Studios' 2017 game shrinks the player inside that giant hostile ship, and a Switch port followed.

Six climbs spoons, hides under floorboards, and avoids guests who want to eat her. The scale is the horror: doors, shoes, and a chef are all enormous.

The Switch port followed the original release of the ship. The Maw, the Janitor, and Six's lighter are the picture.
bioshock-2:
Eleanor Lamb is the reason Subject Delta wears a Big Daddy suit in BioShock 2, a return to Rapture after the original. 2K Marin put the player in that suit for the 2010 sequel.

A rivet gun, plasmids, and the bond with a Little Sister change the first game's lone wanderer into a protector. Sofia Lamb's cult in the dripping art deco halls is the new ideology on the ocean floor.

Rapture is the same city, seen from the suit that used to be the enemy. The sequel is Delta and Eleanor, not a second visit as Jack.
stardew-valley:
Community Center bundles pull a farmer through seasons in Stardew Valley. ConcernedApe built the 2016 life sim largely alone, and the Switch version became one of its biggest platforms.

Parsnips, a mine elevator, and Pelican Town festivals share the calendar with romance and a failing JojaMart alternative. The Community Center or the Joja route decides how the town recovers.

The solo development is part of the story of the game, and the Switch version grew into one of its biggest platforms. Fishing, farming, and the mines are the days.
hotline-miami:
Jacket answers phone calls and wears animal masks in Hotline Miami. Dennaton's 2012 top-down violence puzzle is scored like a club track, and a Switch port came later.

One hit kills the masked intruder or the guard, so a door swing and a thrown weapon are a plan, not a health bar. The soundtrack's pulse is as identifying as the pixel blood.

The Switch port arrived after the computer original. The phone, the mask, and the one-hit rooms are the loop.
bioshock-remastered:
A bathysphere still descends to Andrew Ryan's Rapture in BioShock Remastered. Irrational's 2007 shooter was polished up for this 2016 remaster, which later sat inside the Switch collection.

Splicers, the wrench, and the would-you-kindly twist remain the campaign, with cleaner textures than the first release. The remaster is a polish of that Rapture trip, not a new city.

The Switch collection later included this polished edition alongside the other Rapture and Columbia stories. Ryan's lighthouse is still the front door.
outlast:
Miles Upshur films Mount Massive Asylum with a camcorder and no gun in Outlast. Red Barrels' 2013 horror game was later ported to Switch.

Night vision eats batteries, and the only defense is a locker or a sprint from a variant in the halls. Notes about the Murkoff experiments explain the inmates while the camera shakes.

The Switch port came after the original release. The camcorder, the asylum, and the lack of weapons are the rules.
hellblade-senuas-sacrifice:
Senua hears voices while Ninja Theory walks her through Helheim in Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice. The 2017 game was developed with mental-health advisors, and a Switch port followed the PC and console release.

Binaural whispers comment on puzzles of Norse runes and on fights with spectral enemies. The advisors shaped how those voices are presented, which is the production fact attached to the journey.

The Switch port followed the earlier machines. Senua, the voices, and the advisors are the distinctive frame, not a silent dungeon crawl.
hitman-absolution:
Agent 47 takes a more linear path after Blood Money in Hitman: Absolution. IO Interactive's 2012 story is that follow-up, before the World of Assassination reboot.

Disguises and instinct still open a room, but the missions pull 47 along a tighter plot than the earlier sandbox hits. The World of Assassination trilogy later rebooted the series into larger sandbox levels.

Absolution sits between Blood Money and that reboot. The linear Agent 47 story is the shape of this one.
la-noire:
Doubt, lie, and truth reads sit on facial capture in L.A. Noire. Team Bondi's 2011 detective game, published by Rockstar, is famous for those interrogations, and it was later ported to Switch.

Cole Phelps moves from traffic to homicide desks in a rebuilt Los Angeles, and a suspect's eyebrow can be the clue. The facial-capture interviews are why the game is remembered beside its cases.

Rockstar published Team Bondi's investigation. The Switch port came later, carrying the same desk-by-desk cases and the same face reads.
metro-last-light-redux:
Artyom returns to the Moscow tunnels after the Dark Ones in Metro: Last Light Redux. 4A Games' post-nuclear sequel was cleaned up as this 2014 Redux, part of the Redux pair later brought to Switch.

Filters, homemade shells, and a moral thread about the child of the Dark Ones distinguish the sequel from the first descent. Redux is the cleaned-up edition of that sequel, not a new plot.

The Redux pair later reached Switch together. Last Light is the sequel half, D6 and the surface ruins included.
metro-redux:
Exhibition station and a newer engine rebuild the first metro trek as Metro 2033 Redux. 4A Games' 2014 Redux edition of the Moscow-metro shooter later reached Switch.

Artyom still crosses Hansa checkpoints and spirit-haunted tunnels, but the Redux engine replaces the original's older presentation. It is the rebuilt first game, not the sequel's plot under a similar title.

The Switch arrival came with the Redux pair. Ranger difficulty and the cartridge scavenger hunt belong to this rebuilt 2033 story, told again on the newer engine.
hades-2018:
Zagreus climbs out of the underworld through repeated escapes in Hades. Supergiant's roguelike left early access to huge acclaim in 2020, and the finished game launched on Switch at the same time.

Boons from Olympians change the next room, while Hypnos, Megaera, and Hades himself comment when the escape fails and the prince wakes at the house. Weapons on the rack remember upgrades between those deaths.

Early access was the long test, and the finish is the full release. Switch received that finished game in the same launch window, not years later.
bioshock-2-remastered:
A cleaner coat of paint on 2K Marin's Rapture sequel is BioShock 2 Remastered. The same remaster wave that updated the first Rapture game produced this 2016 release.

Subject Delta's bond with Eleanor Lamb, the rivet gun, and Sofia Lamb's sermons remain the campaign under sharper textures. It is a cleaner release of the sequel, not a new visit with a different Big Daddy.

The first game's remaster was the other half of that wave. This one stays Delta's story, only cleaner.
nierautomata:
2B and 9S carry YoRHa's war against machines in NieR:Automata. PlatinumGames and director Yoko Taro made the 2017 breakout action RPG, later ported to Switch.

Pod fire, hacking as 9S, and multiple routes through the same ruined city change what the androids learn about their orders. Ending routes are part of the design, not a single credits roll.

The Switch port came after the breakout on other machines. Yoko Taro's structure and Platinum's combat are the combination that traveled.
fall-guys:
Hex-A-Gone floors and a crown qualifier define Fall Guys: Ultimate Knockout. Mediatonic's 2020 obstacle-course brawl became a costume knockout show and later went free-to-play, including on Switch.

Seesaws, doors, and a final hill eliminate bean-shaped contestants until one grabs the crown. Costume pieces from each show became the joke as much as the finish.

The later free-to-play shift included the Switch edition. The round is still a short obstacle show, not a sports season with a league table.
resident-evil-7-biohazard:
Jack Baker's Louisiana house turns the series into a first-person haunt in Resident Evil 7: Biohazard. Capcom's 2017 game is that softer reboot after years of action-heavy sequels.

Ethan Winters searches the Dulvey household for Mia, with a flashlight, a limited handgun, and the mold family blocking the halls. The camera sits in Ethan's eyes, which is the break from Leon's over-the-shoulder campaigns.

The Baker dinner, the videotapes, and the mold are the new frame. It is a reboot in tone, not Resident Evil 6 with a different cover.
bastion:
Rucks narrates every step the Kid takes through a fallen Caelondia in Bastion. Supergiant's 2011 debut is an action RPG whose narrator comments on what the player just did, later ported to Switch.

Weapons and tonics change the next fight, and Rucks's line reacts if the Kid walks off a ledge or chooses a risky shard. The narration is diegetic, spoken by the man at the Bastion core, not a tutorial caption.

The Switch port followed the original releases. The Kid, Rucks, and the rebuilding Bastion are the debut's shape.
paladins:
Champion cards and a free roster fill Hi-Rez Studios' Paladins. The 2016 hero shooter joined the wave of class-based team games, with a Switch version following.

A loadout of cards tweaks a champion before the match, and the objective is a team push rather than a lone high score. The Switch version followed the live game onto the hybrid hardware.

It sits in the same era as other class shooters, with champions instead of a single military class. Cards and the free roster are the pre-match choices.
ark-survival-evolved:
Taming pens and dinosaur saddles fill Studio Wildcard's enormous PC sandbox ARK: Survival Evolved. The 2015 survival game is huge on PC, and the Switch port was a notably compromised version of that world.

A tranquilizer, kibble, and a saddle turn a wild dinosaur into a mount, while hunger and a thatch hut decide the night. The Island's obelisks and the creature roster are the PC scale.

The Switch port was notably compromised beside that PC world. Taming and base building are the fantasy that the smaller version had to cut down.
cities-skylines:
Highway exits and zoning squares build Colossal Order's Cities: Skylines. The 2015 city builder picked up players after SimCity's troubled relaunch, and a Switch port followed.

Traffic jams, water pipes, and district policies punish a pretty map that does not actually flow. The SimCity relaunch's trouble sent mayors looking for this alternative.

The Switch port followed the computer city. It is a traffic-and-zoning builder, not a toy diorama with no commuters.
undertale:
A spare option at the Ruins door defines Toby Fox's Undertale. The 2015 RPG lets players spare monsters instead of fighting them, a surprise hit later brought to Switch.

Toriel's battle can end without a kill, and that choice echoes through later areas with Sans, Papyrus, and the Underground. The surprise hit grew from those mercy routes as much as from the jokes.

The Switch version came after the computer surprise. Sparing, rather than grinding every encounter, is the allowed path.
unturned:
Nelson Sexton, a teenager at the time, released the free zombie survival game Unturned. It spread widely on PC after the 2014 release.

Low-poly towns, crafted guns, and a permadeath run against zombies are the PC sandbox that players passed around. The teen developer and the free release are why it traveled so far on computers.

The spread was a PC story. Crafting and the zombie towns are the mode, built by Sexton rather than by a large studio team.
brothers-a-tale-of-two-sons-2:
One thumbstick steers each brother in Josef Fares' Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons. The 2013 adventure puts the older brother on one stick and the younger on the other, and a Switch port followed the original consoles.

A climb, a lever, and a swim need both boys at once, so each hand keeps its own sibling. The story is told without readable dialogue, through the cooperative body puzzle.

The Switch port followed the first console releases. The two-stick brothers are the control idea Fares built the journey on.
titan-attacks:
Bunker shields and a score attack homage to Space Invaders are Puppy Games' Titan Attacks! Curve later published it on 3DS, and the blaster is from 2012.

Waves of invaders descend, and a shot clears them while bunkers crack under return fire. The homage is deliberate: a modern score attack wearing the silhouette of the arcade invader line.

Curve's 3DS publishing brought that score attack to the handheld. Points, waves, and the bunkers are the round.
castlevania-los-mirror-of-fate-hd:
Simon, Trevor, and Alucard share MercurySteam's side-view tale Castlevania: Lords of Shadow - Mirror of Fate. The 2013 adventure debuted on 3DS inside the Lords of Shadow continuity, with HD ports afterward.

Whip combat and a family timeline tie those three heroes into Gabriel's Lords of Shadow story rather than the older search-action continuity. The 3DS release came first, and HD ports on other machines followed.

Mirror of Fate is the side-view bridge in that continuity. The handheld debut is the original home, not a demake of an HD game.
need-for-speed-the-run:
A stopwatch and a cross-country route define Need for Speed: The Run. EA's 2011 race against the clock has Wii and 3DS editions that are separate from the HD drive.

The HD version is a scripted dash across the country with cinematic wrecks between stages. Wii and 3DS do not reuse that HD drive; each is its own edition of the clock race.

The deadline, not an open city of parked cars, is the pressure. Handheld editions stay separate from the HD presentation.
zero-escape-zero-time-dilemma:
Kotaro Uchikoshi closes the Zero Escape trilogy with the Decision Game in Zero Escape: Zero Time Dilemma. The 2016 adventure shipped on 3DS, Vita, and PC as locked-room choices.

Teams wake in fragments of a timeline, and a vote or a puzzle can strand one group while another moves. It follows Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors and Virtue's Last Reward rather than starting a new series.

3DS, Vita, and PC all carry those locked-room decisions. Uchikoshi's trilogy ends on this fragmented vote, not on another ship.
urban-trial-freestyle:
Wheelie gaps and hard crashes define the bike-trials game URBAN TRIAL FREESTYLE. Obstacle courses are the 2013 challenge, which received a 3DS version.

A restart after a bent landing is normal, and the timer judges a clean line through ramps and containers. The courses and the crashes are the whole identity of the bike.

The 3DS version carries those urban obstacle runs. It is a trials bike game, not a traffic race with a city map.
bloodstained-curse-of-the-moon:
Zangetsu slashes through an 8-bit-style curse in Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon. Inti Creates made the 2018 action game with Koji Igarashi producing, and a 3DS version was released.

Limited lives, stage bosses, and a retro sprite scale recall a classic side-scroller while Igarashi produces. The 3DS version is one of the places that pixel campaign shipped.

It is the retro companion in the Bloodstained line, not the larger castle exploration with Miriam's shard set as the only face. Zangetsu's stages and the 3DS release are this game.
streets-of-rage-2:
Blaze Fielding and Axel Stone lead Sega's Genesis brawler Streets of Rage 2, usually ranked as the high point of that trilogy. The 1992 game was later reissued on Virtual Console for Wii and 3DS.

Weapons on the pavement, a cooperative partner, and Yuzo Koshiro's driving soundtrack mark the sequel fans put above the first and third outings. The Virtual Console reissues on Wii and 3DS brought that Genesis high point back.

It is not a new brawler with a modern camera. The reissues are the Genesis game on those Virtual Console shops.
pokemon-y:
Mega Evolution and a fully 3D Kalos region arrive together in Pokémon X, Y, Game Freak's mainline pair on 3DS. That fully dimensional presentation arrived in 2013.

Lumiose City, a group of friends, and the Mega stones change a battle when a held stone triggers mid-fight. Fairy-type matchups and the new camera sit alongside that Mega system.

X and Y are the pair that introduced Mega Evolution. The 3DS generation's first fully 3D mainline games are these two.
a-link-between-worlds:
Ravio rents items while Link merges into a wall painting in The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds. Nintendo's 2013 adventure revisits the shape of A Link to the Past, then lets Link move along walls.

Lorule mirrors Hyrule, and a merge into a crack bypasses a gap that the old top-down sword swing could not cross. The rental shop means the item set is borrowed rather than found once and kept forever.

The Nintendo 3DS eShop has since closed, so the wall-merge quest does not imply a storefront still selling it. It remains the 3DS Zelda that paints Link onto the wall.
garfield-kart:
Odie and the lasagna cat share a budget kart in Garfield Kart. Microids put that comic-strip cast on 3DS in 2013.

Drifting around simple cups and themed tracks is a low-cost race rather than a simulation of real circuits. Garfield's laziness is the joke on the character select, not a handling model.

The 3DS release is that budget kart. Comic timing and a small roster are the package, not a licensed motorsport season.
the-legend-of-zelda-ocarina-of-time-3d:
Grezzo rebuilt the Temple of Time quest, gyro aiming included, as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time 3D. The Nintendo 64 adventure became this 2011 3DS remake with updated graphics.

The Master Sword, the ocarina songs, and Sheik's appearances return under a clearer texture set, and gyro aiming steadies a bow or a slingshot. It is a remake of the 64 quest, not a new timeline branch.

Water Temple routes and the Song of Time still structure the adventure. Gyro control and the updated look are what Grezzo added for the handheld.
pokemon-sun:
Professor Kukui's island trials replace gyms in Pokémon Sun, Moon. Game Freak's 2016 Alola pair on 3DS is built around Z-Moves.

A trial captain, a totem Pokémon, and a Z-Ring dance take the place of a badge podium. Regional forms and the festival battle at the league still sit on the 3DS pair.

Sun and Moon are that Alola experiment together. Z-Moves and the island challenge are the break from the gym circuit.
pokemon-omega-ruby:
Hoenn's seas return with Mega Evolution in Pokémon Alpha Sapphire, Omega Ruby. Game Freak's 2014 remakes bring that battle system back to the 3DS journeys through the old region.

Team Magma or Team Aqua, depending on the cart, still chase the legendary weather of Hoenn, now with Mega stones in the bag. The remakes are not the original Game Boy Advance carts with a new label.

Alpha Sapphire and Omega Ruby are the pair of remakes. Mega Evolution is the system those 3DS journeys add to Hoenn.
super-mario-3d-land:
A Tanooki tail and stereoscopic depth showcase Super Mario 3D Land. Nintendo's 2011 platformer was an early demonstration of the 3DS.

The tail spin breaks blocks and slows a fall, while the stereoscopic picture separates a pit from a platform in front of the face. Flagpoles, Boom Boom, and a second set of harder stages extend the postcard worlds.

The early-showcase role matters because the hardware's depth effect is part of the jump. Tanooki flight and the binocular staging are the handheld's Mario pitch.
wheel-of-fortune:
A spinning wheel and missing letters bring the television word puzzle to DS as Wheel of Fortune. The 2010 edition fills in those letters the way the show does.

A toss hits Bankrupt or a dollar wedge, then a consonant guess reveals tiles on the board. The handheld game follows the show's wheel and the fill-in rather than a crossword magazine.

Bankrupt wedges and a category board still decide the score. The round is the wheel, the phrase, and the letter guess.
kirby-super-star-ultra:
Helper to Hero and other extra games expand the SNES anthology in Kirby Super Star Ultra. HAL Laboratory and Nintendo's 2008 remake puts those additions on the cart above Kirby Super Star.

Copy abilities still create a helper, and Ultra's extra modes, including Helper to Hero, sit on top of the SNES lineup of short games. The Great Cave Offensive and the arena return with the new material beside them.

The SNES original has its own separate entry. Ultra is the expanded remake, extra games included, not the 16-bit cart by another name.
warioware-touched:
Microphone blows and touch-screen taps fuel the first WarioWare built for the DS, WarioWare: Touched! Intelligent Systems made that 2004 microgame set around the new hardware.

A prompt lasts a couple of seconds: slice, rub, shout, or blow, then the next joke starts. Wario hosts the menu, and the hardware trick is the punchline of many of the tiny games.

It is the first WarioWare made for the DS, so later touch entries had this one as the experiment. The microphone and the stylus are mandatory, not optional flavor.
you-dont-know-jack:
Wrong answers get mocked in Jackbox's touch-screen revival You Don't Know Jack HD. The 2011 sarcastic trivia show is a different product from the older console Jack games and is not a DS original.

A question's joke is the point, and the touch interface is how this HD revival asks it. Older console Jack episodes are a separate line, and this product was not born as a DS cartridge.

The sarcasm and the high-speed wrong-answer punishment are the show. Treating it as a DS launch title would misfile the touch-screen revival.
jagged-alliance:
Sir-Tech hired turn-based mercenaries for the PC campaign Jagged Alliance. The 1994 tactics game began on computers, long before any handheld reused the name.

Contracts, ammo, and a mercenary's attitude decide a firefight on the PC map. A later handheld that borrowed the title is not this computer campaign moved onto a small screen.

Metavira-style hiring and the turn grid are the PC game's reputation. The name's later reuse does not make that tactics game a DS original.
hotel-dusk-room-215:
Kyle Hyde questions guests while the hardware is held sideways like a book in Hotel Dusk: Room 215, Cing's point-and-click mystery. The 2007 story is set in that rundown hotel.

Room numbers, a red-tinted past, and conversations in the lobby replace combat. The sideways hold makes the screens read like an open paperback during the investigation.

The hotel's faded guests are the cast. Cing's book-like presentation is as identifying as the missing-person plot.
sega-superstars-tennis:
Ulala and other Sega stars turn a volley into a minigame nod in SEGA Superstars Tennis. Sumo Digital's 2008 tennis game includes a DS version full of those character asides.

A special shot can drop the match into a short reference to the character's own series, then return to the court. The DS version carries that cameo idea onto a handheld.

It is a Sega crossover tennis game, not a licensed athlete season. The minigame nods are the reason the roster is not generic.
mario-party-ds:
Hudson built stylus minigames around a board in Mario Party DS. The 2007 party game brings the series' stars and boards to the dual screen.

A board still hands out stars, while many events ask for a rub, a blow, or a tap that the television entries could not demand. The story curse and the handheld boards are this cart's framing.

Stylus events are the DS idea on top of the familiar star race. Hudson's party structure stays: board, minigames, stars.
castlevania-portrait-of-ruin:
Jonathan Morris and Charlotte Aulin swap in and out during Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin. Konami's DS search-action game from 2006 lets the pair share one castle crawl.

Paintings become doors to other locales, and the partner left in reserve can be called for a spell or a whip strike. The dual leads are the difference from a lone Belmont walk.

That crawl is the portrait castle with those two heroes. Swapping them is the verb, not a costume change on one fighter.
brain-challenge:
Short memory drills from Gameloft ride the brain-training boom in Brain Challenge. The 2008 DS package followed the wave that Nintendo's own series had started.

A few-second test of memory, logic, or focus fills a session, then a score sits on a chart. It is Gameloft's set, not Nintendo's Brain Age under a new cover.

The boom after Nintendo's series is why so many of these drills existed. Brain Challenge is Gameloft's contribution to that shelf.
fire-emblem-shadow-dragon:
Marth reclaims Altea in Intelligent Systems' remake Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon. The 2009 DS strategy RPG retells the first Fire Emblem, the story western players had mostly missed.

Permadeath, weapon triangles, and the prince's campaign follow the original war rather than the later lords western boxes had already shown. Replacement units can fill a grave if a cavalier falls.

Western players meeting Marth here were often meeting that first tale for the first time. Shadow Dragon is the DS remake of it, not a sequel about a new continent.
nintendogs-labrador-friends:
A Labrador answers a microphone whistle in Nintendogs: Labrador & Friends. The 2005 pack is one of the three DS launch sets, using the touch screen and the mic to care for virtual puppies.

Brushing, a walk, and a contest use the stylus, while a voice into the microphone calls the dog. The other launch packs swapped the breed; this one is the Labrador and friends.

It is a care simulation of puppies, not a breed encyclopedia. The launch-window pack and the Labrador focus are this cartridge.
sonic-rush:
Blaze the Cat arrives alongside a boost dash in Sonic Rush. Dimps built the 2005 DS game with tall dual-screen stages for that handheld.

The boost meter spends rings for a burst, and the camera climbs both screens during a long vertical loop. Blaze's story runs beside Sonic's on those tall stages.

It is a Sonic built for the DS, not a port of a home-console zone list. The boost and the dual-screen height are the layout.
iron-man-2:
Whiplash and the suitcase armor follow the second Marvel film in Sega's Iron Man 2, an action tie-in with a DS game alongside the consoles. The licensed set arrived in 2010.

The film's new enemies and the traveling suit frame the licensed missions. The DS game sits in that same tie-in wave, as the first film's game had done with its own handheld.

It is the sequel film's license, not a reprint of the first Iron Man cartridge. Sega's second tie-in is that set.
dragons-lair-2-time-warp:
Dirk chases Daphne through time in Don Bluth's laserdisc sequel Dragon's Lair II: Time Warp. The 1991 cartoon continues the animated quick-time adventures that began with Dragon's Lair.

A late direction press still cuts to a comic death, and the scenes hop eras instead of staying in one castle. Mordroc and the time jumps are the sequel's additions on top of Dirk's timed lunges.

It is not free movement between the pictures. The handheld listing carries that same animated sequel rather than a newly drawn platformer.
juiced-2-hot-import-nights:
Night imports and street duels fill THQ's sequel Juiced 2: Hot Import Nights. The street-racing follow-up from 2007 includes a DS edition made for that release.

Custom cars and after-dark races continue the Juiced line rather than a licensed touring series. The DS edition was built for this sequel's launch, not pasted on years later from a different racer.

Show cars and street competition are the night scene. The handheld edition belongs to that sequel rather than to a touring series.
puzzle-chronicles:
Rune matches and a party of fighters carry another Puzzle Quest-family game, Puzzle Chronicles. The 2010 match-puzzle RPG shipped with a DS version.

Gems still pay for attacks, while the campaign and the cast are their own chronicle rather than a renamed sequel in the Puzzle Quest family. The DS version is part of that family release.

No extra studio line is required to place it: the match-puzzle role and the family resemblance are the description. The handheld version shares the gem battles.
rhythm-heaven:
A flick of the stylus is the joke in Nintendo's Rhythm Heaven. Short rhythm scenes from 2008 use a tap, and that flick is the hardware gag.

A chorus line, a golf swing, or a robot assembly asks for the flick at the right beat, and a miss gets a comic groan. The DS game sits between the Game Boy Advance entry that stayed in Japan and the later Wii and 3DS entries.

Those bookends matter: the Advance game did not leave Japan, and the Wii and 3DS games came after this flick-based set. The DS edition is the one where the stylus flick is the recurring punchline.
metroid-prime-hunters:
Sylux and other rival bounty hunters duel Samus on two screens in Metroid Prime Hunters. Nintendo's 2006 shooter is the DS Prime spin-off, not a numbered console sequel.

The touch screen steers a shot while the local wireless mode drops several hunters into one arena. Weavel, Kanden, and the other rivals each bring a weapon the campaign also uses.

Prime Hunters is not Prime 4 and not a decimal chapter of the home-console trilogy. Local wireless fights and the rival roster are the spin-off's extras.
locks-quest:
Clockwork soldiers test the walls Lock builds by day in Lock's Quest. 5th Cell's 2008 DS strategy game switches to a siege when night arrives.

Daytime is for placing turrets and repairing stone, and the night wave spends that preparation. A gap left in the wall is where the clockwork army walks in.

The day-and-night split is the whole loop. Lock's name is on the quest because the walls are his job, not because a separate hero fights in his place.
cars-mater-national:
Radiator Springs crowns Pixar's tow truck in Disney•Pixar Cars Mater-National Championship. The 2007 racing tie-in puts Mater at the head of the poster, and a DS version was part of that Cars spinoff.

Lightning McQueen still shows up, but the events lean on Mater's tow-truck personality and the town's dirt tracks. The DS version belongs to that spinoff rather than to the first film's original tie-in.

National championship events are the structure. The handheld cart is part of the Mater-fronted set.
professor-layton-and-the-last-specter:
Luke Triton meets the professor during a prequel specter case in Professor Layton and the Last Specter. Level-5's 2011 fourth DS puzzle adventure is called Spectre's Call in Europe.

Misthallery's rumors, a new assistant's introduction, and a suitcase of puzzles frame a story set before the curious village. The European name Spectre's Call is the same prequel, not a fifth case.

It is the fourth DS Layton game on the calendar and a prequel in the plot. The specter mystery is where the partnership starts.
frogger-returns:
Logs, lily pads, and highway lanes call the arcade hopper back in Frogger Returns. Konami's 2009 DS revival sends Frogger across that traffic again.

A mistimed hop into a truck or a sinking turtle ends the crossing the way the cabinet did. The revival adds handheld stages around that same perpendicular traffic.

It is a return to the hopper, not a racing game that only borrowed the green sprite. The DS revival keeps the lane-by-lane risk.
final-fantasy-tactics-a2-grimoire-of-the:
Luso Clemens joins a clan under Ivalice laws in Final Fantasy Tactics A2: Grimoire of the Rift. Square Enix's 2008 DS strategy RPG follows Final Fantasy Tactics Advance with another job system in that world.

Clan trials, a judge's law for the battle, and jobs changing a unit's weapon sit on the tactical grid. The rift and the clan notice board are the campaign's structure after Tactics Advance.

Ivalice is the shared setting, and the laws still punish a forbidden action mid-fight. A2 is the DS follow-up, with Luso's clan as the party.
dragon-quest-ix:
Angel Falls and a class-changing party anchor Dragon Quest IX: Sentinels of the Starry Skies. Level-5 and Square Enix's 2009 DS mainline quest was built for street-pass guests as much as for a solo story.

Vocations swap a hero from mage to martial artist, and a passing player's guest can join the inn. Grotto maps and the Celestrian opening stretch the solo plot, while the local guests are the multiplayer half.

It is the DS mainline Dragon Quest, not a spinoff gaiden. Local play and the vocation party are equal parts of the design.
pokemon-mystery-dungeon-explorers-of-tim:
Time gears go missing around Wigglytuff's Guild in Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Explorers of Time. Chunsoft's DS roguelike from 2008 is one half of the Explorers pair, alongside Explorers of Darkness.

A human who wakes as a Pokémon joins the guild and climbs procedural floors where fainting can cost the bag. Darkness is the partner version, with its own exclusives beside this Time cart.

Sky later adds episodes on top of both. Time is one half of the original pair, not that expanded third cartridge.
pokemon-ranger-shadows-of-almia:
Almia's stylus loops continue the capture line in Pokémon Ranger: Shadows of Almia. The 2008 spinoff is the second game after Pokemon Ranger, still drawing circles instead of opening a battle menu.

The Capture Styler returns in a new region, with a ranger school and a crisis that the first region's union does not host. Shadows in the title point at that Almia plot, not at a rerelease of the first styler.

Pokemon Ranger, the first game, is the predecessor named without an accent on its title. Almia is the second stylus-capture assignment.
battleship:
Alien warships crash the naval film's license in BATTLESHIP. The 2012 tie-in shipped with a DS version in that same wave.

Fleet targets and the movie's sci-fi navy replace a pure pencil-and-paper grid of the tabletop game. The DS version belongs to the film wave rather than to a standalone board adaptation with no aliens.

Aliens in the harbor are the film's addition to the old fleet name. The handheld cart rides that movie wave rather than a quiet parlor adaptation.
bejeweled-twist:
Rotating a cluster of gems replaces a swap in PopCap's Bejeweled Twist. The 2008 match-three spinoff of Bejeweled turns the board instead of exchanging two jewels.

A twist lines up three gems, and the chain can start from a rotation the original swap game never asked for. Special gems still explode, but the hand motion is the turn.

It is a spinoff, so the classic swap mode is the parent game. Twist is the rotation puzzle in that family.
simcity-3000:
Landmark buildings and deeper zoning define Maxis's PC city builder SimCity 3000, a different game from the later DS SimCity. The computer sim is the 1999 city tool.

Ordinances, waste, and a news ticker sit on the computer city alongside the new landmarks. The DS game that reused the SimCity name is not this zoning model in a pocket.

That PC edition is the one with those landmarks and the deeper zoning. A later handheld SimCity does not replace it.
mahjong:
Dragon tiles and bamboo suits clear in pairs from a stacked layout in Mahjong. The 2009 DS solitaire take on the table game removes those free pairs.

A tile must be open on the left or the right, and matching the dragon or the season removes only that couple. It is one player's puzzle, not a four-player reach for a winning hand.

A free dragon leaves only when its match is also free. The DS session is that stacked solitaire, distinct from later deluxe sequels on other hardware.
space-ace:
Dexter flips between a hero and a child under Borf's Infanto Ray in Space Ace. Don Bluth's laserdisc follow-up to Dragon's Lair is that animated quick-time game, later reissued on DS.

Kimberly waits in the scenes, and a late button press still cuts to a cartoon failure the way Dirk's deaths did. The DS reissue brings those Infanto Ray scenes to the handheld.

A DS reissue in 2009 puts those same scenes on a handheld. The play stays animated timing, not free running between the pictures.
the-settlers-2-veni-vidi-vici:
Roman roads and haulers carrying goods define Blue Byte's The Settlers 2: Veni, Vidi, Vici. The PC strategy game from 1996 is remembered far from any DS shelf.

A village grows when settlers walk goods between a woodcutter and a sawmill, and the Roman theme dresses that economy. The reputation lives on computers, not as a handheld original that happened to share a name.

Veni, Vidi, Vici is the subtitle of that PC village builder. A DS listing of the name does not turn that economy into a dual-screen original.
yoshis-island-ds:
Baby Bowser, Baby Peach, and Baby Mario ride Yoshi in Yoshi's Island DS. Artoon's 2006 follow-up to the Super Nintendo classic puts baby Mario on Yoshi's back again, with the other babies changing the kit.

An egg throw and a flutter jump return, while a different baby on the saddle adds a move the SNES game did not split across a nursery. The DS platformer is that return, not the original SNES cartridge.

Artoon's sequel keeps the pastel island and the crying baby timer. The extra babies are the handheld's new passengers.
rocks-and-rockets:
Meteor waves fall toward a city while rockets answer them in Rocks and Rockets. TikGames' 2011 DSiWare arcade game is that last-second defense.

A missed rock damages the skyline, and the rocket supply is the only tool. The DSiWare release is a short score defense, not a story campaign with cutscenes.

TikGames built the meteor fight for that shop. City, rocks, and rockets are the entire toy.
the-sims-2-pets:
Kitten bowls and dog walks expand the PC life sim in The Sims 2: Pets. EA's 2006 pet expansion added animals to that computer game, while the DS release is a separate handheld about looking after creatures.

On PC the expansion drops pets into an existing household of the life sim. The DS release does not play as that expansion pack; it is its own creature-care handheld.

The split matters because the name is shared and the products are not. Computer households gain pets in the expansion, and the DS game is a different way of looking after animals.
rayman-raving-rabbids-2:
Ubisoft sent the white rabbits back to work in Rayman Raving Rabbids 2, a party-minigame sequel, and the Nintendo DS copy was part of that 2007 set. Rayman stays the straight man while the Rabbids seize plungers, cows, and ridiculous costumes.

Each event is a short challenge rather than a long side-scrolling journey. Players shake, tap, or scribble, and the next gag starts before a plot can thicken.

The earlier Raving Rabbids game had already shoved the limbless hero aside for the rabbits' jokes. This numbered follow-up commits to the party format, with the handheld cartridge cutting that idea into smaller bursts.
f1-2011:
Codemasters delivered the official Formula 1 season as F1 2011, and the Nintendo 3DS release is the cut-down companion to the console simulation. A shorter weekend, pit stops, and the real team cars remain, without the home version's full garage depth.

Braking points and tire wear still decide a corner, though the circle pad simplifies the homework. Fuel strategy survives, and a single boost button does not replace it.

Drivers who wanted long practice stints and a deep setup screen stayed on the television version. The handheld build exists so one grand prix weekend fits a commute.
kami:
One color has to flood the whole page in KAMI, the paper-fold puzzle, and a Nintendo 3DS eShop version of that indie was released. The last hue you choose must cover every region of the folded sheet.

A tap spills paint across a bordered patch. Extra creases, a locked color, and a strict move count turn the fill into planning.

No timer duel and no chapter plot interrupt the sheets. The handheld edition keeps the same paper-flood idea the indie started with.
the-legend-of-zelda-majoras-mask-3d:
Grezzo rebuilt the falling-moon quest as The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask 3D in 2015, after that studio's Ocarina of Time 3D. Termina still collapses unless Link plays the Song of Time and rewinds the three-day clock.

The Bombers' notebook, Clock Town's carnival, and the Deku, Goron, and Zora masks all return with revised controls. A gyroscope can aim the bow, and saving is less cruel than the Nintendo 64 dawn reset.

Skull Kid's curse and the inverted Stone Tower remain the late-game tests. The remake retunes how those masks are used rather than replacing Termina with another kingdom.
animal-crossing-new-leaf:
Mayor's duties define Animal Crossing: New Leaf, the 2012 mainline town life on Nintendo 3DS that players kept open for years. Isabelle runs the town hall, and public-works projects slowly reshape the map.

Ordinances, Tortimer Island tours, and the Happy Home Showcase sit beside the usual bug and fossil hunts. Friends still visit, but the mayor's chair is the change from earlier villages.

Main Street grows when bridges, benches, and a cafe get approved. Seasons and the museum keep the daily loop that made the series a long stay.
the-great-ace-attorney-chronicles:
Ryunosuke Naruhodo stands in a British court in The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles, Capcom's pair of historical trials from Japan. Susato Mikotoba assists him, the Old Bailey jurors replace a single judge, and the Nintendo 3DS originals from 2015 later became a worldwide collection.

Herlock Sholmes dances through a deduction the player has to correct. Adventures comes first, and Resolve continues the Meiji-era story.

Victorian London and a Japanese courtroom supply the witnesses. Most players outside Japan met that ancestor of Phoenix Wright through the bundled release.
fire-emblem-awakening:
Chrom's Shepherds and a custom tactician carry Fire Emblem Awakening, the 2012 Intelligent Systems tactics game widely credited with saving the series. Robin can marry into the army, and casual mode lets a fallen ally sit out a map instead of dying for good.

Pair-up boosts and the weapon triangle still decide the Nintendo 3DS battles. Children arrive from the future once supports deepen, which is the system players still name first.

The series story treats this entry as the one that earned further games. Unit pairing, not a new continent's gimmick alone, is the reason that credit stuck.
alter-world:
Hopping between copies of a room is the trick of Alter World, a platformer first sold on the New Nintendo 3DS eShop. The same stage exists in more than one version, and the swap is how a blocked ledge opens.

A shifted enemy, a missing floor, or a moved switch can be the only change after the jump. Timing that hop matters more than a long attack string.

No famous mascot and no cutscene saga carry the levels. Progress is the moment the second copy of a stage reveals the platform the first copy hid.
pokemon-ultra-sun:
Necrozma's light expands the Alola story in Pokémon Ultra Sun, Ultra Moon, Game Freak's 2017 follow-up with a larger plot than Sun and Moon. Ultra Wormholes and the Ultra Recon Squad are the new threads on Nintendo 3DS.

Totem battles and Z-Moves remain, yet the crisis pushes past the first league ending. Necrozma can fuse with Solgaleo or Lunala depending on the box.

The original pair's legendaries still decide which version a player holds. This release is the longer Alola telling, not a trip to a brand-new region.
mario-kart-7:
Hang gliders and underwater driving arrived with Mario Kart 7, Nintendo's kart racer for the stereoscopic handheld. Coins on the asphalt raise top speed, an older idea restored when the 2011 cups added air and water on Nintendo 3DS.

Glider pads launch the kart, and submerged sections use their own handling. Neo Bowser City, Wuhu Island, and a revived Kalimari Desert share the roster of tracks.

A first-person camera sits among the view options. Those air and water sections are the gimmicks this handheld entry added.
puyo-puyo-tetris:
Sonic Team smashed color blobs into falling tetrominoes in Puyo Puyo Tetris, a 2014 versus puzzle that reached Nintendo 3DS. One well clears groups of four matching Puyos, and the other clears completed lines.

Swap, Fusion, and Party are among the rule sets that mix the two boards. A match can flip which rule you are stuck with before the round ends.

Characters from both puzzles taunt across the pair of wells. The handheld copy is the portable seat at that crossover, using the same rulebook.
bloo-kid-2:
Brief hop-and-run rooms make up Bloo Kid 2, the numbered indie sequel on the Nintendo 3DS eShop. A pit, a moving platform, or one enemy is often the whole obstacle in this 2014 follow-up.

The blue hero's jump arc is the skill later stages test. Runs end in a short burst rather than an exploring map.

The first Bloo Kid set that tight length, and this follow-up keeps it. Extra hazards appear, but a stage still finishes fast.
new-super-mario-bros-2:
Gold coins are the obsession of New Super Mario Bros. 2, Nintendo's 2012 side-scroller on Nintendo 3DS built around huge totals. A Gold Flower turns bricks into coins, and Coin Rush is a timed dash for a personal best.

Raccoon Mario and a Gold block sit beside the usual flagpoles. Replaying a stage can push a running counter toward a million.

Bowser is still the last castle, yet the brag is the pile of coins. A careful path and a reckless path through the same course produce very different sums.
gunman-clive:
Pencil-line saloons and trains carry Gunman Clive, the sketch-styled western from Horberg Productions. Clive's single gun and a short jump suit Nintendo 3DS eShop stages that look drawn, and the tiny 2012 release punched above its price.

Boss animals and paper-looking bandits are the opposition. The linework is the identity, not a filter added afterward.

A sequel later reused the same handmade frontier. This first cartridge is the one that made the small price feel generous.
batman-arkham-origins-blackgate:
Cell blocks replace an open city in Batman: Arkham Origins Blackgate, Armature Studio's 2013 side-view Metroidvania on Nintendo 3DS and Vita. Batman works through Blackgate prison after the console Arkham Origins night, crossing paths with Bronze Tiger and Catwoman.

Detective vision, a grapnel, and gadget gates open new wings of the same complex. Combat keeps the freeflow punches, scaled down to corridors and locked doors.

The story sits between the console Arkham games as a handheld side path. The map is a prison cross-section, not another Gotham skyline.
metroid-samus-returns:
MercurySteam remade Metroid II as Metroid: Samus Returns, and the 2017 Nintendo 3DS hunt adds a melee counter to Samus's arsenal. SR388 is still a nest, and the Metroid quota still has to be cleared one creature at a time.

The counter freezes a lunging enemy so a charged shot can follow. Aeion abilities, including a scan pulse and lightning armor, mark the new tools on the map.

The Game Boy original was a spare downward descent. This remake keeps that hunt and gives Samus a parry the old cartridge never had.
slay-the-spire:
Ironclad, Silent, and Defect climb Slay the Spire, MegaCrit's deck-building roguelike that became a hit in 2019, with Nintendo Switch among its platforms. Each of those three starts with a different deck, and a bloated hand is often worse than a small one.

Act bosses such as the Slime Boss, the Collector, and the Time Eater end a run the deck cannot answer. Rest sites, shops, and unknown rooms branch before the next fight.

Relics change the math of every hallway. The handheld version plays that same spire, cards and all.
drawful-2:
Terrible sketches are the point of Drawful 2, Jackbox's 2016 party game where friends guess the caption on a bad drawing. A phone is the pad, and the Nintendo Switch shows the gallery to the room.

Decoy titles steal votes from the real prompt. The worst scribble can score highest when the lie is convincing.

Rounds stay short so a couch can play without a rules lecture. This sequel belongs to the Jackbox living-room set and keeps the same draw-then-guess joke.
vampire-survivors:
Whips, garlic, and a spinning Bible fire on their own in Vampire Survivors, poncle's 2022 swarm game that broke out and came to Nintendo Switch. The survivor only walks, and the weapons level up without a button for each shot.

The horde thickens as the timer climbs, and the reaper called Death arrives when the clock runs out. Gold spent between runs unlocks more characters in the collection.

A build is a pile of passive items and evolving weapons. The appeal is the swarm filling the screen, not a combo that has to be timed.
dragons-dogma-dark-arisen:
