Bitterblack Isle is the added dungeon in Dragon's Dogma: Dark Arisen, Capcom's 2013 expansion of Dragon's Dogma, and a Nintendo Switch port followed. Pawns still learn from the Arisen and can be shared with other players.

Cursed gear and the island's own bosses sit apart from Gransys, the mainland journey. Climbing a chimera or a cyclops remains the close-up way to fight.

The release is the same Arisen story with a deeper endgame hole. It is an expanded re-release, not a new numbered chapter on another continent.
resident-evil-village:
Lady Dimitrescu's castle opens Resident Evil: Village, Capcom's continuation of Ethan's first-person story after the Baker house. The 2021 search sends him through a European village after his daughter is taken, and Nintendo Switch carries that campaign.

Werewolves, a dollmaker's house, and a reservoir of mutated fish belong to separate lords. The Duke buys treasures between those domains.

Chris Redfield returns, while the eyes stay with Ethan Winters. The file is a main-line sequel to the Baker incident.
abzu-2:
Matt Nava, Journey's art director, founded Giant Squid and made ABZU, a wordless ocean dive later ported to Nintendo Switch. A diver swims among schools of fish with no combat prompts, and the original voyage is the 2016 release.

Ruins, a shark, and a mechanical intruder interrupt the reefs. Boosting through a bait ball is the strongest verb besides swimming.

Austin Wintory's score continues a collaboration heard in Journey. The port keeps that silent pilgrimage under the waves.
oxenfree:
Edwards Island hides strange frequencies in Oxenfree, Night School Studio's supernatural mystery told through walking conversations. Alex and her friends carry a radio that tunes into the ghosts, the game arrived in 2016, and a Nintendo Switch port followed.

Dialogue choices float over the hike, so an argument can continue across a beach. Jonas, Ren, and Clarissa bicker while the static becomes a puzzle tool.

The group is young, and nobody fights the island with a weapon wheel. The port keeps those overlapping talks.
tales-from-the-borderlands:
Rhys and Fiona split narration in Tales from the Borderlands: A Telltale Game Series, Telltale's episodic Borderlands comedy later collected on Nintendo Switch. Hyperion leftovers, a con, and a bandit camp stack choices through the 2015 season.

Loader Bot, Gortys, and Handsome Jack's hologram remember earlier lies. Jokes and double-crosses replace the studio's grimmer mystery tone.

Gearbox's shooter supplies the corporations and the guns. This series is the story being steered, and the Switch collection holds the season together.
broken-age:
Vella and Shay occupy opposite halves of Broken Age, Double Fine's Kickstarted adventure that shipped in two acts after a long gap. Tim Schafer's campaign was an early crowdfunding landmark, the acts landed in 2014, and a Nintendo Switch version came later.

Mog Chothra menaces Vella's village, while Shay's supervised spaceship is not what it pretends. Backers played Act 1 and waited before the halves locked together.

Point-and-click inventory puzzles carry both stories. The wait between acts is part of how the fairy tale and the ship were finished.
dying-light:
Harran's rooftops are safer in daylight in Dying Light, Techland's parkour zombie game where night belongs to the Volatiles. Kyle Crane, a GRE operative, climbs the 2015 city, and a Nintendo Switch port followed.

Ultraviolet light pushes the night hunters back. Crafted blades and airdrops support survivors stuck in the tower.

A later sequel continued the rooftop running. This first game made sunset a deadline.
sonic-mania:
Christian Whitehead, Headcannon, and PagodaWest restored classic momentum in Sonic Mania, and Nintendo Switch was one platform for that return. Studiopolis, Press Garden, and Mirage Saloon join Green Hill and Chemical Plant in the 2017 release.

The drop dash is the new midair trick on the old physics. Sonic, Tails, and Knuckles are the trio, with Mighty and Ray added in the later Plus encore.

Encore mode arrived after launch. The base zones are what proved a new stage could still feel like the Genesis years.
the-talos-principle:
Elohim speaks over the test chambers of The Talos Principle, Croteam's first-person puzzle about personhood, later on Nintendo Switch. Connectors, jammers, and cubes redirect lasers onto locks while terminals quote philosophy, and the garden opened in 2014 beside those terminals.

Hidden stars and messenger recordings sit off the obvious path. The rooms ask whether a machine that solves them can be someone.

Road to Gehenna is a later expansion with its own messenger society. The quiet chambers are a sharp turn for the studio known for Serious Sam.
gris:
Painted ruins shift around the girl in Gris, Nomada Studio's wordless platformer with almost no combat, and it came to Nintendo Switch. Her dress changes color to unlock a heavy form or a swim, in the 2018 release.

Conrad Roset's illustration makes the wind and a huge bird feel painted rather than modeled. There is no dialogue and almost no attack.

Grief is the reading most players give the red collapse at the start. Each new color adds a way to move until the palette is full.
vampyr:
Jonathan Reid, a doctor bitten on the way to his ward, leads Vampyr, Dontnod's action role-playing story set in 1918 London during the Spanish flu. Feeding on a named citizen strengthens him and can sicken that district, the wider release came in 2018, and a Nintendo Switch port followed.

Pembroke Hospital and the streets along the Thames form the social map. A victim who dies does not return to the night.

Blood powers and a sidearm handle the fights. The choice players remember is which Londoner gets bitten.
outer-wilds:
Timber Hearth's campfire launches Outer Wilds, Mobius Digital's space mystery on a twenty-two-minute loop, later ported to Nintendo Switch. The sun explodes, knowledge is the only thing kept, and the voyage that drew wide praise is the 2019 release.

Brittle Hollow, Giant's Deep, and the Hourglass Twins hide Nomai writings. A ship, a scout probe, and a signalscope replace any gun.

The Ash Twin Project is the machine those texts circle. The handheld port keeps the same exploding clock.
the-flame-in-the-flood:
Scout and her dog Aesop raft The Flame in the Flood, The Molasses Flood's roguelike trip downstream, later released on Nintendo Switch. Hunger, thirst, and a wet cold end runs as often as bites do, and the river journey is the 2016 original.

Islands offer scraps, clean water, or infection. A church, an abandoned fair, and a flooded town are stops, not safe cities.

Chuck Ragan's songs ride with the current. Death sends the next attempt upriver without the inventory.
deponia:
Rufus schemes to leave a junk planet in Deponia, Daedalic's comedy point-and-click that started a German adventure series. Goal, the visitor from Elysium, is the person he bungles into helping, the junkyard tale is from 2012, and a Nintendo Switch port came later.

A talking robot and a city of scrap fill the screens. The hero is selfish on purpose, and many puzzles turn on his bad ideas.

Chaos on Deponia and Goodbye Deponia continue that pair. This first game is Goal's crash and the scrap-heap romance.
rogue-legacy:
Every death funds the next child in Rogue Legacy, Cellar Door Games' castle platformer, later on Nintendo Switch. Gold from the corpse is spent on the manor before another heir enters, and that family curse began in 2013 inside the manor.

Gigantism, vertigo, or colorblindness can change the screen itself. The rooms shuffle, while manor upgrades persist across the bloodline.

Fairy chests demand a specific class. Rogue Legacy 2 arrived years afterward, but this game made the family tree the continue screen.
crash-bandicoot-n-sane-trilogy:
Vicarious Visions rebuilt the first three PlayStation games as Crash Bandicoot N. Sane Trilogy, a remaster collection that reached Nintendo Switch. Coco is playable in far more stages than on the originals, and the set arrived in 2017 as one package.

Aku Aku masks, time trials, and the animal rides stay tied to their own adventures. Crash Bandicoot, Cortex Strikes Back, and Warped share one menu instead of three separate discs.

New models cover familiar crate paths. The collection is a rebuild of those islands, not a fourth Crash story.
dust-an-elysian-tail:
Dean Dodrill largely drew Dust: An Elysian Tail alone for Xbox Live Arcade, and a Nintendo Switch port followed years later. Dust the amnesiac swordsman travels with Fidget the nimbat and the talking blade Ahrah, in the 2012 release.

Fidget's projectile joins long sword combos in side-view rooms. Those hand-drawn frames are why the adventure is described as a one-person project.

Falana and the village stories fill the gaps between monster packs. The port is that same solo-made journey on a later screen.
sniper-elite-4:
Karl Fairburne sights across Italian cliffs in Sniper Elite 4, Rebellion's World War II marksman game famous for the bullet camera. A generator or a cannon can mask the rifle's report, a Nintendo Switch version followed, and the campaign is the 2017 entry.

The X-ray view tracks a clean shot through bone. Mediterranean forts give those sightlines room to breathe.

Earlier games in the series had already made the kill camera a signature. This one widens the map while keeping that grisly replay.
life-is-strange-2:
Sean Diaz and little brother Daniel take the highway in Life is Strange 2, Dontnod's episodic road trip that leaves the first game's lead behind. Daniel's telekinesis answers how Sean parents him, the episodes began in 2018, and Nintendo Switch received them.

The southwest, a Seattle start, and a cult camp are among the stops. Max and Chloe are not the pair under the player's control.

Stealing, lying, or comforting Daniel feeds a brotherhood score. The season follows a new family far from Arcadia Bay.
machinarium:
Josef the robot solves Machinarium, Amanita Design's point-and-click with almost no written dialogue, and a Nintendo Switch port followed the PC original. Picture bubbles replace speech, a hint book replays a cartoon, and the city of machines dates to 2009 on PC.

Josef's girlfriend is held somewhere above streets of metal citizens. Scrap prisons and inventory objects stand in for sentences.

Amanita, the Czech studio behind Samorost, painted the rooms by hand. The port keeps that silent comic pace.
valiant-hearts-the-great-war:
Emile, Freddie, Karl, and Anna endure Valiant Hearts: The Great War, Ubisoft Montpellier's puzzle adventure through World War I, later ported to Nintendo Switch. Walt the dog digs and comforts between barrages, and the marches first appeared in 2014 from Montpellier.

Comic-book France and Germany frame the story, with historical notes beside the fiction. Barbed wire, a rolling tank, and a field hospital play as puzzles more than shooting galleries.

None of the four becomes a superhuman ace. The burden stays on ordinary people and the medic dog.
yakuza-kiwami:
Kazuma Kiryu walks Kamurocho again in Yakuza Kiwami, Sega's ground-up remake of the first Yakuza, the crime story that started on PlayStation 2 hardware. Nishikiyama's fall gains new scenes, extra fighting styles join the Dragon of Dojima, and the rebuild is the 2016 release.

Heat actions, a batting center, and Pocket Circuit break up the street fights. The plot remains the murder that sends Kiryu to prison and the empty lot waiting afterward.

Brawler, Rush, and Beast sit beside the dragon style. Combat ideas from the prequel feed this telling of the original Tojo Clan tragedy.
stalker-call-of-pripyat:
Major Degtyarev hunts crashed helicopters in S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Call of Pripyat, GSC Game World's sequel set around Pripyat after Shadow of Chernobyl. Zaton, Jupiter, and the city outskirts are the maps, the PC release came in 2009, and Nintendo Switch is a later home for that investigation.

Emissions force a sprint to cover. Anomalies and mutants fill the Exclusion Zone while Strelok's earlier path stays in the background.

The dotted acronym in the title points at a real abandoned city. This third Zone story follows the military disaster north of Chernobyl.
guardians-of-the-galaxy:
Peter Quill calls huddles in Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy, Eidos-Montreal's single-player campaign and a separate project from Telltale's earlier Guardians series. Drax, Gamora, Rocket, and Groot bicker aboard the Milano, and the 2021 story reached Nintendo Switch with the other versions.

A landed huddle triggers team attacks. Songs on Peter's cassette player joke through the firefights.

Telltale's episode choices stay a different tale. Combat here is a shooter with a squad the player directs.
the-lego-ninjago-movie-video-game:
Lloyd, Kai, and the ninja team smash sets in The LEGO NINJAGO Movie Video Game, TT Games' brick tie-in to the Ninjago film. Master Wu's lessons and Garmadon's attacks wear minifigure costumes, Nintendo Switch was among the consoles, and the game shared the film's 2017 release window.

Studs, a character-swap strike, and movie vehicles fill the levels. A broken wall still hides a minikit, the old LEGO habit under new costumes.

The plot follows the movie's Ninjago City rather than an earlier television season. Several home machines received that tie-in together.
stalker-clear-sky:
Scar joins a faction in S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky, GSC Game World's prequel and the second Zone release, set before Shadow of Chernobyl. Faction wars cross the Swamps and the Cordon, the PC version came in 2008, and Nintendo Switch is where this earlier timeline sits now.

Emissions and artifact hunts return, and Scar's health is tied to the blowouts. The plot shows how the camps reached the state Strelok later walks through.

The chronology points backward, toward a disaster the first game already survived. Clear Sky itself is the group trying to study the Zone rather than simply loot it.
outlast-2:
Blake Langermann films Outlast 2 with no weapon, Red Barrels' rural sequel that kept the defenseless camera. Temple Gate, a cult in the Arizona desert, replaces Mount Massive Asylum, and the night is the 2017 follow-up.

Lynn, Blake's wife, is lost in the same wilderness. School-memory flashes about Jessica cut into the chase, and camera batteries stay scarce.

Miles Upshur's camcorder horror was the first game's tool. This sequel keeps the filming and moves it to a village that does not want a witness.
overcooked-2:
Throwing ingredients is the new verb in Overcooked! 2, Ghost Town Games' kitchen sequel full of extra hazards. Portals, moving trucks, and a balloon kitchen refuse to sit still, Nintendo Switch was a major platform, and the panic belongs to the 2018 release.

Orders still burn if chopped food never hits the pot. Online matches join the couch chaos the first game already sparked.

The Onion King returns with a fresh food-monster crisis. A partner across a gap only helps when the throw is aimed.
ghostrunner:
Dharma Tower kills in one hit in Ghostrunner, One More Level's first-person cyber-ninja, including a Nintendo Switch version. Jack restarts the room after every blade or bullet, the Keymaster talks in his ear, and the climb is the 2020 release.

Wall-runs, a sword dash, and a shuriken are the movement kit. Mara waits at the top of the tower as the tyrant to cut down.

There is no health bar to manage. The skill is a clean line through a corridor already failed once.
star-wars-jedi-knight-jedi-academy:
Jaden Korr builds a lightsaber moveset in Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy, Raven Software's third Jedi Knight shooter, later ported by Aspyr. Kyle Katarn teaches at Luke Skywalker's academy, the Disciples of Ragnos are the enemy, and the PC version is the 2003 release before Nintendo Switch.

Force powers and saber styles are chosen as the student advances. Missions hop across planets instead of one continuous corridor.

Katarn carried the earlier Jedi Knight stories. This chapter hands the custom saber and the class track to the padawan.
gone-home:
Katie Greenbriar explores an empty house in Gone Home, Fullbright's story told by walking through rooms, with a Nintendo Switch port later. Sam's notes and the parents' troubled marriage wait in drawers, a storm hits the Pacific Northwest home, and the night is the 2013 release.

There is no combat and no puzzle inventory beyond a letter or a key. The house itself is the whole interface.

The team had come from environmental storytelling on BioShock before making this smaller place. A quiet 1995 evening is the date on the answering machine.
final-fantasy-vii:
Cloud Strife's Midgar job opens Final Fantasy VII (1997), Square's PlayStation leap into 3D, later on Nintendo Switch in its original form. Avalanche, Shinra, and the Mako reactors set the opening fight.

Materia sockets change spells, and limit breaks are the signature surges. Aerith, Tifa, Barret, and Sephiroth are the names the plot turns on.

A later remake is a different project with a different structure. This release is the original polygon version of that Midgar story.
katana-zero:
A therapist asks questions between kills in Katana ZERO, Askiisoft's neo-noir of short cinematic rooms that launched with a Nintendo Switch version. Deaths rewind, a cigarette times the slow fall, and the conspiracy is the 2019 release.

Guards and bullets turn each room into a line you are meant to fail until it is perfect. Conversations with the psychiatrist can be cut short or dragged out.

A small girl and a figure called V keep returning as the jobs get stranger. The handheld launch meant the rewind was available immediately, not added in a later port.
shadowrun-dragonfall-dc:
Berlin's Flux State burns in Shadowrun: Dragonfall - Director's Cut, the standalone Harebrained Schemes expanded from a Shadowrun Returns campaign. Monika's crew falls to the player after the opening disaster, the Director's Cut adds voice and extra missions, and that fuller version is the 2014 release.

A decker, a street samurai, a mage, or a rigger can fill the turn-based squad. Cover matters, and the story is longer than the campaign chapter it grew from.

Magic and megacorps share the streets of an anarchist district, not the Seattle of the first campaign. Nintendo Switch is one home for that expanded Berlin run.
inside:
Playdead followed Limbo with INSIDE, another wordless side-view story about a boy slipping through a grim facility. A mind-control helmet, a flooded stretch, and guards with searchlights are the set pieces, critics treated it as a standout, and the descent is the 2016 game.

The boy never speaks. A mass of bodies in the water is one of the images players carry out.

The ending's shock is the point of the long walk, so the last room is better met than described. Nintendo Switch later carried the same silent facility.
sega-mega-drive-and-genesis-classics:
Sonic's old zones share a menu with SEGA Mega Drive and Genesis Classics, the compilation Sega began shipping on PC and later consolidated onto consoles. Streets of Rage, Golden Axe, and Shinobi sit beside the hedgehog, and that growing library started in 2010 on PC.

The pile expanded over time rather than arriving as one frozen disc. Save states wrap the 16-bit cartridges in a modern list.

Nintendo Switch is one console that received the consolidated set. The package is the Mega Drive library, not a new Genesis sequel.
brawlhalla:
Blue Mammoth Games put Brawlhalla into early access as a free platform fighter in the Smash mold, and it later came under Ubisoft. Legends wield swords, hammers, and blasters on floating stages, signatures are the heavy specials, and the early access start was in 2014 under Blue Mammoth.

The roster is original fighters, not borrowed Nintendo guests. Stocks decide the winner when someone is knocked away.

Nintendo Switch joined the platforms while the game stayed free. Ubisoft's later ownership kept that same air-dodge brawl available without a paid-only cartridge.
firewatch:
Henry hikes to a Wyoming lookout in Firewatch, Campo Santo's first game, told largely through radio talks with supervisor Delilah. The Shoshone forest, a missing pair of girls, and a fenced research site unfold over the summer job, and that post is the 2016 story.

A map, a compass, and the walkie-talkie are the tools. There is no gunplay on the trail.

Julia, Henry's wife, is the reason he took the isolated work, explained on the opening walk. Nintendo Switch later carried the same Two Forks tower.
assassins-creed-odyssey:
Kassandra or Alexios can lead Assassin's Creed Odyssey, the dialogue-heavy adventure Ubisoft Quebec set in ancient Greece. Sparta, Athens, and the ship Adrestia carry a war between city-states, the Cult of Kosmos is hunted one member at a time, and the odyssey is the 2018 release.

The spear of Leonidas is the special weapon of the misthios. Dialogue choices change how people in a town react.

Naval fights return on the Aegean, echoing the series' pirate era. Nintendo Switch is among the platforms that received this Greece.
no-mans-sky:
Hello Games launched No Man's Sky to a harsh reception, then spent years adding bases, story, and multiplayer to the procedural explorer. Atlas stations, the Anomaly, and sentinel drones are recurring landmarks, and that rocky start was in 2016 for Hello Games.

A planet can be crossed on foot, in a ship, or underwater, and the rocks feed the next launch. The early promises and the quieter launch are the controversy those updates answered.

Nintendo Switch received the expanded version, bases included. The loop is still naming a world and leaving it.
alien-isolation:
Amanda Ripley hides from one xenomorph in Alien: Isolation, Creative Assembly's station horror set fifteen years after the 1979 film. Sevastopol's Working Joe androids are a second threat, the motion tracker beeps, and the stranding is the 2014 game.

A locker is often the only plan, because there is no squad to shoot the creature down. Noise and line of sight are what the alien learns.

Creative Assembly, better known for grand strategy, built this slow rescue of Ellen Ripley's daughter. Nintendo Switch later ran that same decaying station.
disco-elysium:
Harry Du Bois wakes on a floor in Disco Elysium, ZA/UM's detective story in Revachol with no ordinary combat, and it swept a long list of year-end awards. Inland Empire, Shivers, and Electrochemistry argue like separate people, Kim Kitsuragi keeps the case sane, and the case is the 2019 game.

Martinaise is a strike, a hanging, and a failed revolution. Thought Cabinet ideas occupy the mind over in-game days.

Nintendo Switch carries that same dialogue-heavy investigation. The city, not a weapon tree, is what the awards were answering.
cuphead:
Studio MDHR drew Cuphead like a 1930s rubber-hose cartoon, a boss-rush run-and-gun scored to jazz. Cuphead and Mugman owe the Devil a debt from the casino, pink objects can be parried, and the hand-drawn fights are the 2017 release.

A flower, a robot, and the Devil himself are patterned shoots rather than exploring levels. The brothers build a super from those parries.

The studio spent years on the frames before anyone could play them. Nintendo Switch is one of the places those debts get paid.
darksiders:
War takes the blame for an early apocalypse in Darksiders, the horseman adventure Vigil Games opened under THQ and often compared with Zelda. The Abyssal Chain and dungeon items gate a ruined city, lock-on combat collects an arsenal, and the ride began in 2010 under THQ.

The publisher's later collapse took Vigil with it and froze the series for a time. Nintendo Switch eventually received this first horseman.

Ruined highways and angelic wreckage replace a bright fairy-tale map. The comparison people make is the item-gated dungeons, while the tone stays wrath and judgment.
doom-eternal:
Glory kills, a chainsaw, and a flame belch feed the Slayer in DOOM Eternal, id Software's faster follow-up to its reboot. Ammo, armor, and health come from the demons themselves, the Khan Maykr expands the plot past Mars, and the aggression is the 2020 game.

A dash and extra platform challenges join the push-forward shooting. The 2016 entry taught the aggression, and this sequel makes the resource economy explicit.

Nintendo Switch runs that same loop. Standing back to reload is the habit the arenas punish.
among-us:
InnerSloth hid an impostor aboard a ship in Among Us, the social deduction game whose huge popularity spike came a couple of years after launch. Crewmates fix wires in electrical and swipe a card in admin while oxygen can be sabotaged, and the quiet start was in 2018 for InnerSloth.

Emergency meetings lead to a vote that ejects someone. The Skeld is the classic map, with Mira HQ and Polus around it.

Nintendo Switch got the same small crewmates. Streamers later turned those meetings into a spectator sport.
transistor:
Red carries a talking sword through Transistor, Supergiant Games' isometric follow-up to Bastion, where fights can be paused and planned. Cloudbank is being eaten by the Process, Turn() queues a string of functions, and the city story is the 2014 release.

Red's voice has been stolen into the sword, and the narrator is the man inside it. Functions such as Crash() are taken from fallen citizens.

A plan plays out after the freeze ends, leaving Red exposed. Nintendo Switch later received that same planned combat.
resident-evil-5-biohazard-5:
Sheva Alomar partners with Chris Redfield in Resident Evil 5, Capcom's campaign that pushes further into co-op shooting. Kijuju replaces the lone-survivor mansions with Plaga parasites, an AI partner shares ammo when no second player joins, and the file is the 2009 entry.

Excella and Albert Wesker wait deeper in the chapters. The inventory grid and melee prompts are what two players coordinate.

Nintendo Switch received that co-op campaign. The series mood here is daylight action beside a partner, a long way from a locked Spencer door.
xcom-2:
ADVENT already occupies Earth in XCOM 2, the turn-based tactics game where Firaxis reversed the reboot's outcome. The Avenger, a stolen ship, is the moving base, guerrilla missions often run on a timer, and the resistance story is the 2016 release after the 2012 loss.

The Commander starts the campaign as a rescue, not a victor. Cover, overwatch, and class abilities still decide a pod activation.

War of the Chosen is the later expansion. Nintendo Switch plays the occupied-planet fantasy of striking and vanishing.
ori-and-the-blind-forest-definitive-edit:
Naru's forest gains another region in Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition, Moon Studios' expanded platformer with new difficulty options. Witches stand trial in Labyrinthia in Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney, the crossover Level-5 and Capcom first released in Japan. Puzzle hints meet courtroom objections, Espella is central to the accusations, and the Japanese release was in 2012 from Level-5 and Capcom.

kirby-triple-deluxe:

pixel-hunter:

super-smash-bros-for-nintendo-3ds:
Smash Run is the portable-only mode in Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS, the handheld half from Bandai Namco and Sora that shipped beside a separate Wii U game. Power-ups collected on a big board feed the next bout, and the handheld brawler arrived in 2014 beside the home version.

skylanders-spyros-adventure:
Figures store progress on a portal in Skylanders Spyro's Adventure, the toys-to-life game Toys for Bob started. Each statue keeps a character's growth, Spyro fronts the new line, and the portal idea is the 2011 debut, including a Nintendo 3DS version.

kirby-planet-robobot:
Kirby pilots a mech in Kirby: Planet Robobot, HAL Laboratory's platformer often ranked with the strongest mainline outings. Robobot Armor copies enemy abilities, Susie and Star Dream drive the invasion, and the suit is the 2016 Nintendo 3DS game.

persona-q-shadow-of-the-labyrinth:
Hand-drawn maps return in Persona Q: Shadow of the Labyrinth, Atlus's crossover of Persona 3 and Persona 4 with Etrian-style charting. Both casts share a labyrinth, FOE monsters patrol fixed paths, and the notebook crawl is the 2014 Nintendo 3DS game.

Atlus built it as a dungeon crawl first. School calendars from the parent games are not the structure here.
the-legend-of-zelda-tri-force-heroes:
Three Links stack into a totem in The Legend of Zelda: Tri Force Heroes, Nintendo's cooperation game for three players. Madame Couture's outfits change abilities, Hytopia has a fashion crisis, and the stacking is the 2015 Nintendo 3DS multiplayer adventure.

blaster-master-zero:
Jason hops out of the tank in Blaster Master Zero, Inti Creates' reimagining of the NES classic. SOPHIA and the on-foot caverns still swap, Eve supports the hunt, and the new telling is the 2017 Nintendo 3DS game.

Overhead caves stay tighter than the side-view driving. Mutants and the planet's depths are the chase.

Inti Creates kept the vehicle-and-driver split. This is a fresh story, not a straight copy of the Sunsoft cartridge.
spyro-reignited-trilogy:
Toys for Bob rebuilt three PlayStation games as Spyro Reignited Trilogy, covering Spyro, Ripto's Rage, and Year of the Dragon. Gems, dragons, and the glide return in new models, and the collection is the 2018 set that reached Nintendo Switch.

Ripto and the Sorceress belong to the second and third adventures. The first remains the holiday of rescuing dragons.

risk-of-rain-2:
Item stacks snowball a run in Risk of Rain 2, the roguelike Hopoo Games moved from a side view into three dimensions. The Commando returns under a new camera, teleporters pull toward a boss, and the game left early access in 2020 for a wider launch.

Difficulty still climbs with the clock. Mithrix waits as a late threat once the loop is understood.

The earlier game was flat and pixelated. This sequel keeps the timer pressure and changes how the player aims.
blasphemous:
The Penitent One climbs a cruel land in Blasphemous, The Game Kitchen's severe side-view fight steeped in Spanish Catholic imagery. Cvstodia's guilt and pixel-art wounds define the march, and the pilgrimage is the 2019 game on Nintendo Switch.

kholat:
Coordinates lead through snow in Kholat, the first-person horror IMGN PRO drew from the Dyatlov Pass incident. The player is lost in the Ural mountains, documents frame the walk, and the hike is the 2015 game later on Nintendo Switch.

surgeon-simulator-cpr:
Each finger is its own clumsy control in Surgeon Simulator, Bossa Studios' physics comedy. A heart transplant is the headline operation, tools slip in a tray, and the slapstick surgery is the 2013 game later on Nintendo Switch.

The joke is failure, not medical accuracy. Dropping a scalpel is expected.

Bossa Studios built the chaos on purpose. Nintendo Switch carries that same awkward operating theater.
sniper-elite-3:
North Africa replaces earlier fronts in Sniper Elite 3, Rebellion's X-ray sharpshooter campaign. Karl Fairburne still lines up long shots, the bullet camera returns, and the desert war is the 2014 release later on Nintendo Switch.

Distance and noise matter in open dunes. This is the entry before the Italian maps of the follow-up.

Rebellion kept the grisly replay and moved the theater. Axis camps in the sand are the new sightlines.
genshin-impact:
Elemental swaps power Genshin Impact, miHoYo's free-to-play open world built on a gacha roster. The twins search Teyvat, reactions such as water meeting lightning decide fights, and the live game launched in 2020 with Nintendo Switch among its announced platforms.

Wishes are how new characters arrive. Resin limits how often certain rewards can be claimed.

miHoYo built an ongoing continent rather than one boxed ending. Swapping heroes mid-battle is the combat verb.
serious-sam-the-first-encounter:
Headless bombers charge in waves in Serious Sam: The First Encounter, Croteam's arena shooter and the first half of the original Serious Sam. Mental taunts from afar, secrets hide in Egypt-styled ruins, and the horde fight is the 2001 release later on Nintendo Switch.

Health and armor wait in the open to be grabbed. The design is crowd combat, not a slow corridor.

Croteam split the original trip into this encounter and a second. The kamikaze scream is the sound players still imitate.
furi:
Sword duels alternate with shooting in Furi, The Game Bakers' boss rush with almost no ordinary levels between fights. The Stranger breaks out one prison guard at a time, and the chain of duels is the 2016 game on Nintendo Switch.

Each guardian has a close phase and a ranged phase. Healing is tied to aggression during the exchange.

The Game Bakers built one fight after another. The walk between arenas is the only breather.
doom-3:
A flashlight and the dark define Doom 3, the slower Mars horror id Software built. PDA logs carry the plot through Mars City, the UAC base fills with demons, and the crawl is the 2004 game later on Nintendo Switch.

The pace is nearer a scare than the later push-forward reboot. Ammo is scarce enough that the shadows matter.

id Software rebuilt the series around that light. Raising the flashlight often means lowering the gun.
titan-quest:
Greece leads onward through Egypt in Titan Quest, Iron Lore's loot-driven trek across myth. Dual masteries combine two skill trees, and the ancient road is the 2006 release later on Nintendo Switch.

A storm tree and a defense tree can share one hero. The journey visits pantheons rather than a single dungeon town.

Iron Lore made the paired classes the character system. Nintendo Switch carries that same walk from one set of gods to the next.
serious-sam-hd-tfe:
The same crowd combat returns with a newer look in Serious Sam HD:  The First Encounter, Croteam's remaster of the wave shooter. Headless bombers still charge, the fight design stays put, and the refreshed version is the 2009 release later on Nintendo Switch.

Arena layouts remain the original encounters. What changes is how clearly those hordes read.

Croteam updated the first episode rather than writing a new one. The HD set is a visual pass over that same scream of bombers.
super-mario-odyssey:
Super Mario Odyssey sends Mario across kingdoms collecting moons, with a hat named Cappy doing the possessing. Capturing a creature replaces Mario's moves until Cappy lets go.

Yoshiaki Koizumi's Nintendo EPD team built it for Switch as a return to the sandbox spirit of Mario 64, but each kingdom is a city or a biome rather than a painting. Capturing a Bullet Bill, a dinosaur, or a taxi changes the move set for as long as the capture lasts.

New Donk City brings Pauline back as a mayor and stages a festival once enough moons are found. The darker side of the moon and the darker side of the mushroom kingdom are postgame spaces for players who thought the brochure was finished.

It is not a port of Sunshine, Galaxy, or 64. Those remain their own pages. This one is Super Mario Odyssey.
banner-saga:
Rook's caravan trudges through The Banner Saga, Stoic's Viking tale of travel plus turn-based fights. Varl giants march with humans, Alette and others can be lost for good, and the storybook journey is the 2014 game later on Nintendo Switch.

Road choices change who is still alive. Supplies and morale drop between battles.

The art looks drawn, like a printed saga. Stoic made the marching itself a resource problem.
crypt-of-the-necrodancer:
Cadence moves only on the beat in Crypt of the NecroDancer, Brace Yourself Games' roguelike where a missed rhythm is a missed step. The golden lute is the quest, the shopkeeper punishes off-tempo thieves, and the dance is the 2015 game on Nintendo Switch.

Danny Baranowsky's soundtrack is the clock. A dig or a dagger on the wrong beat fails.

Brace Yourself Games locked movement to the music. A zone boss is a song as much as a body.
darksiders-iii:
Fury hunts the Seven Deadly Sins in Darksiders III, Gunfire Games' narrower action game about that horseman. Hollows and a linear road replace wider maps, and the hunt is the 2018 release later on Nintendo Switch.

Her bladed whip and counters define the fights. It is a tighter journey than the sealed city or the earlier open kingdoms.

Gunfire Games focused the combat on one rider. The Sins are the bosses spaced along her path.
the-vanishing-of-ethan-carter:
Paul Prospero searches for a missing boy in The Vanishing of Ethan Carter, the mystery from The Astronauts, founded by former People Can Fly developers. Red Creek Valley holds strange scenes, a Redux reissue followed, and the original case is the 2014 release later on Nintendo Switch.

There is little combat. The detective traps supernatural tableaux and solves them.

The Astronauts built a place to walk and deduce. Ethan is the child whose absence structures the valley.
plague-inc-evolved:
DNA points evolve a disease in Plague Inc: Evolved, Ndemic Creations' wider version of its mobile infection puzzle. Countries close borders, extra modes surround the original toy, and the PC-and-console expansion is the 2015 release that reached Nintendo Switch.

A bacterium, a virus, or a parasite can start the outbreak. The goal is total spread before a cure finishes.

Ndemic Creations kept the world map and added ways to play around it. It is a strategy of contagion, not a hospital story.
hogwarts-legacy:
Ancient magic classes fill Hogwarts Legacy, Avalanche Software's open-world game published by Portkey Games. The story sits in the 1890s of the Harry Potter world, long before the famous students, and the castle life is the 2023 release, including on Nintendo Switch.

Lessons, beasts, and highland paths fill the student's time. Duels use spells outside a turn menu.

Portkey Games is the publishing label on the box. Avalanche built a nineteenth-century year at the school rather than retelling one film.
unravel:
Yarny unspools through physics puzzles in Unravel, Coldwood Interactive's platformer published by EA. The yarn figure swings and ties itself across Swedish countryside dioramas, and the string adventure is the 2016 game later on Nintendo Switch.

A thread stretched too far leaves Yarny short. Memories in the scenes carry the story more than dialogue.

Coldwood Interactive made the yarn both body and tool. EA published that small figure's trip.
speedrunners:
Grapples and shoves decide SpeedRunners, DoubleDutch Games' side-view race. The scrolling screen eliminates anyone who falls behind, hooks catch lamps and boxes, and the competitive running is the 2016 release later on Nintendo Switch.

Items are slapstick rather than vehicle upgrades. Four runners share one course.

DoubleDutch Games built it as a party race. A well-timed push is worth more than raw speed.
moonlighter:
Will prices relics by day and raids by night in Moonlighter, Digital Sun's loop of shopkeeping and dungeons. Customers complain if a tag is wrong, the stall funds better gear, and the routine is the 2018 game on Nintendo Switch.

The town is the safe half of the clock. Whatever is carried out of the depths becomes stock.

Digital Sun tied commerce to the crawl. A good afternoon at the counter buys the next weapon.
gothic-1:
A magic barrier traps the Colony in Gothic, Piranha Bytes' PC role-playing game that later gathered a cult following. The Nameless Hero joins camps such as the Old Camp, ore mining feeds the dome, and the colony story is the 2001 release that reached Nintendo Switch.

Choosing a camp changes teachers and quests. Combat is close and deliberate, with a learning curve players still mention.

Piranha Bytes built a society under the dome, not only a monster field. Nobody simply walks out.
risk-of-rain:
Every minute grows harsher in Risk of Rain, Hopoo Games' side-view roguelike, later remade in three dimensions as a sequel. The Commando hunts a teleporter, items warp the run, and the pixel version is the 2013 release on Nintendo Switch as well.

Lingering is a real choice because difficulty scales with time. Death ends that survivor's carried gear.

Hopoo Games made the clock the enemy. The follow-up kept the pressure and left the flat view.
remnant-from-the-ashes:
The Root overruns Earth in Remnant: From the Ashes, Gunfire Games' mix of shooter combat and procedurally arranged worlds. Bosses have their own tells, traits persist as a character grows, and the expedition is the 2019 game later on Nintendo Switch.

A second roll does not repeat the same map. Zones rearrange around the guns.

Gunfire Games aimed it at cooperative shooting. The Root is an invading intelligence, not a simple roadside horde.
rime:
A boy and a fox cross bright ruins in RiME, Tequila Works' puzzle adventure told with very little dialogue. A Mediterranean island, a storm, and shifting color carry the story, and the quiet journey is the 2017 game on Nintendo Switch.

A shout can wake a mechanism. The fox guides more often than it fights.

Tequila Works kept written text scarce. The island's meaning arrives through scenes.
south-park-the-fractured-but-whole:
Superhero play replaces the stick war in South Park: The Fractured But Whole, Ubisoft's sequel about the kids' homemade comic crusade. Grid fights, the Coon, and the New Kid return in new costumes, and the campaign is the 2017 game later on Nintendo Switch.

The children invent alter egos. Combat moved off the previous game's fantasy menu.

Ubisoft published this follow-up. The rude title puns on the team name the show already used.
this-is-the-police:
Jack Boyd counts down his last days in This is the Police, Weappy's management game about a corrupt chief. One hundred eighty days of shifts, mafia calls, and political pressure fill the calendar, and the precinct story is the 2016 game on Nintendo Switch.

Officers have skills and tempers. The wrong pair sent to a call can fail it.

Weappy makes the player share Boyd's compromises. The length of the career left is the campaign clock.
factorio:
Belts and assemblers chew ore in Factorio, Wube Software's builder about automating a hostile planet. Biters attack as pollution spreads, version 1.0 followed a long early access, and that finished mark is the 2020 release later on Nintendo Switch.

Plates become machines, then science, then more machines. The factory is a puzzle that keeps growing.

Wube Software built the automation loop. Turrets and walls exist because the wildlife bites back.
golf-with-your-friends:
Trick holes and moving ramps fill Golf With Your Friends, the mini-golf party game that entered early access and later widened under Team17. Friends putt wild courses, physics beats a formal swing, and the early access start was in 2016 before the Nintendo Switch release.

Courses are toys, not regulation greens. A bounce off a friend can be the point.

Team17 published the broader console edition. The pleasure is a ridiculous line, not a tour scorecard.
my-friend-pedro:
A talking banana gives the orders in My Friend Pedro, DeadToast Entertainment's slow-motion shooter published by Devolver Digital. Kicks, split aim, and wall jumps clear gangster rooms, and the acrobatic run is the 2019 game on Nintendo Switch.

Bullet time is the main verb. Style rises when kicks and shots chain.

DeadToast built the movement, and Devolver Digital published it. Pedro never behaves like an ordinary guide.
hyper-light-drifter:
Diamond shards upgrade a sick swordsman in Hyper Light Drifter, Heart Machine's wordless top-down game funded by a closely watched Kickstarter. Modules change the kit, bosses are large patterns, and the release came in 2016 with a later Nintendo Switch version.

The pink-haired figure does not explain the land in dialogue. Images and debris carry the history.

Heart Machine, associated in public with Alx Preston, shipped it after that campaign. Death returns the drifter to a last safe point with the lesson intact.
dungeon-of-the-endless:
Crystal dust powers both light and defense in Dungeon of the Endless, Amplitude Studios' mix of a dungeon crawl and tower defense. A stranded ship is the setting, heroes hold rooms against waves, and the emergency is the 2014 game later on Nintendo Switch.

Opening a door spends that dust. An unlit room invites the monsters in.

Amplitude Studios set it beside the studio's other Endless fiction. Each floor is a choice about which corridor to hold.
duck-hunt:
That laughing dog mocks a miss in Duck Hunt, Nintendo's light-gun game of ducks and clay pigeons. The Zapper aims at the sky, a clay round can follow the birds, and the cartridge shipped with a huge number of NES bundles in the light-gun era, with the 1984 bundles packed beside the console.

Nintendo packed it with many consoles, so the dog became a shared joke. Clay pigeons are the other target beside the flock.
balloon-fight:
Flapping both balloons keeps a fighter up in Balloon Fight, Nintendo's small arcade-style game often grouped with the early black-box lineup. Popping a rival's balloons drops them toward the water, lightning is the sky hazard, and the flap is the 1985 NES game.

Balloon Trip scrolls without the duel. Fish wait below if a fighter falls.

Nintendo kept the package immediate and small. Players file it with the other simple black-box cartridges.
contra:
Bill and Lance spread their fire through Contra, Konami's run-and-gun that defined the game for NES players. A famous code culture grew around extra lives, the waterfall and the alien base are among the stages, and the home march is the 1988 cartridge.

The NES edition is the one home players mean by the name. This strict side-view assault is the memory, distinct from the arcade cabinet's angle.
dragon-warrior:
Alefgard's hero grinds through towns in Dragon Warrior, the turn-based quest North America met under that name. Chunsoft and Enix sent one champion across a small kingdom, King Lorik gives the task, and the Dragonlord is the 1986 NES goal.

The Japanese title was Dragon Quest. This NES release introduced that first quest under the Warrior name.
startropics:
Mike Jones hunts through islands with a yo-yo in StarTropics, Nintendo's late adventure, a cousin to Zelda with its own story. Dr. Jones is the missing uncle, a packed letter famously needed water to reveal a code, and the voyage is the 1990 NES game.

C-Island and the nearby seas hold the chapters. The yo-yo gives way to a stronger weapon later.

Nintendo hid that hint off the cartridge on purpose. The setting is not Hyrule, even where overhead dungeons feel familiar.
blaster-master:
SOPHIA rolls through caverns in Blaster Master, Sunsoft's action game where the driver hops out for tight overhead caves. Jason leaves the tank for those rooms, gun upgrades wait on the side-view map, and the swap is the 1988 NES design people still name from Sunsoft.

Overhead sections are cramped mazes. Tank sections are the wider destruction.

Switching between driver and vehicle is the idea later remakes kept. Sunsoft's late eighties run is the context players give this cartridge.
ghosts-n-goblins:
Arthur loses his armor in two hits in Ghosts 'n Goblins, Capcom's graveyard march that expects a second full clear. Red Arremer and a lance-or-torch weapon swap fill the NES port, and the strict home version is the 1986 cartridge.

Capcom's arcade game was already harsh. This port is the notoriously strict one players dare each other to finish.
teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles:
Four brothers share one life bar in Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Konami's first NES game of the team, distinct from the arcade-style sequel. An overhead map links side-view fights, the dam is the infamous swim, and the shared health is the 1989 design.

Leonardo, Donatello, Raphael, and Michelangelo each handle differently. April and Shredder sit at opposite ends of the rescue.

The following NES game chased the arcade brawler. This first cartridge is the overhead city and the brutal water.
faxanadu:
The World Tree is dying in Faxanadu, the side-view action role-playing game from Hudson Soft and Falcom. Gear stalls and a password save break up the climb, and the elf hero's quest is the 1987 NES cult adventure.

Dwarf towns and fountains punctuate the vertical road. Magic and a sword share space with jumping.

The title echoes Falcom's Xanadu. Hudson Soft's NES quest is still cited among the deeper action role-playing games on that console.
bionic-commando:
Capcom replaced the jump with a wire in Bionic Commando. The commando hooks a ledge, swings across a shaft, and never gets an ordinary hop.

The NES campaign is its own chain of missions, not a straight copy of the shorter arcade cabinet. In 1988 that longer objective, passed along by radio chatter between bases, sat among Capcom's staples for the console.

Enemy camps and elevators punish a missed swing more than they punish a slow trigger finger. Learning the length of the bionic arm is the skill the stages keep testing.
super-mario-all-stars:
Redrawn sprites packed four NES Mario adventures onto Super Mario All-Stars. Super Mario Bros., the Japanese Super Mario Bros. 2 known in the West as The Lost Levels, Super Mario Bros. 2, and Super Mario Bros. 3 share one SNES cartridge.

Save files, especially welcome inside Super Mario Bros. 3, changed how a rented weekend could reach Bowser. In 1993 many SNES owners met those earlier journeys here, while the original NES cartridges remain their own records.

The 16-bit coats of paint keep the old level maps. A pipe in World 1-1 still drops into the coin room, only the bricks look newly painted.
pilotwings:
Flight lessons, not a combat sortie, structure Pilotwings. Instructors grade a hang glider, a light plane, and a jet pack, and a sloppy landing costs the certificate.

Nintendo shipped it in the SNES launch window of 1990, when Mode 7 could spin a runway under the aircraft. The score is a license test: altitude, rings, and the touchdown all sit on the report card.

secret-of-mana:
Square's charge gauge defines combat in Secret of Mana. Randi plants his feet, the weapon meter fills, and the swing that follows is a different attack from a hurried tap.

Primm and Popoi join the Mana Sword bearer, and a second player can drop onto a spare controller. In 1993 that real-time party, with a ring menu pausing the field, was the Mana journey that reached the widest SNES audience, between the Game Boy predecessor and later sequels.

Co-op changes who watches the charge. One player can keep a spell coming while another holds a stance, which the menu-driven battles of Square's turn-based hits never asked for.
kirby-super-star:
Helper characters share the copy ability in Kirby Super Star. Give up the current power and a partner steps out already wearing it, then follows Kirby through the stage.

HAL Laboratory and Nintendo packed short games onto one SNES cartridge in 1996: Spring Breeze, Dyna Blade, Gourmet Race against King Dedede, The Great Cave Offensive, Revenge of Meta Knight, and Milky Way Wishes. Megaton Punch and Samurai Kirby sit in the same collection as brief contests.

Super Star Ultra later revisited the anthology on DS. The SNES original is the one where Meta Knight's airship and the helper system arrived together.
kirbys-dream-course:
Treating Kirby as the ball is the whole of Kirby's Dream Course. Aim a shot across a floating green, hit an enemy, and the copied ability changes the next stroke.

HAL Laboratory and Nintendo released this SNES spin in 1994, apart from the usual inhale-and-jump journeys. Two players can share a course, and clearing the holes still depends on which enemy you bump on the felt.

King Dedede waits in the harder cups. A tornado copy or a stone drop will move the ball in a way no putter on a normal fairway ever would.
street-fighter-ii:
Special moves made the SNES living room a cabinet when Street Fighter II arrived. Ryu's fireball, Chun-Li's spinning kick, and Guile's flash still come from the same motion the arcade taught.

Capcom's home conversion in 1992 put that roster, from Blanka to M. Bison, on a console pad that had to fake six buttons with combinations. This record is that SNES era, separate from the arcade board and from later PlayStation editions.

Mirrors and bonus stages kept the one-on-one shape. A Dragon Punch still needs the familiar stick motion, which is why the cartridge stayed in so many SNES collections.
mario-party-2:
Costume themes dress every board in Mario Party 2. Pirate hats on the cast make the cup readable. Pirate, western, space, horror, and mystery layouts put Mario and company in outfits while the same shared controller still passes hand to hand.

Hudson Soft and Nintendo used 1999 to enlarge the minigame list and refine the first Nintendo 64 party. Coins, stars, and Bowser's interruptions remain the economy, but items and the costume sets make each board feel like a different party night.

Four players still crowd one machine. A minigame can hinge on a single stick waggle after twenty minutes of buying stars, which is the rhythm the second board game kept.
f-zero-x:
Sparse scenery is the point of F-Zero X. Cylinder tracks leave almost no shoulder to recover on. Tracks loop through open air, the machine count is huge, and the frame rate stays high enough that a jump feels instant.

Nintendo placed this Nintendo 64 chapter in 1998, between the SNES original and F-Zero GX on GameCube. Captain Falcon is one machine among a wide grid, and a wipeout still throws the pilot back onto the ribbon with little scenery to hide the line.

Mute City and the big-name cups reward memorizing a jump rather than admiring a skyline. Silence around the track, more than billboards, is what the eye gets at that speed.
wave-race-64:
Buoys, not banners, judge the line in Wave Race 64. A missed red buoy drops the whole heat. Miss the colored markers on a jet ski and the judges cut the score, while the water itself lifts or buries the hull.

Nintendo shipped the racer in the Nintendo 64 launch window of 1996, as a showcase of moving waves rather than a mascot tour. Dolphin Park and stormier courses change how the same buoy gate should be taken.

Later sequels are separate. The original's trick is the swell: a jump off a crest can clear a gate that a flat-water line would clip.
1080-snowboarding:
Trick lines and clocked descents share 1080 Snowboarding. A spin has to be landed, not just triggered, and a missed grab costs the run more than a pretty animation would suggest.

Nintendo's Nintendo 64 snowboard game arrived in 1998, with contest, time-attack, and match modes on courses that range from open slopes to caves. 1080 Avalanche on GameCube is the later cousin, not this cartridge.

The title trick, a full 1080 spin, is a commitment in the air. Weight on the board and the landing window matter more than a costume change.
goldeneye-007:
Film objectives turned a license into a shooter in GoldenEye 007. The Facility's checklist is stricter than a simple firefight. Plant the covert modem, photograph the scientist, or beat the clock out of the facility, and the gun is only one tool on the list.

Rare built the Nintendo 64 version in 1997, the one living rooms played, with split-screen maps and modes such as Slappers Only. The Dam, the Facility, and Natalya's escort sit beside Oddjob's low hat in multiplayer.

A later reimagining is a different product. Proximity mines and the watch magnet belong to this cartridge's invention of console aiming with a single stick.
kirby-64-the-crystal-shards:
Paired copy powers are the puzzle in Kirby 64: The Crystal Shards. Inhale two abilities and they fuse, so ice and a cutter, or spark and a bomb, solve a gap the platforms alone will not.

HAL Laboratory and Nintendo released it in 2000, the Nintendo 64 Kirby between the SNES games and later handheld adventures. Ribbon accompanies Kirby while Dark Matter scatters crystal shards across planets such as Shiver Star and Ripple Star.

Finding every shard asks for the right fusion, not just a cleared room. A combination that shatters a barrier on one world is useless scenery on the next.
mario-tennis:
Charge shots sit under familiar faces in Mario Tennis. Hold the swing, release a powered ball, and the point becomes a different argument from a flat rally.

Camelot and Nintendo opened a sports line with the Nintendo 64 game in 2000. Waluigi's twisted stance was new on that roster. Waluigi debuted on this roster beside Mario, Luigi, Peach, and Bowser, and later Camelot tennis games on newer Nintendo systems continued the idea.

Tournaments are short and readable. The charge is the mechanic a new player can see, while the character's court coverage still decides a long point.
diddy-kong-racing:
An island hub ties three vehicle types together in Diddy Kong Racing. Karts, hovercraft, and planes share Timber's Island, and each world ends with a boss rather than a simple cup trophy.

Rare shipped the Nintendo 64 racer in 1997, the same generation as Mario Kart 64 and a direct rival for the living-room race. Taj the genie, T.T.'s challenges, and Wizpig give the adventure a campaign the pure cup structure does not.

Balloons feed a boost, and bananas are a weapon. Switching from a plane back to a kart for a boss rematch is the loop Rare built into the hub.
yoshis-story:
Fruit scores replace a long overworld in Yoshi's Story. Each short page clears when the chosen fruit is eaten, and the picture-book look frames a Nintendo 64 side-scroller that is softer than Yoshi's Island.

Nintendo released it in 1997, with six colored Yoshis and a melon that counts for more than a common apple. Baby Bowser's pages are brief, scored, and replayable, closer to a graded snack run than to a fortress siege.

The SNES Yoshi's Island remains the larger island adventure. Here the joy meter and the fruit quota are the finish line, and a perfect page is a high score rather than a rescued baby.
mario-golf:
Approach shots carry the career in Mario Golf. Club selection and the landing spot matter before the putt, and a small role-playing mode sits under the Mario roster's tournaments.

Camelot and Nintendo released the Nintendo 64 game in 1999, a golf sibling in spirit to their tennis entry. Character differences change distance and spin more than they change the rules of stroke play.

Later Camelot golf games are separate. The Nintendo 64 career is the one where a quiet approach, not a special item, decides the hole.
sin-and-punishment:
Stick aiming drives the rail in Sin and Punishment. The shooter moves on a fixed path while the control stick places the shot, which is a different demand from a free camera.

Treasure released the Nintendo 64 game in Japan in 2000, and players elsewhere noticed it later. Saki and Airan run the on-rails stages, and a Wii follow-up, Star Successor, arrived years afterward as its own game.

Score and survival share the screen. A locked path means the skill is leading the reticle, not exploring a corridor for a hidden door.
pokemon-puzzle-league:
Panel stacks wear anime faces in Pokemon Puzzle League. Clear a block the way Tetris Attack taught, and Ash's side of the match reacts, but there is no gym badge at the end.

Nintendo's Nintendo 64 puzzle, released in 2000, skins the panel-matching tradition with the Pokemon cartoon cast. It is a versus puzzle, not a journey through a region with a starter and a league.

Chains and garbage blocks decide the round. The Pokedex never grows here; the combo counter does.
kirbys-dream-land-2:
Animal friends rewrite copy powers in Kirby's Dream Land 2. Rick's hamster back changes a spark into a different tool. Rick the hamster, Coo the owl, and Kine the fish each change what a swallowed ability can do, which the first Dream Land never asked.

HAL Laboratory and Nintendo put this second Game Boy Kirby out in 1995, between the original Dream Land and the later color follow-up. A spark swallowed while riding Coo is a different tool from the same spark on foot.

Dark Matter is the threat at the end of the rainbow islands. Puzzles that need Kine's swimming form will not open for a player who never goes back for the right partner.
pokemon-blue:
Blastoise marks the box, and the tall grass differs, in Pokemon Blue. Wild encounters and a starter story beat diverge from Pokemon Red so a link cable has something to trade.

Game Freak and Nintendo treated this as the other half of the 1996 Game Boy pair, not as a sequel. The same Kanto gym path still runs from a professor's lab toward a league, with version-exclusive creatures filling the gaps Red does not stock.

Blue is not a remake and not a new region. Trainers still need a friend's cartridge if they want the creatures this version never places in the weeds.
pokemon-yellow:
Pikachu refuses the ball and walks behind the hero in Pokemon Yellow. The story leans on the anime's first season, with Team Rocket's Jessie and James turning up in a way Red and Blue did not stage.

Game Freak and Nintendo released this special Game Boy edition in 1998, after the Red and Blue pair, still inside the same generation of monsters. The starter is Pikachu rather than a choice of three, and the following partner reacts on the screen.

Brock and the early anime beats color the towns. It remains Kanto, not a new map, which is why Yellow is a special edition rather than Generation Two.
tetris-game-boy:
Packed cartridges taught a generation the well in Tetris. Nintendo's Game Boy puzzle, the one bundled with an enormous number of systems, made falling blocks a habit you could take on a bus.

The four-square tetrominoes still lock when a row fills, and the music that speeds up near the top of the well is part of the panic. In 1989 that portable loop, not a later themed edition, is what this record means by the name.

Alexey Pajitnov's design is the ruleset. The Game Boy edition is the one that turned those rules into a handheld routine, distinct from cabinet and computer versions that came with other furniture.
pokemon-silver:
Lugia waits at the version's edge in Pokemon Silver. Legendary and wild-encounter differences set it apart from Pokemon Gold, while Johto's gyms and the day-night clock stay the shared journey.

Game Freak and Nintendo released this other 1999 Game Boy Color edition as a pair, not as a sequel and not as the later DS remake. HeartGold and SoulSilver rebuilt the trip years afterward and belong on their own pages.

Kanto still opens after the league. Silver's exclusive creatures are the reason a Gold cartridge stayed in a friend's Game Boy Color.
wario-land-3:
Status effects replace death in Wario Land 3. A flattened Wario still rolls into the next door. A crush, a burn, or a flatten does not end the run; it changes Wario's body so a new path through the level can open.

Nintendo's Game Boy Color puzzle-platformer, released in 2000, cares more about those transformations than about a score attack. Treasures hidden behind the right status are the goals, and a golf mini-interruption is not the point of the map.

Going back into an earlier stage with a new weakness is progress. The music-box treasures stay locked until the correct crushed, snowball, or bouncing form can reach them.
mario-tennis-gbc:
A tennis rookie levels up between matches in Mario Tennis. Camelot's Game Boy Color story mode builds that original character through a school calendar, which the arcade-style Nintendo 64 game does not spend its time on.

The two Camelot games share a name and a year, 2000, and the handheld is the story-heavy sibling. RPG stats, coaches, and tournament brackets sit between exhibition matches against Mario's familiar roster.

Transfer-Pak exchanges with the Nintendo 64 version tied the rookie to the home console. The campaign on the color handheld is still its own school year, not a reduced copy of the N64 tournaments.
metal-gear-solid-gbc:
Ghost Babel is the Japanese name on the box for Metal Gear Solid. Konami built a stealth mission for Game Boy Color in 2000, rather than shrinking the PlayStation scenes one for one.

Solid Snake still hides, watches a radar, and slips past guards, but the rooms and the story were authored for the handheld. Outer Heaven's legacy hangs over the plot without replaying the console game's set pieces.

Cardboard-box gags and codec chatter fit the small screen. Players who wanted the PlayStation radar memories found a different infiltration here, which is why the cartridge stands as its own Metal Gear chapter.
shantae:
Hair whip and a belly dance share a button rhythm in Shantae. The half-genie transforms after the dance, and a monkey, elephant, spider, or harpy form reaches a door Sequin Land will not open for her human shape.

WayForward released the Game Boy Color cartridge late, in 2002, when many players had already moved on. Risky Boots harasses Scuttle Town, Uncle helps from the workshop, and the towns between dungeons are part of the walk.

Later Shantae games continued long after the color handheld ended. Scuttle Town's dance transformation is the key later sequels kept rewriting.
dragon-warrior-iii-gbc:
Class changes reshape the party in Dragon Warrior III. A soldier, a pilgrim, a wizard, or a goof-off can be reclassed, and the hero's group is built rather than handed over as a fixed cast.

Enix's Game Boy Color edition, released in 2000, is the portable color remake of the NES epic. The map eventually opens into a second world, Alefgard, the kingdom players of the first quest already knew, which is the story turn the remake preserves.

Daylight on the color screen makes the towns easier to read than the NES tiles. It is the cartridge many players used when they wanted Dragon Quest III in a pocket, classes and all.
pokemon-sapphire:
Kyogre stirs the sea, and Team Aqua drives the plot, in Pokemon Sapphire. Version-exclusive teams and that legendary set it apart from Pokemon Ruby, while Hoenn's gym circuit stays the shared map.

Game Freak and Nintendo released this other 2002 Game Boy Advance edition as a pair. Alpha Sapphire, the much later 3DS remake, is a different game and not the cartridge described here.

Weather on the field matches the cover beast. A Ruby owner still needs a trade if the creature they want was never programmed into Sapphire's grass.
pokemon-emerald:
Both cover beasts share the story in Pokemon Emerald. Rayquaza joins the conflict between Groudon and Kyogre, and the Battle Frontier opens a post-league challenge the first Hoenn pair did not include.

Game Freak and Nintendo released this third Hoenn version on Game Boy Advance in 2004, refining the same region rather than starting a new one. Wallace's champion room and the Frontier facilities give returning trainers a reason to keep the cartridge after the credits.

It is still Hoenn, not a remake on a later handheld. The two legendaries both matter in the plot, which is the story change from picking only Ruby's path or only Sapphire's.
pokemon-leafgreen:
Venusaur's region returns ready to link in Pokemon LeafGreen. The paired remake of Pokemon Blue was built to trade with FireRed, and the Sevii Islands extend Kanto past the original eight gyms.

Game Freak and Nintendo put this other 2004 Kanto remake on Game Boy Advance. Wireless adapter trades and the postgame islands distinguish the cartridge from the 1996 Game Boy pair it retells.

LeafGreen is not a Johto game and not Emerald's Hoenn Frontier. A FireRed owner is the intended partner, which is why the two remakes shipped as a matched set.
the-legend-of-zelda-a-link-to-the-past-f:
Four colored Links share a quest beside an older Hyrule on The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past & Four Swords. The Game Boy Advance cartridge carries a portable Dark World journey and a separate multiplayer hunt against Vaati.

Nintendo released that double bill in 2002. Vaati's gem steal can undo a friend's progress. The single-player half retells the SNES pendants, the Master Sword, and the light-dark map, while Four Swords asks friends to pull in the same direction or steal a force gem.

The SNES cartridge remains its own record. Vaati's cooperative stages, and the four tunic colors, are the new mode that justified a second listing.
pikmin:
Captain Olimar has until sunset in Pikmin. The Hocotate Freight pilot, crashed with the S.S. Dolphin, directs red, yellow, and blue plant-animals to carry ship parts before the day's light ends.

Nintendo released that first rescue on GameCube in 2001. The Onion spits the squad out again at dawn. A hard day limit means an unfinished bridge is abandoned at dusk, and the next morning starts from the Onion rather than from a mid-combat save.

Nintendo later gathered this crash and its sequel in a Switch collection. That package is a different listing; the sunset countdown and the Dolphin's missing parts belong to the GameCube original.
pikmin-2:
Debt replaces the sunset clock in Pikmin 2. Purple Pikmin lift what the red ones cannot budge. Louie and Olimar hunt treasure for Hocotate Freight's angry president, and caves drop the squad into dungeons that do not end when the surface gets dark.

Nintendo's GameCube sequel, released in 2004, adds purple and white Pikmin and removes the strict day limit of the first rescue. Poison and buried objects ask for the new colors, while the surface still has a clock that only matters between cave trips.

A later Switch collection pairs this treasure hunt with the first game. The caves, the company debt, and Louie's appetite are the sequel's own problems.
f-zero-gx:
License tests are cruel on purpose in F-Zero GX. Amusement Vision and Nintendo built extremely fast tracks, and the story mode fails a pilot for tapping a wall during a certificate run.

Sega's Amusement Vision developed the GameCube chapter with Nintendo, released in 2003, and it stayed the last mainline F-Zero for a long time. Captain Falcon's story chapters sit beside Grand Prix cups that make the SNES and Nintendo 64 games feel slow.

The AX arcade cabinet shared machines with this disc. A missed boost on a cylinder track is the mistake the license exams were written to punish.
pokemon-colosseum:
Snagging replaces gym badges in Pokemon Colosseum. Wes and Rui steal shadow creatures from trainers in the Orre desert, then purify them, and the campaign never hands you a regional starter and eight badges.

Genius Sonority and Nintendo released the GameCube story in 2003. Miror B's dance is a boss pattern, not a gym badge. Cipher's admins and Miror B. are bosses of a 3D campaign that uses the handheld creatures without being a traditional league quest.

A link to a Game Boy Advance cartridge can deepen the roster. The desert towns and the snag mechanic are the console campaign's own shape.
pokemon-xd-gale-of-darkness:
Purifying a deeper roster drives Pokemon XD: Gale of Darkness. XD001, a shadow Lugia, anchors Genius Sonority's follow-up, and Orre's trainers carry more shadow creatures than Colosseum fielded.

Nintendo published this second GameCube story RPG from Genius Sonority in 2005. Shadow Lugia's file sits at the end of the snag list. The new hero's hometown and the purification chamber return, with a longer list of snags than Wes's campaign.

It is not a gym circuit and not a remake of the first Orre story. Shadow Lugia's file name is the prize the plot keeps pointing at.
super-mario-strikers:
Item tackles would empty a real bench in Super Mario Strikers. Next Level Games and Nintendo built arcade soccer where shells and star power decide a goal as often as a clean pass.

The GameCube original of the Strikers line arrived in 2005. A charged strike ignores the whistle a referee would blow. Bowser in goal and a charged super strike ignore the fouls a referee would call, which is the joke the rules are built around.

Later charged-up sequels, including the Wii follow-up, are separate games. This disc is the first version of that lawless pitch.
kirby-air-ride:
City Trial keeps the stats you earn in Kirby Air Ride. A single accelerator is the main control, and the city mode permanently changes how the Warp Star handles after the timer ends.

HAL Laboratory and Nintendo released the GameCube racer in 2003, and it explains little. Air Ride, Top Ride, and City Trial sit side by side, with copy boxes and legendary machines left for the player to discover.

The checklist of challenges is the manual the game never prints. A machine that felt slow in the morning can become the only one that clears a later stadium goal.
fire-emblem-path-of-radiance:
Ike's mercenaries take contracts in Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance. The Greil Mercenaries march for Crimea against Daein, and the cast splits between beorc and laguz, the people of Tellius who do not all share a human shape.

Intelligent Systems and Nintendo released the GameCube tactics story in 2005. The Black Knight's armor ends a careless advance. A 3D battlefield still resolves in turns, with the Black Knight and Elincia tying the chapters to a war Radiant Dawn later continues on Wii.

Permadeath still punishes a careless advance. Laguz transformation meters make a cat warrior a different unit from a beorc swordmaster standing on the same tile.
tales-of-symphonia:
Lloyd Irving escorts a chosen girl across two worlds in Tales of Symphonia. Colette's pilgrimage through Sylvarant uncovers Tethe'alla, and real-time party battles resolve on the field instead of in a separate turn menu.

Namco's GameCube release in 2003 is the original home version of this Tales story. Exspheres, the Desians, and the World Regeneration travel with the party from town to town.

Later ports moved the same pilgrimage elsewhere. The GameCube disc is where Lloyd's wooden sword and the two-realm map first reached a television.
eternal-darkness:
Sanity effects attack the television, not only the hero, in Eternal Darkness: Sanity's Requiem. Alexandra Roivas reads the Tome in a Rhode Island mansion, and the story jumps across centuries while a meter fills with impossible sounds.

Silicon Knights developed the Nintendo-published GameCube game, released in 2002. Pious Augustus and the ancients are the through-line. A fake save deletion or a volume bar that seems to crawl down are tricks the meter spends on the player.

No sequel sits in this library. The chapter select across historical investigators is the whole of the one-off.
chibi-robo:
Happy points pay the bills for a palm-sized cleaner in Chibi-Robo! The robot scrubs a house at appliance scale, plugs into outlets for watts, and learns the family's troubles from the floor.

Skip Ltd. and Nintendo released the GameCube original in 2005. The living room is the world map: a sofa is a cliff, and a conversation overheard beside a toy is the story beat.

Later games continued the tiny housekeeper in a small Nintendo-published series. The watts meter and the happy-point chores belong to this first house.
viewtiful-joe:
A hero's pose slows the film in Viewtiful Joe. VFX powers, triggered when Joe strikes a stance, stretch a punch or speed the reel, and the side-scrolling brawl treats the stage as a movie set.

Clover Studio and Capcom debuted it on GameCube in 2003, before the later versions on other hardware. Captain Blue's lesson and Silvia's kidnapping send Joe into the film world, where Mach Speed and Zoom are weapons.

The PS2 release came afterward. The GameCube brawler is the first time the pose meter decided a street fight.
soulcalibur-ii:
Link brings a Nintendo hero into Namco's weapon duel in SoulCalibur II. The GameCube edition of the 2002 fighter uses that guest, while the ring-outs and the eight-way weapon combat stay Namco's system.

The home release reached GameCube in 2003. Link's spinner is Namco's guest, not a Hyrule dungeon item. Mitsurugi's katana and Ivy's whip still define the roster, and Link's spinner and bombs are the reason this edition sits among Nintendo characters even though Nintendo did not develop it.

Heihachi and Spawn guested on other consoles' editions. Those discs are not this one; the Master Sword on the weapon select is.
super-mario-galaxy:
Rosalina's Comet Observatory hubs the planetoids of Super Mario Galaxy. Each small world has its own gravity, so a walk over the horizon is progress, and orchestral set pieces mark the domes between visits.

Nintendo released the Wii adventure in 2007. Star Bits, Lumas, and Bee Mario's flight belong to these gravity puzzles. Super Mario Galaxy 2 is a different game, with its own ship and its own Yoshi.

A limited Switch compilation included the first Galaxy for a time. The observatory, the pull stars, and Rosalina's storybook are the Wii journey.
wii-sports-resort:
MotionPlus swordplay opens the holiday on Wii Sports Resort. Archery, cycling, and air sports share Wuhu Island, and the add-on in the remote is what makes a wrist turn read as a blade angle.

Nintendo's follow-up to Wii Sports arrived in 2009. The Frisbee dog waits on the same island as the sword duel. Table tennis, wakeboarding, and the Frisbee dog use the same island map, which the original sports pack never had.

Switch Sports is a later product. The sword duel on the island dock, and the cycling race around Wuhu, belong to this MotionPlus sequel.
wii-fit:
Balance Board pressure is the controller in Wii Fit. Yoga poses, strength tests, and a body-test score sell a routine, and there is no final boss waiting after the last pose.

Nintendo released the trainer in 2007. A tree pose fails when the board feels the wobble. The board under the feet measures center of balance, so a tree pose fails for a wobble the remote never needed to see.

Later Fit follow-ups are separate products. The body-test graph and the yoga calendar start on this board.
metroid-prime-3-corruption:
Phazon corruption fuels hypermode in Metroid Prime 3: Corruption. Samus crosses several planets in a PED suit, and the meter that grants the overpowered visor also punishes staying in it too long.

Retro Studios and Nintendo closed the original Prime trilogy on Wii in 2007. Hypermode on the PED suit is a timed risk. Norion, Bryyo, Elysia, and the Pirate Homeworld are separate landings, with Aurora Units and Dark Samus tying the Federation plot together.

The Wii remote aims the arm cannon. Hypermode is the risk the trilogy's last chapter adds, not a color swap on the Gravity Suit.
kirbys-epic-yarn:
Beads and patches replace a life bar in Kirby's Epic Yarn. Kirby is a yarn outline in Patch Land, and falling off a stage costs beads rather than a death in the usual sense.

Good-Feel developed the Wii game with HAL Laboratory and Nintendo, released in 2010. Yin-Yarn stole the yarn that Prince Fluff wants back. Prince Fluff, the yarn whip, and transformations into a tank or a train are the tools, while Yin-Yarn is the thief who unraveled the world.

A later 3DS port exists. The Wii original is the one where a missed platform spills beads and the patchwork goal still waits at the end of the cloth.
animal-crossing-city-folk:
A bus leaves the village for a city in Animal Crossing: City Folk. The Wii town keeps the daily clock, and the city shops, including Gracie's, sit at the other end of that ride.

Nintendo released it in 2008, between the GameCube original and New Leaf on 3DS. Voice chat, tied to the era's microphone accessory, is a feature the series later dropped.

The bus pass is the new geography. Turnip prices and birthday parties still run on the village clock, while the city is a destination rather than a second saved town.
super-paper-mario:
Flipping into the foreground solves walls in Super Paper Mario. The side-scroller jumps into a depth axis, and the result plays closer to an action adventure than to the turn-based battles of earlier Paper Mario stories.
