A swallowed ship and a beast's interior set the scene in Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 3 - Lair of the Leviathan. Third of five episodes in Telltale's 2009 season, it keeps Guybrush Threepwood as the pirate lead while the hunt for a cure continues.

Morgan LeFlay's bounty-hunter interest in Guybrush and the crew trapped with the creature give the jokes somewhere to stand. The Leviathan is not a backdrop; the episode takes place in its shadow and its gut.

LucasArts' older Monkey Island games are a different set of islands. This chapter is Telltale's third slice, the one that walks into the creature named in the title.

LeChuck's last transformation closes the season in Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 5 - Rise of the Pirate God. Telltale ended its five-episode 2009 Monkey Island run with this chapter, the one that has to answer the pox and the pirate god of the title.

Guybrush, Elaine, and the crossroads of the season's deaths and deals meet a final set of conversations. The episode is a finale, so jokes planted on Spinner Cay and inside the Leviathan are expected to pay off.

Four earlier chapters are required if the god's rise is going to mean anything. This fifth one is Telltale's curtain, not a LucasArts sequel with a new subtitle.

A warrant with the hero's name on it drives Tales of Monkey Island Complete Pack: Chapter 4 - The Trial and Execution of Guybrush Threepwood. Fourth in Telltale's 2009 run, the episode puts Guybrush in the dock and lets the title spoil how serious the court claims to be.

Flotsam Island's pirates, a judge with a grudge, and the pox still walking around outside the courtroom keep the adventure from being a single dialogue tree. The cross-examination is a puzzle, and the execution is the threat the chapter's name refuses to whisper.

Telltale's season is five chapters long. This fourth stop is the trial, the one that prints Guybrush Threepwood's name as the accused.
ori-and-the-will-of-the-wisps:
Wisps with separate gifts replace a single light in Ori and the Will of the Wisps. Moon Studios followed its hand-painted platformer in 2020, again published with Microsoft, and Ku the young owl shares the journey through Niwen.

Bash, a grapple, and a wisp that becomes a hammer or a burrow change how a grove is crossed. The Blind Forest was the previous story; this one mourns a different loss and then hands Ori a set of spirits instead of one companion light.

Sein, the light from the first adventure, is not the tool bar here. The wisps, Ku, and Niwen's decay are the sequel's own map.
hotline-miami-2-wrong-number:
Several masked killers, not one Jacket, split the timeline in Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number. Dennaton's top-down sequel arrived in 2015, larger and more divisive than the 2012 original.

A door kick, a melee finish, and a level that fails the moment a bullet touches the body remain the rules. The sequel adds playable fans, soldiers, and a story that argues about the first game's violence instead of only repeating the calls.

The 2012 original is the tighter fever dream. Wrong Number is the argumentative follow-up, more characters and less agreement about whether the series should have continued.
resident-evil-6:
Leon, Chris, Jake, and Ada each carry a campaign in Resident Evil 6, Capcom's push toward broader action. Helena, Piers, and Sherry stand beside those four leads in the 2012 story.

Cover, a melee counter, and a set piece with a vehicle sit on top of the old virus panic. Jake Muller, tied to Albert Wesker's bloodline, is the new face, while Ada's chapters keep the double-cross habit.

Earlier outbreaks were one city and a smaller cast. This entry splits the globe and the save file across four stories that intersect and then leave again.
grim-fandango-remastered:
Manny Calavera sells tickets to the afterlife in Grim Fandango Remastered. Double Fine's 2015 update refreshes Tim Schafer's 1998 LucasArts adventure about a travel agent in the Land of the Dead.

Rubacava, Meche, and the Department of Death remain the noir route, now with updated movement and cleaner art over the original calaca cast. The year of the dead he has to survive is the plot's clock, and the scam is a premium ticket his clients never receive.

LucasArts released the first telling. Double Fine's remaster is the same travel-agent mystery with the stubborn original controls made less hostile.
the-outer-worlds:
The Halcyon colony's corporations own the air in The Outer Worlds. Obsidian's satirical first-person role-playing game, published by Private Division in 2019, lets a thawed passenger take jobs for rival boards.

Phineas, the Hope, and a town that will raise or cut your reputation are the campaign's anchors. Dialogue can skip a gunfight, and a flaw system will brand the character with a penalty in exchange for a perk.

Fallout-style companions exist, but the joke is the letterhead. Spacer's Choice and the other brands are the villains, and Halcyon is the company town in orbit.
broforce:
One life, one bro, and a level that collapses if the explosion is too generous define Broforce. Free Lives' run-and-gun, published by Devolver Digital in 2015, parodies action movies by making each bro a send-up of a film hero.

Rambro and a musclebound cyborg are the kind of aliases on the roster, and the terrain itself is destructible dirt. Friendly hostages flex when rescued, then the next drop loads a different bro without asking.

Devolver's taste for loud indie shooters fits the joke. The game is a film marathon where every star is renamed, armed, and extremely likely to die.
the-walking-dead-season-2:
Clementine holds the flashlight in The Walking Dead: Season 2, Telltale's follow-up with the child as the lead. The comic-based adventure from 2013 leaves Lee behind and puts her choices at the center.

A cabin group, a ski lodge, and choices about who eats or who is left behind are the season's arguments. Walkers are the threat at the door, but the conversations about trust do more damage.

Lee's season taught Clementine how to hold a hammer. This second season asks what she does with that lesson when the adults keep failing.
borderlands-3:
New vault hunters board the ship in Borderlands 3, Gearbox's next looter-shooter. Amara, Moze, Zane, and FL4K replace the earlier quartet in the 2019 campaign.

The Calypso twins, a siren-worshipping cult, and guns whose parts barely fit one description are the campaign. Pandora is no longer the only planet, so a firefight can happen on a swamp world or a city-sized corporation.

Borderlands 2 had ended on Handsome Jack. This sequel picks a new pack of hunters and a pair of streamer-tyrant villains, and it keeps the habit of a gun that should not logically work.
syberia-2:
The clockwork train is still moving in Syberia 2, Benoit Sokal's sequel about Kate Walker and Hans Voralberg. The 2004 journey continues the trip begun in the 2002 game, toward the mammoths Hans has chased for a lifetime.

Youkol people, a frozen tract, and Kate's decision to abandon her law office for good are the new ground. Puzzle panels on the train and in the ice use the same point-and-click patience as the first trip.

The 2002 game ended with Kate choosing the train over her old life. This sequel is that choice played out, Hans fading, the island of Syberia still ahead.
celeste:
Madeline climbs, and a darker double climbs after her, in Celeste. Maddy Thorson and Noel Berry's 2018 platformer sends her up the mountain and was praised for its assist options as much as for the precision of the jumps.

Strawberries, B-sides, and a feather that needs calm steering are the extras around the main ascent. Badeline, the other self, is both antagonist and companion, which keeps the story inside the climb instead of in a cutscene town.

Assist mode can slow the game or grant extra air. The mountain does not get shorter; the options simply admit that the summit should be reachable by more than one kind of player.
to-the-moon:
Sigmund Corp edits a dying man's memories in To the Moon. Kan Gao and Freebird Games released it in 2011, an RPG Maker story about granting Johnny's wish by walking his life backward.

Doctors Eva Rosalene and Neil Watts argue in the machine while the scenes jump from a lighthouse to a school gym. The wish is the moon, and the reason Johnny wants it is the mystery the doctors are not supposed to rewrite carelessly.

Combat is not the point of the tileset. The game is two scientists, one patient, and a life they have to read from the end toward the beginning.
frostpunk:
Coal, hope, and a generator in the town square decide who freezes in Frostpunk. 11 bit studios' 2018 city builder is about keeping the last settlement alive around that generator in an endless winter.

Laws can permit child labor or a house of healing, and the hope and discontent meters move when the captain chooses. New London's streets have to be drawn inside the heat radius or the people beyond it die.

The studio's earlier work had asked moral questions in a smaller frame. Here the moral question is a temperature, a coal pile, and a law book.
smite:
Gods from separate mythologies share three lanes in SMITE. Hi-Rez's free-to-play battleground pits them against each other in a third-person fight, and it left beta for a full release in 2015.

Zeus, Anubis, and Sun Wukong can meet in one match, with abilities aimed in space rather than clicked from a top-down cursor. A titan at each base, a jungle between the lanes, and a relic shop are the battleground's furniture.

Most games of this shape stay overhead and use original heroes. SMITE's camera sits behind a god's shoulder, and the roster is borrowed from actual belief.
borderlands-game-of-the-year-enhanced:
Lilith, Mordecai, Brick, and Roland return with a cleaner picture in Borderlands Game of the Year Enhanced. Gearbox's 2009 looter shooter came back in 2019 with updated visuals and a handful of gameplay additions.

Pandora's vault, Claptrap's annoying help, and the original four classes are still the trip. The enhanced edition is not a new hunter's story; it is the first game's atlas corporation war made easier to read on a newer screen.

Borderlands 2 and 3 are later wars. This edition is the first vault hunt, Jack still absent, the Destroyer still the thing under the ground.
batman-arkham-asylum:
The Joker's takeover of the island is the whole night in Batman: Arkham Asylum. Rocksteady started the Arkham series in 2009, a stealth-action game set inside the asylum and written with Paul Dini.

Detective vision, a gargoyle perch, and freeflow punches against thugs structure the rooms. Scarecrow's distorted corridors and Killer Croc's sewer are detours, while the Joker holds the control room and the PA system.

Later Arkham games open the city. This first one locks Batman inside the asylum with Dini's rogues and makes the building the villain's weapon.
dead-by-daylight:
Generators, hooks, and one killer define a match of Dead by Daylight. Behaviour Interactive's 2016 asymmetric horror game pits four survivors against that single hunter.

Repairing a generator opens the gate, and a hook is how the killer turns a grab into a sacrifice for the Entity. The Trapper's bear traps and the Hillbilly's chainsaw were among the original ways to die, long before licensed guests arrived.

A survivor's win is a gate and a sprint. The killer's win is a set of hooks, which is why the two roles do not share a single objective.
overcooked:
Orders pile up while the floor catches fire in Overcooked. Ghost Town Games' cooperative kitchen game, published by Team17 in 2016, is about cooking under a timer as the kitchen itself falls apart.

Chopping, a pot, a plate, and a delivery window are the verbs, and an onion that has not been cut will not become soup. Some kitchens split in half, slide on a truck, or fill with ice so the chefs cannot stand still.

The Onion Kingdom's disaster is the excuse for the chaos. Two or more cooks have to shout a plan, because one pair of hands cannot watch every burner.
stalker-shadow-of-chernobyl:
The Marked One wakes on a truck and goes looking for Strelok in S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Shadow of Chernobyl. GSC Game World opened its series in 2007 with this first-person survival shooter in the Zone around the Chernobyl plant.

Anomalies, a blowout, and factions such as Duty and Freedom make the road to the plant a political hike as well as a gunfight. The Wish Granter under the sarcophagus is the rumor every stalker is chasing, including the man with the tattoo.

Later Zone games moved the date and the protagonist. This one is the Marked One's walk, the 1986 disaster's fictional aftermath, and the plant as a final door.
human-fall-flat:
Limp hands and a dreamlike obstacle course carry Human: Fall Flat. No Brakes Games' 2016 physics puzzle stars a wobbly human figure whose grip is the only reliable tool.

A lever, a crate, and a friend who can be stood on become the solutions, and the figure's legs are a suggestion. Later updates and a shared online session turned the stumble into a popular party pastime.

The single dreamer is the original image. Co-op is what most groups met afterward, still grabbing, still falling, still treating gravity as the enemy.
the-long-dark:
Wolves, cold, and an empty cupboard are the antagonists in The Long Dark. Hinterland's Canadian wilderness survival game entered early access in 2014, with its story mode, Wintermute, arriving later.

Will Mackenzie and Dr. Astrid Greenwood carry that story across Great Bear, while a separate survival sandbox drops a player into the weather with no plot at all. Matches, a hatchet, and a cave are worth more than a gunshot that attracts everything nearby.

The early-access years were the sandbox. Wintermute is the narrative layer Hinterland added once the cold itself was already a finished system.
stray-2:
A cat and a drone named B-12 share the streets in Stray. BlueTwelve Studio's 2022 adventure, published by Annapurna Interactive, follows that cat through a sealed city inhabited by robots.

Zurks in the dark, a vest the cat can wear so B-12 has a body, and a society of robots who have forgotten the humans are the route. Jumping to a ledge a person could not use is the cat's advantage, and the city is walled shut on purpose.

Annapurna's publishing and BlueTwelve's small team put a wordless animal at the center. B-12 translates; the cat does the climbing.
mortal-kombat-11:
Custom moves and a goddess of time share the roster in Mortal Kombat 11, NetherRealm's mix of guests and regulars. The 2019 kit lets a player edit specials instead of accepting one fixed moveset.

Kronika's hourglass is the plot, rewinding grudges so past versions of fighters can stand next to their older selves. Gear, a variation of specials, and the usual fatality close a round that started as a footsie game.

Earlier chapters had fixed each fighter's toolkit more tightly. This one lets a player edit the kit, then still expects the guest star and the series villain to share a stage.
dark-souls8482-remastered:
Lordran's bonfires burn again in Dark Souls: Remastered. FromSoftware's 2011 action role-playing game returned in 2018, including the Artorias of the Abyss content.

The Chosen Undead, Solaire's summon sign, and a boss such as Ornstein still define the pilgrimage. Artorias, Manus, and the township in the DLC are part of this package rather than a separate purchase, which is the remaster's practical gift.

The original release is the one that created the vocabulary of the bonfire. This edition carries that same undead walk, plus the abyss chapter, onto later hardware.
it-takes-two-2:
Cody and May, turned into dolls, have to cooperate or stop moving in It Takes Two. Hazelight and Josef Fares made the co-op-only platformer in 2021, and it won Game of the Year at The Game Awards.

Dr. Hakim's book and a new toy-sized world every chapter force each partner to use a different verb. One player may swing while the other turns a screw, and there is no mode that lets a single person play both.

The award recognized a game that refuses a solo campaign. The marriage plot is the excuse; the design is two controllers and a level that will not function on one.
darksiders-ii-deathinitive-edition:
Death, not War, carries the scythe in Darksiders II Deathinitive Edition. The 2015 enhanced rerelease updates the 2012 sequel, which shifts the horseman lead from War to Death.

Loot, dungeons, and a skill tree make this horseman's journey closer to a loot adventure than War's more linear wrath. The Crowfather, the Nephilim history, and a split between the land of the dead and a living kingdom structure the ride.

The first Darksiders game is War's apocalypse. Deathinitive is the enhanced form of Death's sequel, the one with the loot and the pale rider.
kotor-ii:
The Exile's missing connection to the Force is the wound in Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Sith Lords. Obsidian's 2004 sequel followed BioWare's role-playing game and is famous for a rushed launch later patched by fans.

Kreia, Atton, and the Sith threats Darth Sion and Darth Nihilus travel a galaxy still broken from the Jedi Civil War. Influence with a companion can change a belief, which fits a story about a protagonist who walks without the Force's usual comfort.

A fan-made restoration later put back scenes the launch discs had cut. The rushed original and that later repair are both part of how players talk about the Exile and Kreia.
beholder:
Cameras in the halls and a ministry quota define a day in Beholder. Warm Lamp Games' 2016 story makes you a landlord in a totalitarian state, ordered to spy on the tenants of your building.

Searching a suitcase, filing a report, and deciding whether to protect a tenant or obey the state are the choices. Rent still has to be collected, because the building is both a home and a trap with a ledger.

The portrait of each tenant is a small life you can ruin for a bonus. The game's cruelty is clerical: a form, a hidden microphone, and a knock at the wrong time.
prison-architect-all-day-and-a-psych:
Cells, a canteen, and a riot meter are the tools in Prison Architect. Introversion's prison-management sim reached a full 1.0 release in 2015 after a long public alpha.

Grants pay for workshops, a regime schedules showers and yard time, and an unfinished toilet will matter more than a pretty admin wing. Prisoners have needs, gangs, and a way of turning a late meal into a fire.

The alpha years let players watch the simulation grow in public. The 1.0 release is the point where that open building set became a finished warden's job.
resident-evil-2-2019:
The Raccoon City police station locks behind Leon and Claire in Resident Evil 2, Capcom's over-the-shoulder remake. Mr. X paces the halls of the 2019 retelling of the 1998 outbreak.

A zapping-style pair of routes, Ada's side path, and William Birkin's mutations keep the original's structure. The licker in a dark corridor and the orphan Sherry still belong to the station and the orphanage night.

The 1998 game used fixed cameras and a tank-like step. This remake keeps Leon, Claire, and the station, and it puts the camera behind their shoulders.
jotun:
Thora proves herself to the Norse gods by fighting giants in Jotun: Valhalla Edition. Thunder Lotus Games' hand-painted boss battles were packaged as this complete form of the 2015 game.

A finger-painted fjord, a god who offers a blessing, and a jotun who fills the screen more than the heroine does are the encounters. Health is a short bar, and the fight is about learning a giant's reach rather than managing a party.

The Valhalla name marks the edition that gathers the whole set of those duels. Thora, the giants, and the painted storms are the game underneath the subtitle.
trine-enchanted-edition:
A thief, a wizard, and a knight share one soul-box in Trine Enchanted Edition. The edition refreshes Frozenbyte's 2009 puzzle platformer, in which Zoya, Amadeus, and Pontius combine grapples, boxes of magic, and a straightforward charge.

Physics puzzles want the wizard's crate, the thief's rope, or the knight's weight on a switch, and only one body acts at a time unless players share the session. The enchanted release updates the original's look and its interface.

Frozenbyte's fairy-tale forest is the setting both versions walk. The three classes, and the rule that their skills must be combined, are what the title's binding spell is for.
enter-the-gungeon:
Blanks, tables, and a gun that should not exist fill Enter the Gungeon. Dodge Roll's bullet-hell roguelike, published by Devolver Digital in 2016, is set in a dungeon whose entire ecology is firearms.

The Marine, the Convict, the Hunter, and the Pilot start with different kits, then lose the run to a Bullet King or a rolling shotgun shell. A blank clears the screen of bullets, which is often worth more than the gun that fired them.

Each descent randomizes the chests. Dying spends the run, and the next trip into the Gungeon starts from the breach with whatever knowledge the player kept and the character did not.
re-revelations-2:
Claire Redfield and Barry Burton share an island in Resident Evil Revelations 2, Capcom's episodic sequel. Claire travels with Moira Burton while Barry's path pairs him with Natalia, and the episodes arrived in 2015.

A bracelet that detects fear, a tower of cells, and Raid mode's extra missions sit around the episode drops. The story arrives in chapters, so a week could separate Claire's cliffhanger from Barry's answer.

Revelations had already taken the series onto a ship. This second one moves to the island, the two Burtons, and a release schedule that did not dump the whole campaign on day one.
resident-evil-3:
Nemesis hunts Jill through a burning Raccoon City in Resident Evil 3, Capcom's shorter companion to the second remake. The 2020 retelling keeps Jill Valentine at the center of the 1999 story.

Carlos Oliveira, a subway escape, and the bioweapon that will not stay down are the beats this version keeps. The remake is tighter than the police-station game beside it, trading some of the old city's optional streets for a chase.

The 1999 original introduced the pursuer in a fixed-camera city. This retelling keeps Jill, Nemesis, and Carlos, and it assumes the player already met Leon and Claire's station.
fornite-battle-royale:
A battle bus and a closing storm define a match of Fortnite Battle Royale. Epic Games launched the free 100-player mode in 2017, and it quickly overshadowed the original Save the World campaign.

Building a wall mid-fight, looting a chest, and being the last person inside the circle are the rules that the campaign of monster waves never used. The storm shrinks the island on a clock, so a quiet loot route still has to move.

Save the World was the game Epic had been making. Battle Royale is the mode that took the island, the building, and the audience, and left the campaign in its shadow.
mark-of-the-ninja:
Sound rings and light cones are visible on purpose in Mark of the Ninja. Klei's 2012 side-view stealth game shows those signals so a takedown can be planned instead of hoped for.

A guard's gaze is a shape on the floor, and a footstep draws a circle the player can see and the guard cannot. Terror, a score for style, and a path that avoids killing are options once the information is honest.

Klei's other games hide different kinds of systems. This one hides the ninja and reveals the senses, which is the opposite of a stealth game that makes the player guess.
bomberman-quest:
Hudson Soft took White Bomberman off the single-screen bomb grid and sent him walking across a world map in Bomberman Quest, a 1998 Game Boy Color journey. Monsters occupy pockets of land, and the bombs he finds do not share one blast. A fight is decided by which effect he brought, whether the charge homes, punches, or sits in place until the fuse ends.

Encounters stay small enough to read on the handheld screen. The creature closes distance while the timer runs, and a poorly chosen bomb wastes the only shot that would have reached it. New bombs turn up along the roads, so later fields assume a kit the opening hills never offered.

Towns break the hiking, and a sealed path often waits until the matching bomb is clipped to his pack. Hudson Soft keeps the round face and the bright danger, while the job is to finish the route rather than to outlast a rival bomber.

Maze cartridges live on soft blocks, shrinking arenas, and a last survivor. Progress on this quest is the ground already crossed, the creatures already beaten, and the strange bombs hanging from his belt.
warlocked:
Queen Azarel's humans and Chief Zog's beasts divide Warlocked into two campaigns of real-time war on the Game Boy Color. Bits Studios built the battles, Nintendo published the cartridge in North America in 2000, and units are summoned only by spending resources pulled off the map. A full menu of troop names means nothing when the stockpile is empty.

Fog covers the enemy until a scout walks close enough to see them. Workers haul the resource home, the commander anchors the camp, and fresh bodies appear beside the buildings after the cost is paid. Spend too early and the next wave cannot be called; hesitate and the other faction is already at the wall.

Humans bring archers and knights, beasts bring heavier brutes, and each army has wizards who can afflict the soldiers across the field. Orders shift from holding a point to razing the far camp, and no turn marker ever freezes the field.

Strategy this direct was scarce beside the platformers on that handheld's shelf. The live argument is the resource number against the headcount already deployed. Lose the gathering and the summon list is only a set of names with no one left to answer them.
bionic-commando-elite-forces:
These soldiers cannot jump, so the claw is the only way up in Bionic Commando: Elite Forces. Nintendo Software Technology built the Game Boy Color adventure, and Nintendo published it in 1999. A male commando and a female commando each walk a slightly different route, with starting guns the other does not carry.

Latch the arm overhead, swing, and let go to cross a shaft. Some rooms open a sniper view for a distant shot, a beat the pure swinging games never asked for. Commander Joe has been taken by the Avar forces, and the mission is to bring him back.

The female commando begins with a lighter weapon and a quieter approach, while the male commando opens with heavier fire and a more direct push. Both still fall if the claw misses, because nothing in the move list replaces that grab. Nintendo Software Technology shapes a long run of vertical rooms around that single limitation.

The NES Bionic Commando tells a different war with a different mission list. Here the paired leads, the sniper moments, and the rescue of Joe are the campaign Nintendo actually shipped on the Color handheld.
legend-of-the-river-king-2:
Yuki's Heaven Jewel has been stolen, and fishing it back is the errand inside Legend of the River King 2. Natsume and Victor Interactive brought the Game Boy Color sequel out in 1999. Two brothers can lead, rods improve when the current tackle cannot hold a strike, and a catch book records every species that actually reaches shore. Yuki is the one waiting on that catch.

The Mountain God and the Sea God took the jewel's halves and turned themselves into giant fish, the River King and the Sea King. Smaller catches feed the trip, pay for better gear, and earn the right to fish the next bank. People along the road trade favors for bugs, flowers, and odd jobs, but the line in the water is still the tool the plot requires.

A timed pier contest would weigh one fish and send the angler home. This journey keeps walking, selling, and rebaiting until those divine fish are landed for Yuki. Victor Interactive's structure and Natsume's release leave the jewel, not a ticket total, as the reason to cast.

Lead with the younger brother and one god-fish comes first; lead with the older and the Sea King and River King duties trade places. Either route still lives in the book, the upgraded rod, and the help Yuki asked for. The day is done when the jewel is whole.
dragon-warrior-monsters-2:
Cobi's Journey and Tara's Adventure are the two United States releases of Dragon Warrior Monsters 2, both built by Tose for Enix. Breeding is the daily work: pair two monsters and the child keeps a mix of their skills. In 2001 the adventure moved from island to island, and the boat between shores is how new families enter the matching pool.

A handsome monster with an empty move list still loses, so a pairing is judged by what the offspring can actually do. The two cartridges are not one plot with the cover art swapped; each lead meets the chain of islands from another side. Tose spends the hours on feeding, scouting, and combining rather than on a single dungeon march.

Enix kept the American boxes in the Dragon Warrior line while the raising did the talking. Skip an island and you may miss a family the team has never produced. The next battle is the audit of whatever traits you chose to pass down.

The earlier breeding quest in this series woke inside a monster kingdom and stayed there. These stories leave that kingdom for open water and two separate leads. The goal is still a child stronger than either parent, only now the horizon is a shoreline.
mickeys-racing-adventure:
Rare parked a garage between Mickey and the checkered flag in Mickey's Racing Adventure. Nintendo and Disney share the 1999 Game Boy Color release with Rare, and the kart improves because a hub of minigames pays out parts. An engine or a set of tires from those errands changes the launch, so a bare chassis is not the car you want on the grid.

One side challenge may be a short chase, another a timing test, always inside a Disney setting and always with hardware as the prize. Bolt the part on, then line up against the rest of the cast. Minnie, Donald, Daisy, Goofy, and the others take their own cars, which keeps every rival inside that stable.

Ignore the hub and the kart stays slow, because Rare tied speed to the errand before the event. The circuit repeats as a side challenge, a new piece of the car, then a race. The scenery changes, and the reason to enter it is whichever part is still missing.

Mario's kart games seat a different cast for a different purpose. This adventure earns its pace in minigames, then spends it on Disney drivers and Rare's own feel for a handheld race.
ninja-gaiden-shadow:
What began as a Shadow of the Ninja design reached the Game Boy in 1991 as Ninja Gaiden Shadow, released by Tecmo with Natsume sharing the development. Ryu takes the sword onto side-view stages crowded with soldiers. The swing is short, the screen is narrow, and a long windup does not fit.

Standing close enough to connect is the real spacing problem, and a thrown blade covers the fighter who refuses to approach. Natsume's side-on stance still shows in his posture even though the name on the box, and the man holding the steel, belong to the Gaiden line. A thin health bar makes a sloppy room expensive.

The Shadow of the Ninja direction supplied the original plan, and Tecmo's choice was to ship Ryu under the Ninja Gaiden name. The cartridge you hold is that finished chapter: corridors, a blade, and groups of enemies who drop once the edge lands. Little happens between those rooms except the next group.

NES chapters in the same series stop for cinema scenes between acts. This one stays inside the side-view fighting, with Ryu already drawn and the corridor already full.
solar-striker:
Nintendo R&D1 and Minakuchi Engineering aimed a small ship up the glass and named the vertical shooter Solar Striker. Nintendo published it in 1990, and shooters carrying that publishing credit were rare on the Game Boy. Icons scooped up during the climb rewrite the shot leaving the nose.

A plain pellet can open into a spread or tighten into a heavier beam, and dropping the power returns the weak stream at the worst moment. Bosses already occupy the top edge when that happens. The view never turns sideways: threats fall from above while the craft stays low.

Minakuchi Engineering keeps the formations legible on the tiny display. Nintendo R&D1's hand in the project, together with Nintendo's name on the box, makes this an official first-party shooter on a machine that seldom received one. Hold the powered gun through the pattern and meet whatever caps the climb.

There is no town and no horizontal trek between waves. The cartridge is the ascent, the changing nose gun, and the large silhouettes waiting at the end of each stretch of sky.
kaeru-no-tame-ni-kane-wa-naru:
Prince of Sablé leaves on a rescue and spends much of Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru in the body of a frog. Nintendo and Intelligent Systems released the Game Boy cartridge in Japan in 1992. English-speaking players took to calling it For the Frog the Bell Tolls. The team that made it later made Link's Awakening.

The frog shape is a way through the land, not only a curse to cure. It reaches gaps and landings the prince cannot manage on two legs, so the transformation opens the map. People in the towns still address him as royalty on an errand, even while he travels low to the ground. Fights stay close and brief beside that exploration.

Nintendo published the script in Japanese and never issued an English edition. The cartridge remains an official Nintendo release, sold in Japan through ordinary channels. Readers abroad coined the bell-and-frog nickname from the meaning of the title, and that nickname does not push the product off to the side.

Intelligent Systems and Nintendo folded the prince, the changed body, and a compact set of towns into one quest. Link's Awakening, from that same team afterward, shares the taste for a small world with an unusual condition at its center. The earlier game is the one where the useful body is the frog.
game-watch-gallery:
Manhole, Fire, Octopus, and Oil Panic share Game & Watch Gallery, the collection Nintendo published in 1997. Each chore can be played with the old LCD stick figures or in a redrawn mode that hands the same clock to Mario series characters. The idea of the cartridge is that double life, not a brand-new sport.

Classic mode keeps the sparse shapes and the original split-second demands: cover the holes, catch the people leaping from the flames, slip past tentacles while lifting treasure, catch dripping oil before it ruins the floor. The redrawn mode puts Mario and the cast around him into those jobs, and some of the falling bodies even move at different speeds. Miss the beat and the penalty arrives either way.

This set lives on the original Game Boy and stops after those four. Later collections numbered 2 and 3 add other LCD toys and longer menus. Their extra titles are separate cartridges, not secret pages in this one.

Scores can be stored, yet the play is still the old reflex test in both costumes. Nintendo's publishing is what pairs the LCD look with the Mario look on a single Game Boy release. Oil, tentacles, open holes, and a burning building remain the four emergencies on offer.
mega-man-v-1994:
Stardroids, alien robots rather than the familiar robot masters, are the bosses to clear in Mega Man V (1994). Capcom published the Game Boy cartridge and Minakuchi Engineering developed it, the last classic-style Mega Man on that handheld. Terra leads the invasion, and the Mega Arm throws a returning fist in place of the ordinary buster charge.

Defeat a Stardroid and its weapon joins the menu, preserving the habit of hunting the tool that hurts the next foe. Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto hold stretches of the planet, chosen from a select screen. A later upgrade lets the flying fist grab and pummel, which matters when a normal shot skids off alien armor.

Sunstar, a doomsday machine, waits after those planet bosses, and Doctor Wily cannot keep control of it. Tango the robotic cat comes along as a new helper while the Stardroids occupy the cities. Minakuchi Engineering drew original routes for this roster instead of replaying NES robot-master stages.

The classic Game Boy formula closes on an extraterrestrial lineup and a throwing arm. Later handheld Mega Man stories leave this select-a-boss structure for other kinds of play. Here you still pick a target, cross the stage, and leave with the weapon.
operation-c:
Konami sent a Contra commando onto the Game Boy in 1991 and named the American cartridge Operation C. Europe sold that same game as Probotector, continuing the regional habit of presenting the lead as a robot. Side-view runs alternate with overhead rooms where the gun can point in several directions, and the spread shot is the pickup that clears a crowd.

A sideways corridor is the familiar dash, jump, and stream of fire. An overhead floor turns the soldier into a figure seen from above, threading lanes of bullets across open ground. Aliens and the widening gun keep the feel inside the Contra series, while the stage order belongs to this handheld cartridge alone.

Players in Japan meet it under the Contra title. All three names are official Konami releases of one compact campaign. The European robot presentation changes the body on the box more than it changes the act of shooting through a mixed set of views.

The NES Contra is a longer, separate mission list. Nothing here reprints that run onto a small screen. You take the commando through both camera angles, chase the spread shot, and finish the route Konami laid out for the handheld.
teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-iii-radical:
Michelangelo is the only brother still loose when Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles III: Radical Rescue begins, and Konami built the 1993 Game Boy game around freeing the rest. Leonardo, Raphael, and Donatello become playable as he reaches them, each with a way through the fortress the others lack. The map pushes backward as often as forward, because a newly freed turtle opens a passage already walked past.

Spinning nunchaku let Michelangelo hang over gaps and spikes. Leonardo drills cracked floors with his swords, Raphael withdraws into his shell to fit tight tunnels, and Donatello climbs walls toward exits that were out of reach. Swapping among them is how a locked corridor becomes a route.

Shredder's Foot hold Splinter and April as well as the brothers. Soldiers fill the space between keys and cells, and the fighting itself stays direct so the puzzle can be which body crosses the next obstacle. Konami expects the select screen of rescued turtles to matter more than a longer combo.

This is not the NES tournament fighter, where the brothers duel one another, and it is not Turtles in Time. The Game Boy chapter is a rescue with backtracking and a fortress that opens only in a certain order. Four abilities, not four identical fighters, are what make the rooms solvable.
mole-mania-1996:
Muddy Mole shoves dirt and sets bombs because his family is trapped underground in Mole Mania (1996). Pax Softnica constructed the puzzles, Shigeru Miyamoto produced them, and Nintendo published the Game Boy cartridge. A room is a small diagram: drop a dirt block into a pit, crack a wall with a bomb, or dig down to the layer beneath.

A block that falls into a hole becomes floor and stays there. Detonate in the wrong cell and you erase the very step he needed. Farmer Jinbe is the one who took the family, so every clever shove aims at reaching them.

Surface trails and buried chambers stack on top of each other, and a dig swaps Muddy Mole between those layers. Miyamoto's production keeps the verbs tiny: push, place, explode, drop. Pax Softnica chains those verbs into rooms that punish a hurried shove with a worse layout than the one you started with.

He is not sprinting a cartoon field for points. The family is the destination, and the dirt is both the barrier and the material that builds a path. Nintendo's cartridge measures progress by how much closer that reunion has become.
avenging-spirit-1991:
You play a murdered man's ghost in Avenging Spirit (1991), and the only durable skin is a body that still belongs to someone else. Jaleco made the arcade original, and the Game Boy version is by C.P. Brain. Gangsters killed him and kidnapped his girlfriend, so the spirit overlaps an enemy and inherits that enemy's jump and weapon.

Step out of the host and a spirit meter drains until another body is caught. A gunner, a high jumper, and a slow bruiser answer different hallways, and a slain host throws the ghost back into open air. Restorative pickups sit in the stages, which means you want to be wearing someone when you reach them.

City streets, rooftops, a factory, and the syndicate's base make up the route. Finding the right keys changes whether the girlfriend can be reached before the finish; miss them and the ending plays without her. The handheld version keeps the possession, softens some of the cabinet's harsher timing, and remains an official Jaleco release.

The body currently worn is the entire move set. No permanent upgrade retires that choice, because the next corridor may want a different host. Both the arcade premise and the Game Boy stages are built on the swap.
sword-of-mana:
Brownie Brown retold the first Mana quest as Sword of Mana, Square Enix released that Game Boy Advance version in 2003, and Nintendo published it outside Japan. Choosing the hero or the heroine changes the story scenes that follow. Ring spirits, worn as equipped magic, sit beside sword swings that happen in real time.

The root is Final Fantasy Adventure, called Seiken Densetsu in Japan, not the sixteen-bit Secret of Mana with its party on the Super Nintendo. Towns, partners, and the ring menu enlarge a journey the old Game Boy game only sketched. A spirit ring swaps the magic in hand, and the blade still has to reach the body in front of you.

Her playthrough is not his script with a different portrait. Who stands at the center of a conversation shifts, so a second trip tells another version of the same crisis. Brownie Brown stages the fights as action: step in, swing, and spend the ring instead of freezing the field for a command menu.

Square Enix handled the Japanese side of an official retelling, while Nintendo carried the release abroad. Secret of Mana remains the other branch of the series. This cartridge returns to the earlier pair of leads and lets you decide which of them you follow.
parodius:
Konami's comic answer to Gradius, born in 1990, reached the Game Boy as Parodius Da! A penguin and an octopus can pilot, and the power-ups are jokes that still rewrite the shot. Side-scrolling dodges and a weapon meter survive from the serious shooter, then every option gets dressed as a gag.

Bells push the arsenal forward the way a military game would, except the things flying in formation beside you may honk or flap. Enemy waves still punish a lazy line. The comedy lives in the sprites and the noises, not in a rule that deletes the bullets.

This official handheld edition, published by Konami, is the parody itself rather than a sober Gradius campaign in a costume. Stages scroll through punchlines built from the parent series' imagery. Dying strips the ridiculous weapons away, and that loss still hurts.

Anyone hunting a straight-faced space fighter will not find its tone here. The penguin, the octopus, and the absurd upgrades are both the cast and the kit. Konami asks for the familiar weave through fire, only everyone on screen seems to know the war is a joke.
pokemon-pinball-ruby-sapphire:
Jupiter laid out two boards, Ruby and Sapphire, for Pokémon Pinball: Ruby & Sapphire (2003), and Nintendo published the cartridge. Hit a Pokémon on the playfield to weaken it, then catch it with the ball, and keep playing if you want that catch to evolve. A rumble motor buried in the shell shakes the Game Boy Advance on the hits that matter.

The two tables do not share a layout. Ramps, sinkholes, and the spots where a wild Pokémon appears are arranged differently, so mastering one board leaves the other unsolved. Evolution gives a reason to protect a catch instead of treating every bumper as a pure score.

An earlier Pokémon pinball game used other tables and another roster. This pair is the Ruby board beside the Sapphire board, with the shaking hardware in the plastic. Jupiter's rules still depend on flippers: aim, strike, and live with the bounce you actually got.

Nintendo's single official cartridge holds both tables. The collection grows because the catch happens on the playfield, not in a quiet menu. Miss the flipper and the evolution you were building rolls away down the drain.
puyo-puyo:
Pairs of colored blobs fall, and Compile's Game Boy puzzle Puyo Puyo pops them only when four of one color connect. The 1991 cartridge is the handheld edition of that first puzzle, and a chain dumps garbage onto the opposing stack. Rotate the pair, nest it, and a linked group vanishes, which can tug the blobs above into another group.

An opponent drawn from Compile's fantasy cast answers with junk of their own. A long chain is how you bury them; a sloppy tower is how you bury yourself. There is no gun and no platforming, only the next pair and the rising ceiling.

The numbered follow-up Compile released later is a different cartridge. This edition stays with the original four-blob rule and with an enemy who will not pause while you tidy the well. Compile's official handheld duel is blob against blob, chain against chain.

A pretty pattern still fails if the fourth blob never touches its color. Garbage arrives as rubble you have to build around. The win is a cascade the other side cannot answer before their pile hits the lid.
mario-tennis-power-tour:
Camelot enrolled a student you create at a tennis academy and named the Game Boy Advance story Mario Tennis: Power Tour. Nintendo published it in 2005. Matches and training build that player, then a circuit of tournaments changes the bounce underfoot.

Clay holds and slows the ball, grass skids, and a hard court sends it back quickly. A weak serve becomes dangerous only after the academy has raised the stat behind it. A partner joins for doubles, so the trip is not a line of solo exhibitions against Mario's friends.

The Game Boy Color tennis game is another cartridge with its own story. This academy, this made-to-order athlete, and these traveling events belong to the Advance campaign Camelot wrote. Ignoring the surface is a good way to lose a point you thought you had read.

In Japan the same story carried a different official title, Mario Tennis Advance. Mario and the familiar roster still appear around the tour, yet the rallies that grow your student are the campaign. Court by court, the custom player is the person the story is actually about.
mega-man-zero-2-2003:
Elpizo breaks from the Resistance with a splinter faction in Mega Man Zero 2. Inti Creates developed the Game Boy Advance sequel and Capcom published it in 2003, sending Zero after that rebellion. Forms earned by the way he fights rewrite his moves, and cyber-elves can still be raised and then spent.

One form may stretch a saber string, another changes the dash or leans on an element, so a boss you barely survived becomes a different duel after the body shifts. Feeding an elf can open a shortcut or lift a stat, and some of those uses destroy the elf for good. EX skills taken from defeated bosses add special attacks on top of the form he is wearing.

Ciel's Resistance remains the side he protects while Elpizo hunts a more extreme end to the war. The first game in the line already covered Zero's awakening and the fall of Copy X. This chapter starts from the rift inside the Resistance and hangs the new forms and the elf costs on that chase.

Inti Creates keeps the dash, the saber, and the harsh grading, then layers the form system over them. Capcom's sequel is not a second tour of the opening war. Elpizo's ambition, and the moves learned while stopping him, are why this cartridge exists.
mega-man-zero-3-2004:
Omega looms over Mega Man Zero 3, the Dark Elf corrupts the field, and Doctor Weil is the one pulling strings. Inti Creates developed the chapter and Capcom published it on the Game Boy Advance in 2004. Cyber-elves can now be set as satellites that stay equipped, instead of existing only as offerings for a permanent boost.

Weil binds Omega, a massive reploid tied to the corrupted Mother Elf, to a scheme larger than the Resistance's last internal break. Saber and dash remain Zero's body language, yet the elf menu asks different questions than it did under Elpizo. A satellite modifies him and remains present, which changes how hard the game pushes a sacrifice.

The splinter-faction crisis is over, and the final war's stealing knuckle and selectable weather are not here yet. Stages belong to Weil's manipulation and to Omega's presence on the map. Inti Creates uses that threat to justify the revised elves and another climb in what the bosses demand.

Capcom shipped a middle chapter with its own villain and its own elf rules. The Dark Elf's ruin and Weil's planning are the history this cartridge tells. The loadout you carry into the fight is part of how Zero stands in front of Omega.
warioware-twisted:
Intelligent Systems hid a gyro sensor in the cartridge and turned the whole machine into the controller for WarioWare: Twisted! Nintendo published the Japanese Game Boy Advance release in 2004. Microgames last a few seconds, and many of them clear only when the plastic is tilted or twisted to the angle on screen.

Europe also received an official cartridge. North America did not, at the time, because that sensor made the hardware difficult to ship there. A prompt that says to rotate the device until a figure stands upright will not listen to the D-pad.

Wario still hurls a rapid stack of these tiny demands, sorted into hosted batches. Wrists replace the usual button mash, and blowing one microgame nicks a life in the chain. Intelligent Systems writes the jokes into instructions that are often as short as the games they introduce.

The territories that took the sensor got a real, official release from Nintendo. Players in North America simply had no local edition then, and the gyro was the obstacle. Japan and Europe's cartridges both ask you to tip the entire handheld, not to tap a button and pretend.
riviera-the-promised-land:
Sting first told Ein's story on the Wonderswan, and Atlus published the English Game Boy Advance release of Riviera: The Promised Land in 2005. Ein is a grimangel sent into the land with companions who join along the way. Items shatter after a limited number of uses, so a strong tool is also a countdown.

Before battle you choose the small set of things worth carrying in. Each swing or cast spends a use, and a count of zero destroys that item for the rest of the journey. A companion changes conversations and the texture of a fight, which keeps the party from being a row of identical attack values.

Much of the travel is a decision about where to go next and what to bring, rather than a long walk across an empty field. Gods and demons frame the grimangel's assignment, with Riviera the place in dispute. Sting's breakable inventory forces a real choice every time a rare object looks useful.

Atlus's English script is an official translation of a game that already existed on the Wonderswan. The Advance edition and that earlier handheld release are the proper editions of Ein's assignment. Companions, a thinning pack, and a grimangel who cannot treat his gear as infinite are what you actually manage.
mega-man-battle-network-2-2001:
Gospel's netcrime spree is the case file in Mega Man Battle Network 2. Capcom released the Game Boy Advance sequel in 2001, with Lan operating MegaMan.EXE. Style Change is the new system: Guts, Custom, Team, and Shield styles bend his stats, and an element can color a style further.

Keep fighting a certain way and the style grows out of the habit. Guts hits harder, Custom reworks the chip setup, Team pulls a partner into the pattern, and Shield pays off a careful guard. Viruses still occupy the familiar battle grid, and battle chips still supply the special attacks.

The opening Battle Network game had none of these styles. Gospel operates as a criminal network rather than as one rival navi, which gives the sequel its plot. Lan's choices in the real world and MegaMan.EXE's body on the net stay locked together, jack-in after jack-in.

Capcom's follow-up is where that style system begins. Someone who only finished the first game will find new forms growing from their own tendencies in a fight. Gospel's scheme is the story, and the styles are how the battles stop feeling like the previous cartridge.
sonic-battle:
Emerl, a Gizoid with an empty move list, learns by watching, and Sonic Team built Sonic Battle around the techniques he copies. Sega published the Game Boy Advance fighter in 2003. Bounded arenas replace the side-scrolling run: bodies move in a ring, throw, and spend specials they have actually acquired.

Story scenes fill Emerl's list as he meets the cast and borrows what they do. A skill he has never witnessed is a skill he cannot perform, so the campaign behaves like a lesson plan. Sonic, Tails, Knuckles, Amy, Shadow, Rouge, and Cream serve as both teachers and opponents.

Loops, robot badniks, and a sprint to the right are not the structure. Spacing in the arena, the special you chose to equip, and the moment you spend it decide the exchange. Sonic Team treats the Gizoid's mimicry as the reason a move can pass from one fighter to another.

Sega's fighter keeps the cast recognizable and changes the verb from running to fighting. Emerl stays at the center even during a bout you play as somebody else. Copying is how the blank list becomes a full one.
mega-man-zero-4-2005:
Craft's defiance, Weil's weapon Ragnarok, and a Z-Knuckle that steals parts set the terms of Mega Man Zero 4. Inti Creates made this last Zero game, and Capcom published it for the Game Boy Advance in 2005. Weather moves over areas you choose, rewriting hazards before the stage even starts. Zero still answers that threat with the stolen parts.

The knuckle punches a component off a foe and equips it, so an enemy's element becomes Zero's for a while. Craft serves close to Weil and does not remain a plain lieutenant, while Ragnarok is the orbital threat aimed at whatever is left of the world. Entering a region under another sky can mean ice, wind, or a clearer field, and that choice is part of preparing.

Ciel and Zero are near the end of the road under Neo Arcadia's rule. Elpizo's split and Omega's Dark Elf sit in the past of this final hunt. Inti Creates uses the knuckle, the weather, and the area select so the closing cartridge does not play like its predecessors.

Capcom's ending of the Zero line puts Weil's plan and Craft's break in one story. No later game in the line arrives to finish the plot. Stolen parts and the skies you travel under are how those last fights are actually fought.
astro-boy-omega-factor:
Treasure and Hitmaker dropped Astro into side-scrolling rooms and a library of manga faces in Astro Boy: Omega Factor. Sega published the Game Boy Advance game in 2003. Two routes structure the campaign, and the entries logged in that library change what the second route becomes.

Astro flies, fires the arm cannon, and chains hits in the crowded style Treasure favors. A combo is the point of a packed room: launch someone, keep the counter alive, and do not drop the juggle. Hitmaker's share of the work sits beside that action, under Sega's publishing.

The library records characters drawn from the wider manga around Astro, and meeting them is how a page fills. The first route introduces the crisis and the cast. A thin first trip and a thorough one do not unlock the same follow-up, because the second route reads the library.

Osamu Tezuka's hero is the body on screen, while the cartridge keeps inviting faces from the surrounding stories. Sega released an official action game with a real second path, not a sketch of the character. Treasure's hit chains and the library's effect on that return visit are the two ideas that run it.
metal-slug-advance:
Noise Factory built a handheld Metal Slug whose loadout lives in a binder of cards, and SNK published it as Metal Slug Advance in 2004. Those cards rewrite which weapons you bring and how a mission is framed. The campaign was made for the Game Boy Advance, not reduced from a single arcade board.

Soldiers still run, jump, shoot, and dive clear of blasts. One card might hand over a different gun, another a vehicle, another a twist on the objective waiting ahead. Filling the binder is progress, because the stage alone does not freeze the kit.

Arcade Metal Slug releases keep their own fixed routes and their own weapon drops along the way. This cartridge asks for a set of cards first, then sends them into missions written for the small screen. Noise Factory holds onto the chunky soldiers and the hectic fire while the binder does the customizing.

SNK's official Advance entry depends on that collection. Leave the cards idle and the marches stay plain. Spend them and the same stretch of war can mean another gun and another goal.
boktai-the-sun-is-in-your-hand:
Django's solar gun reads a real light sensor seated in the cartridge of Boktai: The Sun Is in Your Hand. Konami released the Game Boy Advance game in 2003 as a Kojima production. Sunlight in the room charges the weapon, and a dim corner leaves the shots too thin for the work.

Vampires and other immortals are what he hunts. The gun is how a boss is finished and how a sealing has the power to hold, so closing the curtains is a way to make the dungeon harder on purpose. Otenko, a messenger of the sun, walks the crypts with him.

The sensor is not a slider buried in a menu. Angle the cartridge toward the light and the solar meter climbs; stay in shade and the beam starves. Konami built stealth, coffins, and gunfire around that physical reading.

Calling it a Kojima production points at the way the strange hardware and the vampire plot were designed together. The hunt gives the solar gun a reason to exist. Without sun on the sensor, Django is still in the dungeon and simply less able to end what lives there.
drill-dozer-2005:
Jill ratchets a drill into higher gears and bores through walls in Drill Dozer. Game Freak developed the Game Boy Advance platformer, Nintendo published it in 2005, and the shell rumbles while the bit spins. The studio stepped outside its creature-collecting work: L and R spin the drill opposite ways.

The first gear is a short burst. Finding another gear lets her shift up, and the top gear keeps cutting until a hit breaks the spin. Screws, thick blocks, and enemies all meet the same rotating bit, and direction matters when a fitting must be turned rather than smashed.

That rumble motor kicks during a drill, so the hands can feel which gear she is in. Jill rides the machine through side-view stages and recoils off a surface when the other shoulder is tapped. Game Freak uses the kick to cross gaps a standing hop would miss.

Nintendo put out a platformer whose main verb is drilling. Maps and stronger bits turn up between areas, and a stolen Red Diamond gives the Red Dozers' daughter a reason to keep the bit against the next wall. The famous monster quests from this studio are a different job entirely.
crash-bandicoot-the-huge-adventure:
Vicarious Visions built a warp-room platformer and gave the American Game Boy Advance release the name Crash Bandicoot: The Huge Adventure. Europe called the same cartridge Crash Bandicoot XS, Japan called it Crash Bandicoot Advance, and the release sat in 2002. The stages were drawn for this handheld, not converted from the first home-console Crash adventure.

The hub sends him into a short side-view level and takes him back when the exit is reached. Crates, pits, and a spin through enemies fill those rooms at a scale the small screen can hold. Cortex is still scheming, and the hazards were laid out for this cartridge's own map.

That original console adventure has its own beaches and ruins. Nothing here asks the Advance hardware to restage that run room for room. Vicarious Visions uses the warp room so one portable sitting can be a single level and a return to the hub.

Three official regional titles cover one game. XS and Advance are not sequels hiding behind translation; they are the European and Japanese names. The American structure is the hub, the original stages, and Crash's spin, built for the handheld on purpose.
rhythm-tengoku:
Nintendo SPD, producing with Tsunku, made a Japan-only Game Boy Advance rhythm game called Rhythm Tengoku. It arrived in 2006 as the first entry in the line later known in English as Rhythm Heaven, and no English edition of this Advance cartridge was published. Karate Man punches on a call, a night walk steps to a tempo, and remix stages braid earlier cues into a medley.

A prompt gives a picture and a sound, and the button has to land on that cue. Karate Man's pots and the voice that tells him when to strike are a lesson in listening. The night walk wants footsteps that match a beat while the scene keeps moving, a different demand from the punching stance.

Remix stages behave like exams. They quote pieces of the games just played and shuffle the order, so a cue learned on its own has to be recognized inside a crowd. Tsunku's music gives the cues their hooks, and Nintendo SPD builds the tiny scenes that make each hook visible.

The Japanese cartridge is the official release. Later games in the line traveled abroad on other hardware under the Rhythm Heaven name. This Advance original is where Karate Man, the night walk, and those remix exams began.
boktai-2-solar-boy-django:
San Miguel, a town Django can walk, anchors Boktai 2: Solar Boy Django. Konami released the sequel in 2004 with the sun sensor back in the cartridge, and his weapons are no longer limited to the solar gun. Swords, spears, and hammers can be carried, then fed with daylight so a blade still cares about the weather on the desk.

The Gun Del Sol is stolen at the start, which is why the other weapons exist. A glove that enchants ordinary steel with solar power lets him keep facing immortals until a gun can be recovered. Bright light still fills the meter; shade still starves any magic that depends on it.

Streets in San Miguel connect shops, a way to turn stored sunlight into money, and the roads out to the next dungeon. Forging can join two weapons into a stronger one when the solar work is done properly. Vampires remain the quarry, and a coffin still has to be handled after the fight ends.

Konami kept the physical sensor and widened combat past a single pistol. Someone who only played the first hunt will find a hometown, a missing gun, and a rack of melee weapons. Daylight on the cartridge still shapes the build, even when the thing in his hand is a sword.
mega-man-battle-network-6:
Cybeasts Gregar and Falzar split Mega Man Battle Network 6 into two cartridges, and Capcom shipped the pair in 2005 as the close of the original Battle Network story. Link Navis from earlier games join Lan once their crosses are earned. The cybeast tied to a given version changes which navis, chips, and last battles show up.

MegaMan.EXE still deletes viruses on the net while Lan operates him from the physical world. A Link Navi is playable machinery, not a portrait: after the cross is obtained, that navi can be operated and its attack brought into a folder. Gregar's roster and Falzar's roster do not match, so the two editions are a paired ending rather than copies.

Crosses alter MegaMan.EXE in a way the older Style Change system does not cover. Threads from the long netcrime saga meet the cybeasts here. Capcom treats the pair as the conclusion, with version-exclusive bosses standing in for one shared finale.

Operators who remember earlier navis see them return with actual battle roles. Picking Gregar or Falzar picks an ally list and picks the beast waiting at the end. The original story stops on this official pair.
dk-king-of-swing:
Donkey Kong hangs from pegs by gripping the shoulder buttons in DK: King of Swing. Paon developed the Game Boy Advance game, Nintendo published it in 2005, and holding L and R together is how he sticks. Release one side and he pivots; release at the right angle and he launches toward the next peg.

Boards of pegs sit in jungle scenery, with bananas and hazards in the gaps. A mistimed let-go drops him, and no run-and-roll replaces the swing. The mischief around the boards is jungle slapstick, but the buttons only ever mean grip, pivot, and throw.

Country games send him sprinting past barrels, mine carts, and long platforms. This cartridge barely uses that kind of running. Paon builds the test out of the peg field and the two shoulders, so a player who only mashes a jump will not cross the gap.

Nintendo published a jungle caper whose skill is the timing of a handhold. Charge the swing, choose a peg, and let go. The board itself, not a scrolling footrace, is the stage.
gunstar-super-heroes:
Treasure followed its Genesis shooter with a Game Boy Advance successor, Gunstar Super Heroes, and Sega published it in 2005. Europe knows that same cartridge as Gunstar Future Heroes. Shots can be pointed instead of locked forward, and weapon types merge into hybrid blasts the way the earlier Treasure guns could be combined.

Projectiles, mines, and oversized bosses crowd the screen. Choosing a merged weapon is a decision made before the room gets loud, and the adjustable aim puts the shot where the enemies actually stand. Treasure's dense patterns want movement and fire at the same time, with little empty space left to rest.

The Genesis Gunstar Heroes game is the ancestor, not a level list being squeezed onto a small panel. This Advance chapter continues those heroes on stages of its own, with the same appetite for crowded fire. Sega's publishing and the European Future Heroes name are official labels for that successor.

Two weapon traits together produce a blast neither trait manages alone. Aim that can leave the forward line matters once foes stop lining up in front of the barrel. Treasure stacks both ideas under a storm of moving objects so the handheld fight still feels like a Gunstar room.
tactics-ogre-the-knight-of-lodis:
Alphonse Loeher, a knight of the Lodis empire, is sent into a war on the island of Ovis in Tactics Ogre: The Knight of Lodis, the Game Boy Advance campaign Quest created, with Atlus publishing the English edition of that 2001 tale. Battles sit on an angled overhead grid where facing, height, and who can still act decide a skirmish. Class changes let a survivor study a new discipline after enough combat, so a spearman need not stay a spearman.

The campaign is a side story, separate from Let Us Cling Together and the struggle on Valeria. Noble houses on Ovis treat every truce as a pause between betrayals, and the knights caught in the middle have to decide which order to obey. A sour political choice can change who is still willing to fight in the next deployment.

Equipment and a class path belong to each character rather than to one avatar. Holding the high tiles and keeping a healer inside range matters as much as the printed attack number. A blocked lane can waste a spellcaster for a whole turn.

Quest designed the marches and the talk between them, and Atlus carried that script to English-speaking players. Clearing a map usually means protecting the units a later chapter still needs, rather than sprinting at the enemy leader.
mega-man-battle-network-3:
Programs placed in a Navi Customizer rewrite how the partner moves and shoots in Mega Man Battle Network 3, the White and Blue cartridges Capcom released in 2002. Style Change comes back, but the forms can be swapped instead of locking an operator into the first style earned. The WWW presses its plan through the net, while Lan's friendships keep pulling the plot back to people on the far side of the screen.

Parts that conflict can bug the Navi, so a strong setup is also a risk. Chip duels still occupy rows of panels, with a folder chosen before the fight and movement counted in squares. White and Blue differ in which chips and which encounters are easier to find, while the crisis itself stays the same shape.

Streets lead to jack-in ports, and the net beyond them is a chain of servers crossed on foot. Operators argue, pair up, and get cut off as the trouble moves from one district to the next. Lan's refusal to treat his Navi as a disposable tool sits under every virus fight.

Capcom built both cartridges around that net crisis and the friendships inside it. A style form changes favored chips and the look of the armor, so a folder that suited one form can feel clumsy after the switch.
super-mario-advance-4-super-mario-bros-3:
Physical e-Reader cards, scanned with the add-on accessory, supply extra courses alongside Super Mario Advance 4: Super Mario Bros. 3, Nintendo's 2003 handheld port of the NES world tour. The kings' stolen magic wands, the forked maps, and Bowser's airship still structure the main trip. A Mario Bros. battle mode shares the cartridge with that journey.

Those cards are objects you hold and swipe, a physical add-on kept beside the cart rather than a password typed on a title screen. Without the accessory, the eight worlds and their fortresses remain a full quest. Hammer suits, frog suits, and tanooki tails behave much as they did when the stages were new.

Some courses scroll on their own, some hide a second exit, and a few demand a very short hop onto a moving lift. Chain-link fences and pipes still ask for the older, stricter timing. The battle mode is the separate Mario Bros. arena, where foes are bumped from below on stacked platforms.

Nintendo issued the port in the Super Mario Advance line. The scanned-card stages widen the trip only when the matching cards and the e-Reader are both present.
mega-man-battle-network-5:
Occupied panels have to be won back one square at a time in Mega Man Battle Network 5, Capcom's 2004 pair sold as Team ProtoMan and Team Colonel. Each cartridge fields a different party of Navis for those operations. Lan and MegaMan remain the leads, while the allies standing on the map change with the version in the slot.

A liberation mission behaves more like a small tactics board than an ordinary chip duel. You step across darkened panels, free them, and only then confront the Navi holding the zone. Item cubes and enemy placements turn that advance into a route.

ProtoMan's roster and Colonel's roster do not match, which is why two carts were sold. A Navi's temperament shows up in the mission that Navi leads and in the chips that arrive with the alliance. The other version's team cannot be menu-swapped into your save.

Beneath the grid objectives, Capcom kept folders, row movement, and timed buster shots. Mail, keys, and distress calls in the city point toward the next liberation.
mega-man-battle-network-4:
Dark chips offer a harsher shortcut through the tournament brackets of Mega Man Battle Network 4, which Capcom shipped in 2003 as Red Sun and Blue Moon. Double Soul fusions let MegaMan borrow another Navi's form for a short run of altered shots. Lan travels from one official competition to the next while those chips keep tempting an easier clear.

The two versions exchange tournament lineups, souls, and scenario opponents rather than telling unrelated plots. Win a bracket and the tour shifts to another region with a fresh set of operators. Later cycles repeat matches with different details, so one folder has to survive more than a single pass.

A soul comes from a Navi Lan has already met, and the fusion changes elemental strengths plus the charge attack. Shaping the folder around that soul matters more than stuffing it with unrelated rare chips. Taking a dark chip raises the damage and feeds a corruption that is hard to set aside once it starts.

Towns between the arenas still hide small jobs and virus packs on the net. The tournament is the road the plot travels, with the chip trade running under the sanctioned matches.
ninja-five-o:
Joe Osugi's grappling rope does as much work as his sword in Ninja Five-O, the Hudson Soft side-scroller Konami published in the United States in 2003. He is a ninja police officer, and each building asks him to bring hostages out before the armed men finish the job. Europe received the same cartridge under the name Ninja Cop.

The camera stays in a strict side profile. The rope hooks beams and crates, swings him over gaps, and yanks a thug into a throw. Hostages have to be walked clear while the clock and the gunfire keep moving.

A sloppy swing drops him into a shot he cannot trade, and ordinary contact is already expensive. Shuriken cover the moments when a hook is the wrong tool. Learning a floor means knowing which beam is safe and which guard fires the instant he lets go.

Hudson Soft built the rooms, and Konami handled the American release of that strict rescue run. Later buildings add lasers, extra floors, and less time to pick the next hook.
advance-guardian-heroes:
Enn, Ray, and Hyu open Advance Guardian Heroes, Treasure's 2004 Game Boy Advance follow-up to the Saturn brawler, published by Ubisoft. Fire, lightning, and ice set those three starters apart, and directional weapon strings supply the combos. A demon's offer after a knockout can change which ending plays, a narrower fork than the many routes of the Saturn game.

Holding the attack and steering it changes the string, so one button is not the whole moveset. Launched foes can be chased upward, and a mistimed special leaves a wide opening. Magic spends a gauge that does not refill generously between crowds.

Stage order stays fixed, unlike the Saturn campaign's reshuffling paths. Two players can share story mode, and a versus option waits for a direct fight. Further fighters are earned later, but the campaign begins with the three elemental leads.

Ubisoft published Treasure's handheld brawler for players who never owned the Saturn original. Later chapters punish a repeated pattern, and mashing through a group stops working once the enemy sets overlap.
star-fox-64-3d:
Optional gyro aiming sits beside the medal routes in Star Fox 64 3D, Nintendo's 2011 stereoscopic remake of the rail shooter. Barrel rolls, charged lasers, and the wingmen's radio chatter return, with depth that pushes arches and debris toward the player. The edition in hand is the handheld remake, distinct from the original Nintendo 64 cartridge.

All-range sorties drop the Arwing into an open arena for certain bosses and planetary fights, apart from the on-rails corridors. Earning a medal on a stage opens the harder branch, so a sloppy run can miss the path toward another ending. Gyro aim can be switched off when the circle pad alone is preferred.

Peppy, Slippy, and Falco still call targets and still blunder into trouble you can prevent. A bomb clears a lane when the screen fills. Landmaster and submarine stretches remain among the route changes, along with returns to the Great Fox.

Nintendo kept the short-mission shape: pick a world, fly it, and watch the map redraw the next choices. Collecting every medal is its own task beside simply reaching one last boss.
tomodachi-life:
Songs, arguments, and clumsy dates fill the hours on the Mii island of Tomodachi Life, Nintendo's 2014 sandbox about neighbors rather than a scored contest. You feed them, choose their clothes, and assign apartments they promptly clutter. A face built from your own features can move in and start requesting snacks.

No results screen waits at the end of a tidy afternoon. Hunger, moods, and tiny errands call you back, and leaving a resident alone makes the complaint louder. Relationships form, collapse, and sometimes produce a child who then needs a room of their own.

Concerts, dreams you step into, and whatever the shop is stocking give the island its daily loop. The humor comes from Miis misreading one another and from the babble they use in place of ordinary sentences. Nudging two neighbors into a romance does not stop them quarreling about something petty an hour afterward.

Nintendo shaped the island as a place you look in on. A meal settles an immediate mood, while a catchphrase and a messy interior are how one Mii starts to feel like a particular person.
monster-hunter-4-ultimate:
Gore Magala's frenzy spreads along the roads between settlements in Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate, the Capcom hunt that became the west's major handheld Monster Hunter in 2015. Mounting lets a hunter climb a monster and topple it when the struggle holds. Guild quests, rolled with odd conditions of their own, sit beside a caravan story that travels from one village to another.

Capcom made the weapons, the monsters, and the quests. Help on the English script came from the localization studio 8-4, which did not take over making the game. Frenzied and apex states change how aggressive a familiar species feels on ground you already know.

Long weapon animations commit you, so a clean mount is often the opening that creates a safe punish. Gathering, cooking, and armor skills fill the camp before the next departure. Reading footprints and picking a weapon matchup remain the patient work these hunts demand.

As the caravan moves, the cooks, guild staff, and companions nearby change with it. Clearing an urgent monster in one hub usually opens the next stretch of that journey.
warioware-gold:
Earlier microgames and brand-new ones share a voiced story mode in WarioWare Gold, the Intelligent Systems collection Nintendo released in 2018. Wario and the regular crew introduce toys that last only a few seconds each. It arrived late in the hardware's life, among the last large Nintendo releases for that system.

A stage gives one verb, such as dodge, charge, or match a pose, and then the timer expires. A miss is immediate, and the next gag starts almost at once. Speed climbs from readable introductions into rounds that leave no time to think the prompt through.

Bosses inside the story obey the same split-second rules as the toys around them. Spoken lines fill scenes that older entries often left as text and grunts. Touch-screen gags sit beside button gags drawn from earlier volumes of the series.

Nintendo published the Intelligent Systems compilation, voice tracks included. The story gives the pile a beginning and an end, and a single toy can still be replayed for a stricter score once that plot is finished.
shin-megami-tensei-iv-apocalypse:
Nanashi walks the ruined streets in Shin Megami Tensei IV: Apocalypse, the Atlus side story released in 2016. Human partners join the party and pull the tone toward personal bonds, louder than the stern journey this plot overlaps. The events sit during Shin Megami Tensei IV, and the campaign is its own story rather than a remake.

Demon negotiation, fusion, and press-turn battles carry the fights. Factions already active in that Tokyo try to claim Nanashi, and alignment choices push back. Underground districts and surface ruins hide encounters that can end a run when the party is careless.

Bonds with those partners change scenes and some resolutions, so brushing the group off is a real decision. Resistances and skill sets still decide whether a boss pattern can be broken. Hunter associations and divine powers remain the political weather over the city.
